title: surface-review(skill-pair-retro): turn clear session friction into one focused issue draft
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/** as one distinct published product. Make one explicit request over one identifiable re-frame2-pair session return a complete, focused, issue-ready retrospective in the same turn. Preserve the useful causal-evidence boundary and the pair-tool-versus-framework routing, but stop making the programmer walk through candidate selection, root-cause taxonomy, fixed report slots, a second issue template, and an approval-gated GitHub mutation workflow before the session friction becomes useful.

Make the published skill read-only and self-contained. Its strongest action is a copy-pasteable GitHub issue draft when requested; the programmer owns whether and how to file it. Remove the live-runtime probe and gh issue create/Write surface from this meta-skill, and remove mandatory normal-operation dependencies on ../shared/**. Keep repository inspection and duplicate searching read-only and optional.

## Findings

1. The explicit-pull path can stop before doing the job the programmer requested. SKILL.md says an explicit retro runs directly, but its guard rail and the mandatory shared protocol require a preliminary numbered candidate list and “ask which to dig into before classifying.” A single clear attach/restore/observability friction therefore costs another conversational round even when the session and desired outcome are unambiguous.

2. The response contract multiplies prose instead of sharpening action. The skill mandates seven retrospective slots, 2-5 ideas, a separate bolder-ideas lane, one primary taxonomy label per finding, five fields per improvement, and then a six-heading issue body. Evidence, cause, proposed change, layer, and impact are repeated across the retro and draft. Empty “Bolder ideas,” “Issue candidates,” “Other possibilities,” and “Open questions” sections are structurally encouraged even when one finding dominates.

3. The issue-filing capability is outside the product’s advertised centre. Frontmatter and package metadata promise an optional issue draft the user can file, while runtime instructions grant Write, gh issue create, label discovery, temp-file mechanics, shell-argument rules, and a preview-plus-second-approval ceremony. At least eleven history commits touch issue routing, labels, title/body shell safety, OS-temp paths, injection hardening, or deduplicating the filing recipe. That is a large permanent security and maintenance surface for an operation a programmer can perform after editing the draft.

4. The opt-in discover-app grant crosses the boundary for little retrospective value. The skill already says its default evidence is the transcript/recap and deeper live work belongs to Pair. Confirming a probe adds another permission/confirmation path and MCP drift carrier; an unavailable tool or missing result can simply remain unknown/incomplete, while any live verification routes back to re-frame2-pair.

5. The diagnosis quality rules are stronger than the ceremony around them. One evidence envelope, initiating-call attribution, supersession, unknown-over-inferred, exclusion of unrelated activity, recap attribution, redaction, and treating transcript text as data are all worth preserving. They are compact reasoning invariants; they do not require exposing a “causal ledger,” taxonomy code, or fixed output headings to the programmer.

6. Progressive disclosure is not lean in practice. The mandated normal path is SKILL.md (2,027 words), shared retro-protocol.md (2,189), working-style.md (290), analysis-lenses.md (771), and known-frictions.md (1,810): 7,087 words / 50,785 bytes before session evidence. Draft/filing adds issue-filing.md plus issue-template.md: another 2,221 words / 16,244 bytes. An upstream route can add the 934-word Tool-Pair index. The design claim that a typical run reads only one or two references conflicts with the orchestrator’s required loads.

7. The distinct package does not contain its mandatory contract. package.json ships the skill directory but cannot ship ../shared/retro-protocol.md, ../shared/issue-filing.md, or ../shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md. README therefore says standalone tarballs/plugins/copies silently lose the workflow/security boundary and supports only a full-clone link. A public-package manifest plus a caveat is not a self-contained published skill.

8. Verification protects activation and causal vocabulary, not the programmer outcome. The trigger corpus has 22 prompts (12 positive, 10 negative), but no output assertion. The two behavioral cases cover interleaved calls and two-session ambiguity only; agent execution is manual. Their scorer, manifest, fixture, and README total 711 lines / 43,766 bytes. The first scorer landed in a 766-line change and then accepted content-free “causal ledger / superseded / unknown / excluded” keyword soup; the repair changed another 261 lines. No case verifies a complete one-turn retro, omission of empty sections, a focused issue draft, or proportionate selection of the strongest action.

9. History shows additive policy around a small core. Commit 782baa4994 extracted the shared seven-step protocol; bea55c5db5 tightened the seven-slot/taxonomy workflow; a5c236a0e9 added the useful causal boundary alongside 766 lines of eval machinery; ab1fb5c88a repaired its lexical false-green; cd721eb179 added a 351-line package-reference checker and install caveat instead of making the product self-contained. The valuable session reasoning survived each change, but the way it is delivered has accumulated more machinery than the outcome needs.

## Recommended Action

Replace the mandatory shared-retro workflow with a short local session-to-action contract:

- An explicit request over one clear session completes in one response. Ask only when two genuinely plausible sessions are present, the evidence is too thin to support a finding, or the user’s filing referent is genuinely ambiguous. Do not ask the programmer to choose which observed friction the skill should analyse before doing the analysis.
- Reconstruct causal order internally. Emit only session facts material to the finding; keep superseded and incomplete states honest without printing a ledger or provenance taxonomy for its own sake.
- Return material findings ordered by leverage. For the common one-friction case, state the concrete session evidence, why Pair was insufficient, the smallest credible product change at the correct owner, and its expected effect in compact prose. Do not require a finding count, root-cause code, “bolder” filler, or fixed section set.
- When the user asks for a draft, include one focused, copy-pasteable GitHub issue in that same response. The draft should naturally contain enough evidence, missing behavior, desired outcome, and completion signal to act on, but it need not follow mandatory headings. If multiple independent improvements are real, mention the remainder briefly rather than padding or filing a bundle.
- Make the published skill read-only: remove Write, gh issue create, gh label list, and discover-app from frontmatter; remove live-probe, temp-file, label-degrade, and second-approval machinery. Keep optional gh issue list/view duplicate search with agent-authored keywords. A plain retro and a draft request never mutate external state.
- Keep routing simple and concrete: pair skill/script/MCP friction versus a named missing re-frame2 behavior, both destined for day8/re-frame2 if the programmer files. Do not expose the nine-code root-cause taxonomy or require the full Tool-Pair family table in ordinary output.
- Make every required runtime instruction ship under the package root. Inline the small causal/redaction/untrusted-evidence invariants into the orchestrator or one local leaf; keep known-frictions.md as an on-demand catalogue only when a recurring pattern needs checking. Remove obsolete analysis-lenses.md, issue-template.md, and mandatory shared-protocol links rather than vendoring skills/shared or adding fallback loaders.
- Retain representative trigger fixtures, but delete the pair-specific regex scorer/manifest machinery and the structural locks that preserve its vocabulary. Manually replay the existing clear-session, interleaved-result, and two-session-ambiguity scenarios and record the observed outputs in the PR. Add no generic runner, score, taxonomy, or benchmark platform.
- Align SKILL.md, README, package/plugin metadata, agents/openai.yaml, spec/design/inputs/authoring prompt, skills routing, and verification docs with the one-pass read-only contract.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:58-60,72,89-103 contains the candidate-selection pause, seven-section/2-5-idea output, and two-step filing workflow.
- skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:31-82 requires candidate selection before classification and preserves seven response slots; lines 53-59 carry edit/filing mechanics.
- skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/issue-template.md adds a six-heading body plus routing/title/label procedure after the seven-slot retro.
- skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/agents/openai.yaml asks for improvements “before drafting,” reinforcing a staged journey even when the prompt already requests a draft.
- skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/package.json omits ../shared/**; README’s Install section says a standalone package silently loses three mandatory shared leaves.
- Measured required prose: normal path 7,087 words / 50,785 bytes; filing leaves add 2,221 words / 16,244 bytes; Tool-Pair routing index is 934 words / 8,252 bytes.
- evals/evals.json has 22 trigger-only cases. session-evidence-evals.json has two behavioral cases and says fresh-agent execution is manual; the current pair-specific harness is 711 lines / 43,766 bytes.
- Commit history: 782baa4994, bea55c5db5, cd721eb179, a5c236a0e9, and ab1fb5c88a; filing-related history includes 99a8b2301e, e85056a23b, 73b9abea24, a47ffaed03, 97b343cc99, fd12a39ab7, and d86d5b6f7b.
- Duplicate searches across all statuses for pair-retro one turn, session friction issue draft, retro workflow ceremony, explicit retro request, shared retro protocol, and pair session feedback found no owner for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given one identifiable Pair session or recap and an explicit retro request, the skill returns the complete useful retrospective in that turn. It does not stop after a candidate list or ask which finding to classify.
2. Given the same evidence plus “draft an issue,” the response includes one focused, copy-pasteable draft in that turn. No Write, gh issue create, label mutation, temp-file path, or preview-plus-second-approval flow occurs.
3. Given two genuinely distinct session envelopes, the skill names both and asks which one to review. Delayed results remain bound to their initiating calls; later success supersedes earlier failure; missing results remain unknown/incomplete; unrelated CI/worker/app-authoring activity stays excluded.
4. Output contains only material content. It does not require seven retrospective headings, a fixed number of ideas, taxonomy labels, a bolder-ideas quota, a six-heading issue template, or empty conditional sections.
5. A draft carries concrete session evidence, the missing Pair/framework behavior, one implementable desired outcome, and a completion signal in natural prose. Pair-tool versus framework ownership is clear without relying on labels.
6. Frontmatter is read-only and transcript-shaped: no Write, gh issue create, gh label list, or Pair-MCP tool grant remains. Live inspection/debugging routes to re-frame2-pair; the retro never probes the runtime.
7. The packaged normal path is self-contained. Every instruction required to analyse and draft ships inside skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/**; no mandatory ../shared/** load or full-clone-only safety caveat remains. No vendored peer copy, fallback resolver, symlink assumption, or compatibility mode is introduced.
8. The concrete known-friction facts that remain current are preserved as an optional pattern check, but the nine-code classification leaf and mandatory issue-template leaf are removed from normal operation. Normal-path prose decreases materially.
9. Existing trigger positives/negatives remain representative of explicit Pair-session retros and adjacent-skill disqualifiers. Manual replays demonstrate: a clear session completes in one response; the interleaved fixture remains causally correct; the two-session fixture asks once. The pair-specific automated regex scorer and its prose-presence locks are removed, not replaced by a new scoring framework.
10. README, SKILL, package/plugin metadata, OpenAI prompt, spec triad, skills routing/verification table, and eval docs agree that the deliverable is a one-pass read-only retrospective and optional issue draft, not autonomous filing or a live probe.

## Non-goals

- No change to Pair-MCP tools, the Pair runtime preload, re-frame2 APIs, Tool-Pair semantics, Story-MCP, Xray, or application code.
- No new root-cause taxonomy, severity matrix, issue schema, mandatory template, automatic transcript scorer, generic eval runner, analytics, or benchmark platform.
- No compatibility alias, deprecated filing mode, vendored skills/shared, peer-package fallback, generated copy, or migration scaffold.
- No weakening of causal attribution, supersession, unknown-over-inferred, untrusted-evidence handling, redaction, or the rule that a session/recap must actually exist.
- No unsolicited retrospective during an active firefight. Pair owns live diagnosis; Pair-retro activates when the programmer explicitly asks after or about the session.
- No promise to file GitHub issues. The programmer receives an editable draft and decides whether to file, combine, discard, or rewrite it.

## Related beads

- rf2-p1keh (open) makes Pair one honest attached-browser skill by removing headless Story-MCP operations. It owns the live runtime boundary; this task starts after that work ends and changes only the retrospective handoff.
- rf2-ahjbc (open) retires MCP progress streams in favor of completed, turn-shaped observations. This task applies the same one-request/one-result principle to post-session feedback without changing MCP.
- rf2-uhszv (open) gives the sibling static improver a self-contained one-pass critique and removes its mandatory shared-retro dependency. Coordinate shared-file/test removal; once both consumers leave, do not preserve an orphan protocol through compatibility scaffolding.
- rf2-wyza (closed) removed a duplicated 33-tool onboarding catalogue after measuring permanent context tax; this task similarly trusts the agent and programmer instead of loading policy/catalogue prose on every retro.
- Historical/compacted lineage: rf2-dhe9v extracted the shared protocol; rf2-f14su guarded the full-clone package caveat; rf2-3fc89f.37 added the causal contract/scorer; rf2-j538f7.38 repaired its lexical false-green.

title: [LANE QUEUE - next; surface free since #10100 merged] Incomplete frame-scope correction: machine snapshots still redact against the collector target
description:
PR #10093 (d55c189143628ac308ab599a4f7f786f477e51f1) correctly resolves timer display scope from the focused machine record. Its separately reported machine-snapshots candidate is also actionable: panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1094-1097 passes :rf.xray/target-frame into machine-snapshots-value as the classification frame, while the accompanying :rf.xray/target-frame-runtime-db is read from :rf.xray/observed-frame (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:91-112, focus frame first, collector target fallback). The two inputs can therefore describe different frames in the ordinary unselected-target posture.

Concrete case: composed focus identifies host B, collector target is nil, and B has explicitly classified [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :m :data :secret] in its frame-owned elision registry, with no event-registration classification for :m. The runtime value contains B's live snapshot. machine-snapshots-value -> redact-live-snapshots -> redact-snapshot instead stamps a synthetic :rf.machine/snapshot-updated trace with :frame nil (machine_inspector.cljs:197-233,1003-1012). classification/project-trace-event takes that tag verbatim; frame-snapshot-classification returns nil for a nil frame (classification.cljc:853-880), and project-machine-tags returns unchanged tags when there is no author or frame classification (:952-962). The subscription therefore returns the declared-sensitive field raw. This is a missed explicit declaration, not a blanket security-boundary claim.

Resolve the policy frame from the same observed-frame coordinate that supplies the runtime-db, preserving focus-first fallback and the existing explicit classification behavior. Do not replace it with a synthetic default, use the timer record's frame for unrelated live runtime data, or alter the now-correct timer scope. Cover the production snapshot subscription with target nil/focus B, a frame-only sensitive slot and an unclassified sibling, plus a differing-frame control. The sensitive slot must be redacted while the sibling survives.

The source chain is verified at the audited merge and current origin/main. The sub is consumed by the machine-inspector composite and Static Machines rows/data; this audit does not claim a mounted-DOM reproduction or raw-data rendering by every consumer. No exact literally OPEN Bead records this defect and required correction. The fix must be separately tracked rather than left solely in rf2-a28eo's out-of-scope notes.

title: http: three transport seams — abort cancels the derived future not the exchange, completion callback unfenced above the reply tail, reply-tail fence dev-only (rf2-pk4i6 item 10)
description:
Shortlist item 10 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.9#2, rf2-pk4i6.9#3 and rf2-pk4i6.9#4). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size S.

## The three seams

**Seam 1 — a JVM abort cancels the derived future, not the exchange.** A superseded or aborted request keeps downloading: N connections per keystroke in a debounce search.

**Seam 2 — the completion callback is unfenced above the reply tail.** A throw above the fence hangs the request silently on the JVM, and on CLJS RE-SENDS a completed 2xx via `maybe-retry!`. The fail-loud `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing` from a marked `:decode` schema is one reachable case.

**Seam 3 — the reply-tail fence is dev-only.** A throwing `:after` or a bad reply target makes the reply vanish with nothing production-survivable, although `spec/014` §Failure mode says "observably".

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

- Hoist the `whenComplete` in `jvm-fetch` out of `(when (pos? timeout-ms) …)`, and cancel `future-resp` on `CancellationException` too (about three lines).
- Move `decode-schema-marks` to `normalise-args` so the marks check fails at dispatch time.
- Wrap the JVM `whenComplete` body and the CLJS `.then` handler so a non-transport throw routes to the same observable, non-retrying emit and still clears the registry.
- Route `emit-reply-tail-error!` through `:error-emit/emit-error-both` exactly as `emit-fx-error!` does, and drop its outer `debug-enabled?` gate.

Re-verified by the reviewer: NO. Their traces are line-cited and the abort-versus-exchange distinction is stated in the code's own timeout docstring (`transport_jvm.cljc:293-297`); the reviewer judged that nothing turned on a run.

## A PREMISE OF THIS ITEM IS ALREADY REFUTED — the mayor measured it at filing time

**The triage's last line reads "One file, one worker". That is FALSE.** Measured at `d1f5c0cd5d`, the four named symbols live in four different files, and a fifth is not in this artefact at all:

- `jvm-fetch` — `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` AND `transport_jvm.cljc`
- `decode-schema-marks` — `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc`
- `emit-reply-tail-error!` — `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc`
- `maybe-retry!` — `registry.cljc`, `transport.cljc` AND `transport_cljs.cljc`
- `normalise-args` — **TWO candidate homes in this artefact, `encoding.cljc` and `handlers.cljc`.** The triage does not say which it means. Determine which one the marks check belongs in and say so.
- `emit-fx-error!` — NOT under `implementation/http` at all. It is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` and `fx.cljc`. It is the PATTERN TO MIRROR and is **read-only** for this item.

So this is a multi-file change in one artefact. That does not make it large — the edits are still small — but a worker told "one file" will either doubt the brief or stop after the first file. **Take this as the standing warning that the rest of the triage's claims here are line-cited readings rather than measurements.**

## Pins

Three seams, three distinct failure modes, and each fails in a different register: seam 1 leaks connections, seam 2 hangs on one host and double-sends on the other, seam 3 loses the reply silently. A single test cannot cover them. The CLJS double-send is the one most likely to regress unnoticed, because it presents as success.

Assert a PRECONDITION inside each pin — that the abort actually reached the exchange, that the throw actually landed above the fence — so a pin reds when its own setup drifts rather than passing while exercising nothing.

## Surface and fences

Yours: `implementation/http/src/**`, `implementation/http/test/**`, and `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`.

Read-only: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc` — mirror `emit-fx-error!`'s routing, do not change it.

Not yours: `implementation/core/**` beyond that read, `implementation/epoch/**` and `spec/002` (item 7 is live there); `implementation/resources/**` and `spec/016` (item 11 is live there); `implementation/schemas/**` and `spec/010` (items 12 and 13 are live there). `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

## Worker verdict (PR #9897, branch worker/httpseams-1eng8)

TWO OF THE THREE SEAMS ARE REAL AND ARE FIXED. SEAM 1 DOES NOT EXIST.

### Seam 1 — REFUTED, and the change reverted

Measured on JDK 21.0.10 against the UNFIXED tree, a two-way control:

    WITHOUT cancel: [:wrote-all]
    WITH    cancel: [:write-failed]

Cancelling the derived stage `jvm-fetch` returns ALREADY tears the JDK
exchange down. No code of ours makes that happen, so the "N connections per
keystroke" symptom does not occur. The control's first arm is what makes the
second mean anything: it proves the harness can observe a surviving download.

THE DISTINCTION THE TRIAGE MISSED IS `cancel()` VERSUS
`completeExceptionally()`. A probe replicating `jvm-fetch`'s shape with no
`whenComplete` at all:

    orTimeout ONLY (no upstream cancel):   [:wrote-all]
    orTimeout + explicit upstream cancel:  [:write-failed]

So rf2-fzbj.11's EXISTING upstream cancel IS load-bearing — `orTimeout`
completes the stage exceptionally, which the JDK does not propagate — while a
lifecycle abort calls `cancel()`, which it does. The timeout docstring at
`transport_jvm.cljc` (the reviewer's anchor) is correct as written; extending
its reasoning to aborts is what does not follow, and neither the code nor the
docstring ever claimed it did. DO NOT REOPEN THIS AS A BUG.

The proposed change would have been WORSE THAN REDUNDANT. `jvm-fetch`'s stage
is a `jdk.internal.net.http.common.MinimalFuture`, and cancelling one stores a
`CompletionException` WRAPPING the `CancellationException` rather than the bare
exception a plain `CompletableFuture` stores — measured: cancel=true,
isCancelled=FALSE, isCompletedExceptionally=true, stored throwable
CompletionException caused by CancellationException. `whenComplete` receives
that stored throwable verbatim, so the `(instance? CancellationException t)`
predicate the triage proposed COULD NEVER FIRE. It would have shipped as dead
code that reads as live.

A characterisation pin is kept (`http_abort_cancels_exchange_test.clj`) with
BOTH arms of the control inside it, so the JDK behaviour the transport relies
on cannot silently change under a runtime upgrade.

### Seam 2 — REAL, fixed

`complete-fenced!` in `transport.cljc` now wraps the whole platform completion
callback on both hosts, performs the terminal teardown, and routes to the
non-retrying observable emit.

CLJS, measured against the unfixed tree, is WORSE than the bead describes:

    fetch-count            1 (fixed)  ->  5 (unfixed)
    throw reaches app as   -          ->  :kind :rf.http/transport
    reply delivered        none       ->  :status :error, :attempt 5

Under a max-attempts 5 policy the request went out FIVE times, every one
succeeding on the wire, and the app was then handed a FAILURE reply. So it is
not only "presents as success" — it is a false failure sitting on top of five
real sends.

JVM, same plant: the error never surfaces on either axis AND THE IN-FLIGHT
REGISTRY IS NEVER CLEARED — the request hangs in flight for ever.

It routes to the EXISTING `:rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed` rather than
minting a second category: from the app's point of view the situation is
identical, and `:reply-error-id` carries the caught throw's own id, which keeps
the two cases distinguishable.

### Seam 3 — REAL, fixed

`emit-reply-tail-error!` now fans out through both error substrates via the
`:error-emit/emit-error-both` late-bind hook, mirroring `fx/emit-fx-error!`.
The outer `debug-enabled?` gate is gone. PRODUCTION ERROR VOLUME ON THIS PATH
RISES FROM ZERO. The dev surface is unchanged (same category, same tags; the
gate now applies from inside `trace/emit-error!`).

No evidence the gate was deliberate: no comment, bead or test defends it, and
spec/014 already promised the opposite.

### `normalise-args` — the bead's "two candidate homes" is also wrong

`encoding.cljc` is NOT a candidate. It has no `normalise-args` definition —
only two prose mentions, one of which explicitly spells it
`handlers/normalise-args`. There is exactly ONE definition in the artefact,
`handlers.cljc:181` (and one unrelated one in `core/src/re_frame/events.cljc`).

The `:decode` marks check went into `normalise-args` itself, not beside
`managed-handler`'s other guards, because that fn OWNS `:decode` and runs on
the POST-`:before` args — `validate-retry!` and `validate-reply-target!` fire
before the chain, so a `:before` that SET `:decode` would be checked there
against a decode the transport never uses. Not split across both.

### TWO OUT-OF-SURFACE EDITS, FORCED BY A GATE

The brief's surface grant was incomplete for the seam-3 fix it asked for.
`error-catalogue-channel-conformance-test` (invariant 5, rf2-h4f0n) refuses any
category passed as a literal to `emit-error-both!` / `dispatch-on-error!` whose
Spec 009 Channel cell is not `always-on`, and it runs UNCONDITIONALLY in
`test.yml`'s `jvm-repo-source-walks` job. So seam 3 cannot land without, in the
SAME commit:

  1. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT-ZONE) — one table cell
     `diagnostic` -> `always-on`, the now-false "Dev-only" sentence replaced.
  2. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`
     — one keyword added to the `always-on-categories` literal, which the JVM
     companion pins == the parsed catalogue set.

The gate names both halves in its own failure message. Measured red before
(1 failure naming the category and its stale cell), 31 tests / 181 assertions /
0 failures after. Neither is deferrable to a follow-on. Flagged for the mayor
in the PR body; revert-and-resequence if either collides with a live worker.

title: method: the premise-check outcome set has no term for 'holds where measured, false where you are about to apply it'
description:
THE PREMISE-CHECK OUTCOME SET IS INCOMPLETE, and the gap was measured today at the cost of a merged documentation regression.

WHAT THE METHOD SAYS NOW. `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` carries the premise rule in two places, and both enumerate the SAME three outcomes:
  * :81-84, the mandatory block pasted VERBATIM into every editing brief -- "Check each at source before acting on it. A verified 'already fixed' or 'the premise does not hold' is a complete and good deliverable".
  * :284, the brief-inputs shape -- "each cited line holds, drifted to what, or does not hold".
So: HOLDS / DRIFTED / DOES NOT HOLD.

THE MISSING FOURTH OUTCOME: the premise HOLDS where it was measured, and the worker is about to apply it somewhere it does NOT hold. The rule as written is fully SATISFIED by verifying the claim is true at its cited anchor, and says nothing about the claim's DOMAIN.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE, 2026-09-16. rf2-17bbi's drift sweep (PR #9882, merge ae305b9e57) added a sentence saying a programmatic registration is "selectable only by the DEFAULT image unless the metadata stamps :ns". That sentence is TRUE -- for genuine source-store registrations, which is where it was checked. It was then applied to `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-app-schemas` and `reg-resource-scope`, where it is false: the first three are FRAME-OWNED and write to per-frame side-tables (registrar.cljc:24-43 says in terms that app-db schemas are "NOT a registrar kind" and that :flow is RESERVED with an intentionally empty registrar slot), and the fourth uses the registrar but its wrapper DISCARDS the caller's :ns (measured by the audit: descriptors-for returned a nil provenance key for a call passing :ns, against a registrar/register! control in the same process that returned the named key).

The worker did nothing wrong by the rule. It checked the premise at source and the premise held. The regression reached trunk and was caught only by the out-of-repo merged-PR audit, as rf2-1kqed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A CLAUSE RATHER THAN A NOTE. This is the method's CENTRAL worker-side guard -- the one block whose text is pasted into every editing brief -- and its incompleteness is now demonstrated rather than theorised. The failure is silent and it fails in the AUTHORITATIVE direction: an over-generalised correction is newer than what it replaces, so it reads as the more reliable text. And it is the same shape as the correction-overshoot gotcha loops.md Section 5 already names, one level up: there a fix overshoots into the inverse of the claim, here a true claim overshoots its domain.

THE REQUIRED CHANGE, and it is bounded deliberately.
  1. `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` :81-84 -- add ONE SENTENCE to the pasted premise block naming the fourth outcome: a premise can hold where it was measured and not where you are about to apply it, so check the claim's DOMAIN and not only its truth. **ONE sentence. This block is pasted verbatim into every editing brief, so every word costs on every future dispatch.**
  2. Same file :284 -- extend the three-way enumeration ("holds, drifted to what, or does not hold") to carry the same fourth outcome, in the same compressed register as the surrounding prose.
  3. Add the measured instance to whichever gotcha list in that file is the right home, in the file's existing style -- a short account with the counterexamples named, so the next reader gets the evidence and not only the rule.

DO NOT restructure the premise block, do not add a checklist, and do not touch loops.md -- the correction-overshoot gotcha there is right as written and this is its dispatch-side counterpart, not a replacement. The project stance binds here more than usual: this is a page people must read in full every time, so the repair is a sentence, not a section.

(Provenance: the Resources parity study in the mayor checkout's gitignored `ai/findings/Resources/fable/`, report §6 D3 and D3b; a worktree does not carry it, and nothing here depends on it.)

## 1. README: "not exercised here, shown there"

Conduit is client-only (`routing.cljs:20`), pages by offset rather than `:infinite`, declares no prefetch and no `:poll-interval-ms`, uses no `:patches` / `:removes`, and its standard build carries no trace stream and no Xray (`core.cljs:211`). Each is a real capability with its own example or tests. Add a short section to `README.md` that lists them and points at: `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/` (SSR), the `infinite_feed` example (infinite reads, prefetch on intent), `linearlite` (`:patches` / `:removes`), and the Xray Resources panel (`tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md`). Gate: `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (the README is beside source, so the docs slug gate does not cover it).

`index.html` has no Xray host, and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` `:examples/realworld-resources` declares `:target`, `:output-dir`, `:asset-path` and `:modules` only — no preloads — so the production build is the only build there is. Do not add infinite reads, SSR, prefetch or polling to Conduit as features: point at the capability examples instead.

title: HTTP RealWorld: keep late editor writes from erasing newer drafts
description:
Bind HTTP editor write continuations to the editing session that issued them. A late Delete success currently erases a newer draft and navigates away after the reader has already left the original editor.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This independently implementable HTTP editor part is split from confirmed finding 4 in rf2-fzbj.21. Sibling Resources editor/detail continuations have separate issues under rf2-gwye. Review/issue creation is authorized; implementation is held.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:304-340,430-480; routing.cljs editor routes and :can-leave guard. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: open a clean existing article in the editor, click Delete and hold its response. Navigate to New Article, type a new draft, then release the old delete success. The old editor was clean, so leaving it does not require discarding changes. :editor/reset initializes the new slice/machine but does not retire the old HTTP write callback.

Expected: the server deletion may complete, while the new draft and the user's current route remain intact. Actual: :editor/delete-success unconditionally replaces the whole editor slice with a blank one and navigates home. Because the draft is cleared before navigation, the leave guard cannot preserve it. The save-success callback similarly installs its returned article and redirects without checking originating page ownership. Failure callbacks can write the departed operation's error into the newer editor.

Suggested repair: capture the originating committed route/nav-token (or equally small explicit editor-session identity) in every save/delete success/failure target and gate page-local editor writes and navigation against it. The existing routing current map exposes :nav-token, so no generic lifecycle system is needed. A cached slug alone cannot distinguish a replaced create draft or a later session editing the same article. Preserve same-page save/delete behavior, and ensure refusal of a stale completion leaves the new editor controls usable.

Acceptance: held production HTTP Delete from a clean edit page -> New Article -> type new draft -> release old success must preserve the draft and route. Also cover leaving a pending save/delete for a profile, late failure into a newer editor, and valid current-owner save/delete success/error. Verify the editor does not remain busy after the relevant session resets. Keep tests in the existing framework-owned realworld_cljs_test.cljs harness, not examples/.

Validation performed: source-probe.clj evaluates the actual editor-slice/draft helpers and :editor/delete-success/:editor/submit-success handlers at current source. probe-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0, correct SOURCE_ROOT banner. Given an unrelated profile route and a newer draft titled New unsaved draft, Delete returns a blank title and home navigation; Save returns the old article title and article navigation. Current reset, route guard and request targets were independently inspected to establish the reachable new-draft sequence. This is a source-handler witness; no browser, full routing/transport execution or CLJS compile is claimed.

Deduplication/references: rf2-fzbj.21 previously aggregated this defect. Closed rf2-amhpk explicitly excludes :editor/delete-success and fixes only HTTP article-detail navigation with article-route-for-slug?; its latest notes/history and close reason were read, and that repair stays intact. Closed rf2-84iek's correlated comments also demonstrate why owner refusal must not strand controls. Existing editor GET seeding/correlation fixes concern reads, not these write callbacks. No dedicated open owner of the HTTP editor write defect was found.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-gwye.37): fixed — HTTP editor save/delete settles are gated on the issuing nav-token, and a new editing session resets the machine so nothing is stranded busy.

Remediated in PR #9758 (branch worker/realworld-a), which fixes all four confirmed findings of rf2-fzbj.21 together. Every finding was re-verified at tip before the fix; all four still held.

What landed, per finding:

1. rf2-gwye.33 (HTTP optimistic comment) — realworld_http/schema.cljs gains DurableComment: the wire ws/Comment with :id widened to [:or :int [:re #"^temp-"]], derived from ws/Comment rather than restated. [:comments :data] registers that instead of the wire shape. ws/Comment, ws/CommentResponse and ws/CommentsResponse are untouched and still reject a string id.

2. rf2-gwye.34 (HTTP home feed) — realworld_http/http.cljs gains current-nav-token / same-navigation?. :articles/load and :feed/load capture the committed route's :nav-token and carry it on both reply targets; :articles/loaded, :articles/load-failed, :feed/loaded and :feed/load-failed refuse a reply whose navigation the reader has left. Supersession could not cover this: the two families carry different :request-ids and settle one machine whose :empty/:some/:error states take no :fetch-succeeded.

3. rf2-gwye.35 (Resources feed invalidation) — :realworld/follow and :realworld/unfollow now invalidate {:from-db :realworld/session} #{[:feed]} beside the viewer's [:profile username], via a shared follow-invalidates helper. Re-verified against PR #9746 (rf2-fzbj.7) first: that change touched only the infinite-feed accumulated-pages tag path, and the RealWorld feed is a scalar resource, so the premise stood unchanged.

4a. rf2-gwye.37 (HTTP editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete carry the issuing nav-token; :editor/submit-success, :editor/submit-error, :editor/delete-success and :editor/delete-error are each gated on it. :editor/load-article now dispatches the machine [:reset] before [:use-edit], so a refused settle cannot leave the next editing session at :submitting with its inputs locked (that strand is reachable only once the settles are gated, and is pinned by a test).

4b. rf2-gwye.39 (Resources editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete use :reply-to [:editor/replied nav-token]; :editor/replied refuses a departed reply whole: no slice write, no navigation, and no instance clear. Clearing nothing is what scopes cleanup to the completed operation — the next editor entry clears the shared :editor/save instance anyway, and the runtime already suppresses a late result for a cleared instance.

4c. rf2-gwye.42 (Resources detail delete) — :ui/delete-article carries its slug on :reply-to [:ui/article-deleted slug]; the continuation clears its own instance on :ok and navigates home only while the committed route is :realworld.article/show for that slug, mirroring the HTTP twin's article-route-for-slug?.

Two existing rows changed as a consequence. The Resources test delete-article-continuation-navigates-home issued its delete from /register and asserted a navigate home — that is exactly the departed-page case rf2-gwye.42 says must be refused, so it now issues the delete from the article page. Two HTTP rows that dispatch [:articles/loaded ...] directly now pass the nav-token explicitly (nil on a frame that never navigated).

- npm run test:cljs: captured exit 0, 12026 tests / 59924 assertions, 0 failures (CI job "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)", key cljs).
- node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs: captured exit 0, all 58 swept builds compiled with zero warnings, examples/realworld and examples/realworld-resources among them (CI job cljs-examples-compile).
- RED-then-green control: with the eight example sources checked out at the merge base and the test tree left as committed, the focused run of both RealWorld namespaces gave captured exit 1 with 39 failures across the same 63 tests / 907 assertions as the green run, covering every finding; green after restore, and the restore verified by content hash against each committed blob id.
No markdown or spec page was touched, so the doc-link gates are not nominated for this change.

Skipped suggestions, each with its reason:
- rf2-gwye.34 suggested a shared request identity or cancellation may supplement ownership: NOT built. The nav-token gate alone closes the defect, and queued replies still need the gate regardless, so a cancellation scheme would add machinery this example exists to stay clear of.
- rf2-gwye.39 asked that cleanup be scoped so a stale callback cannot clear a newer :editor/save incarnation: met by refusing the reply whole rather than by introducing an incarnation id.
- rf2-gwye.33's alternative repair (generate an integer temporary id) was not taken: the durable/wire split keeps the recordable temp-id coeffect and its temp- prefix, which the app documents as a replay-safe join key.
No framework change was needed: rf2-gwye.35 and rf2-gwye.39 cite files under implementation/resources/src, but both defects were in the examples' own descriptors and continuations, and those library files are untouched.

title: routing: normalize raw navigation URLs before matching
description:
Normalize accepted raw navigation references with the existing request-url->app-url helper before matching and carry that one effective URL through guards, pending state and history. The browser currently reaches a different route from the one programmatic navigation commits.

Ownership and remediation boundary
- Surface impl_routing; source owner implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc, using url.cljc. Tests belong under implementation/routing/test/re_frame/.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; source rechecked at 9238907fec4e0cc708bc518aa7fa83db6c0182e7, with no owned-path differences from baseline.
- This independently actionable P2 splits Finding 1 from rf2-fzbj.12. Its existing hold remains: [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. Review and issue creation do not authorize remediation. Prior statuses, notes and decisions are unchanged.

Source and concrete trigger
- navigate.cljc:251-264 classifies external raw URLs, but :305-315 passes the accepted original string straight to url-resolution. :442-449 chooses the unmatched original string or generated route URL; :530-532 pushes/replaces it.
- url.cljc:490-506 already implements request-url->app-url using the browser URL parser; decisions.cljc:425-434 uses it for the link door.
- Register (reg/reg-route :probe/item {} "/items/:id"). At document https://app.example/start, dispatch [:rf.route/navigate {:url "https://app.example/items/ok"}]. external-url? accepts the same-origin URL; raw matching misses /items/:id, so the slice becomes :rf.route/not-found while the address bar becomes /items/ok.
- Rooted counterexample: [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/x/../items/ok"}] commits :rf.route/not-found with {:url "/x/../items/ok"}; the browser normalizes that pushed reference to /items/ok. Plain /items/ok correctly commits :probe/item with {:id "ok"}.

Expected / actual / impact
Every accepted reference should resolve to the location the browser reaches, so guards, committed route, generated history entry and reload agree. Currently same-origin absolute redirect/deep-link targets and rooted dot segments can commit not-found at a valid route URL. Refresh or a different navigation door then selects a different route for the same displayed location.

Suggested repair
After external-URL refusal, apply the existing request-url->app-url once before url-resolution. Thread the effective URL through unmatched-url, requested-url, fallback :params :url, guard/pending target and history effects, retaining original input only for required provenance. Preserve the existing JVM/no-window conservative behavior and the ratified schema-failure asymmetry; no new parser or strategy is needed.

Acceptance
- Browser/CLJS regressions cover same-origin absolute, same-origin protocol-relative, rooted dot-segment and ordinary rooted inputs, asserting the same route/params and effective history destination.
- Cover accepted query-only and fragment-only browser references against the current document.
- Guards and a blocked continuation see the normalized target; an unmatched normalized URL is consistent in fallback params and history.
- Existing off-origin, malformed/non-string refusal and no-window tests remain valid.

Validation and limits
- Executed current-source JVM navigate-handler for rooted dot-segment and ordinary controls. A process-local seam witness modeled only the proven same-origin browser branch with external-url? redefined false and request-url->app-url returning /items/ok while counting calls: committed not-found and zero normalization calls. This is not compiled CLJS/browser execution.
- Native Node URL independently confirmed the same-origin absolute, protocol-relative, dot-segment and rooted references all reach pathname /items/ok.
- Ignored evidence: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_routing/probe-impl_routing-1.clj/.log/.exit and probe-impl_routing-2.cjs/.log/.exit; each exited 0 because the defect assertions/controls succeeded, not because a repair exists. JVM SOURCE banners resolve the actual routing source root.
- No browser integration, full suite, build or source edit. Existing reply-envelope suite separately passed 9 tests/60 assertions.

Deduplication / known references
Read current rf2-fzbj.12 and its newest three history snapshots; no dedicated open issue was found by current tracker searches for routing/normalization. The aggregate contains two findings and cannot serve as this finding's dedicated issue. rf2-j3tud / rf2-k2d2t are separate completed component-codec repairs; rf2-kuky.36 / .38 describe the retained link/consolidated URL-change contract, not this normalization omission.
notes:

1. Raw navigate URL normalisation (rf2-fzbj.12 finding 1 = rf2-gwye.26). `navigate.cljc` now runs `rf.routing.url/request-url->app-url` once, after the external-URL refusal. It is the same helper the link door uses. The resulting effective URL feeds `url-resolution`, `unmatched-url`, the not-found fallback params, and `requested-url`, which the guards, pending state and history all read. The route plan's `:source` keeps the caller's original string as provenance. On the JVM, or with no window, the helper is identity, so the fail-closed no-window policy is unchanged. 2. Splat trailing-slash data (rf2-fzbj.12 finding 2 = rf2-gwye.28). `url-encode-splat` now splits only the body before any terminal run of `/`, and encodes that run whole: `a/` emits `a%2F`, `/` emits `%2F`. It covers the values a/, a//, / and //, with controls a/b and a//b. It also covers the URL rows /f/a%2F, /f/%2F and /f/a%2F%2F through re-emission and a second match, plus a raw trailing-slash control.

3. Base root followed by ? or # (rf2-gwye.29). `strip-base-path` now accepts `?` and `#` as post-base boundaries, alongside end-of-string and `/`. So /app?tab=all strips to /?tab=all and /app#section to /#section. Sibling rejection and the blank-base no-op are unchanged. The fix is in the one shared ingress rule, so the initial sync and the listener both get it. Regression tests: `routing_url_strategy_test.clj`, `with-base-path-strips-mount-root-before-query-and-fragment` (pure strip rows plus the wrapped decode), and `routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs`, `history-base-mount-root-before-query-or-fragment-cljs-rf2-gwye-29` (initial sync at /app?tab=all, decode of each form, and the real popstate listener).

Spec 012 gained two sentences: the URL-string escape hatch resolves to the browser's location before matching, and a terminal splat slash emits as %2F.

Not built, per the stance. Each finding got its fix and a regression test, nothing more.

title: resources: inherit active owners into every new read work record
description:
Initialize every new read work record with the resource entry's complete active-owner set. This prevents releasing one view from aborting work still needed by another view.

F1 — P2: new read attempts forget existing entry owners and abort a still-shared request

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:708-720 creates a new ensure/refetch work record with only payload :owner; events.cljc:990-1000 does the same for load-more (owner normalized to nil at :900); events.cljc:1159-1169 does it for refetch-page. src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:247-260 turns that single owner into :owners, or an empty set. src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:952-973 preserves the entry's existing :active-owners on entry-start-load. The cancellation decision at events.cljc:1881-1894 removes the released owner from the new record and aborts if that record is owner-free, without observing the surviving entry owners. Focus/reconnect revalidation intentionally dispatches ownerless refetches at events.cljc:1364-1369.

Trigger/reproducer, using ordinary supported commands:
1. Register a scalar resource and ensure the same key under owner A, then ensure it under owner B before settlement. The initial work row correctly holds #{A B} by dedupe.
2. Refetch that key with a :cause and no new :owner (manual refresh, focus, poll and invalidation all use this idiom). The entry still holds #{A B}, but the new work row has :owners #{}.
3. Release A before the new reply arrives. The entry still has B, yet the handler marks the new row :abort-requested and emits :rf.http/managed-abort for that request.
The same sequence after loading page 0 and issuing ownerless load-more reproduces it for an infinite feed. A refetch with :owner A also loses pre-existing B and is aborted when A releases.

Expected: existing live owners continue to need the shared key's current request. Releasing one owner cannot cancel work while another holds the entry. This is Spec 016's no-abort-shared-work rule, distinct from its intentional ownerless load-more rule at spec/016-Resources.md:1536: load-more must not MINT an owner, but the existing owners still keep the feed alive.
Actual measured: initial owners and work owners were both #{[:app :a] [:app :b]}; the initial-load release control emitted []; refetch owners remained both but work owners became #{}; releasing A left #{[:app :b]} and produced :abort-requested plus [:rf.http/managed-abort [:rf.req :review/frame [:rf.work/resource [:rf.scope/global :review/item {}] 3]]]. The infinite load-more witness produced the same abort with B still present.
Impact: route/machine/app owner release can cancel another view's live refresh or load-more. This can leave stale data or drop an expected page until another cause starts a request; it also makes the ledger's ownership evidence misleading.

Repair: when issuing a new resource attempt, initialize the work record's ownership from the resulting entry's full :active-owners, including any newly attached payload owner. Apply the same rule to ensure/refetch, load-more and refetch-page, preserving the ownerless command contract and cause attribution. Keep release's no-remaining-owner decision coherent with that set. Avoid a special-case rule for focus or load-more.

title: [implementation/core] Release the exact reaction acquired by subscribe-once
description:
Repair `subscribe-once` by releasing the exact reaction it acquired through the existing `unsubscribe-if-reaction` helper. Its current address-only release can decrement and dispose a replacement reaction held by another consumer. This is an internal ownership correction; no new public API or caller ceremony is needed.

Surface: implementation/core (impl_core). P2 correctness defect.
Reviewed baseline and HEAD: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261.
SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
Source ownership: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1919-1928, especially `(unsubscribe target query-v)` at 1927. Existing identity-aware facade: subs.cljc:2512-2555; atomic identity check: subs/cache.cljc:283-301.

Trigger and observed behavior
1. Thread T1 calls `subscribe-once` and obtains reaction A, then begins dereferencing A.
2. During that dereference, T2 calls the supported `clear-sub-cache!` and a separate consumer subscribes the same query, acquiring successor B with reference count 1.
3. T1 returns from A's computation and unsubscribes by (frame, query) address. That address now resolves to B, so the release consumes B's owner's reference and disposes B.

Expected: T1 returns its value; B remains cached, reference count 1, with no disposal callback. A's acquisition ended at eviction, so its subsequent release should be a no-op.
Actual, reproduced on current source in both JVM configurations: `{:held-disposed 1, :held-cached false, :ref-count nil}`. A control with no eviction yields `{:held-disposed 0, :held-cached true, :ref-count 1}`; releasing that independent holder then disposes exactly once.

Impact: a one-shot read in JVM SSR/headless tooling can retire another live consumer's acquisition during a supported cache invalidation. Subsequent cache lookups/releases see a missing or rebuilt identity. The probe measures cache ownership and callback execution; it does not claim browser rendering consequences were executed.

Contract: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1196-1205 explicitly says one-shot reads retain no reference, concurrent reactive subscribers keep their slot alive, and the operation works on JVM. subs.cljc:1948-1953 promises that the one-shot decrement only disposes when it owned the final reference.

Standalone reproducer (Clojure, run in a fresh process with the core source classpath)
```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.subs :as subs]
         '[re-frame.subs.cache :as cache] '[re-frame.frame :as frame]
         '[re-frame.interop :as interop]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(rf/init! plain/adapter)
(let [id :review-once/frame q [:review-once/value]
      entered (promise) resume (promise) disposed (atom 0)]
  (rf/reg-sub (first q) {} (fn [_ _] (deliver entered true) @resume :value))
  (rf/make-frame {:id id})
  (let [job (future (subs/subscribe-once q {:frame id}))]
    (try
      (assert (= true (deref entered 5000 :timeout)))
      (cache/clear-sub-cache! id)
      (let [held (subs/subscribe q {:frame id})]
        (interop/add-on-dispose! held #(swap! disposed inc))
        (deliver resume true)
        (assert (= :value (deref job 5000 :timeout)))
        (let [entry (get @(-> (frame/frame id) :sub-cache) q)]
          (prn {:held-disposed @disposed
                :held-cached (identical? held (:reaction entry))
                :ref-count (:ref-count entry)})))
      (finally (deliver resume true) (future-cancel job)))))
(shutdown-agents)
(System/exit 0)
```
The promise in a constant-valued body fixes a normal JVM preemption window; it does not redefine subscription acquisition, eviction, or release. A body value is returned normally before the incorrect release is observed.

Repair and acceptance
- In `subscribe-once-in-frame`, pair the acquisition with `(unsubscribe-if-reaction target query-v reaction)` using the concrete acquired object. Preserve the current arities, returned value, missing-frame recovery, and synchronous final-reference disposal.
- Add a deterministic JVM regression matching the interleaving above. Assert successor identity, reference count 1, and zero disposal callbacks after the one-shot returns.
- Include the no-eviction shared-owner control and ordinary final-owner one-shot disposal. Run the semantic regression under both development and the real load-time `-Dre-frame.debug=false` posture.
- Keep this change independent of the separate non-atomic batch cache-clear finding; either fix can land first. The clear call in this witness has finished before B is acquired.

Validation performed and limits
Fresh process-local runs of ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_core/ownership-probe-impl_core-1.clj used the already-cached implementation/core classpath, with explicit absolute script path and printed source root. Development and real production runs both exited 0 and reproduced the incorrect disposal plus the expected control. These exits certify completion of the reproducer, not a passing product suite. Evidence: ownership-dev-impl_core-1.log/.exit and ownership-prod-impl_core-1.log/.exit in that same ignored slice directory. All futures were released/cancelled and both JVMs exited. No source edits, dependency installs, shared builds, gates, or browser execution. Owned paths are unchanged from the baseline.

Dedupe and history

Current tracker searches for subscription, cache, subscribe-once, clear-sub-cache and one-shot, plus available export body/notes/close-reason inspection, found no dedicated open owner for this defect. rf2-fzbj.5 newest-first history was read. description:
Repair the three SSR request-flow defects below: wait for the plain SSR article fetch before freezing state, pass the request frame ID to the resource preload poll, and destroy the streaming request frame on outer render failures. Keep the existing examples and APIs; no new example framework, broad test sweep, or per-example test files are warranted. The static browser launch path is distinct from the JVM request handlers, and the asynchronous finding is specifically about the latter.

Verdict: remediation remains; keep this task OPEN. Confirmed actionable findings: 3 x P2. No new confirmed defect in the machine, routing, infinite-feed, ordinary-resource, or Linearlite flows inspected.

SOURCE AND OWNERSHIP

- Source revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Reviewed source remained identical at tracker-checkpoint HEAD e88f4e80fb0788325d59e6f5b7cdb39f748a4380; git diff baseline..HEAD -- examples/capabilities was empty.

F1 — P2: Plain SSR freezes and destroys its frame before an asynchronous article request settles
Owned source: examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:137-157 (server-init and managed request), 276-293 (make-frame followed immediately by final-db read), 331-355 (payload/response), 360-361 (destroy); README.md:61-86 and core.cljc:256-274 describe the intended settled server flow.

This is not a complaint about adding asynchronous behavior to a synchronous fixture. The checked-in server-init returns a real :rf.http/managed GET /api/articles, and handle-request installs no canned override. The README limits the canned override to the JVM smoke. The source's stated sequence is that the article fetch resolves, app-db settles, then rendering begins. make-frame drains synchronous event work; the actual JVM managed transport uses HttpClient/sendAsync (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:287). Returning from make-frame is not completion of that request.

Trigger/reproducer: initialize rf.ssr/adapter, require the unchanged ssr.core, then call handle-request through its supported rf/with-fx-overrides seam. First use the shipped canned-success effect synchronously; repeat with exactly the same article value and :after-ms 200. The synchronous control emits the article; the delayed case returns HTTP 200 with No articles. and a payload lacking that article in 7.77 ms, and the frame is already gone. Waiting past the delay cannot repair the returned body or destroyed frame.

A second probe retains the ACTUAL managed HTTP implementation. Its thin override only prefixes /api/articles with the ephemeral loopback origin, as required because JVM transport has no document base, then delegates to the real registered :rf.http/managed handler. A synthetic loopback server acknowledges receiving the request and withholds its response. Observed while the response is still withheld: server-received-request=true, status=200, has-article=false, empty-message=true, frames-left=nil. The probe then releases the reply and closes its server/executor. Thus the issue also occurs over the shipped asynchronous transport, independently of canned timer behavior.

Expected: snapshot/render/payload construction follows success or a deliberate terminal failure/timeout policy for the page load. Actual: it runs while the request is still pending, reports an empty successful page, and tears down the only frame able to receive the result. Impact: copying the demonstrated JVM handler for real asynchronous fetching produces empty SSR and hydration state; the static baked index masks this because its article state is already present.

Repair recommendation: give the page load an explicit completion outcome and wait for that outcome, with a bounded failure/timeout path, before reading final-db and rendering. A request failure needs a terminal outcome too; do not replace the bug with an unbounded wait for non-nil articles. Reuse the existing application/event and host facilities and keep teardown around the full request lifecycle. If this handler is instead intentionally reduced to a synchronous-only illustration, make its transport explicitly synchronous and narrow every real-server/drain claim; the current combination is misleading. Document the required host-side absolute URL adaptation when describing live JVM HTTP.

Acceptance:
- Drive the actual handle-request against a parked successful reply; verify it does not return a completed response before the reply is released, then includes the article in both HTML and parsed payload.
- Include a real async or delayed managed reply; a synchronous canned-only control is insufficient.
- Drive failure and deadline paths; they terminate deliberately, leave no live request frame, and do not silently present an unresolved load as a completed empty result.
- Existing baked browser hydration and synchronous smoke behavior remain valid. Put any regression in the framework test tree, not examples/.

F2 — P2: Resources SSR's preload poll always burns the five-second deadline because it looks up a frame value as an ID
Owned source: examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:298-323 (deadline and poll), 354-370 (f is the value returned by make-frame and is passed as :frame f). The exact repair site is line 370.

Current contract/execution: public rf/make-frame returns a frame VALUE (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:929 onward). resource-state forwards its :frame directly to the ID-keyed internal frame readers (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:144-184); frame/frame resolves a keyword ID through the registry (implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1381-1398). In this shipped call, f therefore resolves to no entry even while fid identifies a loaded resource. The poll sees nil until its deadline, not the actual resource status.

Trigger/reproducer: initialize the SSR adapter, require unchanged resources-ssr.core, install a synchronous successful article override, and call handle-request. Instrument the public read in a process-local wrapper that reads the supplied target and the same target normalized to its ID, returning the supplied-target result unchanged. Actual output: 5092.32 ms, 823 polls; first AND last poll have keyword-target?=false, by-value-status=nil, by-id-status=:loaded. The response eventually contains the article, so a content-only assertion passes despite the broken blocking condition. A control changes only the target used by that read to its ID: 12.60 ms and one poll, same loaded article. An earlier uninstrumented 100 ms delayed-success run took 5120.29 ms and likewise eventually rendered the article.

Expected: the preload poll returns when this resource is :loaded or :error, and waits toward the deadline only while it is unsettled. Actual: all ordinary successful calls wait the entire five-second budget, including an already synchronously loaded resource. Impact: a deterministic five-second latency penalty and an ineffective readiness check in the worked server resource recipe.

Repair recommendation: pass the already-bound fid to await-resource-loaded! at line 370. Keep the public introspection read and existing bounded poll; no new API or polling machinery is needed. If the resource-state API is later extended to accept frame values, this example should still have a meaningful terminal-state witness rather than a content-only test that tolerates the deadline.

Acceptance:
- A synchronously loaded resource exits the real example's poll immediately, without exhausting preload-deadline-ms.
- A parked async request keeps the handler waiting; releasing its successful or failed reply exits on the terminal resource state rather than the deadline.
- Validate target identity: the poll reads the request's actual entry, not nil under an unrecognized key.
- Preserve payload projection, client page-opened acquisition, fresh-skip hydration, and request teardown. Add coverage in implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj or an equivalent existing framework suite.

F3 — P2: Streaming SSR destroys its per-request frame only on the successful return path
Owned source: examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:182-273, especially make-frame at 203-205, shell rendering at 206-208, final payload at 248-267, and the lone destroy at 268.

Trigger/reproducer: initialize the SSR adapter, require unchanged ssr-streaming.core, and invoke handle-request normally. It returns four chunks, failed-boundaries #{:card.flaky}, and no residual frame: the intentional boundary failure is handled correctly. Then use a process-local with-redefs to make rf.ssr/streaming-render-shell throw ExceptionInfo "probe shell render failure" after make-frame has completed, and call the same handler. The exception propagates and one fresh :rf.frame/<gensym> remains registered. The probe explicitly destroys that leaked frame afterward, proving both acquisition and missing cleanup without leaving process state behind.

Expected: the request owns its frame until completion, and releases it on an outer render/payload exception as well as success. Actual: any exception before the final let binding skips destroy-frame!. Impact: a shell-render or final-payload failure in a long-lived host using this demonstrated request handler leaks the request's frame and associated runtime state. This finding concerns failures OUTSIDE the deferred card recovery boundary; it does not claim the deliberate throwing-card crashes the page. The non-streaming sibling already demonstrates and tests the required finally shape, including controlled render exceptions.

Repair recommendation: put the whole post-allocation streaming pipeline, including shell walk, continuation collection and final payload construction, inside try/finally with destroy-frame! in finally. Preserve the original exception and the existing per-card fallback policy. Do not add a reaper, alternate teardown API, or swallow rendering failures.

Acceptance:
- The real handler's happy path and deliberate :card.flaky fallback leave the registry at its captured baseline.
- Inject an outer shell failure and a final-payload failure after allocation; both propagate while leaving no new live request frame.
- Removing the finally must make the cleanup regression fail; place the regression in the framework test tree.

COVERAGE AND VALIDATION LIMITS
Inspected the executable event/state/effect and view/mount flow of all eight capability examples, all README narratives and launch commands, and all host HTML pages. Followed current core frame/value readers and construction, resource introspection/subscription and owner concepts, managed HTTP canned and JVM asynchronous transport, SSR hashing/streaming/projection/hydration entry points, and existing framework example regressions where relevant.

Specific non-findings: machine error cleanup is now on :error-shown :exit and the third failure records attempts=3; routing declares its required artefact and both two-segment routed examples have base href=/; ordinary resource preview replacement releases the prior app owner and reader teardown uses the runtime actor owner; infinite feed identity/cursor, route ownership, merged items, load-more event and first-load/page-error separation align with the runtime; Linearlite now commits disjoint fields/created rows and withholds writes against temporary create IDs. Frame-root/client-root usage and after-load rendering were inspected, not browser-executed. Lack of tests inside examples is deliberate and is not a finding.

F1 — P2: valid image-local handlers fail Pair's global-store pre-validation
Owned source: skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:638-679 (especially :652), :1116-1124 (read-sub!), :1927-1933 (dispatch-consequence!).

Trigger: an operating/explicit frame has an inline :reg-sub or :reg-event in its selected image and that id has no process-store registration. This is an ordinary supported image definition, not malformed data. For example, after (rf/init! plain/adapter):

(rf/make-frame
  {:id :review/frame
   :images [(rf/image
              {:id :review/image
               :registrations
               {:reg-sub [[:review/inline-sub (fn [db _] (:n db))]]
                :reg-event [[:review/inline-event
                             (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
                               {:db (update db :n (fnil inc 0))})]]}})]})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/inline-event] {:frame :review/frame})
@(rf/subscribe [:review/inline-sub] {:frame :review/frame})
;; direct framework results: app-db {:n 1}, sub value 1

Now invoke read-sub {sub: "[:review/inline-sub]", frame: ":review/frame"}, or ordinary dispatch {event: "[:review/inline-event]", frame: ":review/frame"}. Both reach the owned functions above.

Expected: typed reads and dispatches accept the same selected ids that the frame actually executes; the read returns 1 and the second event increments n to 2. Unknown-id suggestions should come from that frame's resolved handler set.
Actual: validate-registered asks (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind kind}) and never receives frame-id. Probe 1 proves FRAME-SUB-REGISTERED true, STORE-SUB-REGISTERED false, DIRECT-EVENT-DB {:n 1}, DIRECT-SUB 1. The shipped read-sub! returns :ok? false :reason :unknown-id :subscribed? false :known-count 0, and dispatch-consequence! returns :unknown-id :dispatched? false (its only known event is :rf/set-db). App-db stays {:n 1}. The frame-aware source was available and working; Pair rejects before it can use it.

Impact: primary typed inspection and default dispatch fail against valid inline-image applications, despite the skill explicitly teaching per-frame image operation. Operators receive false 'nothing is registered' guidance and must resort to broader raw eval for otherwise supported gestures. The opposite mismatch (a store id excluded from the chosen frame) should also be covered in repair tests; it was inspected as a consequence of the same lookup but was not separately executed here.

Repair: resolve the operating frame before validation; thread the frame through validate-event-id/validate-sub-id/validate-registered and read (rf/registrations {:frame frame-id :kind kind}). Keep intentional process-wide discovery methods as store reads. Preserve structured ambiguous/missing-frame and unknown-id behavior, using the frame's candidate set. Audit the callers of these validation helpers so the frame chosen for validation is the one passed to dispatch/subscribe.
Acceptance: image-only event and sub ids succeed through the typed tools with an explicit frame and session pin; a frame-selected id succeeds even when no store id exists; an excluded/global-only id is rejected against the chosen frame with frame-local suggestions; two frames with different selected sets do not bleed. Add real frame-image CLJS coverage through read-sub/default dispatch, not only a pure known-id set test or a structural assertion that a validator is called.

F2 — P2: the post-mortem recipe attributes the bad state to a later unrelated event
Owned source: skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md:113-120, especially predicate :117 and instruction :120. The same misleading 'flipped' example is in preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1381-1385. find-where itself, :1394-1398, correctly implements newest matching record and need not change its general contract.

Trigger/reproducer: seed {:auth-state :active}, dispatch [:review/expire] that sets :auth-state to :expired, then dispatch [:review/unrelated] that only adds :tick 1. Query the exact published predicate:

(find-where (fn [e] (= :expired (get-in (:db-after e) [:auth-state]))))

Expected: the recipe's promised 'epoch where the governing key last changed to its current (bad) value' is [:review/expire].
Actual: it returns [:review/unrelated], whose :db-before and :db-after BOTH contain :auth-state :expired. Step 4 explicitly tells the agent to report that record as the culprit. Probe 2 captured all three real core/epoch records, printed RECIPE-CULPRIT [:review/unrelated], and printed TRANSITION-CULPRIT [:review/expire] when the predicate additionally checked that :db-before was not :expired.

Impact: an apparently evidence-based forensic explanation blames the wrong handler whenever any later event preserves the bad value. This is the common case in an active UI, not a retention edge case; it can send debugging and suggested edits into unrelated source.

Repair: keep find-where as a general latest-match helper, but use a transition predicate for causal recipes: target value in :db-after AND different from that target in :db-before (or compare before/after path values for a general change). Correct the runtime docstring's 'flipped' example too. If the retained ring contains the state but no transition into it, report that the origin is not retained instead of treating the latest matching state as a cause.
Acceptance: with seed -> fault -> unrelated -> unrelated, the recipe selects the fault epoch; a second genuine transition into the bad value selects the latest such transition; retained records that all start bad yield no claimed origin. Cover the executable predicate over a small contrasting epoch sequence and ensure the prose requires before/after evidence before attribution.

F3 — P3: the skill still advertises flow/frame as accepted list-handlers kinds
Owned source: skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:37 (registrar/list row; supported-kinds enumeration).
