title: [surface-review] Story: execute and render resolved scenarios; retain run-owned loader cleanup
description:
Recommendation: make the compiled plan the source for registered-run loader lifecycle and effective args, and retain the loader teardown belonging to the run that actually opened resources. Three confirmed P2 correctness defects remain. Keep this bead OPEN for remediation; no production change is part of this review.

Owned slice and revision
- Owned: tools/story/**.
- Baseline and reviewed HEAD: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- This is the single tools/story deliverable under rf2-fzbj, per the independent surface-review contract of 2026-09-12.

Coverage and limits
Focused source-path review of src/re_frame/story.cljc and story/{registrar,schemas,plan,runtime,frames,loaders,lifecycle,args,render,save_variant}.cljc; adjacent play/runner_events.cljc cancellation/teardown code and ui/{canvas,share}.cljs callers. Read README.md, deps.edn, and the applicable authoring/runtime/strict-composition clauses of spec/{001-Authoring,002-Runtime,017-Testing-Story}.md. Sampled runtime, lifecycle, teardown, save-variant, and render-shell tests to compare direct cases with inherited/composed paths. This covered registration-to-plan-to-run, allocation/reset/destruction, render preparation, effective args, Save Current/snippet paste, and relevant packaging declarations. The entire directory was inventoried, but this is a focused substantive review, not a claim that every test, UI control, recorder gesture, artifact export, or static-build path was exhaustively inspected.

Validation: three lightweight JVM processes evaluated actual current CLJC source with the plain-atom adapter, existing cached dependency jars, and the absolute tools/story/src path. No dependency resolution/install, compilation output, server, browser, network request, external resource, source edit, or broad gate was involved. Each process exited 0 after printing the witnesses described below; the third also asserted the save/plan mismatch and explicit-cell control. Resource ownership was represented by an in-process calls atom. The CLJS UI consequences below are source-traced, not browser-tested. No full JVM/CLJS/build/packaging suite was run. No green-suite claim is made. Shared source git status remained clean before bead creation.

Finding 1 — P2: registered variants silently skip inherited and composed loaders

Locations:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:309-316 and 967-979: registered phase 1 uses the raw variant body; only inline runs supply a normalized :loader-body.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:769 and 803: allocate! reads raw v-body and gives it to events-only-variant?; 842-843 chooses mount-ready! from that classification.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/loaders.cljc:331-358: an empty raw :loaders / absent :loaders-complete-when qualifies for the fast path.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:1044-1048: registered teardown also reads the raw :loaders-teardown.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:1501-1513 and 1712-1719 correctly retain resolved loader slots, so compilation/explain and execution disagree.

Trigger/reproducer, after requiring re-frame.core as rf, re-frame.story as story, re-frame.story.plan as plan, and re-frame.substrate.plain-atom as plain:

    (rf/init! plain/adapter)
    (story/install-canonical-vocabulary!)
    (def calls (atom []))
    (rf/reg-event :review/load
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
        (swap! calls conj :load)
        {:db (assoc db :loaded true)}))
    (rf/reg-event :review/close
      (fn [_ _] (swap! calls conj :close) {}))
    (story/reg-story :story.review {})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/base
      {:loaders [[:review/load]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close]]})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/child {:extends :story.review/base})
    (select-keys (:world (plan/variant-plan :story.review/child))
      [:loaders :loaders-teardown])
    ;; => {:loaders [[:review/load]], :loaders-teardown [[:review/close]]}
    @(story/run-variant :story.review/child)
    ;; => :status :pass, :lifecycle :ready; @calls => []
    (story/destroy-variant! :story.review/child)
    ;; @calls still []

Positive control, in the same process: run the base directly, then destroy it; calls are [:load :close]. A separate actual-source witness registered :fragment.review/loader with :loaders/:loaders-teardown and a variant with only :compose [:fragment.review/loader]. The compiled world contains both slots, but run/destroy again leaves calls empty and reports :pass/:ready.

Expected versus actual: spec/017:1491 explicitly gives composed-fragment loaders followed by the extends-merged variant chain; the normalized plan supplies exactly that. Registered execution instead classifies a child-only raw body as events-only and returns true from run-loaders! without visiting the plan's loaders. Even if a decorator prevents the fast path, registered phase 1 still reads only raw loader events. Inherited/composed completion predicates and loader teardown are likewise bypassed by the raw-body readers.

Impact: a normal derived or composed scenario runs without its documented fixture, can report a passing run, and disagrees with explain/plan. This breaks the primary state/config reuse mechanism; it is not malformed author input.

Repair: thread the already-compiled plan's loader slots through registered allocation classification, phase-1 execution and teardown, as the inline path already does. Do not repair only the :ready short-circuit: that leaves the other raw readers wrong. Retain the normalized cleanup with the allocated run as described in finding 2.

Acceptance: focused end-to-end registered tests for direct, extends-only and compose-only fixtures, plus composed+own loader ordering; a derived false :loaders-complete-when must prevent setup/play and report loader-incomplete; destroy/reset must run the resolved cleanup once. The test must execute run-variant and inspect calls/app-db, not stop at variant-plan. Keep an inline and a no-loader direct control.

Finding 2 — P2: hot reload replaces the cleanup of the active loader run

Locations:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:1044-1048 reads the CURRENT registry body's cleanup during run-teardown-walks!.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:1050-1064 already captures and uses allocation-time decorators for precisely this ownership problem, but there is no corresponding loader capture.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:1099 and 1147 route destroy and in-place reset through this teardown walk.

Trigger: run a variant whose :loaders opens resource A and whose :loaders-teardown closes A. Re-register the same variant with cleanup B (or remove the cleanup), as an ordinary edit/hot reload does, then destroy or re-run the mounted variant.

Executed witness:

    (def calls (atom []))
    (rf/reg-event :review/open
      (fn [_ _] (swap! calls conj :opened-a) {}))
    (rf/reg-event :review/close-a
      (fn [_ _] (swap! calls conj :closed-a) {}))
    (rf/reg-event :review/close-b
      (fn [_ _] (swap! calls conj :closed-b) {}))
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/reload
      {:loaders [[:review/open]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close-a]]})
    @(story/run-variant :story.review/reload)
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/reload
      {:loaders [[:review/open]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close-b]]})
    (story/destroy-variant! :story.review/reload)
    ;; Actual @calls: [:opened-a :closed-b]
    ;; Expected:      [:opened-a :closed-a]

Expected versus actual: loader cleanup must release what the active run opened. Runtime spec/002:518-551 describes :loaders-teardown as the symmetric counterpart of loader-owned external resources; the neighboring decorator implementation explicitly protects this across hot reload. Reading the newest registry entry runs a cleanup whose matching setup never ran, and does not run A's cleanup.

Impact: ordinary story edits can leak subscriptions/timers/sockets or tear down the wrong resource. The witness itself opens no such resource; it proves which cleanup event is selected. This is independent of finding 1: the direct non-inherited variant also fails.

Repair: retain the resolved :loaders-teardown associated with the prepared/allocated run alongside its decorator capture. Consume that capture before overwriting it on reset, and evict it on destruction. Preserve the existing loader-before-decorator teardown order and exception handling. A newly compiled registry body must not retroactively own an old run's cleanup.

Acceptance: a run with cleanup A followed by re-registration with cleanup B and by removal of cleanup must still invoke A exactly once on destroy and on in-place re-run; the next allocated run must subsequently use B. Include a parent/fragment edit once finding 1 is repaired. Do not require real external resources: effect/event call records discriminate the ownership.

Finding 3 — P2: render/save effective args ignore extends and compose

Locations:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/args.cljc:126-135 resolves only the raw variant's :args, omitting inherited/composed arg layers; get-effective-args at 137-141 exposes the same answer.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:497-510 uses this resolver for the rendered view and arg-dependent sub overrides, whereas runtime.cljc:775-799 uses the compiled plan's effective args.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/save_variant.cljc:60-79 and 462-465 capture the same raw-body result; gen-variant-snippet:290-329 emits it as the new variant's own :args.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:334-343 also uses this resolver for Copy EDN (source-traced only).

Executed witness, using the same Story setup:

    (story/reg-story :story.review {:args {:count 0}})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/parent {:args {:count 42}})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/child {:extends :story.review/parent})
    (def source-run @(story/run-variant :story.review/child))
    (def snapshot (save/snapshot-args :story.review/child))
    (def emitted
      (save/gen-variant-snippet
        {:variant-id :story.review/saved
         :extends :story.review/child :args snapshot}))
    (def form (read-string emitted))
    (registrar/reg-variant* (second form) (nth form 2))

Here save is re-frame.story.save-variant and registrar is re-frame.story.registrar. Read/register uses the real generator output and the registration macro's runtime helper, not a hand-built substitute.

Measured:
- source-run :effective-args = {:count 42}.
- snapshot = {:count 0}.
- emitted = (story/reg-variant :story.review/saved {:extends :story.review/child :args {:count 0}}).
- saved variant-plan [:world :effective-args] = {:count 0}.
- explicit-cell control {:cell-overrides {:count 99}} captures {:count 99} correctly.

Expected versus actual: spec/017:1486 requires deep merge of inherited and composed args before child overrides, and the runtime plan does so. The canvas/save resolver substitutes the story default for the inherited value. The resulting saved scenario changes a value the user never overrode. Without a conflicting story/global default, inherited-only keys disappear from the resolver instead. Compose is affected by the same absence of any fragment resolution; that extension is source-confirmed, while the executed witness specifically covers extends.

Impact: the interactive rendering path can show different props from the scenario the run/test result describes, and exported saved variants can permanently replace inherited args. Save is consistent with the flawed canvas resolver, so this is not a claim that the executed JVM probe observed browser DOM or a mismatch between those two flawed consumers.

Repair: make consumers that need effective scenario args use the normalized plan with the same run-arg-layers and control overrides as execution. Preserve one inheritance/composition authority; avoid adding a circular args -> plan -> args dependency. Route consumers through an appropriate higher-level resolver or extract the minimum shared pure resolution boundary. No new facade API or compatibility vocabulary is needed.

Acceptance: an inherited args fixture with conflicting story defaults must give identical effective values in run result, canvas props, save snapshot, and a generated-snippet read/register/plan round trip. Add a composed-fragment counterpart, nested arg merge, active-mode precedence, and explicit cell override controls. At least one actual CLJS canvas test must observe a view prop or rendered value, since this review only traced that caller.

Known work and duplicate check
- Read open AND closed Story-title records plus targeted full title/description searches for inherited/composed loaders, loader teardown, snapshot-args and inherited save/resolve args. No extant defect owner for these three counterexamples was found.
- rf2-7dewo is closed; its completed :setup/:script vocabulary convergence correctly preserves raw bodies in the registrar. Do not undo that contract to mask the runtime consumers above.
- rf2-shx4 is closed after the explicit-image network fix. Its plan-to-runtime fixture wiring is nearby precedent, but these are loader/args defects and do not reopen its network work.
- rf2-fjax is closed; it owns Copy EDN self-extension identity. This review does not duplicate that defect: the finding-3 generated saved ID is distinct from the source and still changes args.
- rf2-k6y2 is the known closed step-debugger prepare/run fix; no new debugger finding is claimed here.
- Source cites rf2-2g7ebs for plan loader composition and rf2-x76af2.19 for allocation-time decorator capture; bd show currently reports neither ID found. Their source comments are supporting implementation history, not proof of a live tracker owner or ruling.
- rf2-wd2t is a separate ongoing read-only Story review at this revision; its current notes request a findings artifact, not a remediation owner. Root should reconcile overlapping findings from that review before dispatching fixes.

Unverified risks / exclusions
No additional speculative defect is promoted. Async supersession/cancellation, full DOM isolation across substrates, recorder gestures, privacy-sensitive export branches, static-build integrity and published dependency resolution were not exhaustively exercised. Partial inline allocation failures are explicitly discussed as an accepted risk in frames.cljc and are not re-filed here. No missing example tests are treated as a defect.

Handoff: three confirmed P2 findings, one open bug bead, no source edits. Root owns the durable tracker checkpoint and push for this read-only review session.

title: gate: check_retired_spellings rule (g) walks the gitignored .clj-kondo cache — 36423 false findings on any built checkout, green in CI
description:
Found by the mayor immediately after merging PR #9572 (rf2-d1nr.4), by running the new gate on the mayor checkout at trunk 281d9a00a3 rather than trusting the PR's green.

THE DEFECT. Rule (g) of `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` scans the WHOLE REPO by walking the FILESYSTEM with `os.walk`, pruning only the directory NAMES in `_EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES`. That set is `node_modules`, `target`, `.shadow-cljs`, `.git`, `.beads`, `.cpcache` — a considered list of build caches — and it does not carry clj-kondo's. So the gate descends into `.clj-kondo/.cache/`, whose transit JSON files are packed with PRE-RENAME namespace names, and reports every one.

MEASURED: `python scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` on the mayor checkout at trunk exits 1 with 36423 findings. Every finding inspected is under `.clj-kondo/.cache/`. `.gitignore:81` names `/.clj-kondo/.cache/`, so the whole tree is untracked; `git ls-files .clj-kondo/` returns 2, and those two are the tracked CONFIG, which is legitimately in scope and must keep being scanned.

WHY CI IS GREEN AND THE CHECKOUT IS RED. A fresh CI checkout has never run clj-kondo, so the cache does not exist there. `Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)` passed on #9572 and is passing on trunk. The gate is correct in CI and wrong everywhere a human or a worker actually runs it — which is the inverse of the usual local-green-is-not-CI hazard, and it is worse, because a red that CI cannot reproduce reads as the developer's own breakage.

WHY IT IS URGENT RATHER THAN COSMETIC. The gate runs UNCONDITIONALLY in `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`, the local pre-checkin spine. Every local spine run on any built checkout now fails with a five-figure finding count that has nothing to do with the diff. A worker meeting that will either chase 36423 phantom findings or, worse, "fix" it by deleting a shared build cache to get a green.

title: Pin evidence integrity: Xray's own renders must never appear in the app frame's epoch records
description:
CONTEXT IS ON THE PARENT EPIC rf2-k97c. Read it first — it is the durable record (the
analysis lived in an untracked ai/findings/ tree and is gone). Line numbers drift; verify.

PIN EVIDENCE INTEGRITY WITH A TEST. Can start in parallel with .1/.3 — it is valuable
whether or not either design lands, and it protects the change when one does.

THE HAZARD, ALREADY REALISED ONCE (rf2-tqlmq): Xray's shell-view render trace LEAKED into
the INSPECTED APPLICATION's epoch :renders, because the shell rendered bare and
current-frame-id fell through to :rf/default. The fix (mount.cljs:379) moved the
frame-provider out one level so the shell resolves to the trace-disabled :rf/xray frame, and
the existing :rf.trace/frame-no-emit? gate then suppresses it.

That fix is currently protected by nothing but a comment. Any change to where Xray's views
render can silently re-open it, and the symptom is not a crash — it is a debugger quietly
reporting its own activity as the application's, which is the worst failure mode this tool
has.

DELIVER: a regression test that mounts Xray against an application frame, drives one
application event, and asserts the application frame's epoch record contains ZERO renders
attributable to Xray's own shell or panels. Assert on the epoch record's contents, not on
absence of exceptions.

Take the test in BOTH directions: it must FAIL if the frame-provider is moved back inside
the shell body. A test that cannot fail is not a pin.
notes:
VERDICT (2026-09-09) — DELIVERED, PR #9567, awaiting merge. Premise CONFIRMED: the mount site was unpinned.

WHAT WAS ALREADY PINNED, AND WHY IT WAS NOT ENOUGH. The epoch suite's inv-7 in
implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_attribution_test.clj (added by the rf2-tqlmq fix
commit a90ffc8af4, alongside the mount.cljs change) pins the EMIT-SIDE GATE: a render
already TAGGED with a trace-disabled frame does not reach the app frame's epoch :renders.
It hand-builds that tag via its own emit-render! helper, so it stays GREEN if the
frame-provider moves back inside the shell body — the tag is precisely what that regression
changes. So inv-7 is not a pin on the mount site, and nothing else was: the only other
observation of the wrap is INCIDENTAL, in mount_cljs_test.cljs's shell-view-mode-of helper,
which reads (get-in (:tree call) [2 1]) — the index 2 silently depends on the wrap existing,
but no assertion states it, and unwrapping would fail two unrelated tests for the wrong
reason. Nothing under tools/xray/test asserted anything about epoch :renders and Xray's own
views.

WHAT LANDED. One test, xray-shell-render-never-lands-in-inspected-app-epoch, in
tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount_cljs_test.cljs (+176 lines, purely additive, no
deletions). Placed there to reuse that file's js/document stub, substrate-render stub and
Xray runtime fixture rather than duplicating roughly 100 lines of DOM stub in a new
namespace.

HOW IT DRIVES REAL MACHINERY. Node-test has no jsdom, so there is no React commit to
observe. The test mounts via mount/open! with the suite's render stub capturing the hiccup
mount-shell-into! hands to the substrate; reads the frame scope out of THAT REAL TREE
(modelling re-frame.views.provider/current-frame tier 2, closest enclosing frame boundary);
emits the shell's :rf.view/rendered through the REAL re-frame.trace/emit! under the frame
that tree resolves to; and reads the app frame's epoch back through the REAL
rf/epoch-history. Only the React commit is modelled — the frame-no-emit gate, the back-fill
and the epoch projection are the shipping code. It asserts on the epoch record's CONTENTS
(zero renders), not on absence of exceptions.

TWO INSTRUMENT CONTROLS, because a zero is not a passing check. (1) The tree walker asserts
it LOCATED shell-view, so an empty :renders means absence rather than a walker that matched
nothing. (2) A positive control emits the same render tagged with the APP frame and asserts
it DOES back-fill into that same epoch — so the emptiness is the gate suppressing Xray, not
a dead read.

BOTH DIRECTIONS DEMONSTRATED. The frame-provider was moved back inside the shell body in
mount.cljs (the exact pre-fix state, a single anchored replacement whose match count was
verified as 1 before writing). Captured RED exit code 1: 3 of 10 assertions failed, the
epoch assertion reading (not (empty? #{:shell-view})) — the rf2-tqlmq leak reproduced
through the real machinery, with the positive control still passing. The plant recompiled
229 files, proving it was in the build's module graph rather than a no-op patch. Source then
restored and verified by git blob hash 66366f08d028dc6bcb489db142640573fd051128 (exact
match), working tree clean.

GATES. compile-node-test node-test exit 0 (1924 files, 0 warnings); node out/node-test.js
exit 0 (11486 tests, 57797 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors); the new test alone exit 0 (1
test, 10 assertions); tools/xray JVM clojure -M:test exit 0 (1276 tests, 6118 assertions);
check-ai-tracking-ratchet, check-no-hardcoded-paths, check-beads-pr-boundary and
check-commit-attribution all exit 0.

BUILD LANE. Determined by reading implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, not by guessing: the
:node-test build takes the global source paths including ../tools/xray/test (lines 313-314)
and selects on :ns-regexp "cljs-test$" (line 664), so the test is compiled and run by
npm run test:cljs. The :node-test-xray-manual-epoch lane was NOT used — its :ns-regexp
(line 899) is anchored to the single manual-epoch-delivery namespace, and widening it would
defeat that lane's graph-isolation purpose.

SCOPE HELD. No change to the substrate denylist or the refusal path (rf2-k97c.3/.4
territory); no design work from rf2-k97c.1/.2/.3; no refactor of the mount path; one test
only. Bundle isolation untouched (a test under tools/ requiring from implementation/ is the
permitted direction).

KNOWN NOT COVERED, recorded deliberately rather than fixed: popout! in mount.cljs carries
its OWN copy of the same frame-provider wrap. This pins the inline/overlay mount path only,
per this bead's one-test scope. A second pin for the popout path would be a separate item if
wanted.

title: EPIC: Xray's SHELL mounts on every browser adapter (root swap + denylist retired); the EMBED DOOR is still ratom-family — rf2-l1jm
description:
GOAL: Xray must be usable on a re-frame2 application whichever BROWSER adapter that
application installs — stock Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, Fresco, and adapters that do not
exist yet — without losing the two it serves today.

THIS DESCRIPTION IS THE DURABLE RECORD. The analysis behind it lived in an untracked
ai/findings/ tree and is NOT available to workers. Everything load-bearing is restated here
with file:line citations. Verify at source; line numbers drift.

== THE CURRENT FAILURE ==

Xray refuses to mount when the installed adapter is element-shaped. It works on stock
Reagent and reagent-slim; it refuses on UIx and Fresco — two of four live browser adapters,
one of which (Fresco) is re-frame2's own native view layer, taught by its own installation
chapter (docs/core/fresco/00-installation.md:154).

The denylist: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:237
  react-element-render-kinds = the set of :rf.adapter/ui, /uix, /helix, /freehand, /fresco
The refusal: same file ~:286, refuse-unsupported-substrate! — publishes an
:unsupported-substrate diagnostic, one console.warn, no mount.

THE REFUSAL IS PROTECTIVE, NOT A BUG. Xray's shell is hiccup; it paints by calling the
installed adapter's :render (mount.cljs:396 and :1688 — those two sites are the ENTIRE
render coupling). On an element-shaped adapter the hiccup vector reaches React as raw CLJS
data: "Functions are not valid as a React child ... frame_provider" plus an uncaught
"Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {key, val, ...})" from the
props map's MapEntries. The core now also refuses that input first, via
:rf.error/hiccup-on-element-render-slot thrown by the spine's make-render before any root is
created.

DELETING THE DENYLIST WITHOUT A PAINT PATH IS NOT A SOLUTION.

== WHAT IS NOT THE PROBLEM ==

* Not inspection. Xray reads app state through the Spec 009 instrumentation API
  (:rf.trace/*) and the Tool-Pair contract (spec/Tool-Pair.md), which are already
  substrate-independent. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp is a shipped consumer of that same
  contract with no view technology at all.
* Not "apps containing Fresco views". Fresco is a VIEW LAYER and needs some adapter; which
  one is the adopter's choice. The two counted pilot applications deliberately keep the
  Reagent adapter while migrating views to Fresco
  (docs/design/fresco/product/pilots/workspace.md:297, "Why the adapter does not change").
  Those pilots are NOT blocked. Do not build a release-blocker argument on this.
* Not the single-adapter ruling. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2337 (Single adapter per
  process) needs no change for either candidate design. Multiple React roots in one page are
  ordinary and do not require a second adapter installation.

== VERIFIED FACTS THE DESIGN RESTS ON ==

1. THE TWO FAMILIES STORE STATE THE SAME WAY.
   spine.cljs:466 (rf2-w1g0d2): "make-state-container is the only point of the container
   quartet that genuinely differs between the React-hook spine and the ratom family ... The
   ctor is the ONLY variable."
   spine.cljs:454: React-only substrates lack a reactive atom primitive, so the spine uses a
   plain clojure.core/atom + add-watch — "observably equivalent to the Reagent adapter's
   r/atom for the substrate contract surface (read, replace, subscribe)".
   So read-container, replace-container! and subscribe-container are semantically identical
   on every adapter. They are public at
   implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:397 and :692 (make-state-container
   :377). Bundle isolation bans implementation/ -> tools/, not the reverse, so a tool may
   require them.

2. THE FAMILIES DIVERGE ONLY AT VIEW-SIDE HOOKUP.
   Reagent tracks a ratom deref; the spine uses useSyncExternalStore (spine.cljs:463). Both
   are consumers of the same two contract ops.

3. A WATCH ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — ACTIVATION IS MANDATORY, AND IT IS PUBLIC.
   implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:85 activate-derived-value!, docstring:
   "reagent.ratom/Reaction captures its sources only through deref-capture, and a plain deref
   taken OUTSIDE *ratom-context* ... runs the body raw and leaves watching nil — a reaction
   that is watchable, and watched, and NOTIFIES NOBODY. A Reagent COMPONENT never notices
   because its render IS the capture context ... This op is that missing capture, and it is
   the ONLY thing the ratom family needs to satisfy the spec's push clause."
   add-on-dispose! is public in the same ns (:121). On the React-hook spine
   activate-derived-value! no-ops (those derived values are push from construction), so one
   code path serves both families.

4. FRESCO IS ALREADY A RENDERER THAT IS NOT AN ADAPTER.
   implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:252 calls
   react-dom-client/createRoot DIRECTLY. Measured: that file calls substrate.adapter/render
   0 times; Xray's mount.cljs calls it 3 times.
   Fresco's collector already implements the full cross-adapter observation sequence —
   collector.cljs:296 "Give cell a live subscription: subscribe, activate, take the one ...
   and again when the substrate disposes the reaction out from under it", with
   activate-derived-value! :318, add-on-dispose! :323, dispose-cell! :161, a
   disposed-while-still-held path :167, idle disposal :188.

5. MEASURED SCOPE (2026-09-09, over the 142 .cljs/.cljc files under tools/xray/src/;
   negative control 0):
     (rf/subscribe    125 occurrences / 37 files   (118 of them @(rf/subscribe )
     rf/reg-view       51 occurrences / 35 files
   The SUBSCRIPTION surface is LARGER than the VIEW surface. Re-measure before committing.

6. XRAY ALREADY PARTLY OWNS ITS VIEW STACK. tools/xray/deps.edn:82-92 declares stock Reagent
   directly for component-local ratom state, "independent of the reagent-slim adapter above".
   Core itself is Reagent-free.

7. XRAY NEVER CALLS (rf/view ...) — zero call sites under tools/xray/src; mount and panels
   pass Vars in hiccup. Preload load-order means those Vars are the Reagent-shaped wrappers
   reg-view* seeds before any adapter wrap is applied.

== THREE COUPLINGS TO SEVER (not one) ==

  (1) which :render is called — the denylist;
  (2) which :adapter/current-frame hook ambient subscribe resolves through — a tool-owned
      root must establish frame context DELIBERATELY;
  (3) whether rf/subscribe returns a Reagent reaction or a React-spine IDeref+IWatchable.
(1) is why nothing paints. (3) is why first paint is not enough. (2) is easy to miss.

== THE TWO CANDIDATE DESIGNS ==

Both own a root and stop calling the host's :render. Both keep the :rf/xray frame, the
collectors, events, subs and time-travel targeting. Neither needs a second adapter or a core
change. They differ in WHAT RENDERS Xray's views.

DESIGN A — own a Reagent root, observe through public interop.
  Mount the existing hiccup shell on Xray's own React root using stock Reagent (already a
  dep). Replace subscription reads with a tool-local binding performing the four interop
  calls Fresco's collector makes: subscribe -> activate-derived-value! -> baseline deref ->
  add-watch -> add-on-dispose! -> re-wire on invalidation. Roughly 20 lines.
  Cost: ~125 MECHANICAL call-site substitutions, greppable and count-verifiable, plus the
  binding. Views stay hiccup, in the idiom their authors know.

DESIGN B — re-author Xray's views in Fresco.
  Port Xray's own views to Fresco and mount through Fresco's root API, reusing the shipped,
  maintained collector instead of writing a binding.
  Cost: ~51 SEMANTIC view rewrites across 35 files, plus plain helper fns used as component
  heads (Fresco does not accept arbitrary Reagent component fns as hiccup heads).
  Benefit: no new observation layer to maintain; dogfoods the native view layer.

Both are migrations differing in KIND: mechanical-and-numerous vs semantic-and-fewer.
A third option — a separately booted debugger realm (iframe or window plus a transport) — is
real but stronger isolation than this requires. Record it as future work, not the answer.
REJECTED, instructively: making the spine's :render accept hiccup. Wrong layer — it solves a
tool's problem inside the core, adds a hiccup converter to every application's dependency
graph, and weakens a deliberate app-author error.

== HARD CONSTRAINTS ==

* Bundle isolation: nothing in implementation/ may :require from tools/. A design may change
  the core's substrate layer; it must NOT make the core aware of Xray.
* EVIDENCE INTEGRITY IS RELEASE-GRADE, AND HAS ALREADY BEEN BREACHED ONCE.
  mount.cljs:379 (rf2-tqlmq): Xray's shell-view render trace LEAKED into the inspected app
  frame's epoch :renders because current-frame-id fell through to :rf/default. Fixed by
  moving the frame-provider out one level so the shell resolves to the trace-disabled
  :rf/xray frame. Any change to where Xray's views render MUST re-establish this, pinned by a
  test. A debugger that pollutes the evidence it reports is worse than no debugger.
* Xray is dev-only, excluded from production bundles. Solutions may exploit that.

== POSTURE ==
Pre-alpha, aiming at a masterpiece: elegance, power, correctness. No back-compat shims.
Trust the programmer. Do not over-engineer, do not gold-plate, do not build a general
extension framework to promise zero future changes. State the minimum host contract instead.

== SUCCESS CRITERIA (behavioural) ==
1 first display; 2 updates as the app changes; 3 Xray's own interactions; 4 tool-local state
separate from the app, with commands targeting the intended app frame; 5 Xray's activity
never masquerading as application evidence; 6 clean teardown and reopen without disturbing
the host. Preserve today's inspection and time-travel workflows, or price the loss.
A future non-React browser adapter supplying only the container quartet plus the listener API
should get Xray with no Xray-side work.

== CHILDREN ==
.1 spike (both designs, one real panel, two adapters) -> .2 operator decision -> .3
implementation -> .4 retire the denylist -> .5 evidence-integrity pin -> .6 popout/Story ->
.7 docs and the minimum host contract.

== NAME CORRECTION, 2026-09-10 (mayor) ==

This description was written before the view layer was renamed and used the RETIRED
PRODUCT NAME throughout: 18 occurrences, and zero of the current one. The source tree
had already been renamed -- `mount.cljs` reads `:rf.adapter/fresco` -- so the durable
record was the only thing still carrying the old name, and it cited three paths that
resolve to nothing:

  docs/core/<old>/00-installation.md               -> docs/core/fresco/00-installation.md
  docs/design/<old>/product/pilots/workspace.md    -> docs/design/fresco/product/pilots/workspace.md
  implementation/<old>/src/.../impl/mount.cljs     -> implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs

All three replacements were verified tracked at tip 03d4af871c before this edit; the
LINE NUMBERS in the citations above were not re-derived and this description already
says to verify at source because they drift. `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` gates
the retired name in tracked SOURCE but does not read bead prose, which is why this sat.

Nothing else in this description changed: the substitution was name-only, and the diff
was checked line by line to confirm every changed line differs by the name alone.

== NO OPERATOR RULING IS REQUIRED FOR THIS EPIC (recorded 2026-09-09) ==

Mike has delegated the design choice. Do NOT surface this epic to him as a decision, and do
not park any child waiting on his opinion.

STANDING DEFAULT: DESIGN A (Xray owns a stock-Reagent root; subscription reads go through a
tool-local binding making four PUBLIC interop calls — subscribe, activate-derived-value!,
add-watch, add-on-dispose!, with re-wire on invalidation; views stay hiccup).

The default is chosen because the binding calls public ops rather than reimplementing them
(interop.cljs:85's docstring: activation is "the ONLY thing the ratom family needs"), and
because its edits are mechanical and therefore lower-risk per site than Design B's semantic
view rewrites. The margin is NARROW and was disputed by competent reviewers — which is why
the choice is settled by a pre-committed rule, not by taste.

THE RULE LIVES ON rf2-k97c.2 as five ordered steps with numeric thresholds (binding growth
beyond the four interop calls; touched sites over 190 or more than 15% needing per-site
judgement; evidence-integrity failure; Arm B at half Arm A's site count or better). The mayor
APPLIES it to child .1's report. It is mechanical: the spike's measurements decide, not
anyone's preference.

SO THE FLOW IS: .1 spike (ready now) -> .2 mayor applies the rule -> .3 implement the chosen
design -> .4 retire the denylist, .6 popout/Story, .7 docs. .5 (evidence-integrity pin) is
independent and ready now.

THE ONLY ESCALATION PATH: if .1's report is too incomplete to apply the rule, send .1 back
for the missing measurement. Do not ask Mike to guess.

lines in a file the PR opens"), so .6 no longer owns that edit. That is recorded on .6 itself.

=== TITLE CORRECTED 2026-09-12, trunk 547d418e5b. The old one asserted something that stopped being true two hours earlier. ===

WAS: "EPIC: Xray must work on every browser adapter — it refuses UIx and Fresco today"
NOW: "EPIC: Xray works on every browser adapter — root swap and denylist retirement landed;
      .6 pop-out and .7 docs remain"

WHY. The clause "it refuses UIx and Fresco today" was the epic's whole premise and it is now false:
rf2-k97c.3 (PR #9708) moved the shell onto Xray's own React root, and rf2-k97c.4 (PR #9709) deleted

`mount.cljs:245-249` — `;; ---- substrate render-shape gate — RETIRED (rf2-qgfo4 -> rf2-k97c.4)` —
which is this project's convention for recording what stood somewhere and why it went, not residue.

WHY IT IS WORTH AN EDIT RATHER THAN A NOTE: the title is what the ready list prints, and a listing
is what the next reader sizes and schedules from. A title that says the tool refuses two adapters
invites somebody to dispatch against a defect that was fixed today — the same class of misread the
disposition banner on rf2-k97c.3 exists to prevent, arriving through the one field a note cannot
reach.

'refuse-unsupported-substrate!' mount.cljs` read 0 — correct in its conclusion, but partly for the
wrong reason: the tombstone comment DOES mention the symbol, hyphen-wrapped across lines 247-248,

An hour ago I replaced "Xray must work on every browser adapter — it refuses UIx and Fresco today"

feels like evidence for its opposite, so the fix arrives with the original's confidence pointing the
other way, reading as MORE reliable for having been written in response to being caught.

THE DISCRIMINATING TEST, applied: what would I expect to SEE that is different if "Xray works on

title: Stop the per-PR audit-memory writer, and record the ruling in CLAUDE.md (rf2-ornb ruling (a))
description:
RULED by rf2-ornb 2026-09-08. Per-PR audit records stop being memories. An audit of one merged PR is a ledger entry, not knowledge that generalises, and it is already triple-recorded — the `chore(beads): audit merged PR` commits on main, the bead notes, and the PRs on GitHub. Only the memory copy was being serialised into every session start.

WHY IT MATTERS. The class regrows at ~113,500 chars/day (Sep 5-7 mean of 46 audit commits/day x 2,468 chars mean record size, matching the bead's own estimate), and it went 0 -> 32 -> 42 within hours of 212 memories being culled on 2026-09-08. `bd prime` is 1,858,076 bytes of which 99.71% is memory bodies. THIS IS THE ONLY LEVER THAT STOPS THE GROWTH, and it is cheap.

STEP 1 — RE-IDENTIFY THE PRODUCER. Do NOT assume it is a script. The earlier analysis named `ai/audit-checkpoint.py`, `ai/audit-query.py`, `ai/audit-verify-owners.py`, `ai/audit-wait-next.py` and per-PR `ai/prepare-audit-*.py`. NONE OF THEM EXIST — verified 2026-09-08: `ls ai/*.py` returns nothing, `ai/` contains no Python at all, `find ai -name '*audit*'` returns nothing, and the string `merged-pr-audit` appears nowhere in `scripts/`, `.claude/` or `ai/` except inside decision dossiers and extended-context notes. The likeliest producer is the live mayor loop calling `bd remember` directly, i.e. a prompt/behaviour change rather than a file edit. Find it before claiming a one-file fix.

STEP 2 — STOP IT writing `merged-pr-audit-pr-<N>` memories. The audit continues to land on the bead and in the commit, unchanged.

STEP 3 — RECORD THE RULING IN A TRACKED FILE. This is not optional. The producer lives outside git, so a ruling recorded only locally is invisible to a fresh clone and the class regrows silently. One sentence in CLAUDE.md's Beads-durability section: per-PR/per-run bookkeeping goes on the bead and the commit, never into a memory; `bd remember` is for findings that generalise.

VERIFY BY EFFECT: watch the `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` key count hold flat across the next several merges (42 as of 2026-09-08 23:14 AUSEST). Count by key prefix with controls both directions — a nonsense prefix must return 0.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: this deletes NOTHING. The 42 standing records stay. No pruning, no eviction rule, no rolling window, no `bd flatten`/`gc`/`compact` — rf2-cve7 (P1, 210 keys vanished) is unresolved and nothing may be trimmed while it is open.
acceptance_criteria: Producer identified (it is NOT ai/audit-*.py — those do not exist) and stopped writing merged-pr-audit-pr-<N> memories; one tracked sentence in CLAUDE.md's Beads-durability section says per-PR/per-run bookkeeping goes on the bead and the commit, never a memory; the merged-pr-audit-pr-* key count holds flat across several subsequent merges (42 at 2026-09-08 23:14 AUSEST), counted by key prefix with a nonsense-prefix control returning 0. Nothing deleted.
notes:
=== PRODUCER LOCATED 2026-09-08 23:2x AUSEST — STEP 1 OF THIS BEAD IS DISCHARGED ===

It is NOT `ai/audit-*.py` (those do not exist) and NOT any tracked file. It is generated Python UNDER `.git/`:

    .git/codex-pr-audit-<PR>/checkpoint.py

11 such directories present right now, PRs 9489-9499, each carrying a full per-PR audit kit (`checkpoint.py`, `query.py`, `verify.py`, `record-findings.py`, `receipt.txt`, `pr.json`, gate logs, `merge-diff.patch`, and more). The two `bd remember` calls are `checkpoint.py` lines 20-21:

    run('remember receipt',['bd','remember',(out/'receipt.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8'),
                            '--key','merged-pr-audit-pr-9489'])
    run('remember cursor', ['bd','remember',cursor,'--key','merged-pr-audit-cursor'])

WHY EVERY EARLIER SEARCH CAME BACK EMPTY, and it is the instrument lesson worth carrying: `.git/` is skipped by default by the ripgrep-backed search tool and was outside the `scripts/` / `ai/` / `.claude/` scopes that were searched by hand, so four independent sweeps and a process check all returned an honest-looking zero. It surfaced only from an UNRESTRICTED `grep -rn` at the repo root, which descended into `.git/`. When a producer is invisible to every scoped search, widen the ROOT before concluding it does not exist.

*** THE TWO KEYS ARE NOT THE SAME CLASS. DO NOT REMOVE BOTH. ***

  - `merged-pr-audit-pr-<N>` (line 20) is the ACCUMULATING class — one new key per merged PR, ~2,468 chars each, 42 standing. THIS is what rf2-ornb ruled must stop.
  - `merged-pr-audit-cursor` (line 21) is a SINGLE ROLLING KEY updated in place. It does not accumulate, and it is LOAD-BEARING: `query.py:5` and `verify.py:5` both `bd recall merged-pr-audit-cursor` to resume, and `checkpoint.py:19` asserts the old cursor before advancing. Deleting or stopping it BREAKS THE AUDIT HARNESS's resume logic. LEAVE IT.

A blanket "remove the bd remember calls" edit therefore breaks the harness. Stop line 20 only.

*** WHERE THE FIX GOES — NOT IN THESE FILES ***

These directories are DISPOSABLE PER-PR ARTEFACTS regenerated for each PR, and there is no shared generator or template on disk (`ls -d .git/codex-* | grep -v 'pr-audit-[0-9]'` returns nothing). So editing `.git/codex-pr-audit-9489/checkpoint.py` changes nothing for PR 9500. THE FIX BELONGS IN THE EXTERNAL HARNESS THAT EMITS `checkpoint.py` — the Codex-side merge-audit agent — which is outside this repository entirely.

THAT SHARPENS STEP 3 OF THIS BEAD RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. Because the producer is not just untracked but out-of-repo, the tracked CLAUDE.md sentence is the ONLY durable artefact this repo can hold, and it is what a future harness author reads. It should state the rule rather than name a file: per-PR/per-run bookkeeping goes on the bead and in the commit, never into a memory; `bd remember` is for findings that generalise. Note also that `record-findings.py` sits beside `checkpoint.py` in the same kit — the harness already has a findings path distinct from the receipt path, so the rule has somewhere to land.

VERIFY BY EFFECT, unchanged: `merged-pr-audit-pr-*` key count holds flat across subsequent merges (42 at 2026-09-08 23:14 AUSEST), counted by key prefix with a nonsense-prefix control returning 0. `merged-pr-audit-cursor` should still be present and still advancing.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9503 (2026-09-08; full three-commit landed range f3205b8051dd7f7ce3c9750bb18baec4d6c9a932..8fb4d4545cedd1e53c069bdf8d80d169806da934): append-only P3 documentation correction on this existing open owner.

CLAUDE.md's new per-PR-bookkeeping bullet says the memory copy "is serialised into every session start where it is the dominant cost". That is already false on the paired landed tree: #9504 merged at 13:57:21Z before #9503 at 14:15:51Z, and the same #9503 diff explicitly documents that .beads/PRIME.md overrides the default completely. Independent installed-command capture during the #9504 review confirmed bd prime returns the full 3774-byte canonical primer (3844 checkout bytes), while bd prime --hook-json contains exactly those 3844 checkout bytes in SessionStart additionalContext. No per-PR memory bodies are present. .claude/settings.json still invokes bare bd prime for both SessionStart and PreCompact. The 1,858,076-byte/99.71% measurement can remain useful as HISTORICAL DEFAULT-output evidence, but must be labeled as such rather than stated as the current session-start path or proof of current latency.

Action: qualify that rationale as the pre-PRIME default behavior, keeping the separate generalisation/routing rule and the standing-record/cursor protection intact. This is a small truth correction to prose agents execute, not a new timing diagnosis. It does not implement or claim that the outside-repo producer stopped; this owner remains open for that disposition. The active audit's explicit user instruction still requires per-PR bd remember receipts and cursor pushes, so no producer-policy change or memory deletion was performed during this review.

Other additions independently checked: removing only four inserted strings reconstructs the entire original CLAUDE.md byte-for-byte; all three authored commits are in the review range; the bd show long phrase is 0 in rendered output versus 1 in description, with WORD WRAP 1/1 and nonsense 0/0 controls. Description markdown is stripped; current close-reason text is printed separately and contributes backticks, so whole-output counts now differ from the earlier open-bead measurement. The JSON-field remedy is correct. Existing rf2-g2br is closed, and the PRIME allow-list/override was verified in #9504; neither needs a duplicate owner.

---
MEASURED 2026-09-09, and it CHANGES THIS BEAD'S PREMISE. Read before starting work.

(b) HAS LANDED. `.beads/PRIME.md` exists (3,844 bytes, written 2026-09-08 23:57), is
TRACKED (`git ls-files .beads/PRIME.md` = 1), and the allow-list obstacle is DISCHARGED:
`scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh:96` now carries an explicit
`.beads/PRIME.md) return 0 ;;` arm, with the rationale at :62 and the refusal message
updated at :234. Working tree clean.

EFFECT ON PRIME: `bd prime` now emits 3,844 chars — byte-for-byte the PRIME.md override —
against ~1,830,000 chars measured 2026-09-08. A 99.8% reduction. Memory bodies no longer
reach a session at SessionStart or PreCompact at all; they are now PULL-ONLY via
`bd memories <topic>`.

(a) HAS NOT LANDED — the class is still growing, faster than before:
  - audit-class records `merged-pr-audit-pr-*`: 74 (was 42 when rf2-ornb was ruled, 0
    immediately after the 2026-09-08 cull). Highest PR seen: 9530.
  - audit-class value bytes: 168,733.
  - whole corpus: 989 memories / 1,893,398 value chars (was ~911 after the cull).
  - trunk still carries `chore(beads): audit merged PR #9528/#9529/#9530`, so the
    out-of-repo Codex harness at `.git/codex-pr-audit-<PR>/checkpoint.py:20` is live.

INSTRUMENT NOTE, because it cost a false zero here: `bd memories --json` returns a
key-to-value OBJECT, not an array. `.[].key` silently yields nothing and a grep over it
reads 0 for EVERY class — the reassuring answer. Use `jq -r 'keys[]'`, pipe through
`tr -d '\r'` (jq writes CRLF on this box), and take `merged-pr-audit-cursor` as the
positive control: it must read 1. `length` on the object happens to be correct.

SO THE PRIORITY IS NOW QUESTIONABLE. This bead was set P2 "go now" because the audit class
regrew ~113,500 chars/day AND memories were 99.7% of prime output — the second clause is
what made it urgent, and PRIME.md has removed it. What survives as justification is corpus
hygiene and `bd memories <topic>` search dilution, which is real but not urgent. RECOMMEND
re-pricing P2 -> P3 unless the operator wants the corpus held down for its own sake.
Nothing here changes the RULING (stop writing the per-PR class); only its urgency.

UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: `merged-pr-audit-cursor` (checkpoint.py:21) is a single
rolling key read by `query.py:5`, `verify.py:5` and `checkpoint.py:19` to resume. Do NOT
remove it. Only the accumulating `merged-pr-audit-pr-<N>` class stops. And the fix belongs
in the external harness — the per-PR kits under `.git/` are disposable, so editing one
fixes nothing for the next PR.
close_reason:

WHAT THE AUDIT CAUGHT, and it is a good example of the audit reading the MAYOR's merge rather than the worker's diff: PR #9503 landed three commits, and its THIRD made its SECOND false. title: [implementation/hicasso] Refresh an open popover's anchor when its :anchor prop changes
description:
At snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd (unchanged in relevant files at mayor HEAD 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795), an already-open popover does not follow a changed :anchor prop.

Supported caller / minimal reproduction:
Render two persistent triggers with distinct stable IDs "a" and "b", and one unchanged component/key:
[overlay/popover {:open? true :anchor selected-trigger-id :placement :bottom-start} [:p "Menu"]].
Mount with selected-trigger-id = "a", then update ordinary application state so the same open popover renders with selected-trigger-id = "b". Both trigger elements remain mounted. The public :anchor contract is the DOM id of the trigger to position against (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/overlay.cljs:151,204; docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md:74); neither contract makes :anchor an initial-only prop.

Expected: release this overlay's claim on A, claim B, and keep the open panel anchored to B. Actual: A retains the generated anchor-name, B never receives it, and the panel's position-anchor still resolves against A. Removing :anchor while open similarly leaves the old claim active.

Exact causal trace:
- impl/overlay.cljs:333-363 creates one per-instance cell and one stable ref callback. claim-anchor! and anchor-panel! run only when that callback attaches (347-354); release-anchor! runs only in its cleanup (359).
- body at 411-433 rewrites cell.anchorId from the latest props (426), but reuses the same native element ref (433). It has no commit update for the changed anchor ID.
- React preserves the div and does not reattach an equal ref on an ordinary prop update. The pinned local react-dom-client.development.js markRef (10115-10127) marks attachment only for a new fiber or changed ref.
- Placement and dismissal handlers are updated declaratively, so they do not refresh this separate imperative anchor claim.

Impact: a normal shared action/menu popover reused for a newly selected trigger stays positioned at the previous row/control even though its content and caller state have changed.

Smallest repair: reconcile the anchor claim at commit when :anchor changes, balancing the old release and new claim while preserving the open top-layer node. Keep anchor tokens out of server bytes and avoid closing/reopening the overlay for unrelated renders; no new public API or global registry is needed.

Dedupe: all-status title and description searches for anchor/popover/claim-anchor!/anchorId, plus relevant memories. Fully read rf2-4e5b (frameless dismissal ownership) and rf2-s2ta (fresh :on-dismiss on an open panel); neither handles :anchor changes. Existing deliberate out-of-order same-trigger claim teardown behavior is not challenged.

Verification limits: source-only causal validation with public contract, current implementation, existing overlay test paths, and pinned React reconciler source. No browser/build/test suite was executed, no code changed.
acceptance_criteria: A focused real-DOM test keeps the same open popover/native node and changes :anchor A -> B. Assert A's prior anchorName restored, B claimed with the name used by panel.positionAnchor, and no close/reopen or focus disturbance. Cover B -> nil and final unmount cleanup; an unrelated rerender with unchanged anchor must not churn the claim. Preserve existing SSR deterministic bytes and shared-trigger teardown rows.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07, worker/hicasso-a, PR #9367 ---

Reproduced in Chromium from the bead's own minimal reproduction (two
persistent triggers with distinct stable ids, one unchanged popover), watched
failing before the fix and passing after.

Failing-first, `npm run test:browser` with the fix reverted (exit 1). Five
reds, every one an ENGINE reading rather than an attribute the module just
wrote:

  A got back exactly what its author wrote
    actual: (not (= "--mine-a" "--rf-overlay-34"))
  B is claimed now
    actual: (not (not= "--mine-b" "--mine-b"))
  and it is the name the panel's `position-anchor` uses
    actual: (not (= "--mine-b" "--rf-overlay-34"))
  so the ENGINE moved the box to B. B.left=24.90625 panel.left=0 A.left=0
    actual: (not (< 24.90625 2))
  and A is still holding its own   [the :anchor -> nil arm]
    actual: (not (= "--mine-a" "--rf-overlay-34"))

Post-fix on the same base: exit 0, 0 failures. Post-rebase onto c835b15c6b:
exit 0, 811 tests / 4435 assertions, 0 failures.

Repair. `claim-anchor!`/`anchor-panel!` and `release-anchor!` are now reached
through one pair of doors (`take-anchor!` / `drop-anchor!`), and
`reconcile-anchor!` runs them when the anchor id the standing claim was taken
for (`claimedFor` on the instance cell) no longer matches the prop. Release
before claim and through those same doors, so `release-anchor!`'s
"only while my ident is still the name on it" guard keeps the shared-trigger
and out-of-order teardown behaviour the suite already pins. Idempotent by
`claimedFor`, so the render that OPENS a panel — where the ref callback has
already claimed — and every unrelated re-render touch nothing. The panel keeps
its node, its fiber and its top-layer entry; no close/reopen, no focus
disturbance, no new public API and no registry.

THE ONE DESIGN COST, recorded because the bead did not price it. It is driven

callback cannot serve: React re-attaches a ref whose identity changed, and for
an open popover that is `hidePopover()`/`showPopover()` in the same commit — a
real platform dismissal that fires `beforetoggle` with newState "closed" and
would dispatch the author's own `:on-dismiss`. So the ref's identity stays
stable, deliberately, and the reconciliation is a hook. A LAYOUT effect and not
a passive one, because what it corrects is a position and a position corrected
after paint is a visible jump; React attaches the panel's ref before it runs
the parent's layout effects, so the ordering is the ref's own.

title: api(observability): Tool-Pair DCE tier rule is false at tip — rewrite it; tools attach via rf/register-listener!
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.4); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`spec/Tool-Pair.md:633-639` (anchor `facade-vs-home-verb-the-dce-tier-rule`, landed by rf2-rfid2x `eba72089b0`) rules that "canonical devtools attach via the per-stream home-namespace verbs… because a tool preload MUST NOT require `re-frame.core` into a production build", that "those namespaces do not require `re-frame.core`, so a dev-only tool preload that requires them is dead-code-eliminated out of production bundles wholesale", and that "the re-frame2 project template registers its default error sink via `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`". It then carries Story as "a deliberate exception". The same rule is restated in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1382-1406` (comment plus the `:status` / `:justification` strings of `re-frame.core/register-listener!` and `unregister-listener!`) and `:2029-2037` (`re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!`), copied into `spec/api-manifest.edn` rows 160, 180, 198.

Measured at HEAD, every premise is false:

- `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:52`), which requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally on both platforms (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:39-49`); the facade's `:trace` arm and the home verb swap the same atom (`trace.cljc:951` → `trace/tooling.cljc:81`). Every bundle with the facade has the registry; the only elision lever is the `goog.DEBUG` gate around the CALL SITE (`trace.cljc:28-34`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1124-1135`), which both spellings need equally.
- The exemplar, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs`, requires `re-frame.core` at `:13` (for `rf/with-frame` + `rf/dispatch` at `:79-80`) two lines above the comment at `:15-16` saying the home namespace keeps the tooling surface "independently elidable". 7 of the 10 non-test `:trace` home-verb files already require `re-frame.core` (measured: install.cljs, pair `runtime.cljs`, both testbeds, Story `frames.cljc` / `play.cljc` / `runtime.cljc`).
- `:events` / `:errors` are always-on — there is nothing to elide.
- The template's own test lists `register-listener!` among substrings that must NOT appear in any emitted file (`tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:68-78`); `git grep -n "register-listener" tools/template` → that test line only.
- What actually keeps tools out of production is `:devtools/preloads` (dev builds only) plus the call-site gate; what kept Story's `:epoch` registration on the facade (Mike's revert `037f7d999e`) is that `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` is a hard classpath dependency — a fact of the REQUIRE line (`install.cljs:18`), not of the verb.

The rule protects nothing and licenses a second spelling; two tools straddle it (`install.cljs:67` home, Story `invariants.cljc:395` / pair `runtime.cljs:1272` / Xray runner `core.cljs:169` facade). A dual whose written discriminator the require graph contradicts is not a legitimate dual (`ai/findings/API-review/fable/README.md` §Ethos bar).

## Target API

No new API. One rule sentence replaces `Tool-Pair.md:633-639`:

> Listeners attach through `rf/register-listener!`, apps and tools alike. A tool stays out of production builds by being a `:devtools/preloads` entry and by gating its registration call site on `goog.DEBUG` ([009 §User-side listener registration]) — not by which namespace the call names: `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally, and both spellings swap the same registry. The home-namespace verbs (`re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`, `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!`, `re-frame.event-emit/register-event-listener!`, `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!`) are implementation seams — late-bind targets, framework-internal registrations and fixture clears — not a second public spelling. `:epoch` carries the one dependency fact: the facade no-ops when `day8/re-frame2-epoch` is absent; a tool that hard-requires `re-frame.epoch` at boot fails at compile time from the require, whichever verb it then calls.

Keep the anchor id (inbound links: `git grep -n "facade-vs-home-verb"`). The Story "deliberate exception" paragraph goes — Story is no longer an exception to anything.

Tool sites move to the facade (11 sites, 9 files; migrate each site's matching `unregister` too):

```clojure
;; install.cljs:45 — before / after
(rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! :rf.xray/trace-collector trace-collector/collect-trace!)
(rf/register-listener! :trace :rf.xray/trace-collector trace-collector/collect-trace!)

;; install.cljs:67 — before / after (KEEP the [re-frame.epoch] require at :18 — it is the hard dependency)
(rf.epoch/register-epoch-listener! :rf.xray/epoch-collector (fn [record] …))
(rf/register-listener! :epoch :rf.xray/epoch-collector (fn [record] …))
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; codex on the July doc: "Prefer… use the facade by default while retaining home operations only for demonstrated dependency needs… Story needs no special folklore if optional-producer tolerance is the stated reason… If a call site changes spelling, migrate its matching unregister operation as well and retain the same stream/id." Codex on this doc: "The DCE criticism usefully invalidates an unsupported blanket teaching rule… Verify any claimed bundle improvement with the existing positive-control build, not source greps alone." Grok: "The DCE sentence in Tool-Pair:633-639 is replaced, not enforced."

## Deletion list

- `Tool-Pair.md:633-639` (rule + Story exception) → the paragraph above.
- `install.cljs:15-16` comment; `:27` prose naming `re-frame.trace/register-listener!`.
- `api-manifest-metadata.edn:1382-1406` comment + the two rows' `:status` / `:justification` strings; `:2029-2037` comment + `register-epoch-listener!` `:status` ("tool-embedding form" wording) — rewritten to the rule above; then regenerate.

## Consumers to migrate (all → `rf/register-listener! <stream> …` / `rf/unregister-listener!`)

- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:45` (`:trace`), `:67` (`:epoch`).
- Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:225,329`, `play.cljc:202`, `recorder.cljc:1023`, `runtime.cljc:103`, `ui/trace_buffer.cljs:164` (`:trace`). `recorder.cljc` and `ui/trace_buffer.cljs` do not yet require `re-frame.core` — add it (27 of Story's 138 source files already do).
- Pair preload `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1422` (`:trace`).
- Testbeds `testbeds/ssr_basic/core.cljs:94`, `testbeds/ssr_hydration_mismatch/core.cljs:81` (`:trace`).
- NOT migrated (framework-internal, stay on the home verb): `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:404`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:1221`, `frame.cljc:2810,3909` (late-bind hook).
- Do NOT delete or demote `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` here — `@trace-epoch.1` owns that door and its manifest rows; if that bead lands first and has already moved `install.cljs:67`, skip it.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` HOT-ZONE (one paragraph). Attach table `:598-603` already names the facade — unchanged.
- `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:606-614` names `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` for the trace panel → facade spelling; `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:2777` names the retired `re-frame.core/register-epoch-listener!` → `(rf/register-listener! :epoch …)`.
- Xray spec: `git grep -n "register-listener\|register-epoch-listener\|trace.tooling" tools/xray/spec` → 0 at tip; the PR body states "Xray spec unchanged because no page names the verb".
- Manifest: after editing the sidecar, `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen`, then `--check`, `api-md-check`, `story-spec-check`, `xray-spec-check`, `skills-check`, `doc-api-check` (the `lint.yml` `api-manifest` job runs them).
- Tests: existing Xray install / Story invariants / pair preload suites; Story's `with-invariants` must still no-op without the epoch artefact (existing test); testbed builds are gated by `test.yml` `cljs-examples-compile` — `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` names them.
- Examples: 0 listener registrations. Migration README: no v1-era name. Skills: `skills/re-frame2-pair` preload is code, not prose.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

`Tool-Pair.md` is one-toucher — serialise with any `@egress` / `@trace-epoch` bead that edits it. Otherwise independent of observability.1/2/3/5 and of the ruling (the sentence holds under both targets; under Target A the stream list in it shrinks — observability.6's implementation bead edits it again).

## Risks

None to bundles (measured: the require graph is unchanged by the spelling; `npm run test:bundle-isolation` is the proof, and its `trace-tooling` sentinel must still read 0). A reader who learned the old rule from the manifest strings finds the new one in the same rows.

title: surface-review(http): thread the destroying frame into the actor-destroy HTTP abort hook
description:
## Scope

Close the remaining half of rf2-o8ek: make an actor destroy abort only the
destroying FRAME's in-flight managed HTTP. rf2-o8ek landed the registry half
(the actor index is keyed [frame-id actor-id] and `registry/abort-on-actor-
destroy` has a frame-bearing 2-arity); what remains is threading the frame at
the two hook CALL SITES, which live outside the http artefact.

## Why it was not done in rf2-o8ek

rf2-o8ek's worker was fenced to `implementation/http/**` and
`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`. Both callers of the `:http/abort-on-actor-destroy`
late-bind hook are outside that fence and pass an actor address with no frame:

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`
  `abort-actor-in-flight-http!` takes `[actor-id]` and calls `(abort! actor-id)`.
  Its caller in `.../lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc` already has `frame-id` bound as
  its first parameter, one line above the call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (~3983) has the machines-absent
  fallback: `(abort-http machine-id)` inside `destroy-frame!`'s per-snapshot
  walk, where the frame `id` is likewise in scope.

## What to do

Give `abort-actor-in-flight-http!` the destroying frame and pass it through to
the hook, and do the same at core's fallback site. `registry/abort-on-actor-
destroy` already accepts `[frame-id actor-id]`; its `[actor-id]` arity is the
documented ANY-FRAME sweep retained precisely so this change could be made
separately without a flag day, and it can be left in place or retired with the
last caller.

## Exposure

A spawned actor's address is frame-LOCAL, so two isolated frames running the
same application code spawn actors under the same address. Until the callers
thread a frame, destroying one frame's actor still sweeps the same address in
every frame. Measured on tip before rf2-o8ek and re-measured after it, via the
registry probe in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_frame_scoped_
cancellation_test.clj`:
`actor-destroy-any-frame-arity-preserves-the-hook-contract` pins the current
behaviour, and `actor-destroy-is-frame-scoped-when-the-frame-is-known` pins the
behaviour this bead should make reachable from the destroy cascade.

Exposure is narrower than the request-id half rf2-o8ek fixed: it needs spawned
state-machine actors issuing managed HTTP in two frames under one address,
whereas the request-id half was reachable from any direct `:rf.http/managed`
caller.

## Acceptance

- The destroy cascade (parent state exit, parent `:after`, `:spawn-all` join,
  frame destroy, imperative destroy) aborts only the destroying frame's
  actor-owned HTTP; a same-named actor in a sibling frame stays live.
- Core's machines-absent fallback in `destroy-frame!` does the same.
- Spec 014 §Abort on actor destroy §Frame scope loses its closing sentence
  about the hook currently taking the any-frame form.
- Existing actor-destroy tests stay green on JVM and CLJS.

## Fence note

This one touches `implementation/machines/` and `implementation/core/`, so it
must not be dispatched concurrently with other work in those artefacts.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9212 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9212). Premise HELD and was reproduced.

CENSUS — the bead named TWO call sites; five axes found FOUR, all with the destroying frame already in scope, all threaded:
  1. machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc      — spawn-destroy pipeline (parent state exit, parent :after, :spawn-all join, imperative destroy)
  2. machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc     — final-state auto-destroy tail   [NOT named by the bead]
  3. machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc — singleton-straggler pass       [NOT named by the bead]
  4. core/frame.cljc                          — machines-absent destroy-frame! fallback

Axes: effect keyword; helper symbol; multiline/ws-collapsed; frame-less registry arities; PROSE. The prose axis was the one that paid — it found two sites naming no symbol (registry.cljc's ANY-FRAME seams block and abort-on-actor-destroy's docstring), both asserting the cascade passes an address alone. No call site lacked a frame, so nothing was frameless-by-design. The bead's 'one line per call site' prediction held.

SHAPE — followed rf2-o8ek's worker: no dev warning (nag-diagnostic, and mechanically impossible for a registry fn with no ambient ctx). finalize/abort-actor-in-flight-http! — the funnel the three machines sites share — now REQUIRES the frame rather than defaulting it, because its hook call is wrapped in a catch-all so a frame-less call fails SILENTLY.

The resources seam :http/abort-in-flight! — correct as-is, its token is frame-qualified. rf2-s4dp (xray testbed, peer surface) — untouched.

WITNESS — 3 deftests in implementation/http driving the REAL destroy entry points against the REAL registry with one address live in two frames.
