title: bug(skill-setup): custom-name manual scaffolds bypass the generator's identity derivation
description:
## Problem

`re-frame2-setup` treats an author-supplied project name as a first-class zero-friction override, but its default manual route never defines how that name becomes the several identities a CLJS project needs. It says only to rename `acme` / `my-app` consistently. The generator route uses a real derivation instead: Clojure namespace, filesystem path, npm package name, output directory, `:init-fn`, headings, and requires are related but not identical strings. Therefore the two routes advertised as producing the same files are deterministic only for the fixed reference name.

A common qualified name exposes the gap. For `com.acme/my-cool-app`, the generator emits namespace `com.acme.my-cool-app`, source path `src/com/acme/my_cool_app`, and npm name `my-cool-app`. A manual textual rename can naturally produce `src/com.acme/my_cool_app`, which does not back the namespace named by `shadow-cljs.edn` and fails namespace resolution. Bare and mixed-case names have different hazards: deps-new currently doubles bare `my-app` into the almost-certainly-unintended `my-app.my-app`, while npm identity must be lowercased and validated independently.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:42` says an author-supplied project name overrides the default, without restricting its shape.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:55` says manual and generator routes land on the same files.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:67` and `references/first-counter.md:3` give the manual operation only as renaming `acme` / `my-app` consistently across paths and contents.
- `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:119-162` defines separate `->file-path`, `->ns-form`, lowercasing, and npm-name validation; `data-fn` at lines 166-191 derives `:namespace`, `:nested-dirs`, and `:npm-name` separately.
- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:294-320` proves the nontrivial mapping `com.acme/my-cool-app` -> `com.acme.my-cool-app`, `src/com/acme/my_cool_app`, and `my-cool-app`. Lines 332-360 separately cover qualified, dotted, bare, mixed-case, and invalid npm names.
- `tools/template/spec/API.md:160` explicitly records that a bare name is accepted by deps-new but becomes doubled (`my-app.my-app`) and recommends a group-qualified name. The setup skill exposes a natural-language "project name" override without carrying that rule or choosing a different normalization.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/first_counter_derivation.clj:78-82` renders only the fixed `{:name "acme/my-app" :top "acme" :main "my-app"}` identity. The setup drift suite and `evals/evals.json` grade the reference default, empty-project merge, and generator route, but no custom-name manual result.
- History confirms the split: `18b9486664` added deterministic npm/name derivation to the generator, while `98aa4b1f5f` made the setup leaf a derivation of the one reference identity and described all custom identities only as a rename.

## Programmer and AI impact

Naming the app is one of the most ordinary scaffold requests. A programmer or AI can follow every stated setup instruction, write all twelve files, and reach the terminating compile only to discover a missing namespace or invalid npm name. Repair then requires reverse-engineering the generator's rules after the skill promised one prompt and one served SPA. Even when a capable agent guesses the CLJS path mapping correctly, route parity is accidental and untested, so model or wording changes can silently reintroduce the failure.

## Posture fit

This is not a request for a naming system. A single small identity rule removes guesswork from a high-frequency override, keeps the API ergonomic, and lets humans and agents start the SPA successfully on the first pass.

## Duplicate research

Targeted searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` for setup/custom names, dotted groups, name derivation, npm names, and manual-route naming found no issue owning this residual. Closed `rf2-zq34m` fixed generator output and npm-name validity, not the setup skill's manual override. Closed `rf2-rc0yh` established the fixed `acme/my-app` default. `rf2-h4q82` and `rf2-pygpw` concern generator location and post-emission coordinates; `rf2-0ddz3` concerns merging into a shadow-only project. Open `rf2-eiev` covers optimized release proof and `rf2-1c60` distribution metadata. None defines manual custom-name parity.

## Uncertainty

This read-only review did not execute a generated project. The concrete bad path is a permitted result of the current underspecified instruction, not a claim that every capable model will choose it. The objective defect is that the promised deterministic override has no specified derivation and no parity test, despite the adjacent generator already proving the distinctions matter.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The manual route documents or executes one unambiguous mapping from a supplied project identity to every emitted identity-bearing field; it no longer says only to rename tokens consistently.
2. `com.acme/my-cool-app` produces the same observable identity on both routes: namespace `com.acme.my-cool-app`, files under `src/com/acme/my_cool_app` and `test/com/acme/my_cool_app`, npm name/output directory `my-cool-app`, matching `:init-fn` and internal requires, and consistent human-facing labels.
3. Bare and mixed-case inputs have an explicit shared policy. An invalid npm artifact is rejected before any manual-route file is written just as the generator fails before emission; no partial scaffold remains.
4. A focused setup eval grades an explicitly named manual scaffold, including source path, namespace, package name, and successful compile/handoff rather than merely checking that the name appears in prose.
5. A deterministic test compares manual identity derivation with the template hook for the dotted, bare, mixed-case, and invalid cases. At least one non-reference qualified identity reaches the existing compile proof, or an equivalently strong namespace-to-path resolver test demonstrates that the emitted `:init-fn` can be found.
6. The zero-interview `acme/my-app` default and explicit UIx override remain unchanged, and the fix adds no new scaffold files, dependencies, selector, or user questionnaire.
design:
## Bounded fix

- Define one canonical project-identity normalization for both setup routes. At minimum, specify how a supplied coordinate yields the group/artifact, namespace, source/test directories, npm name, output directory, `:init-fn`, internal requires, README/title, and heading.
- Reuse the generator hook's current semantics as the oracle, or deliberately improve a questionable case in both places together. Do not leave manual and generator behavior different. In particular, make the bare-name policy explicit: either reject it before writing, normalize it intentionally, or document and reproduce the doubled deps-new identity; never let the routes improvise different answers.
- Put the compact rule in the normal setup path, close to the custom-name override. Keep `first-counter.md` as the one reference scaffold rather than copying twelve custom variants.
- Add a focused custom-name outcome eval and a small derivation/parity test driven by the template hook. Cover one dotted qualified name plus bare, mixed-case, and invalid-artifact boundaries. Extend the existing emitted compile fixture for one non-reference identity only if static parity cannot prove namespace/path coherence.

## Non-goals

- No naming DSL, wizard, profile system, compatibility aliases, or clarification round for the existing unqualified default.
- No change to the counter, substrate choice, dependency pins, twelve-file manifest, build/watch workflow, or publication-coordinate handling.
- No matrix of arbitrary Unicode/package-manager policy and no attempt to replace deps-new.
- No duplicated hand-maintained scaffold per project name.
close_reason: PR #9239. SKILL.md now carries one `## Project identity` rule, stated for both routes and taken from the generator template's own semantics (hooks.clj ->ns-form / ->file-path / ->npm-name): normalise to group/artefact (an unqualified name is doubled, as deps-new doubles it); namespace root = the whole coordinate with / -> . and _ -> -; source/test path = the whole coordinate with . -> / and - -> _; npm name = artefact segment lowercased, project dir = that segment verbatim; <h1>/<title>/README heading = the coordinate verbatim. An npm-invalid artefact is refused BEFORE the first file is written, matching the hook, which throws before emission. The manual route was NOT folded into the generator, deliberately: it is the default route, needs nothing beyond the skill's allowed-tools grants, and cardinal rule 4 already falls back to it when the globally-installed -Tnew tool is absent. What is single-sourced is the DERIVATION: tests/project_identity_test.clj load-files the template's real hooks.clj and compares data-fn against the rule as SKILL.md words it, over the reference / dotted-qualified / bare / mixed-case inputs plus the npm-invalid rejection. CI-wired via test.yml's skills-structural job (it loops skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/*_test.clj), so no workflow change. Behavioural witness: 15 failures / exit 1 before the doc fix, 0 failures / exit 0 after, and 6 failures / exit 1 when the documented derivation is planted to diverge from the hook. AC deviations, both stated in the PR: AC2's 'same observable identity on both routes' is proven by static parity against the hook rather than by emitting a second scaffold, because design.md L13 locks first-counter.md as the ONE reference scaffold rendered for acme/my-app (the item's own design section agrees: 'keep first-counter.md as the one reference scaffold'). AC3's bare-name policy is 'document and reproduce the doubled deps-new identity' - the third option the item's design permits - because the fence excludes tools/**, so improving the generator's semantics in both places together was not available; parity was the binding constraint. AC4's eval (id 18, custom-qualified-name-manual-scaffold) is gated STRUCTURALLY, not executed: there is no eval executor in this repo. Also recorded as design.md L14.

title: bug(pair-mcp): get-path turns operating-frame ambiguity into false missing-path answers
description:
## Finding

`get-path` does not honor Pair's normative operating-frame refusal. With no explicit `frame`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:170-175` emits `(re-frame2-pair.runtime/snapshot)` and separately uses `(current-frame)` only as an elision option. Runtime `snapshot` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:394-399`) calls `(rf/app-db-value (current-frame))` directly. In a genuine multi-app session with no pin, `current-frame` returns nil (`runtime.cljs:303-318`), and `rf/app-db-value nil` returns nil for the unregistered frame (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1918-1925`). The singular form then runs `get-in` against nil and constructs `{:ok? false :reason :path-not-found ...}` (`get_path.cljs:55-95`); the batch form constructs a successful map in which every requested path is `{:exists? false :value nil}` (`get_path.cljs:97-126`). The tool is answering a different question than the caller asked.

This contradicts the authoritative Tool-Pair contract: every frame-targeted call must resolve explicit override -> session pin -> sole app frame -> nil (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:477-490`), and a tier-4 read must refuse with `:ambiguous-frame`, never read another/default frame (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:506-516`). The Pair-MCP descriptor says `frame` defaults to the operating frame (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1044-1045`). The preload itself explains that callers must turn nil into a clear refusal (`runtime.cljs:311-315`), and sibling reads already do so: `sub-cache-info` calls `ambiguous-frame-error` at `runtime.cljs:1024-1028`; `read-sub!` does the same at `runtime.cljs:1118-1119`.

History makes the omission legible: the generated `snapshot` call in get-path dates to 2026-05-31 (`git blame` commit `410f2202a43`), while the reserved-aware operating-frame policy arrived 2026-06-02 (`28cc8c959b`) and subsequently tightened; that policy commit did not touch `get_path.cljs`. Current conformance fixtures cover happy/missing-arg/path-miss by stubbing the eval result (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/conformance_test.cljs:1195-1232`), so they never execute the emitted browser form under a multi-frame runtime.

## Impact

In the exact situation where frame identity matters most, an agent/programmer receives false evidence about application state. A singular query sends them down a pointless path-discovery chase; a batch query can falsely assert that several values are absent. The recovery that already exists (`available-frames` plus the `set-operating-frame`/explicit-frame hint) is withheld. This is a correctness break and avoidable pairing friction, not a request for more machinery.

## Bounded fix

Make both singular and batch get-path forms resolve the target frame once before reading app-db. If resolution is nil, return the existing runtime `ambiguous-frame-error` envelope for `:get-path` without doing path lookup/elision; otherwise read and elide against that resolved id. Route the refusal through the existing `run-eval` `:ok? false` -> `wire/err-text` path. Add one focused emitted-form/live-runtime-level regression for each shape (singular and batch), plus positive guards for an explicit frame and the sole/pinned-frame path.

## Non-goals

Do not redesign the four-tier resolver, invent a new error vocabulary/helper layer, change `snapshot`'s broad multi-frame mega-op semantics, or add policy/gates. Reuse `ambiguous-frame-error`, existing result envelopes, and operating-frame tools.

## Duplicate search

Used `rg` over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for `get-path.*ambiguous|ambiguous.*get-path`, `path-not-found.*frame|frame.*path-not-found`, `get-path.*current-frame`, `get-path.*multi-frame`, and `snapshot.*ambiguous-frame`: zero direct matches. Broader `rg 'get-path|ambiguous-frame|operating frame'` produced only closed, tangential skill/spec issues (notably `rf2-3cjhl` about retro prose); no bead owns this behavior.

## Posture fit

This is a small correction at an existing resolution boundary: no new abstraction, option, policy, or compatibility layer. It makes the minimal ergonomic API tell the truth and immediately presents the programmer/agent with the recovery tools that already ship. That is high-leverage pre-alpha polish without gold-plating.

## Uncertainty

Static proof is high-confidence and closes through source composition. No browser/runtime was launched during review because the review brief forbade runtime mutations. The best regression may sit in the Pair preload runtime tests rather than the current canned conformance corpus; acceptance requires executing the emitted form/real branch, not a particular test file.

Reviewed at `afe446ea71bf7d0eb2e4ce5960caca864a091778` on 2026-09-04.
acceptance_criteria:
- With two app frames, no session pin, and no `frame` arg, singular `get-path` returns MCP `isError: true` with `{:ok? false :reason :ambiguous-frame :operation :get-path :available-frames [...] :hint ...}`; it does not emit `:path-not-found`.
- The same setup with `paths` returns the same refusal; it does not emit an `:ok? true` all-missing results map.
- An explicit `frame`, a valid session pin, and a sole-app-frame session continue to return the existing hit/miss shapes and use the resolved frame for elision.
- A regression test executes/asserts the emitted form's multi-frame branch rather than supplying a canned `:ambiguous-frame` response.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9248 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9248).

Both get-path forms now resolve the operating frame ONCE, browser-side, before any app-db read, and branch to the runtime's existing ambiguous-frame-error when resolution yields nil. The refusal rides the existing run-eval :ok? false -> wire/err-text path out as an isError envelope carrying :reason :ambiguous-frame, :operation :get-path, :available-frames and the recovery hint. Detection sits where the ambiguity arises, not where the verdict is printed.

The walker now receives the same resolved id (frame-edn was a SECOND, independent (current-frame) call that could disagree with the read), and the batch rebuild gained the singular arm's ok? guard so a refusal is not dressed with :results nil.

Acceptance, all four met:
1. Two app frames, no pin, no frame arg, singular -> isError with :ok? false :reason :ambiguous-frame :operation :get-path :available-frames :hint; no :path-not-found, and no :deepest-valid-prefix breadcrumbs.
2. Same setup with paths -> the same refusal; no :ok? true all-missing results map, and no :results key at all.
3. Explicit frame, session pin and sole-app-frame sessions keep their existing hit/miss shapes and elide against the resolved frame — pinned as controls, along with a genuine :path-not-found and a real per-path batch miss inside a resolved frame.
4. The regression executes the emitted form's multi-frame branch: test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/get_path_frame_test.cljs drives get-path-tool against a simulator that DERIVES its answer from the emitted form (resolving the frame the way pure/resolve-operating-frame does) rather than supplying a canned :ambiguous-frame response — which would have passed on the defect, since the relay was never the bug.

Witness measured both ways: pre-fix production with the same tests, 4115 assertions, 22 failures, exit 1; with the fix, 4116 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors, exit 0. Gate is npm --prefix tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp test, re-run green on the final rebased base.

Spec unchanged because it already required this: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md names get-path in 'Every frame-targeted op ... REFUSES with {:ok? false :reason :ambiguous-frame} rather than guess', and repeats it in the get-path section. This was a code/spec conformance gap, not a spec gap.

One correction to the bead's analysis: it located the fix at 'the existing runtime ambiguous-frame-error envelope for :get-path', but the runtime has no get-path fn — get-path composes its own eval form in the MCP server. The refusal is therefore emitted INTO the form (calling the runtime helper) rather than added at a runtime call site, which kept the change wholly inside tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/** and touched no skills/ file. Everything else in the bead reproduced exactly, including the cited line ranges.

Sibling census (controlled against five runtime fns known to refuse): two siblings share the shape — trace-window and watch-epochs emit implicit (epoch-history) / (epochs-since ...), and state/history-for returns [] for an unknown frame, so an ambiguous session reports :count 0, with watch-epochs additionally claiming :id-aged-out? true. Filed as rf2-yo4s (discovered-from this bead) rather than fixed here: this bead scopes to get-path, its non-goals forbid widening, and both siblings are cursor-paged with sticky frame state needing separate care. Not defects: precheck, replace-app-db, restore-epoch, probe/health, snapshot.

title: ssr-node: render exceptions can leak application data and spoof refusal status
description:
## Evidence

- The package states the response law repeatedly: README.md:275 and :668 say Node returns body markup and nothing else; test/egress.test.cjs:31-37 tightens that to “nothing the render module authored” outside chunk HTML and says a refusal must not carry the payload through the error channel.
- The success/return-value door enforces that law, but the exception door does not. In src/worker.cjs:221-225 the render catch copies application-authored error.code, error.message, and error.detail into the worker error message. src/isolate.cjs:200-208 preserves the code/message and spreads detail into the public Refusal. src/http.cjs:67-76 serializes that Refusal to JSON and statusFor maps the copied code to HTTP status.
- A read-only worker probe loaded an in-memory render module whose render threw an Error built from allowlisted request state. The module set message to "message:state-secret-7b2", detail to {echo:"state-secret-7b2"}, and no custom code. The actual worker output was:
  {"t":"error","id":7,"code":":rf.ssr-node/render-threw","message":"message:state-secret-7b2","detail":{"echo":"state-secret-7b2"},"afterChunks":0}
  This proves the state sentinel crosses both live fields; it is not inferred from source alone.
- The repository's own throws fixture provides the HTTP half without a synthetic file: POSTing app/before returned HTTP 500 with JSON message "fell over immediately", the exact string authored at test/fixtures/throws.cjs:20.
- error.code is the same untrusted path. A render module can set it to a known protocol member such as :rf.ssr-node/unknown-entry, service-saturated, or render-timeout; statusFor will then present an application render bug as HTTP 400, 503, or 504 instead of the documented render-threw 500. It can also emit an arbitrary refusal-code string.
- The green egress row at test/egress.test.cjs:311-323 exercises only a module that returns a payload. It does not throw an Error carrying code/message/detail, so the package gate remains green (108 rows, 9 suites) while the second channel is live.
- History localizes the gap: git log -S "err.detail" attributes the pass-through to the initial service commit b2b35bf6e9. The later response-egress hardening (67d4d9338a, b34fe600fa) closed returned values but did not touch this catch.

## Impact

A routine renderer exception can put server-only render state, environment-derived data, or other application values into the in-process Refusal and the sidecar's HTTP JSON response. The JVM consumer then retains the sidecar message/detail on its internal ssr-node-refused error. Independently, application code can spoof the closed refusal taxonomy and its caller-fault/deadline/saturation status, sending operators and retry policy down the wrong path. This is a correctness and boundary failure, not a request from hostile code: error messages that interpolate the value being processed are ordinary.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a valid module with an app/root entry and an allowlisted :secret state key.
2. In render, construct an Error whose code, message, and nested detail are derived from state[":secret"], then throw it before emit.
3. Call Service.renderFrames or POST /render.
4. Observe the module's message/detail in the Refusal/JSON. If code is set to a known non-render member, observe the corresponding non-500 HTTP status.

The read-only probe above establishes steps 1-3 at the worker boundary, and the checked-in throws fixture establishes the message-to-HTTP leg.

## Recommended bounded repair

Close the exception path at src/worker.cjs, the first boundary that can enforce it. A caught render-module exception should always cross as CODE.RENDER_THREW with service-owned wording and a small service-owned detail shape (for example entry plus the existing afterChunks fact); do not copy error.code, error.message, error.detail, or other module properties. Preserve the existing pre-chunk refusal versus post-chunk torn-response behavior. If retaining full diagnostics locally is required, keep that as a sidecar-local logging decision rather than putting application-authored values on the response protocol.

Add the focused adversarial case to test/egress.test.cjs with a fixture that demonstrably throws distinct sentinels in code, message, and nested detail, and check both the in-process Refusal and HTTP response.

## Posture rationale

This is one missing closure on an existing boundary, not a new subsystem. The ergonomic rule should be simple for SPA authors: throw from a renderer and get one honest render-threw failure; never learn a redaction DSL or remember which Error properties are safe. A fixed service-owned refusal is smaller, safer, and easier for people and AI-generated integration code to reason about than configurable projection.

## Non-goals

- No new refusal code, public option, redaction framework, safe-key registry, or exception wrapper API.
- No change to successful chunk/complete frames, request validation, allowlists, timeout, pool replacement, or JVM/browser error projection.
- No redesign of sidecar logging or observability; local diagnostics may be decided separately.
- Do not broaden this into boot-error handling. Module boot fails before the service listens and has different operator-diagnostic needs.
- Do not terminate a healthy isolate merely because application render code threw; current reuse semantics are separate.

## Related and duplicate search

Searched all 935 tracker records, including closed/deferred, across title, description, notes, and close reason for ssr-node, body markup, egress, render-threw, err.code/err.detail, render exception message/detail, diagnostic-shaped leak, refusal-code spoofing, and application-authored error data. No issue owns this exception pass-through. Closest is closed rf2-6r9j.77, which removed worker stack fields because receivers discarded them; this finding is distinct because code/message/detail are live and serialized. Closed rf2-6r9j.70-.74/.84/.86 and .176-.179 cover boot-test validity, envelope scope, selector/residue cleanup, and naming. The crossing parent rf2-8arzr and success-egress commits establish the law but do not close this path.

## Uncertainties

The repair must choose the exact service-owned message/detail wording and whether the original exception is logged only on sidecar stderr. Those choices do not alter the required boundary: no application-authored exception property may enter a public Refusal or HTTP frame. The JVM host sanitizes what reaches the browser, but that is downstream defense and does not repair the Node service's own public in-process and HTTP contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A controlled render module throws an Error whose code, message, and nested detail each carry distinct sentinels sourced from request state; a direct fixture control proves all sentinels really exist before the service handles it.
2. Service.renderFrames/renderToString rejects that render with exactly :rf.ssr-node/render-threw, service-owned wording, correct afterChunks, and no sentinel anywhere in the public Refusal (code, message, detail, stack serialization).
3. The same request over HTTP returns 500 with x-rf-ssr-refusal :rf.ssr-node/render-threw; its JSON body and headers contain no sentinel. Choosing known 400/503/504 protocol codes in the thrown Error cannot change that outcome.
4. Both pre-emit and post-emit exceptions are covered: pre-emit is a clean refusal; post-emit remains a torn response and streaming HTTP destroys rather than completes the socket.
5. A negative control restoring any code/message/detail pass-through makes the new egress test fail.
6. Existing successful rendering, ordinary throw, return-value egress, timeout, byte-fidelity, and all ssr-node suites remain green.
notes:
## Verdict (worker ssregress-a) — every premise held; fixed in PR #9258

REPRODUCED BEFORE EDITING, both arms, against the tree at tip.
- Data leak: a render module whose Error was built from allowlisted request
  state put the sentinel into BOTH live fields of the in-process Refusal and
  of the HTTP JSON body:
  {"code":":rf.ssr-node/render-threw","message":"message:\"state-secret-7b2\"",
   "detail":{"echo":"\"state-secret-7b2\"","nested":{"deep":"detail:\"state-secret-7b2\""},"afterChunks":0}}
- Status spoof: the same module with err.code = :rf.ssr-node/unknown-entry
  returned HTTP 400 with x-rf-ssr-refusal: :rf.ssr-node/unknown-entry, in
  place of the documented render-threw 500.
- The checked-in test/fixtures/throws.cjs supplied the HTTP half with no
  synthetic file: POST app/before -> 500 carrying "fell over immediately",
  the exact string authored at throws.cjs:20.
- Baseline gate before any edit: 108 rows / 9 suites, exit 0 — the figures
  in the description, confirmed rather than assumed.

THE REPAIR (implementation/ssr-node/** only, 7 files).
1. src/worker.cjs render catch: one code (CODE.RENDER_THREW), the contract's
   own wording (RENDER_THREW_REFUSAL, new in protocol.cjs beside
   MODULE_RETURN_REFUSAL), and a service-built detail of {entry, afterChunks}.
   No application-authored property crosses. Pre-chunk refusal vs post-chunk
   torn-response behaviour is preserved, as is isolate reuse.
2. The same file's last-resort .catch() arm, which posted String(err), is
   service-owned too — a law with one arm stating it differently is a law
   with a way around it.
3. src/isolate.cjs error branch: a SECOND independent reading, matching the
   discipline its own complete branch already states. Any code outside the
   closed family (protocol.cjs isRefusalCode) becomes RENDER_THREW, so
   nothing unpublished can reach http.cjs statusFor. The two readings are
   complementary, not redundant — measured: the worker's fix is what catches
   a spoof of a REAL member, the isolate's check is what catches an INVENTED
   code string.
4. Diagnosis preserved with no new subsystem and no flag: the full exception
   with its stack goes to the sidecar's stderr under the [rf.ssr-node] prefix
   bin/serve.cjs already uses (a worker thread's stderr is piped to the
   parent's). 15 such lines appear in the green gate log, so it is live.

THE CONTROL THAT COULD NOT REACH ITS OWN CASE — replaced, not patched.
egress.test.cjs's "the refusal does not carry the payload out through the
error channel" drove the LEAKY fixture, which RETURNS, so the error channel
it checked was the return door's; a throwing module was never on the table.
Renamed to its real scope, and a new section 4 drives a throwing fixture
(test/fixtures/throws-data.cjs) with a distinct sentinel on code, message and
a NESTED detail, each from a separate allowlisted state key.

Also reconciled: timeout.test.cjs asserted /fell over immediately/ — the
exact authored string — which made it a standing WITNESS that the module's

Gates, captured, re-run on the rebased base after the trunk moved 8 commits: gen --check 0 (548 public vars in sync); story-spec-check 0 (69 var-rows checked, floor 20); clojure -M:test 0 (98 tests / 194 assertions); both ratchets 0; clj-kondo --fail-level error 0. Sabotage controls, since neither gate prints its root: a planted banned word turned the residue ratchet red at exit 1 naming the planted line, and repointing story-ns turned the projection check red at exit 1 with 64 unresolved rows. Both restores verified by git blob hash against the committed object (40c9827add), with plant match counts read before each run.

A GATE-NOMINATION CORRECTION I OWE THE RECORD: I named scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh and scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh in the brief. Neither reaches this path — the worker read both rosters at source and neither artefacts=(...) nor tools=(...) contains implementation/scripts/api-manifest. The gate that does cover it is lint.yml's api-manifest job, whose steps the worker ran directly.

Coverage, honestly: nothing validates the prose of a Clojure docstring. Every green above says only that behaviour is unchanged — which is the claim being made, but it does not grade the new sentences. Each was hand-verified against the code it describes, with the specific code and diff hunks quoted in the PR body.

NOT THIS BEAD'S TO CLOSE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: story_spec_check has no dedicated test namespace where its sibling xray_spec_check_test.clj does. Pre-existing gap; the shared parsing contract is covered by projection_test.clj.

title: Reconcile Machines-Viz design rationale with the shipped architecture
description:
Evidence
- spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md Lock #10 still says implementation has not begun, Xray 003 remains the source of truth, spawn-all visualization will land in a future 001-Rendering.md, and detailed rendering/layout/export specs are future work.
- The same document's Open questions still defers the layout engine, SVG-vs-Canvas-vs-HTML renderer, substrate, test corpus, and dense-edge-label handling. Those decisions are all shipped and documented elsewhere: xyflow + ELK, Reagent plus React/UIx adapters, extensive JVM/CLJS/DOM tests, and events-as-nodes/retired collision overlay.
- One open-question statement says MachineChart is registered via reg-view, contradicting the current host-fed component contract and Principles/API documentation.
- spec/README.md says CLJS and DOM coverage use only consolidated implementation/shadow-cljs.edn builds, omitting the artifact-owned tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn lane that CI and implementation/package.json invoke.
- 000-Vision.md, API.md, and 001-Topology-Parity.md already carry the current decisions, so the stale scaffold is duplicate and contradictory rather than the only historical record.

Impact
DESIGN-RATIONALE is advertised as the record future contributors should use to avoid reopening settled decisions. Its vestigial pre-implementation sections currently do the reverse: they direct readers to a superseded source, invent a nonexistent future spec, and misstate the component architecture and test enrollment.

Recommendation
Rewrite Lock #10 as a completed migration/accountability map, replace resolved Open questions with concise locked outcomes and links to current authority, and correct spec/README.md's lane description. Preserve genuinely open roadmap triggers and explicitly labeled historical/superseded sections in API.md.

Risks and contracts
Do not erase decision history or silently change product scope. Retain Xray's ownership of host-side concerns, page-versus-jar boundaries, accessibility trigger, and candidate-on-demand items. This is a truth-alignment change against shipped code and current normative specs.
acceptance_criteria:
- DESIGN-RATIONALE no longer says implementation is pending or points to a future 001-Rendering.md.
- Resolved architecture questions state the shipped xyflow/ELK, host-fed Reagent/React/UIx, test-corpus, and events-as-nodes outcomes with links to API/Topology-Parity authority.
- No text claims MachineChart is registered through reg-view.
- spec/README.md accurately distinguishes the artifact-owned CLJS node lane from consolidated/browser DOM coverage.
- Genuinely open scope triggers and useful historical rationale remain intact.
- Documentation link/anchor gates pass and referenced headings are verified manually where excluded from site build.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9094 (branch worker/mvizb-a, commit 2f6dbe2264). Premise HELD on every claim. AUTHORITY: the SHIPPED CODE was treated as authoritative and the design doc moved to match, because every disagreement was DESIGN-RATIONALE describing a pre-implementation PLAN the implementation then diverged from, while API.md / 000-Vision.md / 001-Topology-Parity.md already carried the current decisions with bead trails. No third thing was invented; each outcome was read out of a named source. Lock #10 no longer says implementation is pending or that Xray 003 is the read-the-spec source of truth - it is now a completed migration map with a 'Where each topic landed' table naming, for the two rows that pointed at a future 001-Rendering.md, where the content actually went: the :spawn-all row to API.md's :overlays slot descriptor schema (the :spawn-all-join descriptor, rf2-3ow55 / rf2-7w4qr; the 'row of mini-machines' sketch is explicitly NOT what shipped), and the auto-pan row to API.md Auto-fit on async layout settle + Fit-on-entry signal (rf2-6tw7t), with the auto-pan TOGGLE still Xray's. A repo-wide git grep -F census confirms no 001-Rendering.md exists and nothing waits on one; 001-Topology-Parity.md took the 001- slot, and its own roadmap row D1 (whether a narrower rendering-internals doc is ever worth writing) is cited rather than erased. The Open questions section is now 'Questions the implementation settled', with all five answered from source: ELK/elkjs Layered + ORTHOGONAL + edgeCoords ROOT (chart.cljs require and default-elk-options; 001 1.7); @xyflow/react rather than any of SVG/Canvas/HTML alone - HTML div nodes (chart/nodes.cljs), SVG BaseEdge paths and HTML EdgeLabelRenderer labels (chart/edges.cljs); a host-fed Reagent component with ONE reactify bridge plus a thin UIx defui shell, NOT reg-view; three test lanes plus the rendered-topology geometry gate rather than snapshot fixtures; and edge-label collision dissolved by events-as-nodes (rf2-qo5xy), the rf2-r7vsr overlay retired as inert in rf2-0xbgx. The reg-view claim was the sharpest: a fixed-string census found reg-view in exactly ONE place across tools/machines-viz - that sentence - with the control firing on implementation/core/src. spec/README.md now distinguishes three lanes, naming the artefact-owned tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn :machines-viz-node-test build (invoked by implementation/package.json's test:tools-machines-viz and by expensive-tests.yml) alongside the consolidated :node-test / :browser-test builds and the viewer page build. Genuinely open scope, Xray's host-side ownership, the page-versus-jar boundary and labelled-historical sections are intact. GATES: check_doc_slugs.py and check_readme_links.py --ci both exit 0, each PROVED LIVE on this exact diff by a planted broken link that reddened it (exit 1 naming the file and line) before removal. mkdocs build --strict was deliberately NOT nominated and the PR says why: mkdocs_hooks.py's _STAGE table stages only top-level spec/ and migration/, so tools/*/spec is neither staged nor inside docs_dir and a strict build would have inspected none of these files. title: ssr-node boot-once test never observes the boot hook
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/test/isolation.test.cjs:121-133 claims to prove that the module boots once per isolate, but the row only proves that two renders used the same worker thread and each observed overlapMax === 1.
- overlapMax is render-concurrency state (test/fixtures/reference.cjs:24-26,78-94). It has the same value if boot() is never called, called once, or called before every sequential render, so neither asserted outcome discriminates the stated contract.
- The fixture's only boot signal is module.exports.booted: initialized at test/fixtures/reference.cjs:73, written at :75, and never read anywhere in the repository. A whole-repo exact-identifier search finds only those two fixture sites.
- The worker's actual contract is load-bearing: src/worker.cjs invokes the optional module hook during isolate boot, and the Hicasso server bundle has a real hook that initializes its substrate. A regression in that call site would remain green in the dedicated package row.
- The row and inert booted signal date to the initial isolation witness (8ab673ea78); later egress changes did not make the assertion observe boot.

## Impact

The package gate can report that per-isolate boot is protected after the hook is removed, skipped, or moved to per-request execution. That leaves a real application initialization contract without the regression witness named for it.

## Disposition

Replace the inert boolean with a boot-call count (or an equally direct observation) owned by each loaded fixture instance, include it in the emitted observations, and assert that both sequential renders on one isolate observe exactly one boot. Keep the existing same-thread precondition so the row still proves the requests reached one isolate.

## Risks

The reference fixture is also required directly by some in-process controls, so the observation must not let the main process module cache contaminate the worker-thread measurement. Do not weaken the separate overlapMax concurrency rows; they protect a different guarantee.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The normal two-render, one-isolate case reports exactly one boot invocation on both responses.
2. A controlled mutation that removes the worker boot call makes this row fail.
3. A controlled mutation that invokes boot for each render makes this row fail.
4. The dead booted write-only boolean is removed or replaced by the direct measured signal.
5. All 9 ssr-node suites (currently 104 rows) remain green after restoring the controls.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. The premise held exactly: test/isolation.test.cjs's row 'the module boots once per isolate, not once per request' asserted overlapMax === 1 on two sequential responses, and overlapMax is render-concurrency state that reads 1 whether the boot hook is called never, once, or before every render. The fixture's booted boolean was written at reference.cjs:75 and read nowhere — a scoped census over implementation/ssr-node found it only at :73 and :75 as an identifier (the two other hits are prose), line-oriented and whitespace-flattened agreeing, with a control needle that fired.

REPAIR: the fixture counts boots on the isolate's own globalThis (Symbol.for key) rather than in module scope, and publishes the count in its observations. Module scope was rejected deliberately: a counter a re-require resets would report 1 for a per-request require-and-boot too, which is one of the two failures the row exists to catch. Each worker thread has its own global, so the count cannot see another isolate's boots nor the main process's copy of the fixture, which addresses the bead's stated contamination risk (the in-process controls require reference.cjs directly). AC4: the dead boolean is removed.

AC1/AC2/AC3 PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, both directions, each plant anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1) and each restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff. AC1: normal case reports boots === 1 on both responses, captured exit 0. AC2: deleting 'if (typeof mod.boot === function) mod.boot();' from src/worker.cjs gives 'AssertionError: the isolate must have booted the module exactly once', actual 0 expected 1, captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. AC3: calling mod.boot() before every render gives the same row '2 !== 1', captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. Each plant failed exactly ONE row — the repaired one — so neither broke the file out from under its neighbours. Both restores hashed to e0eab3d1f6a674613277bc8ffbb1b782dd1d4086.

AC5: all 9 ssr-node suites green after restore — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0, on the final rebased base. Baseline before any edit was 104/104; the +3 are the two envelope rows and the bytes row from siblings .71 and .72. isolation.test.cjs stays at 7 rows: this was repaired in place, not added to. overlapMax remains asserted in concurrency.test.cjs where it is the subject, per the bead's risk note.

title: hic: workspace.md hardcodes :dev-http 8080 for BOTH pilots — a parallel second pilot boot-checks the FIRST pilot's app and passes
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, operator half, re-run after PR #9050 and #9049. Workspace pin cfcc30ae93. Measured, not reasoned.

SYMPTOM. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md gives BOTH pilots the identical shadow-cljs.edn line ':dev-http {8080 "public"}' and step 5 says 'npx shadow-cljs watch app  # then open http://localhost:8080'. rf2-hic-063's ruling explicitly permits the two pilots to run IN PARALLEL ('separate workspaces, no shared branch'). Those two facts are incompatible, and the failure mode is silent.

MEASURED. Both pilot watches started ~20s apart from their own assembled workspaces:
  - workspace A (realworld) binds 8080 and serves conduit.
  - workspace B (linearlite) prints, as a WARNING and not an error, ':shadow.cljs.devtools.server.dev-http/http-start-ex ... BindException Address already in use: bind' — then continues and prints '[:app] Build completed. (277 files, 0 compiled, 0 warnings, 9.82s)'.
  - With both live, the operator boot check against http://localhost:8080 returns #app innerHTML length 2350, 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, and renders 'conduit / Home / Sign in / Sign up'.

That is pilot A's application, returned to pilot B, with a clean bill of health. LinearLite's own boot reading in isolation is 3535; the collided reading is 2350, i.e. entirely the other app.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT FAILS OPEN. The BindException is a WARNING sitting ABOVE the 'Build completed' line, so the last thing on screen is success. A blinded pilot executing step 5 literally gets a compile that says it worked, a page that renders, and a boot check that passes — while reading the other pilot's app. Nothing in the log the pilot is looking at contradicts it. The blinding is intact but the INSTRUMENT is cross-wired, and every outcome-1..6 observation the second pilot records would be about the wrong application.

SCOPE. This bites only when the two pilots run concurrently on one machine, which is precisely what the ruling authorises. It did not bite the first rehearsal or this one, because both ran the pilots sequentially.

REMEDY IS THE OPERATOR'S CALL, NOT FILED AS RULED. Options, cheapest first: (a) give pilot 2 a different :dev-http port in workspace.md's 'Pilot 2 uses :init-fn linearlite.core/run' sentence, which already exists as the place where pilot 2's shadow-cljs.edn is said to differ, and update step 5's URL alongside it; (b) say in step 5 that the two pilots must not run concurrently on one host, which contradicts the ruling and is worse; (c) have step 5 tell the operator to read the ':dev-http' line shadow actually prints rather than assuming 8080. (a) is the smallest change and keeps the parallel run the ruling wants.

DO NOT hand this to a blinded pilot to work out — per workspace.md's own reasoning for the outcome-7 variant, a rehearsal's differences are applied by the operator so the pilot meets one instruction rather than a choice between two.

NOT A BLOCKER for a SEQUENTIAL dispatch of rf2-t4jpz. Both pilots pass their boot check and baseline when run one at a time; see the rehearsal report on rf2-t4jpz.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058. Pilot 2 now carries :dev-http {8081 "public"} on workspace.md's existing 'Pilot 2 uses :init-fn linearlite.core/run' sentence -- the bead's own option (a), the place already designated for pilot 2's shadow-cljs.edn delta -- and step 5's command comment reads '# then open http://localhost:8080 - pilot 2 uses 8081'. Those are ALL the sites: a search of the whole package found exactly two occurrences of the port (workspace.md:114 and :190) and no other place printing a URL; neither brief mentions a port, a URL or 'shadow-cljs watch' at all. 8081 collides with nothing in-repo -- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn claims 8020-8061 and 8765, and 8080/8081 sit outside that range. ON THE 'IS A SCROLLED-PAST WARNING ACCEPTABLE' QUESTION, decided with a reason and WITHOUT machinery: no, so step 5 gains one clause asking the operator to confirm the page is THIS pilot's application (pilot 1 renders conduit's masthead, pilot 2 the LinearLite board) rather than merely counting errors. Shadow classifies BindException as a warning and nothing in this package can change that, so the collision cannot be made loud in shadow's log; it CAN be made loud in the operator check that already exists -- which is precisely the instrument that passed on the wrong app in the rehearsal. Distinct ports also change the residual failure's shape: a wrong port now yields nothing or an obviously different app rather than a plausible one. NOT RE-MEASURED WITH TWO WATCHES -- that needs two clones, two npm installs and two cold compiles on a host carrying ~20 worker worktrees. What was measured cheaply: both 8080 and 8081 bind free on this host, and a second bind of a held port raises the OSError shadow reports as a warning. The warn-and-continue behaviour is this bead's measurement, cited, not re-run.

title: bug(story-mcp): missing adapter yields a false passing run
description:
## Scope

Make Story-MCP's headless `run-variant` / `preview-variant` path fail clearly when the consumer JVM has not installed a re-frame adapter, and teach the existing consumer-project launch recipe to install the renderer-free `plain-atom` adapter when variants are meant to run. Keep the fix on the existing lifecycle and README surfaces; add no server flag, bridge, default-adapter registry, or new tool.

## Correctness finding

PR #8866 made the project-stories conformance witness non-vacuous and discovered the prerequisite needed to make that witness execute: without `(rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)`, the headless server's setup dispatch reaches no adapter, the script produces no assertion, yet `run-variant` returns the ordinary `:status :pass` envelope over `{}` and `[]`. The PR correctly installs `plain-atom` in its fixture, but the published `tools/story-mcp/README.md` golden-path alias only requires the project's story namespace and lists JVM-loadability/stdout as the two namespace rules. A real consumer following it can therefore receive a success-shaped non-run.

The no-adapter state is directly detectable through the existing `rf/current-adapter-spec` surface, and core already names it `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed`. ## Non-goals

No automatic substrate choice, browser bridge, adapter registry, blanket assertion requirement, new MCP option/tool, or redesign of Story's vacuous-pass rule.

title: bug(skills): issue-body recipe never materializes its temp path
description:
## Scope

Correct the executable temp-file handoff in `skills/shared/issue-filing.md` and every surviving consumer-local copy of that recipe, currently `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md` and the `re-frame-migration` path that inherits the shared leaf. Keep the existing `Write` + `gh issue create --body-file` injection boundary; this bug is only about producing one concrete path that both tools can address.

## Correctness finding

The recipe tells the agent to create the body with the non-shell `Write` tool, but gives the path only as shell expressions:

- POSIX: `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/re-frame2-issue-$$-$RANDOM.md`
- Windows: `$env:TEMP\re-frame2-issue-$([guid]::NewGuid()).md`

`Write` receives a literal `file_path`; it does not run Bash parameter expansion, PowerShell environment expansion, process-id expansion, `$RANDOM`, or `NewGuid`. The later permitted shell call is `gh issue create ... --body-file ...`; if it receives the displayed expression, it expands in a different shell context (and each random/GUID evaluation produces a new name), so it cannot name the file `Write` created. On Windows the recipe additionally presents a PowerShell expression inside a workflow whose shell permission is declared as `Bash(gh issue *)` / `Bash(gh issue create *)`.

The text says to carry "that exact path", but never supplies an allowed step that materializes the expression once, captures the result, and passes the resulting concrete string to both tools. A recipe advertised as the safe runnable path can therefore fail before `gh` reads the approved body.

## Evidence

- `skills/shared/issue-filing.md:37-49` mandates `Write`, shows the two shell-expression path shapes, then requires the exact path in `--body-file`.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md:55-68` carries the same local recipe and expressions.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:35-40,71` grants only the named `gh issue` shell commands plus `Write` and loads the shared recipe; it grants no general shell command with which to evaluate and persist a temp-path assignment before `Write`.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:15-22,53` similarly grants `Bash(gh issue *)` plus `Write` and routes filing through the local recipe.
- `skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj:464-503` checks only that prose contains `per-filing` and an OS-temp token (`TMPDIR` or `$env:TEMP`). It does not exercise literal `Write.file_path` → `gh --body-file` identity, so the non-runnable examples pass green.
- `skills/README.md:287-304` repeats the expression-shaped guidance as the published allowed-tools baseline.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start from a clean temp root and follow the Windows recipe with only the tools the consumer grants.
2. Pass `$env:TEMP\re-frame2-issue-$([guid]::NewGuid()).md` as the `Write` tool's `file_path`. Because `Write` is not PowerShell, the value is not converted into one concrete temp path; a strict Write implementation rejects it as non-absolute, while a permissive one treats the metacharacters literally.
3. Run the documented `gh issue create --body-file` step. The shell interprets the expression independently (or, under Bash, does not interpret the PowerShell expression as intended), so `gh` looks for a different/nonexistent pathname and fails instead of filing the approved body.
4. The POSIX shape has the same identity failure if the textual `$$-$RANDOM` expression is evaluated independently: a later expansion does not reproduce the name chosen earlier.
5. As a control, choose a nonce in the agent, construct one concrete OS-temp pathname before `Write`, and pass that exact concrete string byte-for-byte to both `Write.file_path` and `--body-file`; the body is found and its bytes reach the `gh` stub unchanged.

## Failure scenario / invariant

After the user approves an issue, the filing workflow must create exactly one body file and make `gh --body-file` read that same file. Path identity is part of the security mechanism: `Write.file_path == gh.body-file` as concrete strings, not two recipes that might expand to paths.

Today a migration or porting session on Windows can reach an approved upstream finding, safely redact and compose its body, then fail with a missing body file. If a permissive Write implementation accepts the literal expression relative to the repo, it can also leave the approved issue body in the project rather than the OS temp directory. Retrying by improvising a shell here-doc or inline `--body` reopens the injection boundary the shared recipe exists to close.

## Recommended minimal fix

State and demonstrate a tool-neutral two-step value flow: the agent first chooses a nonce itself and resolves a concrete writable OS-temp directory available in the host context, then constructs one concrete absolute path string; it passes that stored string unchanged to `Write.file_path` and later to `gh --body-file`. Examples must show concrete placeholders substituted before either tool call, not executable `$RANDOM` / `NewGuid` syntax.

Carry the correction into the implementor's local copy and whichever migration-local filing sentence survives `rf2-fqjys`. Replace the current token-presence assertion with a focused path-identity smoke test or behavioral eval. Do not add a temp-file library, helper script, generic shell grant, or new abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical/surviving filing instructions explicitly distinguish a path template from the concrete path value. They require one concrete per-filing pathname to be selected before `Write`, stored conceptually once, and reused byte-for-byte in `gh --body-file`; no step asks `Write` to evaluate shell syntax.
2. POSIX and Windows examples are executable using only each skill's declared tools. The `Write.file_path` shown to the agent is an already-substituted concrete OS-temp path, and the `gh` call uses that same value; the examples do not re-evaluate `$$`, `$RANDOM`, `$env:TEMP`, `NewGuid`, command substitution, or another nonce source at the second step.
3. A focused executable smoke test/eval uses a fake `Write` with literal-path semantics and a fake `gh` that records/opens `--body-file`. For both POSIX and Windows path forms, a body containing `$()`, a backtick, a backslash, quotes, and a newline reaches the fake `gh` byte-for-byte, and the captured `Write.file_path` equals the captured `--body-file` argument exactly.
4. Non-vacuity/control: the same test is run with the current expression passed literally to `Write`, or with the nonce regenerated for the `gh` call, and it fails on path inequality/file-not-found. Removing the concrete-path reuse from the fixed recipe must make the gate red.
5. `skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj` (while it exists) and any successor consumer check no longer declare mere presence of `TMPDIR` / `$env:TEMP` sufficient proof of a runnable filing path. The test follows whichever owner remains after `rf2-fqjys`; it does not preserve the shared layer solely for this fix.
6. Existing boundaries remain intact: reviewed body text is written with `Write`, never interpolated into shell argv; `gh issue create --body-file` remains the only filing command; title/search arguments remain agent-authored; filing still requires the consumer's existing conversational approval rule.

## Non-goals

- No change to issue body shape, target repository, labels, duplicate-search policy, redaction categories, or approval semantics.
- No general-purpose temp-file manager, cleanup daemon, random-number API, shell wrapper, expanded `Bash(*)` permission, or compatibility layer.
- No preservation of `skills/shared/` against the already-owned pre-alpha retirement in `rf2-fqjys`; apply this invariant to the surviving consumer-owned recipe.
- No changes to re-frame2 runtime, Pair-MCP, Xray, or application code.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status searches across 1,138 beads for `Write temp path`, `issue body path expansion`, `NewGuid body file`, `TMPDIR`, `RANDOM`, `literal path`, `body-file`, and shell expansion found no issue owning concrete `Write.file_path` → `gh --body-file` identity.

- `rf2-fqjys` (open P1, owned) retires the shared directory and co-locates concise filing instructions. It does not identify or test this path-materialization defect; this invariant must be applied to the consumer-local recipe it leaves behind. This bead does not alter that task's ownership or architecture.
- `rf2-uhszv` (closed) replaced the improver's old edit-provenance policy and is unrelated to issue-body paths.
- `rf2-t19ve` (closed) made Pair-retro read-only, removing that consumer from filing rather than fixing the remaining migration/implementor path.
- Historical references `rf2-ca5v9s` / `rf2-de7pqw` introduced the current per-filing expression shapes to replace a fixed `/tmp` filename; their structural guard checks OS-temp tokens but not cross-tool path identity.
notes:

The recipe survives as per-skill copies (e.g. skills/re-frame-migration/references/issue-filing.md; likely siblings in other skills). The defect itself (Write cannot expand shell/PowerShell temp-path expressions) may still hold in each surviving copy — the dispatch must RE-DERIVE the copy list at tip and fix every survivor, reporting the delta against this bead's original list.
VERDICT (worker, 2026-09-01, PR #8892): CONFIRMED AND FIXED. The premise holds exactly as described, and it was reproduced end to end on a Windows host rather than argued from the text.

The two filing consumers are exactly re-frame2-implementor and re-frame-migration, agreeing with skills/README.md and with TITLE_SAFETY_RULES in the drift gate.

WHERE THE CONCRETE PATH COMES FROM
The injection boundary is unchanged — the body is still composed with Write and still passed with --body-file, never through shell argv. What changed is that the path is now a VALUE rather than a template. The agent resolves the host temp directory to a concrete literal it can already see (/tmp on a typical POSIX host, or the AppData Local Temp directory on Windows), picks its own nonce, and substitutes BOTH before the first tool call; that one string then goes to Write.file_path and again to --body-file. It works on both hosts because the result is an ordinary absolute filesystem path needing no expansion anywhere — the two variants exist only because the directory differs. The gh argument is single-quoted so a Windows path keeps its backslashes literal.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC1, AC2, AC6 are met by the three doc corrections. AC5 is met vacuously and was verified rather than assumed: skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj went with skills/shared/ under rf2-fqjys, and no successor check asserts TMPDIR or env:TEMP presence — the drift gate pins --body-file and never-interpolate, not OS-temp tokens.

Structurally: every --body-file ARGUMENT must be one concrete absolute path with no expansion syntax, and that same string must appear elsewhere in the recipe as the path Write is given; both host shapes need a worked example; and a recipe with no --body-file argument at all fails, because a zero-match census is not a check that passed. The ban is scoped to the argument position, so prose that merely NAMES the banned tokens is untouched — warning the agent off them is the fix, not the defect. Behaviourally, the --self-test arm runs a fake Write with literal-path semantics and a fake gh that reads --body-file over the concrete paths the SHIPPED recipes actually print, on both host shapes, with a body carrying $(), a backtick, a backslash, both quote kinds and a newline; the body must arrive byte-for-byte and the captured Write.file_path must equal the captured --body-file argument.

NON-VACUITY (AC4)
Run against the REAL pre-fix docs extracted from HEAD, the new axis fires on BOTH recipes with expression-body-path — it would have caught this bug. Its self-test controls bite too: the pre-fix expression passed literally to Write, and a nonce regenerated for the gh step, both fail the handoff; and synthetic recipes reintroducing the expression, the prose placeholder, an unpaired path, an absent argument, or a POSIX-only example each fire.

GATES
Coverage was settled empirically, not from a roster. A broken link and a broken anchor were planted in prose at a line the PR edits, both gates run, then restored and the restore verified against the pre-plant git blob hash 927d4144b1919f1aa9a4019c9203a6af1b49f941 (matched exactly). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py went RED at exit 1 naming both the broken target and the broken anchor at the planted line — it is the covering gate for skills/. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci stayed green at exit 0; skills/ is outside its roster. The plant existed only in the worker worktree, so the red is also positive evidence the gate read that checkout.

33 gates re-run after the rebase onto 8451531aed, every exit code captured on the runner's own command line: all exit 0. That is check_skill_mcp_drift.py in both its --verbose --ci and --self-test --ci arms, the other 29 python gates of the verify-skill-mcp-drift job, plus check_doc_slugs.py and check_readme_links.py --ci.

TWO COVERAGE LIMITS, RECORDED HONESTLY
1. Neither link gate reads inside fenced code blocks, and one changed line — the --body-file line in the gh issue create block in cardinal-rules.md — sits inside one. More broadly both gates validate only link targets and anchors, and this change introduces no links, so their green says nothing about the substance of the edit. Markdown was therefore hand-checked: list renumbering 1 to 3, fence indentation inside item 3, and no heading, anchor or link target added, moved or removed.

THE RECIPE WAS EXECUTED

`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/evidence.cljs`, in its own docstring:

    The contract is docs/design/fresco/product/lanes/testing-xray.md §Evidence contract.

`:no-static-analysis` reads **0** across every tracked file under `implementation/` (1718 tracked, live
control `:opaque` reads 8 files). `:opaque` is pinned by an **equality** assertion in
`evidence_schema_cljs_test.cljs` against the whole loss-reason set, so the phantom could not rejoin that set
without reddening a test. The pairing's old meaning belonged to the `:naming` sub-projection, which schema
v3 explicitly dropped — the code says so in its own words.

## Why this copy is not like the others

A census over the tree finds four tracked copies (excluding `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is a
whole-database export and must be excluded from any tree-wide census). Two are **design records** —
a naming ledger and a Freehand studio note — and were deliberately left alone by the worker that found
them: a record of what was decided then is not a claim about what is true now.

**This one is different because the CODE POINTS AT IT.** A reader who follows the producer's own docstring
to find the authoritative shape lands on a stale spelling, and nothing in the path warns them. That is the
worst position a stale doc can occupy.

## What to do

Re-derive everything at tip first and report the deltas including zeros — this was read once.

Then correct the pairing so the contract says what the code says. **Do not invent a replacement gloss for
the phantom half**: its meaning was retired with the projection, so the repair is to drop it, exactly as
the glossary repair did. Check the surrounding §Evidence contract section for any other claim about the
loss-reason set while you are there, and report what you checked even where you change nothing.

**Do not widen into the two design records.** If you think either genuinely needs changing, say why and
stop.

## Fence

    docs/design/fresco/product/lanes/testing-xray.md

Read the producer namespace and its schema test freely; edit neither.

## Gate note, and this one is unusual

**`mkdocs build --strict` does NOT cover your file**: `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` block lists
`design/fresco/`, so the design trees are deliberately outside the built site. And `check_doc_slugs.py`
skips every directory named `findings` but does cover `docs/`, so check whether it reaches this path rather
than assuming either way — nominate the gate that actually inspects your file, and if neither does, **say
so plainly and verify the links and anchors by hand.** A green from a gate that never read your file is

title: Incomplete: Story args validation ignores optionality and required key presence
description:
Merged-PR audit #9812 at ac070375e74ec1a6e1ffe8d17d419bbfee9d3408. The live-value/reactivity correction in closed rf2-lzzrw works, but the shared args-validation claim remains incomplete: args-violations ignores map-key presence and entry optionality. The source notes mention the optional-key case only as an unmeasured claim; this audit reproduces it and the inverse required-key case. A separate open correction is required.

Real Malli JVM discriminator using the same public helper Controls and the Schema panel call, validator pair {:validate m/validate :explain m/explain}:
* schema [:map [:heading {:optional true} [:string {:min 1}]]], args {}: m/validate returns true, args-violations reports [:heading]. An omitted OPTIONAL prop is incorrectly shown as invalid.
* schema [:map [:heading [:maybe :string]]], args {}: m/validate returns false, args-violations returns []. An absent REQUIRED key is incorrectly accepted because the child schema accepts nil.
* Controls: optional {:heading ""} is rejected by both, optional {:heading "Sign in"} accepted by both, required-nullable {:heading nil} accepted by both. This distinguishes absence from a present nil/invalid value.

Cause: schema_validation.cljc map-entries drops the entry opts, then args-violations validates (get args k) against each child without contains?. Controls.cljs and the panel both call this helper, so matching each other's args does not make their map verdict correct. No browser dependency needed to reproduce this shared CLJC calculation. Actual node CI for #9812 passes 12102 tests/60364 assertions; these cases are not covered there. Scratch artifact C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-merged-pr-audit-a-pr9812-probe-1.clj plus matching .log/.exit, exit 0, exact landed worker root printed. File unchanged through fetched main.

Correction: preserve top-level map entry optionality and key presence when producing per-key violations (or derive equivalent per-key rows from whole-schema validation). Missing optional entries must pass; missing required entries must fail even for nullable children; present entries must still validate normally. Keep the existing nil-validator/schema soft-pass and non-map behavior. Add real Malli regression cases for the five-shape discriminator, in the shared JVM/CLJS suite. Stay within this validator helper and tests; no broader schema redesign or new API. No exact open finding in the 24-item inventory.
acceptance_criteria: With real Malli validators, missing optional props produce no violation; missing required nullable props produce a per-key violation; present nil/valid/invalid controls agree with the whole-map schema. Shared JVM/CLJS regressions retain existing panel reactivity and soft-pass behavior.

The finding itself is recorded above and is not disputed. == RULING (Mike, 2026-09-14 20:33 AUSEST, delegated — Mike: 'for the rest of the beads listed, go ahead and rule with your recommendation'; the re-frame2-fe session rules its recommendation) ==
OPTION A — release and fix inside the helper. args-violations in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc respects top-level map entry optionality and key presence. Preferred route: derive the per-key rows from the whole-map :explain result the helper already receives, so the schema library decides what optional and required mean; fallback if the explain shape is not dependable: keep the entry opts and check key presence before validating the child. Missing optional entry: no violation. Missing required entry, even with a nullable child: a per-key violation. Present entries validate as now. The nil-validator/schema soft pass and the non-map behaviour are unchanged. Controls and the Schema panel both go through this helper, so they stay in agreement. TESTS: the five-shape discriminator from the description as real Malli cases in the shared JVM/CLJS suite; the existing panel reactivity tests stay green. No new API, no schema redesign. This bead is NOT a child of epic rf2-0ae7o — ordinary bug work off rf2-lzzrw; leave it unparented. Fence: schema_validation.cljc and its tests; no overlap with anything in flight. Not a hot zone. Size S.
MAYOR DISPATCH NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-14 20:37 AUSEST, trunk 9550ef4fea, worker/storyschemaval-a): dispatched as ordinary work on the delegated ruling above. Verified at trunk: ui/schema_validation.cljc map-entries :188, args-violations :199 (per-child walk :241-251, whole-map explain :260); callers controls.cljs :972, save_variant.cljc :94 and the Schema panel :487; tests in schema_validation_cljs_test.cljc :233-351, including args-violations-skips-missing-keys-when-validator-accepts :279, which the fix may legitimately change. Unparented, per the ruling. No overlap with any live worker. No browser and no shadow-cljs watch.
== WORKER VERDICT (worker/storyschemaval-a, PR #9831, rebased on trunk 18e2098456) ==
FIXED on the fallback route. args-violations in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc now judges an absent top-level map key by entry optionality before any child validation. Absent optional: no violation. Absent required: a per-key row ({:key k :value nil :schema child}), even when the child accepts nil. Present: validated against the child as before. The nil-validator / nil-schema soft pass and the non-map root path are unchanged. No new API; map-entries keeps its shape.

WHY THE FALLBACK, NOT THE WHOLE-MAP EXPLAIN ROUTE. The explain shape is not dependable across the validator pair. :explain is optional in the validator-fn contract. Its shape is port-specific (Malli on the CLJS reference). And the helper's own suite plus save_variant_cljs_test drive it with synthetic PER-CHILD validator pairs, one with no :explain at all, which would change verdict if called on the whole map. The fallback is exactly Malli's own map rule (malli.core 0.20.1 map -validator: an absent key yields (boolean optional); the -explainer adds ::missing-key only when not optional). It is also the rule re-frame.story.plan/validate-effective-args already applies at plan construction, so Controls and the panel now agree with the plan compiler too. An absent required row's :explain is the validator's account of the one-entry map [:map entry] against {}, so Malli reports the missing key at [k] rather than nothing for a nullable child.

TESTS (shared JVM/CLJS suite schema_validation_cljs_test.cljc). New deftest args-violations-respects-optionality-and-key-presence: the audit's five shapes against real Malli {:validate m/validate :explain m/explain}, each asserting Malli's whole-map verdict as an oracle before the per-key rows. The old args-violations-skips-missing-keys-when-validator-accepts encoded the old behaviour (an absent key's nil routed through the child validator). It was CHANGED DELIBERATELY, not deleted: renamed args-violations-decides-absent-keys-by-presence-not-by-validator, it now asserts that a nil-rejecting and a nil-accepting validator agree on an absent required key, and that an absent optional key is no violation under a nil-rejecting validator.

RED THEN GREEN. The tests-only commit ran on the unfixed helper: JVM 25 tests / 96 assertions / 6 failures (exit 1); CLJS 34 / 120 / 6 failures (exit 1). Shapes 1 and 2 were red; 3, 4 and 5 and all oracles were green. After the fix: JVM 25/96/0 (exit 0), CLJS 34/120/0 (exit 0).

CONTROL. The presence check replaced by true (the old nil pass-through): JVM 6 failures (exit 1), CLJS recompiled and 6 failures (exit 1). Restored from HEAD and verified: the default-form git hash-object equals the committed blob id, and git diff --quiet exits 0.

FULL GATES on the final base. JVM tools/story clojure -M:test: 1990 tests / 7425 assertions / 0 failures (exit 0). CLJS :node-test: compile exit 0, 0 warnings; run 12113 / 60420 / 0 failures (exit 0). Require-alias dialect ratchet exit 0 (self-test 79/0). clj-kondo error level exit 0; the helper's 6 warnings match the pre-change baseline. Splint fail-on-errors exit 0, with 2 style warnings on unchanged lines.

CALLERS (read-only, none edited). No caller depends on the old behaviour; every caller test passes present keys or no schema. login-form.stories-cljs-test (real Malli, present :heading) 8/30/0; save-variant-cljs-test + controls-validation-diff-cljs-test 40/131/0. Behaviour note for review: Controls renders rows only for keys present in the effective args, so an absent REQUIRED prop now raises its banner count with no inline row, and shows as a Schema-panel row. Previously an absent OPTIONAL prop with a nil-rejecting child did the same.
WORKER DONE (mayor, 2026-09-14 21:10:48 AUSEST): worker reported done; PR #9831 is ready, 2 files (ui/schema_validation.cljc, schema_validation_cljs_test.cljc). It merges on the criterion. Close this bead on merge; the worker left it in_progress and unparented.

Route: the ruling's FALLBACK, with reasons given. :explain is optional in the validator contract, explain shapes differ by port, and existing tests use synthetic per-child validators. So entry opts are kept and key presence is checked before the child validates. That is Malli's own map rule and the rule the plan compiler's validate-effective-args already applies (017 :614-624), so Controls and the Schema panel now agree with plan construction.

The :279 test was changed deliberately, not deleted: it was renamed args-violations-decides-absent-keys-by-presence-not-by-validator.

Visible change, within the ruling: Controls renders rows only for present keys. A missing required prop shows in the banner count and as a Schema-panel row.

The worker found a fourth caller the brief missed: testbeds/login_form/stories_cljs_test.cljs:296 (rf2-w72ij's fence). It has the key present and stays green.
