title: story-mcp: release the CLI executor promptly at stdin EOF
description:
Release CLI-owned execution resources when stdin closes, so a completed Story MCP session exits promptly. After a real variant run the read loop and -main return, but Clojure's non-daemon future executor keeps the JVM alive for its approximately 60-second idle timeout. This P3 finite delay is finding 3 split from rf2-fzbj.31; preserve the remediation fence until Mike rules who owns remediation.

Ownership/revision: tools_story_mcp; baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, revalidated at 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned paths unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source: tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:178 creates a Clojure future for every actual run/preview. server.cljc:399-408 returns after EOF without releasing the executor. test/stdio-roundtrip.js ends with child.kill() and does not run a registered variant, so it cannot prove graceful process exit after real lifecycle work.

Fresh actual-command witness: Node launches java with the cached absolute classpath, clojure.main -i <synthetic-prelude> -m re-frame.story-mcp.server. The prelude registers a valid Story and installs plain-atom. Wait for the final ping response, close stdin, record the 'stdin closed; exiting' stderr signal and the child PROCESS close event. No kill on the successful path; the harness has a 90-second emergency bound.

- Same prelude, initialize + ping: EOF log after 2 ms, process exit 0 after 60 ms.
- Initialize + successful run-variant + ping: EOF log after 0 ms, process exit 0 after 60,027 ms.
- Separate in-memory run-loop! witness: after return :eof, clojure-agent-send-off-pool-0 is alive, non-daemon, TIMED_WAITING.

Expected: the process releases its owned resources and exits promptly after the completed session reaches EOF. Actual: a measured one-minute delay, not an infinite hang and not failure to see EOF. Impact is slower host restart/shutdown and temporary orphaned JVMs; hosts can terminate the process and the executor eventually expires, hence P3.

Repair: put process-level cleanup at -main, for example finally/shutdown-agents when the CLI owns the process, or use a narrowly owned executor with explicit shutdown. Do not globally call shutdown-agents from reusable run-loop! or each handler: embedded callers and subsequent requests must stay usable. Preserve the existing deadline around synchronous Story work.

Acceptance: real -main performs a registered run, returns its result and ping, receives stdin EOF and exits 0 within a short bound (e.g. 2 seconds after EOF) without test-driven kill. Keep the no-run control and a library-use control proving run-loop! does not globally disable Clojure futures. Timeout/cancellation should also allow prompt CLI exit.

Validation: probe-tools_story_mcp-2.cjs/.log/.exit under ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story_mcp/ exited 0 and both child JVMs exited naturally. probe-tools_story_mcp-1.clj independently inspected the non-daemon worker. Both use current source, Clojure 1.12.4 and existing cached dependencies. A separate fresh timeout control in probe-tools_story_mcp-4.clj returned status error after about 26 ms for a 20 ms deadline over a 300 ms wait, permitted a ping, and prevented the post-wait event; the 1000 ms control executed and passed. No source/build/install/Git mutations or broad suites, SDK/browser or external-host tests. All probe processes finished.

Deduplication: current all-status Story-MCP/executor/EOF/shutdown titles and relevant descriptions found no dedicated same issue. Read rf2-fzbj.31 and its latest three newest-first history entries. Keep prior fixes, statuses and notes intact. This issue records review evidence and authorizes no fixer.
notes:
FIXED in PR #9759 (branch worker/storymcp-a, commit 7d76bf9c81 post-rebase). Re-verified at tip before fixing. The ownership hold is lifted by Mike's 2026-09-13 ruling on the parents (rf2-fzbj / rf2-gwye).

Fix. -main now runs boot!/run-stdio! inside a try whose finally calls shutdown-agents, releasing the cached send-off pool that tools/lifecycle.cljc's run-variant-blocking uses for every run and preview. Those threads are non-daemon with a 60-second keep-alive, which is the whole of the measured delay. It is at the CLI entry point because -main owns the process, and it is deliberately NOT in run-loop! or any handler: run-loop! is the embeddable half, and a library caller's later futures — and later sessions — must keep working.

Regression test — a real spawned session, no test-driven kill on the success path. test/stdio-roundtrip.js now performs registered variant runs, receives their results and a following ping, then closes stdin and waits for the child's own exit within a bound of 10 seconds, asserting exit code 0. The bound is 10 s rather than the suggested 2 s so a cold CI runner cannot flake it while still separating the two cases by a factor of six against the 60 s keep-alive.

Evidence, isolating THIS finding. With the whole change in place the stdio test is green, so the red was produced by planting a revert of ONLY the -main finally against the committed tree: the run then failed with "server still running 10000 ms after stdin EOF", exit 1, while every earlier step stayed green. The plant was confirmed applied before the run (diff: 1 file, 5 deletions) and the restore verified by content hash — git hash-object's default form reproduced the committed blob exactly, and git diff --quiet HEAD exited 0. Fixed runs: exit 0, EOF-to-exit 77 ms, 106 ms and 161 ms across three runs, against the 60,027 ms this bead measured.

The library-use control the acceptance asks for is kept as a JVM test (run-loop-leaves-clojure-futures-usable-after-eof): after a session that ran a variant through run-loop!, a freshly submitted future still runs. It would go red on the obvious wrong fix — putting shutdown-agents inside run-loop!.

Recorded and NOT built: the no-run control spawn. It characterises the pre-fix delay rather than guarding the fix (the session that DOES run variants now exits in ~100 ms, which subsumes it), and it would add a second JVM boot to every CI run of this job.

Known limit, deliberately not widened here: shutdown-agents releases Clojure's future/agent executor, which is what this finding measured. re-frame's JVM interop (implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj) keeps its own single-thread and scheduled executors for async :dispatch / :dispatch-later; those are core's, outside this surface, and no finding filed against them. Story's own JVM play runner dispatches synchronously, so a variant run does not reach them.

title: [adapter_test_react] Invalidate exposed parent handle after failed initial mount
description:
Recommendation: make failed INITIAL mount rollback invalidate the failed parent record as well as draining its descendants. One confirmed P3 correctness defect remains in this local test harness. The fix should be a small lifecycle-state correction plus an extension of the existing captured-parent regression; no reconciler, publishing, smoke, or production feature work is warranted.

Scope and revision
- Slice: adapter_test_react.
- Reviewed baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. The entire owned slice still has an empty diff against that revision in the shared source checkout after validation.
- Exactly five owned tracked paths:
  implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md
  implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn
  implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc
  implementation/adapters/test-react/test/re_frame/adapter/test_react_cljs_test.cljc
  implementation/adapters/test-react/test/re_frame/adapter/test_react_dispose_sub_cache_cljs_test.cljc
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No worktree guard claim: no source edits, build outputs, installs, servers, commits or pushes were made by this reviewer. Root owns tracker durability.

Confirmed finding 1 — P3: failed initial render leaves its exposed mount handle live and updateable

Source: implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:272-305, specifically initial :mounted? true at line 277 and the failure branch calling only force-teardown-descendants! at line 300. The observable continuation is trigger-update! at lines 503-525, which accepts any record still marked mounted. Whole-adapter cleanup at lines 407-409 cannot repair this record because failed initial mounts never enter active-mounts.

Trigger: an :rf/component body retains the mount argument supplied by the public simulator and then throws. Capturing that argument is already part of an existing owned test, failed-mount-leaves-no-did-mount-and-spares-live-sibling-rf2-3fc89f2, at test_react_cljs_test.cljc:576-610; this counterexample does not fabricate a record or mutate private state.

Minimal reproduction, executed against the actual namespaces in a fresh JVM:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.adapter.test-react :as tr]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as sa])
(sa/install-adapter! tr/adapter)
(let [captured (atom nil)]
  (try
    (tr/mount! {:rf/component
                (fn [mount]
                  (reset! captured mount)
                  (throw (ex-info "initial-render-failure" {})))})
    (catch Throwable _))
  (let [failed @captured]
    [(count (tr/mounted-components))
     @(:mounted? failed)
     (some? (tr/current-render-tree failed))]
    ;; actual: [0 true true]
    (tr/trigger-update! failed [:div :impossible-update])
    (mapv :phase (tr/lifecycle-log failed))
    ;; actual: [:constructor :render :render :did-update]
    (sa/dispose-adapter!)
    [@(:mounted? failed) (tr/current-render-tree failed)]
    ;; actual: [true [:div :impossible-update]]
    (tr/unmount! failed)))
```

Expected: once an initial render aborts, its exposed record is terminal, its candidate tree is cleared, and trigger-update! rejects it through the existing :rf.error/update-after-unmount path. It must never acquire :did-update without having committed :did-mount. Descendants remain drained, the original render exception escapes unchanged, and unrelated live mounts survive.

Actual: the forest is empty but the failed parent still says mounted=true and retains the throwing candidate tree. trigger-update! returns the same record successfully and appends :did-update after no :did-mount; it still does not register the record. Adapter disposal subsequently leaves that record and its replacement tree unchanged. The JVM witness also checked identical? on the caught original exception and obtained true, so exception preservation itself is correct.

Impact: the simulator can accept a stale captured update callback after failed mount, report a lifecycle that never committed, and hide the handle from both the live-mount census and fixture cleanup. This undermines the harness's lifecycle/transaction assertions. This is deliberately P3: the adapter is local-test-only with no demonstrated production consumer, and the trigger requires retaining the publicly supplied mount argument. It is not an application memory-leak claim when nobody retains that record; an unretained failed record is collectible.

Precise repair: in mount-tree!'s initial-render catch, finish the parent record's state as well as rolling back descendants, without registering it and without masking the original exception. Reuse the existing force-teardown-record!/force-teardown-subtree! primitives where appropriate instead of adding another registry or generic validation mechanism. Keep :did-mount and :did-update absent for the failed attempt. If the repair adds a :forced-teardown phase for this exposed parent, align the initial-failure documentation with that deliberate observation contract.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Extend the existing captured-parent failed-initial-mount test to assert mounted=false, current-render-tree=nil, and rejection of a later trigger-update! with no added :render/:did-update phases.
2. Keep the original exception identity, no :did-mount, empty live forest, descendant rollback, and unrelated-sibling survival. The nested failure path should also invalidate an exposed failed child record.
3. Ordinary successful mount/update and all existing teardown/order/cache regressions remain green on the adapter's supported JVM and CLJS test lanes. No new publishing or smoke requirement.

Coverage, history, and limits
- Inspected all five owned files in full, plus the relevant shared adapter routing/disposal seams and Spec 006 contracts. Covered stable-kind identity guard, dynamic-frame hook routing, derived reads, normal/forced teardown, recursive children, render failures, inspection aliases, SSR emitter chaining/reinstall, single-frame and every-frame sub-cache cleanup, fixtures, packaging claims and README limitations.
- Executed both owned test namespaces directly with clojure.test in a fresh JVM, using cached Clojure 1.12.0 jars and absolute source/test classpaths: 35 tests, 157 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, own runner exit 0. This is a targeted JVM namespace run, not a claim that the CI alias, broad spine, CLJS compiler or browser suite ran. The process printed the resolved test-react source resource as its gate root, verified to be this source checkout.
- The same JVM process executed the counterexample before the suite and printed the observed state shown above; the exposed handle was explicitly cleaned up afterward. Evidence: ignored ai/surface-review-20260912/review-adapter-test-react-jvm-1.log and matching .exit (0). A preliminary Babashka require probe succeeded; a first stdin invocation using unsupported '-' failed before loading the witness and is not counted as validation.
- Dedupe: searched all-status Test-React titles/descriptions and failed-initial/render-depth descriptions, plus bd memories test-react. Read closed rf2-ytyq and its latest history (normal teardown order is already fixed), rf2-6r9j.141 (scope-accurate descendant helper), rf2-6r9j.85 (local-only status/no UIx consumer), and rf2-6r9j.81 (cache-test consolidation), and inspected .142's live-only inspection contract/source. None owns invalidation of the exposed failed parent record. Historical source commits 488bf70df6 and bd14ef705e establish the earlier descendant rollback and failed-update fixes; their old rf2-3fc89f.2/rf2-j538f7.1 references currently return no issue from bd, so no unread close-reason ruling is inferred.
- Parent review's rf2-fzbj.5 concerns distinct shared sub-cache release/atomic-clear defects; this finding does not duplicate or reassign them.
- Excluded by design: real React reconciliation, automatic rerenders, context-provider traversal, DOM annotations/measurement, browser timing, publication coordinates and smoke coverage. Those are explicit local-fixture limitations, not defects. No separate actionable finding is asserted from stale wording in test explanations. No unverified runtime risk is promoted to a finding.

title: Stale post-root-swap render-coupling prose outside tools/xray/spec: tools/story/deps.edn and shell.cljs docstring
description:
Routed out of rf2-k97c.7 (PR #9712) with a REASON, not deferred for lack of time.
Both sites are post-root-swap stale prose that sit OUTSIDE tools/xray/spec, so taking
them there would have widened a docs PR's gate surface — which .7's fence forbade in
terms for tools/story.

Neither is urgent: in both cases the CONCLUSION the stale sentence supports is still
correct, so nothing is currently misleading anyone into a wrong action. What is wrong
is one supporting sentence in each.

SITE 1 — tools/story/deps.edn, the day8/re-frame2-xray :exclusions rationale.
The block under "THE STATED REPLACEMENT (this is a re-point, not a silent drop)" says:
"Xray renders through re-frame.substrate.adapter and the adapter the HOST installs
governs the runtime path, so Xray is fully served by Story's stock-Reagent adapter."
Half-stale since rf2-k97c.3. The mount verbs (open!, open-overlay!, popout!) no longer
render through the host adapter at all — they paint through a re-frame.fresco client
root Xray owns. What IS still true is the half Story actually uses: panels/mount-shell!
and the per-panel mount-<panel>! facades still delegate to rf.substrate.adapter/render
with a hiccup tree, so Story's embed door really is served by its stock-Reagent adapter.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE PROSE FIX, and the reason it wants a bead rather than a
drive-by: writing the replacement sentence takes a determination nobody has made —
whether Story's embed door stays on adapter/render or follows the mount verbs onto the
owned root. Answer that first; the sentence falls out of it.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the :exclusions itself and the whole argument for it. That
argument is about PUBLICATION and classpath — two jars both carrying
re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs, with nothing but classpath order deciding which adapter
an app gets — and the root swap does not touch any of it. The line "THE :exclusions IS
LOAD-BEARING - do not drop it (rf2-qvyr)" stands.

SITE 2 — tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs, the ns docstring's closing
"## Pure hiccup" paragraph: "Per rf2-tijr the view code is pure hiccup. The substrate
adapter's render fn (rf/render) handles the substrate-specific mount in mount.cljs."
The second sentence is false as of rf2-k97c.3 and the SAME DOCSTRING says so about 60
lines above, under "## rf2-k97c.3 - the Dynamic chrome is a FRESCO TREE": "the shell no
longer paints through the installed adapter's :render at all - mount.cljs owns a Fresco
root". So one docstring contradicts itself, and the stale half is the one a reader
reaches last.

Both sites verified at source at the tip PR #9712 branched from (4ad6e9446a).

GATE NOTE: site 2 is CLJS, so it arms the cljs test surfaces; site 1 is a deps.edn.
That difference in gate surface is the whole reason they were not folded into a
markdown-only PR. They can still land together - one commit, both files - since neither
is on a hot-zone path.

title: [FENCED - NOT DISPATCHABLE, precondition unmet] Collapse the eleven Xray *-bridge scaffolding pairs once no Reagent parent heads them
description:
FENCED — NOT DISPATCHABLE. The precondition is not met today for ANY of the eleven bridges, and
this bead's own notes say so after measuring it. It reaches `bd ready` because its fence is a
measured precondition rather than a tracker dependency, so the ready list overstates it.

WHAT CLEARS IT, per bridge rather than in one sweep: **no Reagent parent heads that bridge any
more.** Three things still do, and all three were measured rather than assumed —
`panels.cljs`'s `render-panel!` chokepoint still mounts several from a Reagent tree; roughly eight
shipped boundary witness suites head them from Reagent deliberately; and five of the eleven
boundaries are `^:private`, so heading them directly also means de-privatising five foreign files.

DO NOT START BY DELETING BRIDGES. Start by measuring, per bridge, who still heads it from Reagent.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR ANYTHING, and the current shape is strictly cheaper than what shipped before, so
this should not be ranked above work that changes behaviour. Full reasoning in the notes below.
notes:
Eleven `*-bridge` / `*-component` scaffolding pairs across nine Xray satellite files were shipped by
slices B1-B6 with a DEFINED END written into their own docstrings: "when `shell-view` becomes a
boundary it heads [[handle-view]] directly and both this and [[handle-component]] are deleted."

rf2-k97c.3's root swap satisfied the first half of that condition -- `shell-view` IS a boundary now
(PR #9708) -- but the bridges CANNOT collapse yet, and that was measured rather than assumed:

  * `panels.cljs`'s `render-panel!` chokepoint still mounts several of them from a REAGENT tree.
  * Each file's own shipped boundary witness suite heads the bridge from Reagent deliberately --
    `[palette/Modal]`, `[filters/Modal]`, `[spine-filters/Modal]`, `[spine-filters/RowContextMenu]`,
    `[resize-handle/Handle :inline]`, `[settings-popup/Modal]`, `[edn-inspector-popup/...]` and
    more. Collapsing the bridges reddens roughly eight suites.
  * FIVE of the eleven boundaries are `^:private` (palette `ModalView`, filters `ModalView`,
    cancellation-cascade `PopoverView`, spine-filters `RowContextMenuView` and `ModalView`), so
    heading them directly also means de-privatising five foreign files.

So rf2-k97c.3 did the correct minimal thing instead: `shell.cljs` stops HEADING the bridges and
CALLS them (`[palette/Modal]` -> `(palette/Modal)`), which answers the same `[:> ...]` escape and is
a legal Fresco head form. That is this epic's own ruled call-site rule for a shared plain fn.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. When no Reagent parent heads a given bridge any more, collapse THAT bridge: the
boundary takes the public name, the `[:>]` and the `*-component` def go, and the file's scaffolding
comment goes with them. It is per-bridge and gated on a real precondition, not a sweep.

DO NOT START by deleting bridges. Start by measuring, per bridge, who still heads it from Reagent.
The precondition is genuinely not met today for any of the eleven.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR ANYTHING. The current shape is correct and strictly cheaper than what shipped
before -- under Reagent the chain was Reagent component -> `[:>]` -> `as-component` -> boundary, and
it is now `[:>]` -> `as-component` -> boundary. This is tidiness with a precondition, so it should
not be ranked above work that changes behaviour.
MAYOR FOLD-IN 2026-09-13 (from xraydoor-a's PR #9786 report; not filed as its own bead). When this bead opens `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs`, also correct the `ManagedFxList-bridge` docstring, which still promises "When `render-panel!` itself builds a Fresco tree…". That promise was retired by the rf2-l1jm ruling (the embed door stays ratom-family), and PR #9786 already corrected the same promise at the `render-panel!` docstring and the `mount-resources!` comment. One docstring sentence; it rides along at zero marginal cost and does not change this bead's fence.
FENCE (2026-09-16 19:0x AUSEST). Held by a live worker in C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xraystale-q5n7d on branch worker/xraystale-q5n7d.
Do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch until it reports.
Release: a completion report, or a recorded death.
The worker holds tools/xray/** for the duration.

THIS IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FENCE and it does not replace the one this bead already carries. The bead's own precondition fence -- no Reagent parent heads a given bridge -- was measured unmet and is unchanged; nothing here bears on it. What is added is a SURFACE fence: rf2-vyvo8 is live on tools/xray/** right now, which includes tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs, the file this bead's fold-in note directs a worker to open for the ManagedFxList-bridge docstring correction.

SO BOTH MUST CLEAR, not either. A future tick that finds the precondition newly met still must not dispatch while a worker holds tools/xray/**. Recorded because this bead reaches `bd ready` despite being fenced -- its own text says the ready list overstates it -- so the scan that reaches it is exactly the scan most likely to act on a single cleared condition.
FENCE WORDING AMENDMENT (2026-09-16, mayor). This applies to the FENCE paragraph above and to every other fence carrying the line "Release: a completion report, or a recorded death". It is recorded in identical words on every affected bead so a scanning tick catches it wherever it lands first.

THE FENCE PARAGRAPH CONFLATES TWO RELEASE CONDITIONS THAT ARE NOT THE SAME EVENT. Read it as two fences:

  1. THE RE-DISPATCH FENCE -- "do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch".
     RELEASES ON: a completion report, or a recorded death. As written. This is the condition the
     reaping rule uses, and a report really does discharge it.

  2. THE SURFACE FENCE -- "the worker holds <surfaces> for the duration".
     RELEASES ON: THE PR MERGING. Not on the report. "For the duration" means the duration of the
     CHANGE, not the duration of the agent.

WHY THE SECOND IS NOT THE FIRST, and it is CLAUDE.md's rule rather than a preference: "two beads touching the same hot file = sequence them, second waits for the first's PR to MERGE." A worker that has reported still has an OPEN PR editing those files. A second worker branched off trunk today would not carry that PR's changes, so the two diffs collide at merge -- which is precisely what the fence existed to prevent, now reached by way of the fence's own release line.

THIS IS LIVE RIGHT NOW, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. As of this amendment three workers have REPORTED while their PRs remain OPEN on the surfaces they held: #9900 (implementation/resources/**, spec/016), #9902 (epoch tool_pair.cljc), #9903 (tools/xray/**). Under the unamended wording each of those surfaces reads as released.

SO THE OPERATIONAL TEST WHEN YOU MEET A FENCE IS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE:
  * "Can you quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?" -- answers the re-dispatch fence, and the reaping rule.
  * "Has the PR that edits this surface MERGED?" -- answers the surface fence, and it is the one that governs a DISPATCH decision.
A yes to the first and a no to the second means: reap the worktree if you like, but DO NOT dispatch onto that surface.

FOR FUTURE FENCES, the surface line reads "The worker holds <surfaces> until its PR MERGES" rather than "for the duration".
PRECONDITION RE-MEASURED AT TIP (2026-09-16, mayor, trunk c39d0922dd). STILL UNMET FOR ALL ELEVEN. This bead stays fenced; nothing here changes its ruling.

WHY IT WAS RE-MEASURED. This bead's fence is a MEASURED PRECONDITION rather than a tracker dependency, which is why it keeps reaching `bd ready` — its own description says the ready list overstates it. A measured fence goes stale silently, and tools/xray/** has moved since the original measurement (PR #9903 landed on it). A fence nobody re-measures is indistinguishable from one that has quietly lifted.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, each against the figure this bead already records, so the comparison is to a stated number rather than to an impression:

  * ELEVEN `*-bridge` defs still exist across the Xray satellite files. The bead says eleven. None has collapsed.
  * `render-panel!` is still present as the chokepoint (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs:246).
  * The shipped boundary witness suites still head bridges from Reagent — eight test files plus five source files carry the `[palette/...]`, `[filters/...]`, `[spine-filters/...]`, `[resize-handle/...]`, `[settings-popup/...]` and `[edn-inspector-popup/...]` head forms. The bead says "roughly eight suites".
  * FIVE boundaries are still `^:private`: ModalView 3, PopoverView 1, RowContextMenuView 1. The bead says five of the eleven.

CONTROLS, so the readings are not a broken instrument agreeing with itself: 143 tracked files under tools/xray/src (the search reaches the tree), and a nonsense bridge token reads 0.

BOTH FENCES ON THIS BEAD ARE THEREFORE INTACT, and they are independent. The SURFACE fence lifted when PR #9903 merged — tools/xray/** is unheld today. The PRECONDITION fence has NOT lifted, and it is the one that governs: no bridge may be collapsed while a Reagent parent still heads it. A future tick that notices the surface is free must not read that as the item being dispatchable.

NOTHING TO DO. The current shape is correct and strictly cheaper than what shipped before, so this stays ranked below anything that changes behaviour. Re-measure again only if somebody is in these files for another reason.

title: False: Machine Inspector W1 proves its chart island mounted
description:

That marker is emitted by panels/machine_inspector.cljs:402 on the parent div outside (as-child [machine-canvas/Chart ...]). It exists even if as-child returns nil and the entire Chart subtree disappears. All other W1 checks concern panel wrappers or the five boundary reads, so they do not establish that Chart ran either. This is a concrete selector/ownership mismatch visible in the landed code, not a claim that the current production Chart is broken. The relevant test and panel blobs remain unchanged at fresh origin/main.

Select a node actually produced by Chart, e.g. its rf-xray-machine-canvas-host marker from machine_canvas.cljs, inside the mounted panel container. Add a focused negative control removing the island child and demonstrate that the island assertion fails while the outer wrapper remains. Preserve the existing frame/cache checks. The full feature-matrix run reported by the worker is separate evidence; it does not make this new W1 assertion discriminate the claim it states. No open Bead explicitly owns this selector/control defect.
acceptance_criteria: W1 observes actual DOM emitted by machine-canvas/Chart below the migration seam. A controlled absent island leaves the outer focused-event-chart wrapper present but makes the island check fail; the real island passes. Run the focused browser lane and preserve frame-targeting/ref-count witnesses. No chart migration or wider test framework needed.

title: docs(spec): finish the two-space nested-list sweep across spec/ and migration/ (70 sites, 17 files)
description:
The `docs/` half of rf2-3bq6 has landed. This is the `spec/` + `migration/` half,
which was left out deliberately: 7 of its 17 files are HOT ZONE and one is behind an
open PR, so the sweep has to be sequenced rather than dispatched in one go.

=== MEASURED BY RENDERING, NOT BY COUNTING SPACES ===

Counts below are from a rendering instrument, not an indentation heuristic. Each file
is rendered with python-markdown under the exact extension list `mkdocs.yml` produces
(loaded through mkdocs' own config loader, so the mkdocs builtins `toc`, `tables` and
`fenced_code` are included alongside the nine declared ones). A unique sentinel is
injected into every source list item; the sentinel render, with sentinels textually
removed, must equal the baseline render, which proves the injection was structurally
inert; then each item's nesting depth is read off the parsed HTML. A DEFECT is a pair
of document-consecutive items sharing a root list where the source indents deeper but
the render does not nest.

The heuristic in rf2-3bq6 read 209 sites across 45 files. Measured by rendering the
same corpus reads 205 across 49 files: 23 heuristic false positives and 19 sites it
missed entirely (it resets its parent on a blank line, so it cannot see a two-space
child that follows one).

=== THE PARTITION. 70 SITES ACROSS 17 FILES. ===

DISPATCHABLE NOW - not hot zone, no open PR. 38 sites, 9 files:

        16  spec/Implementor-Checklist.md
         4  spec/012-Routing.md
         4  spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md
         3  spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md
         3  spec/016-Resources.md
         3  spec/Construction-Prompts.md
         2  spec/014-HTTPRequests.md
         2  spec/Derivations.md
         1  spec/010-Schemas.md

    Implementor-Checklist at 16 is the densest and the most valuable: it is a
    CHECKLIST, the document shape where losing a level of nesting changes what a
    reader thinks they have to do.

HOT ZONE - sequence these, one toucher at a time. 28 sites, 7 files:

        11  spec/005-StateMachines.md
         7  migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md
         5  spec/009-Instrumentation.md
         2  spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md
         1  spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md
         1  spec/API.md
         1  spec/Conventions.md

    NOTE spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md: the heuristic in rf2-3bq6 read ZERO there and
    did not list it as a hot-zone holder. Rendering finds one site, at line 2303. The
    hot-zone set for this defect is SEVEN files, not the six the parent bead names.

BEHIND AN OPEN PR - wait for #9598 to merge, then re-measure. 4 sites, 1 file:

         4  spec/011-SSR.md

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: `docs/design/freehand/**` and `docs/design/fresco/**`
carry one site each and `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` keeps those trees out of the
built site, so a flattened list there reaches no reader.

=== HOW TO DO IT ===

Rebuild each defective list block's indentation as base + 4*depth, where depth comes
from the SOURCE indentation tree and base is the block's own first-item column.
Python-Markdown wants exactly four columns per level regardless of marker width - a
`1. ` parent is NOT a three-column parent, measured: a three-space child under `1. `
at column 0 still flattens, and eight columns under a column-0 parent becomes an
indented CODE BLOCK, so the target is exactly 4*depth and never more.

Repair BLOCK BY BLOCK and keep only the blocks whose repair leaves the invariants
intact, rather than rewriting a whole file at once. Three invariants, all measured on
rendered HTML: the ordered sequence of each list item's OWN text, the whole document's
text content, and the non-list HTML with `ul`/`ol`/`li`/`p` stripped. The `p` is in
that strip list on purpose - nesting an item that was a sibling of a LOOSE list makes
it an item of a TIGHT inner list and python-markdown drops the wrapper, which is a
consequence of the nesting being correct rather than a content change.

TWO TRAPS THAT COST REAL TIME ON THE docs/ HALF, both caught only by the invariants:

  1. A CONTINUATION paragraph of the parent sits at the SAME column as a two-space
     child item. Shifting it with the child silently reparents the prose under the
     child. Attribute a continuation line to the innermost open item whose CONTENT
     COLUMN it actually reaches, never to the item that happens to precede it.

  2. Some blocks cannot be repaired at all in isolation - see the sibling bead on
     continuation blocks that escape their list item. Leave those alone and report
     them; a half-fix there produces a code block, which is worse than the flattening.

title: gate scheduling: bench/ is on no classifier surface, so CI never runs data_archive.test.cjs
description:
MEASURED BY THE rf2-d1nr.2 WORKER ON 2026-09-10, IN PASSING, AND NOT INTRODUCED BY THEIR PR. Reported at
source rather than inferred: `bench/` is on NO classifier surface — the surface report reads false for every
one — and the nightly `fresco-bench-compile` job runs the COMPILE gate, not the lane's own `npm run check`.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this is worth a bead rather than a note. Nothing in CI runs
`bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/data_archive.test.cjs`. That file now includes the corpus-backed
check added by PR #9580 SPECIFICALLY to stop a future raw read from silently omitting the native arm — the
repair for a hollow gate. A gate that CI never runs is hollow one level up: it goes red only for someone who
happens to run it locally, which is exactly the population that did not catch the original defect.

THE SAME SHAPE ALREADY BIT US TWICE IN THIS FAMILY, which is why the pattern matters more than the file:
rf2-20h4 and rf2-d1nr.2 were both "green in CI, red on any checkout a human has actually worked in". This is
the mirror — green everywhere because the check never runs at all.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is NOT a request to put `bench/` on the PR critical path. The bench lane is a local
research surface with heavyweight fixtures and a restorable 237-file corpus, and loading every PR with it
would be exactly the over-engineering the project stance refuses. The question to settle is narrower: which
bench checks, if any, are cheap and deterministic enough to belong on a surface, and whether the nightly is
the right home for the rest.

FIRST STEPS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, each a measurement rather than a change:
  * Read `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` and confirm the "false for every surface" reading
    against a bench-only diff, with a control on a diff that DOES arm a surface.
  * Enumerate what `npm run check` in the bench lane actually runs, and time each part. `data_archive.test.cjs`
    reads 7/7 with the corpus and 4/4 plus 3 skipped without it, so it has a corpus-free mode already — that
    mode may be cheap enough for a surface where the full one is not.
  * Establish whether a CI clone can restore the corpus at all, since the archive is in-repo. If it can, the
    cost is time; if it cannot, the corpus-free mode is the only candidate and the answer is bounded.
  * Check `scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py` and `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` — one of them may already be
    the right place to REGISTER a deliberate decision that bench is nightly-only, so that the gap is recorded
    rather than merely true.

A DELIBERATE "no, and here is why, recorded" is a complete and good outcome for this bead. What is not
acceptable is leaving the gap undocumented, because the next author to add a bench test will reasonably
assume CI runs it.
notes:
=== RULING (rf2-50fe), measured 2026-09-10, worker benchsurf-a, zero edits ===

VERDICT: NO to a per-PR surface for `bench/`. YES to one bounded nightly addition.
The "gap is undocumented" risk this bead names as unacceptable does NOT exist: it is
documented in four places, one of them machine-enforced. But the bead's central
CONSEQUENCE is TRUE and worth closing at the nightly.

--- 1. THE PREMISE, CORRECTED ---

"bench/ is on NO classifier surface" is TRUE OF ONE CLASSIFIER AND FALSE AS A FLAT
STATEMENT. This repo has three PR classifiers and the claim was measured against one.

  * .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (test.yml): bench arms 0 of 29
    outputs. CONFIRMED across 8 path shapes (.cljs .cljc .cjs .edn .md .json,
    package.json, bench/README.md) - all 29 false, exit 0 each.
    CONTROL BOTH WAYS: --all = 29/29 true; implementation/core/src/re_frame/db.cljc
    = 16 true; a nonexistent path = 0 true. So the instrument bites, and the
    bench all-false is a real reading rather than a broken invocation.
    IMPORTANT: a bench-only diff and a garbage path produce IDENTICAL output. The
    difference lives in the SOURCE, not the output.
  * lint.yml's own classifier: bench DOES arm it, by EXTENSION, wherever the file
    lives. data_archive.test.cjs (a .cjs) measures js_surface=true. Bench .cljs and
    .cljc measure lint_surface=true. Measured by extracting the detect block and
    running it; controls: garbage path false/false, a docs path lint_surface=true.
  * docs.yml's docs_surface: no bench arm. Confirmed false.

AND THE test.yml SILENCE IS A RULING, NOT A HOLE. The classifier carries an explicit
bench/* case arm that deliberately sets nothing, with the reasoning inline, citing
rf2-6c12m.1. It is pinned by a named test in the mirror
("a bench-lane diff is CLASSIFIED to no gate, not left unclassified").

--- 2. THE GAP IS ALREADY REGISTERED, AND MACHINE-ENFORCED ---

implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs carries a
DECLARED_NO_SURFACE_OUTPUT registry with a bench/fresco entry giving a "why" and a
"coveredBy" list. Three enforcement arms, all measured green (mirror test: 369 passed,
exit 0):
  (a) every tracked tree must arm an output OR be declared - a new dark tree fails;
  (b) a declared tree that STARTS arming an output must have its entry DELETED - so
      the declaration cannot outlive the hole (an anti-rot ratchet);
  (c) every coveredBy path must exist.
Also documented in TESTING.md (the Fresco-modules-compile row states the bench lane is
off every per-PR lane by ruling and that the mirror pins it) and in
bench/fresco/README.md, which requires the lane's own check before publishing a
bench change.

SO: NEITHER scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py NOR scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py is the
right registration site, and neither needs changing.
  * check_gate_scheduling.py reads implementation/package.json ONLY;
    bench/fresco/package.json is out of scope, and its script is named "check", which
    is outside the test:/bench:/build: prefix set that gets asked. Two mismatches.
  * check_fast_pr_gap.py maps REQUIRED CI JOBS to local spine lanes; bench has no
    required job, so it has nothing to map. Its one bench-looking lane,
    "spine node tier: fresco bench-lane compile", is npm run test:fresco-compile =
    implementation/fresco/scripts/check_modules_compile.cjs - an implementation-side
    gate, NOT the bench lane.
Both run green at tip: check_gate_scheduling exit 0 (34 gate commands, 30 scheduled,
4 declared); check_fast_pr_gap exit 0 (79 required jobs, gap map clean).

--- 3. THE CONSEQUENCE IS TRUE ---

Nothing in CI EXECUTES data_archive.test.cjs, nor 20 of its 21 siblings.
  * The nightly fresco-bench-compile job runs exactly TWO steps, both compiles
    (the browser lane id, then the node lane id via lane_build). It is step 1 of
    the lane's 22-command check chain and nothing else. The bead's reading is right.
  * npm run test:scripts (the always-on js-harness-self-tests job) globs
    scripts/*.test.cjs, core/test/re_frame/bench/*.test.cjs,
    fresco/scripts/*.test.cjs - all relative to implementation/. Only ONE chain
    member is reached that way: lane_cache_wiring.test.cjs, which lives under
    implementation/core/test. The other 20 are under bench/fresco/ and reach nothing.
  * ESLint LINTS the file but does not EXECUTE it, so it cannot see a failing assertion.

BUT THE PR-TIME COVERAGE OF bench/ IS WIDER THAN THE REGISTRY SAYS - FOUR READERS,
NOT TWO. The registry's "why" names only verify-readme-links and js-harness-self-tests.
Measured, there are two more, both in lint.yml, both armed by bench itself:
  3. ESLint - 54 of the 276 files in the "eslint ." roster are under bench/.
     VERIFIED BY PLANTED FAULT: an unreachable-code probe placed in the bench tree
     reddened the gate, exit 1, naming the planted file; removed after.
  4. require-alias-dialect - check_require_alias_dialect.py reads EVERY git-tracked
     .clj/.cljs/.cljc via git ls-files (roster 2829 files; 156 of them under bench),
     and scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn carries a named "bench" surface at
     floor 0. Ran green, exit 0.
This is a PRECISION correction to a hot-zone file's comment, not a defect. Recorded,
not edited.

--- 4. THE MEASUREMENTS THAT DECIDE IT ---

Cost of the 21 non-compile chain members, run individually and timed, from the lane
directory, with NO npm install of any kind (they need none):
  * corpus ABSENT:  8.5s total, 21/21 exit 0, 133 checks.
  * corpus PRESENT: 22.8s total, 21/21 exit 0, 223 checks.
  * DETERMINISTIC: a second corpus-free pass measured 8.46s vs 8.48s, identical exit
    codes and identical per-command check counts.
So cost is NOT the reason bench is off the PR path. Which matters, because it means a
cost measurement cannot be the argument for putting it back - see section 5.

data_archive.test.cjs split CONFIRMED: 7/7 with the corpus, 4/4 plus 3 skipped
without, exit 0 both ways. (Cosmetic wart worth knowing: a skipped corpus check still
prints an "ok" line, so the corpus-free run prints SEVEN ok lines beside its "4/4"
summary. The summary is right; the ok-line count is not a check count.)

CAN A CI CLONE RESTORE THE CORPUS? YES, and cheaply - this was the question the bead
thought might bound the whole answer, and it does not.
  * The archive commit is 3283 commits behind HEAD and IS an ancestor of origin/main.
  * MEASURED IN A REAL DEPTH-1 CLONE: git fetch --depth=1 <remote> <full-40-char-oid>
    exit 0 in 9.7s against github.com; the restore then wrote 237 files / 77 MB in
    0.54s; the full suite then read 7/7, exit 0.
  * So the corpus costs about TEN SECONDS in CI. No fetch-depth: 0 needed.

AND THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE REDDENED A NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION. In a depth-1 checkout -
which is exactly what actions/checkout gives by default, and what fresco-bench-compile
uses - data_archive.test.cjs FAILS: exit 1, 3/4, "fatal: Not a valid object name".
Its FIRST check is not corpus-backed but IS history-backed: it resolves the archived
tree via git ls-tree. So the corpus-free mode is not history-free.
Two further specifics for whoever implements:
  * The pinned SHA in the source is the 10-char ABBREVIATION, and an abbreviated sha is
    NOT a fetchable ref: measured exit 128, "couldn't find remote ref", against
    github.com. The full 40-char oid is required and is not currently spelled anywhere
    in the tree.
  * A local file:// remote refuses the arbitrary-sha fetch too (exit 128) because that
    transport does not enable it by default. That is NOT evidence about GitHub, which
    permits it - measured separately, exit 0.

--- 5. THE RULING ---

NO to arming a classifier surface for bench/. Three reasons, in order of weight:
  1. rf2-6c12m.1's ground is untouched by anything measured here. It ruled the lane off
     every per-PR lane because its suites exercise LOCAL COPIES of the runtime, so a
     per-PR run cannot catch a regression in the SHIPPED one. That is an argument about
     what the suites can prove, not about what they cost. My timings say it would be
     cheap; cheapness was never the objection, so it cannot be the rebuttal.
  2. The cost of reversing is three coordinated edits, two of them hot-zone
     one-toucher: the classifier's bench/* arm, the mirror test that pins every output
     false, and the DECLARED_NO_SURFACE_OUTPUT entry - which the ratchet in (b) above
     FORCES you to delete the moment the tree arms anything. That is a lot of moving
     parts to buy a check that cannot see the shipped runtime.
  3. The lane's own README already requires the check before publishing a bench change,
     and the ruling made it hand-run deliberately: "Hand-run only; NO new CI job or
     workflow for the bench tree - the bench README states the check command is
     required before publishing a bench change."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: evidence that a bench self-test can fail for a reason
ORIGINATING IN THE SHIPPED RUNTIME rather than in the lane's local copies. That is the
premise rf2-6c12m.1 rests on, and it is the only thing whose falsification reopens this.
A second, weaker trigger: if the bench tree ever stops carrying local copies and starts
requiring the shipped artefact directly, the ruling's ground disappears with it.

YES, NARROWLY, TO ONE NIGHTLY ADDITION - and this is the part worth sequencing as its
own dispatch. Add the lane's NON-COMPILE self-tests as a further step of the EXISTING
nightly fresco-bench-compile job.
  WHY IT IS PROPORTIONATE: the job already checks out, sets up JDK 21 and Node 24, runs
  npm ci, and budgets 30 minutes for two compiles. The addition is ~8.5s corpus-free, or
  ~33s including the corpus. It touches ONE file. It touches NO classifier, NO mirror
  test, and NO registry entry - the tree still arms no surface output, so
  DECLARED_NO_SURFACE_OUTPUT stays exactly as it is, which is what keeps this cheap.
  WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: the job is named "Fresco bench lane compiles" and runs 1 of the
  lane's 22 checks. The corpus-backed check PR #9580 added specifically to stop a raw
  read silently omitting the native arm currently runs in no scheduled place at all.
  The nightly is already the system of record and already has failure-signature
  alerting wired to this exact job.
  HOW, PRECISELY - three constraints, each measured, each easy to get wrong:
    (i)   Do NOT run the lane's check script wholesale. Its first member is the same
          compile the job already runs as its own step, so a naive call pays for a
          multi-minute shadow-cljs compile twice. Run members 2..22.
    (ii)  Give the job history, or data_archive.test.cjs reds on arrival at 3/4 for a
          purely environmental reason. Cheapest measured route: after checkout, fetch
          the archive commit by its FULL 40-char oid at depth 1 (9.7s). The alternative
          is fetch-depth: 0 on the checkout, whose cost I did not measure and which is
          almost certainly worse on a repo this size.
    (iii) Restoring the corpus is optional and recommended: +0.54s once (ii) is done,
          and it lifts the run from 133 checks to 223. The nightly is the ONLY place
          those 90 corpus-backed checks could ever run in CI.
  NOT A BLOCKER FOR THE PR PATH: this changes nothing a PR is graded on.

If the operator prefers to spend nothing at all here, that is defensible and the gap
stays as it is - but then the nightly job's NAME should be read as literal, and this
note is the record that 21 of the lane's 22 checks run only on a developer's machine.

--- GATES RUN (own captured exit codes, unpiped) ---
  check_gate_scheduling.py            exit 0
  check_fast_pr_gap.py                exit 0
  check_readme_links.py --ci          exit 0  (and exit 1 under a planted fault in the
                                              bench README, restored - blob hash back to
                                              its committed value)
  check_require_alias_dialect.py      exit 0
  _changed-surfaces.test.cjs (mirror) exit 0, 369 passed
  eslint .                            in-roster confirmed; exit 1 under a planted
                                              unreachable-code fault in the bench tree,
                                              probe removed
  bench lane members 2..22            exit 0, twice, both corpus states
Worker worktree guard ran and exited 0. NO tracked file was modified; the tree is clean.
No AI-attribution trailers were used anywhere (harness asks for them; CLAUDE.md wins).

title: spec/005: correct the false 'reg-event :schema cannot reach a machine's inner events' claim and make [:schemas :events]'s declaration-only status author-visible
description:
spec/005-StateMachines.md states something FALSE about a live surface, twice, and it is the
reason the `[:schemas :events]` question kept re-opening. Fix the text; wire NOTHING.

Split out of rf2-1r69 by the 2026-09-08 ruling (read that bead's notes for the full measured
analysis). rf2-1r69 itself stays PARKED — do not implement any runtime validation here.

=== THE FALSE CLAIM ===
spec/005-StateMachines.md:523 (the `:schemas` table row for `:events`) and :531 (the SA-4
wire-when trigger) both assert that `reg-event`'s `:schema` "cannot reach a machine's internal
event vocabulary". IT CAN. The `reg-machine` opts `:schema` validates the whole OUTER vector
`[:machine-id [:inner-event <payload>]]` at the `:where :event` boundary, and the inner event is
element 1 of it.

PROOF (a passing test, already on main — read it, do not re-derive):
implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_schema_arity_test.clj:159
`event-schema-arity-validates-outer-vector` rejects a malformed nested `:auth.login/submit`
payload BEFORE the handler runs, using:
    [:tuple [:= flow-id] [:tuple [:= :auth.login/submit] Credentials]]
`:tuple`, not `:cat` — `:cat`'s sequence-regex semantics would flatten the nested inner vector.

=== WHAT TO CHANGE (all in prose; no code, no runtime behaviour) ===
1. spec/005:523 — rewrite the `:events` row so it states the truth: the gap `[:schemas :events]`
   would close is CO-LOCATION, PER-EVENT KEYING and TOOLING LEGIBILITY, plus ONE genuine
   capability gap — a SPAWNED ACTOR. Opts (including `:schema`) are stored for the registered
   TYPE at implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:1327, but
   `handler-meta-for` at :1420 builds spawned-actor metadata carrying only the machine
   discriminator fields, so the type's opts `:schema` is NOT inherited. The outer-vector
   workaround therefore covers singleton machines and cannot reach spawned actors at all.
2. spec/005:531 — same correction inside the SA-4 wire-when trigger, and sharpen the trigger to

title: docs(claude): the imperative-justification census is contaminated in both directions — add it to the instrument-misreport list

title: [implementation/core/subscriptions] Resolve live cache metadata through the inspected frame
description:
Reviewed snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Before filing, mayor HEAD e4d949e8e87893ad638ed97e3d087fda1f62f0d4 has no changes on the relevant tooling, registrar resolution, Pair preload, or Xray paths.

Problem / expected behavior
The two live subscription inspection functions accept a frame-id and read that frame's cached reactions, but combine them with metadata from whichever registrar generation happens to be ambient. An inline-image-only sub is consequently reported as :input-kind :db, even if it has declared/parametric inputs. A conflicting global or inspector-frame registration supplies the wrong :input-kind, and the algebra view also attaches its :derive, :schema, :doc, and source coordinates to the target frame's value. The result is internally inconsistent inspection evidence for a supported same-id/different-image application.

Exact causal proof
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/tooling.cljc:160-182 (sub-cache-snapshot) resolves (:sub-cache (rf.frame/frame frame-id)), then gets subs-meta with (rf.registrar/registrations :sub) at :162. Per entry it uses that map for :input-kind, defaulting to :db at :181, while values/realized-inputs come from the target cache.
- The sibling sub-cache-algebra-view at :415-444 repeats the same split at :417-422 and calls with-source-coords at :441. That helper (:287-299) projects the ambient descriptor's schema, doc, source and handler-fn into the live node.
- Neither reader establishes re-frame.live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution. The internal registrar read deliberately respects dynamic *generation*: this is correct for its runtime callers, but these frame-targeted inspectors have not supplied their target generation.
- Normal subscribe does establish target generation (subs.cljc:1700-1757), so cached values can correctly belong to image A while inspection metadata belongs to global/B. Correct values therefore do not validate this tooling result.

Actual consumers without a repairing wrapper
1. skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:963-969 calls sub-cache-snapshot directly. sub-cache-info at :1020 does the same after resolving only a frame id, then carries :input-kind and :realized-inputs in the include-values response. snapshot-frame-slice at :3714 also calls it directly. The Pair MCP list-subscriptions tool reaches sub-cache-info at tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/list_subscriptions.cljs:115.
2. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph.cljs:120 selects sub-cache-algebra-view as its live subscription contributor. Its live graph read at :384 calls implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc:811-821, which dispatches the frame id to contributors without binding the observed generation. Xray therefore cannot rely on its own rendering frame to resolve the target's subscription metadata.

Smallest reproducer to add on the CLJS lane
Initialize the plain-atom/reactive test adapter. Register global :review/value as a :db reader with {:doc "GLOBAL" :schema :global-schema}. Build image A containing inline :review/base => 5 and inline :review/value with metadata {:inputs [[:review/base]] :doc "IMAGE A" :schema :a-schema} and body (fn [[n] _] n). Make :review/frame-a from that image and subscribe to [:review/value] there.
Outside any generation binding, call (sub-cache-snapshot :review/frame-a). The value is 5 and realized inputs are [[:review/base]], but actual :input-kind is :db from the global registration; expected is :static from image A.
Call (sub-cache-algebra-view :review/frame-a): actual :doc/:schema/:derive come from the global reader; expected values are the descriptor that image A runs. Repeat with no global registration (actual :db fallback and absent local metadata), and from inside a different frame's generation binding to prove the explicit target wins in all three contexts. Use unvalidated schema tokens only as inspection metadata, or install a permissive validator in the fixture.

Impact
P3: incorrect developer-tool answers and wrong source/function attribution, not wrong app subscription values. A developer or AI inspecting an image-local graph is shown an app-db reader or unrelated implementation instead of the actual derivation. No claim of an independently demonstrated privacy leak is made.

Smallest repair
Resolve metadata through the requested frame's generation at these live tooling boundaries, using the existing frame-resolution seam (or the existing explicit target query mechanism where appropriate). Share the small scope operation between the sibling readers, retain their current nil/dev/JVM contracts, and keep production tooling elimination intact. Do not change internal registrar semantics or add another public query grammar. Coordinate with rf2-4lp1 so generation changes cannot leave a cache node reporting a successor descriptor while computing an old body.

Dedupe / decisions
Searched open and closed beads by subscription/cache/sub-cache-snapshot/sub-cache-algebra-view and relevant generation descriptions/memories. Fully read rf2-kuky.30: it owns public registrar source-selection grammar and explicitly leaves internal registrar/registrations generation-routed. Its enumerated consumer migration does not fix these internal target-to-metadata joins. This issue preserves that decision and needs no API ruling. Current :inputs grammar and always-vector delivery are also retained.

Validation limits
Source-and-caller causal proof only for these CLJS-gated readers. Their JVM branch returns nil, so the separate isolated JVM freshness probe is not claimed as execution evidence for this bug. No CLJS/browser build, full suite, or implementation change was performed. Existing adapter runtime tests inspect global/default-frame declarations and do not exercise the conflicting image-local case above.
acceptance_criteria: CLJS coverage materializes the same sub id in two distinct images plus a conflicting global descriptor, then inspects A without a binding and from inside B. Both live readers report A input-kind and local metadata alongside A value and realized edges. Include an inline-only sub absent globally. Exercise the Pair include-values or Xray contributor path to prove caller behavior; preserve missing-frame nil, JVM nil, and production dev-tool elision. Internal registrar resolution and public query grammar remain unchanged.
close_reason: PR #9387: both live cache readers (sub-cache-snapshot, sub-cache-algebra-view) now resolve :sub registration metadata through the INSPECTED frame's generation via a shared private seam over the existing live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution. Values and metadata now come from the same frame: an image-local declared-input sub reports :static with its realized edges instead of :db, and the algebra view carries the inspected frame's own :doc/:derive/:inputs instead of a conflicting same-id global's. Static surfaces (sub-topology, sub-algebra-view) keep their ambient read - they are not frame-targeted. Internal registrar semantics and public query grammar unchanged (rf2-kuky.30 preserved); missing-frame nil, JVM nil and production elision preserved. Coverage: re-frame.subs-tooling-inspected-frame-metadata-cljs-test - two frames materializing one sub id from different images plus a conflicting global, inspected from no binding and from inside the other frame's generation binding, an image-only sub absent globally, and the missing-frame nil contract. Gates: implementation/core clojure -M:test exit 0 (2258 tests / 11674 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors). The readers are CLJS-bodied and return nil on the JVM, so the new namespace is owned by CI's node CLJS lane.

title: xray-spec-check returns exit 0 on a planted fault in tools/xray/spec/API.md — coverage unestablished, mechanism unchased
description:
MEASURED BY WORKER trace-a, 2026-09-07, while delivering rf2-kuky.54 (PR #9351). Reported to the
mayor as a side observation and filed here rather than actioned, because it is a gate defect
rather than part of that bead.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. In `tools/xray/spec/API.md`, the real call `(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)` was
replaced with a bogus name. `xray-spec-check` returned EXIT 0, and its reference count did not
move — it stayed at 23. So the check did not see a planted fault in the file it exists to grade.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. This is the fail-open shape this repository
already hunts elsewhere: a check that answers "nothing wrong" in the same voice whether the tree
is clean or the instrument is blind. Every PR touching `tools/xray/spec/**` has been reading that
exit 0 as coverage. CLAUDE.md's own rule — "run the search once against something it SHOULD find"
— is exactly the control that caught it, and it caught it by accident here rather than by design.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be assumed by whoever takes this. The mechanism was NOT
chased: trace-a recorded the measurement and stopped, correctly, because it was mid-delivery on
another bead. So it is unknown whether the check is scoped to a path that excludes API.md, whether
it matches on a pattern the plant did not disturb, whether the count is read from a cache, or
whether it is behaving exactly as designed. The workflow describes this check as REPORT-ONLY,
which is a live candidate explanation and would make this a naming/expectations defect rather
than a broken gate — in which case the repair is to stop nominating it as coverage, not to fix it.

FIRST STEP FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: reproduce the plant, then read the check's own definition and
the job that runs it, and decide which of those four it is BEFORE proposing a repair. Do not
raise a floor or widen a pattern until the mechanism is named. If it is report-only by design,
the deliverable is a correction to whatever asserts it as a gate, plus a note here — that is a
complete and good outcome, not a non-result.
close_reason: DIAGNOSED then repaired (PR #9388). The gate was NOT broken and NOT report-only: xray-spec-check extracts exactly two shapes from tools/xray/spec/API.md -- 21 qualified day8.re-frame2-xray.*/ panel symbols + 2 mount-*! names = the 23 the bead reported unmoved. The plant, (rf/trace-buffer frame-id), is a call-position facade reference, a THIRD shape the extractor never read. So of the four candidates it is 'matches on a pattern the plant did not disturb'. Report-only is refuted: -main exits 1 and lint.yml runs it as a hard step; 'report-only' in the docstring means it does not EDIT the spec. Reproduced: baseline exit 0 / 23; plant A exit 0 / 23; in-remit control plant B (panels.trace/Panel -> bogus ns) exit 1 naming file+line, which also proves the run read this worktree. THE REAL DEFECT was an adjacent coverage gap the exit 0 was hiding: the same file documents the framework surface Xray consumes as 14 distinct (rf/<var> forms and NO check reconciled them -- doc-api-check owns that contract but scans spec/Privacy.md + docs/api/** + docs/story/api/**, doc-guide-check owns docs/core/, skills-check owns skills/; tools/xray/spec/ fell between them. Folded that third shape in reusing projection/alias-call-references + doc-api-check's bare-name resolution -- an existing sibling-defined contract applied to a surface that lacked it, NOT a widening until the plant fails. Evidence it is principled: it went red on the first run for a reason unrelated to the plant -- the spec still named (rf/sub-cache frame-id), a facade alias rf2-80mmlf REMOVED; reconciled to (rf.subs.tooling/sub-cache-snapshot frame-id). After: exit 0 at 37 refs; the bead's exact plant now exit 1 naming API.md:502. Non-coverage recorded in the docstring rather than engineered around: only the bare rf alias is anchored so (rf.machines/... stays outside; resolution is bare-name not namespace-exact; and the vacuity floor is an AGGREGATE so it cannot see one extractor collapsing while the others hold the total above it. Unit contracts added. Gates: api-manifest clojure -M:test exit 0 (101 tests/199 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors); check_doc_slugs exit 0. Plants restored and verified by blob hash.

title: api(ssr): delete install-render-to-string!, :ssr.streaming/* hooks, emitter :emit-hash?; add home 1-arity
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from ssr.md (ref ssr.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Four SSR seams have zero consumers outside their own definition and tests, and one of them carries a false spec sentence.

1. `re-frame.ssr/install-render-to-string!` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:54` → `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:922-933`): a fn that takes a setter and calls it with `render-to-string`. Consumers: none in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/` or any adapter — only its own def, the façade re-export, one contract test (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj:1404-1437`), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:84-89`, and two Conventions sentences that cite it as an example (`spec/Conventions.md:1728,1854`). Every bundled adapter is armed by the three other paths in `emit.cljc:889-920` (plain-atom direct set, the `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` chain, the durable `:ssr/current-hiccup-emitter` slot that `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` replays at every install).
2. The three `:ssr.streaming/*` late-bind hooks (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:806-808`; directory rows `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:787-801`). The only host adapter, `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming`, requires the ns directly (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:51`) and calls `streaming/render-shell`, `streaming/render-continuation`, `streaming/build-final-payload` at `:199`, `:328`, `:401`. Consumers of the hooks: none — no `late-bind/get-fn :ssr.streaming/…` exists anywhere. `spec/011-SSR.md:1749` says "Host adapters call these three hooks in order … The Ring adapter wires them via `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming/stream-handler`" — false at tip. The same false claim sits in `streaming.cljc:803-804`, `directory.cljc:788-789` and `ssr.cljc:123-125`.
3. description:
PR #9131 rewrote chapter 20 section 3 to make shadow comparison executable, but retained an incorrect scriptless-mode claim at docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:387-388: omit :script and each committed render becomes a checkpoint.

The authoritative hm/shadow! implementation says the opposite. Its public docstring states that automatic per-commit checkpoints are not built because the runtime publishes no commit callback. Scriptless shadow! returns a live handle with :checkpoint! and :stop!; the caller decides when to call :checkpoint!, which settles both mounts and records that reading. The implementation comment at mounted.cljs:2104-2106 repeats that the caller chooses when a reading is a checkpoint.

As written, an interactive migrator can exercise both mounts believing comparisons are being recorded when no checkpoint is taken. This is a correctness gap in the same named migration proof step PR #9131 aimed to make executable.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the automatic-checkpoint claim with the actual scriptless contract: retain the returned handle, drive the two live mounts, explicitly invoke :checkpoint! at each comparison point, and invoke :stop! when finished. Keep the chapter consistent with hm/shadow!'s public docstring and verify the documentation gates.
notes: AUDIT PR #9139: Fix skills/reagent-migration/references/procedure.md:201-202, which still repeats the disproved automatic-checkpoint claim. Also make docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:583 state the bifurcated contract: scripted calls return green/red and tear down; omitting :script returns the live handle with explicit :checkpoint! and :stop!.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: this close REVERTED and the payload is on the trunk.

Delivered by worker/hicch20-b in PR #9139, MERGED. Verified in SOURCE at origin/main, not from the PR record. The false claim is GONE — a fixed-string search for 'each committed render becomes a checkpoint' and for 'omit :script' returns zero across the chapter — and the real contract is in its place at docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:406-417: 'Retain the handle, drive both mounts by hand, call :checkpoint! at each ...', with a worked ((:checkpoint! s)) call returning {:status :green :checkpoints 1}, and the sentence 'Each :checkpoint! call settles both mounts, compares them, and numbers the ...'.

That matches hm/shadow!'s public docstring, which says automatic per-commit checkpoints are NOT built because the runtime publishes no commit callback, and the implementation comment at mounted.cljs:2104-2106 that repeats it. An interactive migrator can no longer drive both mounts believing comparisons are being recorded when no checkpoint is taken.

Gates on that PR: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, check_guide_samples.py --self-test and live both exit 0 (74 verbs, 384 sites, 29 pages), mkdocs build --strict exit 0 — with a planted broken anchor driving the slug gate red at 20-migration-from-reagent.md:34 and the restore verified by git blob hash.

WHY IT REVERTED: the documented .beads checkout/checkpoint race (CLAUDE.md §Beads durability; rf2-51uz1). Note the PARTIAL shape: rf2-o80n, closed by the SAME worker in the SAME PR, did not revert — so the race is per-close, not per-PR, and verifying one bead of a set does not clear the others. That is the second partial revert observed today, after rf2-rrp6/rf2-ma8r.

title: hic docs: 09-interop.md's h/as-component section does not say what a Reagent parent's props do at the crossing
notes:
FOUND while closing rf2-4387 (PR #9131, chapter 20).

09-interop.md "Render a Hicasso view from native React" names "UIx, raw React, JavaScript, or TypeScript parents" and does not name Reagent - the one parent a *migration from Reagent* guarantees you have. It then says React props return "with canonical names ... and identity-preserved values", which is true of the DECODE half and says nothing about what the parent did before the decode.

The statement to add, verified against Reagent 2.0.1 (the version implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn declares) and against implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:

- reagent.impl.template/convert-prop-value: a keyword or symbol becomes its `name`; a CLJS map becomes a camel-cased JS object with its values recursively converted; any other `coll?` goes through `clj->js` (deep); anything `js-val?` - strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions - crosses unchanged.
- Prop NAMES round-trip on this route: reagent.impl.util/dash-to-prop-name camel-cases `:article-id` to "articleId" and codec/prop-key reads "articleId" back to `:article-id`. VALUES do not.

So a Reagent parent rendering `[:> bridged {...}]` hands the Hicasso view converted values under correctly-spelled keys. The practical consequence - cross an id and read the rest with h/sub - is now written in chapter 20's new "Views shared across the boundary" section; 09-interop.md wants the mechanism sentence at h/as-component so a reader who never opens chapter 20 still meets it.

NOTE this refutes half of rf2-4387's reported observation: the pilot recorded a CLJS map and a vector surviving "intact", which Reagent's source contradicts for both.

FENCE: docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md. Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict (both apply; the page is under docs/ and not under docs/design/). implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py gates any h/ verb in a new fence.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9149 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. The patch fixes 09-interop.md but not the complete public contract. docs/core/hicasso/glossary.md:382-384 and api-reference.md:193 still enumerate React/UIx/JavaScript parents without Reagent, the migration path this issue is about. The new conversion text also omits symbols even though Reagent 2.0.1 convert-prop-value uses named? (keywords and symbols), and its categorical “values do not” sits beside primitives/functions crossing unchanged; state this as structured-value conversion or loss of guaranteed identity/shape. The source as-component docstring carries the same parent/props half-truth; rf2-ip7a owns that exact docstring and was updated instead of duplicating it.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: same .beads race. Payload verified in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main — docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md now documents the prop crossing (3 hits for camel/round-trip).

Delivered by worker/hicinterop-a in PR #9149, MERGED. The worker read Reagent 2.0.1's convert-prop-value out of the DECLARED JAR rather than trusting the bead: a keyword becomes its name; a CLJS map becomes a camel-cased JS object with values recursively converted; other collections get a deep clj->js; anything js-val? (strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions) passes unchanged. Hicasso's outward-props decodes shallow and by identity and does not convert back.

The one-line contract, now in the guide: NAMES ROUND-TRIP, VALUES DO NOT. That is also the measured basis for sibling bead rf2-rx99 (hm/shadow!'s docstring example crossing :article-id and arriving as :articleId), currently with worker/hicdoc-a.

title: hic docs: no cookbook recipe for a reusable control the caller parameterises - the intent-prefix + conj shape that replaces a Reagent :on-select closure prop
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F07 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `api`

**Trying to**

Port `pagination`, a shared control whose Reagent contract was
`:on-select` — a one-argument closure, `#(dispatch [:home/show-page %])`, so
each caller decides where its own `?page=` lands.

**Expected**

A recipe. Passing a parameterised handler to a child is not exotic; it is how
every reusable control in every codebase is written.

**Instead**

Nothing in the corpus covers it. The chapters teach three callback shapes and
each is about the *leaf*: an intent vector at an `on*` prop, `h/event` where the
callback's own arguments matter, and a plain function for imperative work. The
missing case is one level up — **a parent handing a child the identity of an
event the child will parameterise**. Chapter 02 tells you what not to do
(a function prop "defeats the bail-out on every parent render"); chapter 03
tells you a hand-rolled dispatch closure raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
So both obvious spellings are ruled out and none is offered.

**Looked at**

- `03-events-as-data.md` "One callback form: `h/event`", "Ordinary functions
  remain available"
- `02-views-and-reads.md` "Equal props skip the body"
- `04-controlled-inputs.md` "Forward caller attributes safely" — the closest
  thing, but it is about forwarding *attributes*, not a handler contract
- `cookbook.md` — read all nine recipes; the list recipe's row builds its own
  intents from its own props, so the question never arises there

**Resolved by**

Guessing that an **intent prefix** is the intended idiom: the parent passes
`[:home/show-page]`, the child appends its own argument —
`[::h/prevent (conj on-select page)]`. It works, and it is better than what it
replaced: a vector compares by value, so unlike the old closure it does not
defeat the props bail-out. But it changes the prop's published contract, which
means every caller has to move, and I had no documented ground for choosing it
over the alternatives (an `h/event` closing over a captured frame; a keyword
event-id; splitting the control per caller).

**Bead**

Cookbook recipe: "a reusable control the caller parameterises" — intent prefix
plus `conj`, and why it beats a closure prop.
close_reason: Done in PR #9140. New cookbook recipe 'A reusable control the caller parameterises', placed straight after the buffered-field recipe because that recipe already shows the same contract from the caller's side (:on-commit passed as [::events/title-committed id] and dispatched with the draft appended). The idiom was verified as shipped framework contract rather than invented: forms/buffered-field dispatches (conj on-commit candidate), impl/boundary.cljs accepts a vector :on-error and dispatches (conj on-error error), and chapter 13's combo passes the prefix through to its handler; forms_cljs_test.cljs and forms_dom_cljs_test.cljs witness the prefix shape. The recipe uses the pilot's own pagination case and teaches both arms of the one contract - conj in the body when the argument is a render-time fact (a page number), conj in the handler when it is only known when the event fires (a combo's active item) - plus the ::h/value case where the marker IS the argument. The 'why it beats a closure prop' half is grounded in verified guide claims: a vector compares by value so the child keeps the equal-props bail-out that a fresh closure defeats on every parent render (ch02), and an ambient rf/dispatch from a callback raises :rf.error/no-frame-context because the rendering extent has gone (ch03). h/event is scoped to callbacks whose own arguments matter. No framework surface added. Gates: check_guide_samples.py exit 0, and a planted h/ verb in this very recipe made it exit 1 naming 'cookbook.md block 8', so the gate demonstrably read the new sample.
