title: Name test-quiet subprocess harness process and stream roles
description:
## Naming finding

The JVM and CLJS contract suites rely on expensive subprocess harnesses whose most important values use terse, inconsistent names. `test_quiet_runner_contract_test.clj` names the runner boundary `run-runner`/`run-runner-with-env` and uses `proc`, `out-f`, `err-f`, `done?`, `sep`, `cp`, `cmd`, `builder`, and `child-env`. `test_quiet_runner_lifecycle_test.clj` shortens the same roles further to `drain`, `run-program`, `src`, `tmp`, `os-win`, and `cmd`. The CLJS harness uses `self` and `res` for the runner script and Node spawn result. These are central diagnostic paths where a confused process, stream, or timeout result produces misleading gate evidence.

## Proposed names

Use `invoke-quiet-runner` / `invoke-quiet-runner-with-env`, `process`, `stdout-future`, `stderr-future`, `exited?`, `path-separator`, `classpath`, `command`, `process-builder`, and `child-environment`. In the lifecycle suite use `drain-process`, `run-lifecycle-program`, `program-source`, `program-file`, and `windows?`. In the CLJS spawn harness use `runner-script` and `spawn-result`. Update all test consumers and prose; retain result-map keys and external command arguments.

## Ambiguity cost

These helpers distinguish a spawned process from future drains, a child environment from inherited state, and a real exit from a timeout/kill result. Abbreviations require readers to reconstruct those roles while diagnosing already expensive and platform-sensitive contract failures.

## Compatibility / risk

All function/lexical renames are private to test namespaces. Preserve subprocess commands, classpaths, inherited-env semantics, `RF2_MIN_TESTS` stripping, timeout/kill/reap policy, concurrent drain order, result-map keys (`:exit/:out/:err/:timed-out?` and CLJS spawn keys), fixtures, marker text, public runner APIs, and every Phase-1 deletion target. Do not remove or consolidate rows tracked by `.89`/`.92` in this naming change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. JVM runner and lifecycle harness helpers/locals name process, stream future, environment, classpath, command, timeout, and program roles consistently.
2. The CLJS spawn helper names its script and spawn result explicitly without changing its public test result-map keys or options.
3. All private helper consumers and prose are updated; exact searches leave no stale executable references to the renamed helpers/locals.
4. JVM and consolidated CLJS contract suites preserve subprocess commands, output capture, timeout/reap behavior, exit status, and diagnostic maps.
notes: Completion evidence: commit e2922c71e313619ece4b50008e487d37afe07f21 (refactor(test-quiet): clarify internal naming roles) changed subprocess harness process/stream role names; available full clj-kondo gate gate-kondo-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (errors 0), test-quiet JVM gate implementation/test-quiet/gate-jvm-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (54 tests, 279 assertions, 0 failures/errors), and consolidated CLJS gate implementation/gate-cljs-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (11,209 tests, 55,849 assertions, 0 failures/errors).

title: Epoch off-box projection: name trace-event and projector roles explicitly
description:
Evidence:
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc off-box helpers name payload/frame-state values v/fs and repeatedly call trace events ev, operations op, and late-bound tag projectors project.
- resource-family-op? takes op and derives ns*; elide-whole-output-large-slots uses m, mark, k, and v for a projected record/map, elision marker, slot key, and slot value; trace/trigger elision helpers both take v despite different input shapes.
- The projector chain is security-sensitive: profile selection, built-in sensitivity projection, optional host redaction, tag-family projection, whole-output caps, and trace/trigger elision run in a fixed order.
- Repo Tool-Pair/spec/MCP consumers establish projection profiles/options, late-bind hook keys, trace and record keys, failure policy, and serialized output as contracts. The HTTP payload projector is live and retained per Phase-1 rf2-6r9j.41.

Impact:
Generic value/map/function names obscure which stage is handling a payload, whole frame state, raw trace event, event-tag family, or record slot. That makes audit of fail-closed egress policy and projection order unnecessarily difficult.

Rename only private parameters and lexical bindings to payload, frame-state, trace-event, operation, operation-namespace, event-tags, tag-slot, tag-vector, project-*-tags, projected-record, elision-marker, slot-key, and slot-value vocabulary.

Risks/contracts:
Preserve projector order, fail-closed behavior, built-in profiles/options, public APIs/arglists, late-bind hook keys, trace/record/wire keys, whole-output caps, production elision, and HTTP projector behavior. No public or serialized vocabulary changes.

title: Spell out machine classification registry transform roles
description:
## Locations and evidence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/classification.cljc:121-201` has a private transform named `apply-decls` with long-lived parameters `reg`, `decls`, and `set?`, an inner `abs`, and callers that bind `decls` / `xf`. The function both adds and drops per-actor claims, so `set?` does not say which direction true selects.

## Ambiguity cost

This is privacy-sensitive registry code: a reader must repeatedly decode abbreviations and infer that true means ADD (not “is this a set?” or “replace”). `abs` and `xf` also hide that they are absolute snapshot paths and the full registry transform.

## Recommendation

Rename the private helper to `apply-declarations`; rename locals/parameters to `registry`, `declarations`, `add?`, `absolute-paths`, and `transform`. Update in-namespace docstrings and both lower/drop callers.

## Compatibility / migration risk

The helper is private and repository search finds no external reference. Public `machine-declarations`, `lower-at-spawn!`, `drop-at-destroy!`, registry owner maps, keywords, and behavior remain unchanged. The edit must be identifier-only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact search finds no `apply-decls` symbol and no ambiguous `reg` / `decls` / `set?` / `abs` / `xf` bindings in this transform/callers.
- The renamed helper remains private and add/drop paths still call the same elision operations with identical values.
- Machine classification, SSR redaction, spawn, and destroy focused tests pass.
- `git diff --check` is clean.
notes: Completion evidence: commit abaa3808feea5dd489d2b92e0df4b4d21e81c9f7 (Clarify machine runtime internal naming) changed machine classification transform role names and affected tests; available full clj-kondo gate gate-kondo-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (errors 0), consolidated CLJS gate implementation/gate-cljs-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (11,209 tests, 55,849 assertions, 0 failures/errors).

title: Remove unused API-manifest projection index helpers
description:
Evidence
- implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/projection.clj defines public index-by-var-name and index-by-ns+var helpers.
- Repository-wide exact-symbol searches find no executable call to either helper: index-by-var-name appears only in its definition and a stale doc_api_check.clj comment; index-by-ns+var appears only in its definition and historical duplicate-row comments in gen.clj/gen_test.clj.
- Both date to the initial projection module (commit 70a1b11bc2) and targeted history finds no consumer. Live checks build purpose-specific sets/indexes instead: API.md needs tier sets, docs need a bare-name set, and Xray needs a strict [namespace var] set.
- index-by-ns+var uses assoc and would overwrite duplicates; generation now rejects duplicate [namespace var] rows before projection.

Impact
These public helpers imply a shared projection contract that no caller uses and whose value shapes do not match current validators. Their stale references obscure which duplicate and name-resolution semantics each checker actually relies on.

Recommendation
Delete both helpers and rewrite the three historical/doc comments to describe the live purpose-specific projections rather than nonexistent functions.

Risks / contracts
Do not consolidate live checker indexes merely to retain these helpers: bare-name latitude, tier sets, strict namespace identity, and duplicate rejection are distinct contracts. Confirm there is no external consumer of this internal, unpublished JVM tool namespace.
acceptance_criteria:
- projection.clj no longer defines index-by-var-name or index-by-ns+var, and repository search finds no stale symbol references.
- doc_api_check.clj and duplicate-generation commentary accurately name the live set/index behavior.
- Bare-name docs resolution, strict Xray resolution, API.md tier checking, and duplicate [namespace var] rejection retain their existing tests and semantics.
- clojure -M:test passes in implementation/scripts/api-manifest with 0 failures/errors.
close_reason: Deleted index-by-var-name and index-by-ns+var from api_manifest/projection.clj; the three stale references now name the live purpose-specific projections (doc_api_check.clj builds a bare-name SET; gen.clj and gen_test.clj duplicate-generation commentary now cite xray-spec-check's strict [namespace var] SET, which cannot represent a duplicate at all). A note at the deletion site records why there is deliberately no shared index - bare-name latitude, tier sets, strict namespace identity and duplicate rejection are distinct contracts, and bare-name resolution is unsound for the Xray panels where ten namespaces carry the same :var Panel. title: Remove unnecessary re-frame adapter boot from the machines-viz viewer
description:
Evidence
- page/.../viewer.cljs calls rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter, then mounts viewer-view directly with reagent.dom.client/create-root and render. It registers no frame, event, subscription, or re-frame view.
- MachineChart is a Reagent component and does not consult re-frame.core or the installed substrate adapter. The chart DOM suite independently mounts that same component through adapters.react-chart/chart-element plus raw react-dom/client createRoot without rf/init!, proving adapter boot is not a rendering prerequisite.
- The only machines-viz require/use of re-frame.adapter.reagent is this viewer. The :cljs-test alias carries day8/re-frame2-reagent solely to compile it.
- rf/init! installs a framework substrate and reseeds framework registrations; it does not initialise Reagent rendering. The viewer's direct Reagent root already does that.
- The mistaken rationale dates to initial viewer commit 9644e0b4d8 and now drives lengthy coupling commentary across viewer.cljs, deps.edn, README.md, and API.md.

Impact
A presentation-only static viewer performs unrelated framework-global boot, loads an adapter dependency, and documents a false requirement. This increases bundle/classpath coupling and makes embedding/reusing the page more stateful than its no-runtime contract promises.

Recommendation
Remove the re-frame.core and re-frame.adapter.reagent requires and the rf/init! call from viewer/run; remove day8/re-frame2-reagent from :cljs-test; update the affected docs to say the page mounts Reagent directly. Keep viewer.cljs in page/ because it remains an application entry and non-jar delivery surface.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the main day8/re-frame2 dependency: library namespaces still use re-frame.error, trace, and interop. Preserve the exported run symbol, URL decoding, DOM output, read-only behavior, page/source-root split, and staged viewer artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- viewer/run mounts with reagent.dom.client only and has no re-frame adapter/core boot call.
- No machines-viz dependency alias declares day8/re-frame2-reagent solely for the viewer.
- Viewer and dependency documentation no longer claims Reagent rendering requires rf/init!.
- page/ remains excluded from the published jar and included in the viewer build/test classpath.
- Viewer unit/DOM tests and npm run build:machines-viz-viewer pass; the staged HTML finds a callable exported run and renders valid share URLs.

title: mcp-base/args: retire or justify orphaned parse-non-negative-int
description:
Evidence
- A repository-wide exact-symbol search on 2026-09-03 finds `parse-non-negative-int` only in tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc, its own args/CLJS tests, and tools/mcp-base/spec/args.md. No production namespace in implementation/, tools/, examples/, skills/, scripts/, or CI consumes it.
- The last actual production call was story-mcp's `record-as-variant` duration parser. Commit ff0b7c3e02 (2026-09-01) deleted that transport-unreachable blocking recorder and its call `(args/parse-non-negative-int (:duration-ms arguments) 0)`.
- Pair-mcp's former progress-stream subsystem had its own result-returning `parse-non-negative-int-arg`, not this base helper; commit 89bb4d49f1 removed that subsystem too. Current numeric consumers use parse-positive-int, cursor/parse-limit-arg, cap/max-tokens, or coerce-finite-long directly.
- The function remains advertised in the published mcp-base parser catalogue and keeps dedicated JVM/CLJS regression cases, so this is maintained public surface with no in-repo behavior depending on it.

Impact
Every numeric-domain change must continue preserving and testing an otherwise unused zero-admitting coercion contract. That adds API/spec/test surface and obscures which shared parsers actually serve the two MCPs.

Recommendation
Make an explicit compatibility-aware disposition. If no known external `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base` consumer needs the var, deprecate/remove `parse-non-negative-int` and its dedicated catalogue/tests in the next permitted pre-alpha/library release, retaining the shared `coerce-finite-long` used by live callers. If external use is intentional, document that supported consumer and add a consumer-level contract pin so the surface is no longer justified only by itself.

Risks / contracts
mcp-base is a separately published Clojars library and this is a public var, so do not silently delete it without checking the release/back-compat posture. Removing the helper must not change parse-positive-int, cursor pagination, max-token validation, or cross-host finite/safe-integer behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- A repo-wide consumer inventory and release/back-compat decision is recorded.
- Either the orphan var plus only its dedicated spec/tests are removed/deprecated, or a real supported consumer and consumer-level test justify retaining it.
- Live numeric parsers preserve JVM/CLJS finite, safe-integer, defaulting, and clamping contracts.
- mcp-base JVM and CLJS suites and relevant MCP consumer/conformance gates pass.
notes: Audit of PR #9087: the recorded census still shows no production consumer, and current origin/main contains this public var only in its catalogue, definition, and self-tests. The Bead acceptance criteria permit retention only with a real supported consumer and consumer-level test; the new justification instead cites parse-int*'s floor parameter and a hypothetical future zero-admitting argument. That is circular/speculative maintenance, not a live contract. Under the pre-alpha minimal-API posture, remove/deprecate the orphan and its dedicated catalogue/tests unless an actual external consumer can be named and pinned. The other three PR cleanups are sound.
close_reason: PR #9109 (b4238a79c5). Worked the PR #9087 audit ruling, which REJECTED the keep-with-justification disposition: removed the public parse-non-negative-int, its spec/args.md catalogue bullet, surface-table row and cross-runtime-domain mention, its four dedicated JVM deftests and two CLJS assertions; parse-int* loses the now-constant floor parameter with it. title: Remove superseded test-quiet green subprocess rows
description:
## Vestigial test coverage

Two green subprocess rows in the test-quiet contract suites are strictly superseded by stronger rows that execute the same production paths. They add no unique assertion but retain real process-start cost.

## Evidence

### JVM

- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_runner_contract_test.clj:189-209` (`green-runner-contract`) creates one passing fixture, invokes the real runner, then asserts exit 0, absence of `Running tests in`, at most three nonblank lines, and the `0 failures, 0 errors.` tally.
- Lines 222-258 (`green-runner-exact-shape`) create the same one-test passing suite and invoke the same `run-runner` path. They assert exit 0, absence of the identical `Running tests in` marker, exactly two nonblank lines, `Ran ...` first, the exact zero tally second, and the single permitted leading blank. Every assertion made by the older row follows from these stronger assertions.
- History shows the generic row arrived in `953dffc80d`; the exact-shape regression arrived the next day in `f1ce33adbd` and did not retire the superseded row. `green-runner-contract` has no references or distinct fixture semantics elsewhere.

### CLJS

- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:487-518` (`real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet`) spawns `--test=re-frame.test-quiet-green-fixture-cljs-test` and asserts no spawn error, exit 0, canonical summary-only output, no `Unknown arg`, no `Testing` banner, a `Ran ...` line, and the zero tally.
- Lines 563-575, the clean negative control inside `unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green`, spawn that exact same argument and assert only no spawn error, exit 0, and no `Unknown arg`. Those are a strict subset of the earlier real-green row's assertions; the malformed plural and space-separated argument cases remain independently covered at lines 527-562.
- History shows the real green row arrived in `cdd684b2ec`; the weaker duplicate was added later in `23442f1c76` as a local negative control.
- The suite documents at lines 355-390 that every CLJS spawn reloads a 4,201-module / 484 MB dev build and has measured healthy runtimes from roughly 10 seconds to 449 seconds under load. Removing an exact duplicate therefore has material gate value.
- All-state bead searches for both test names, green runner shape, clean focused invocation, duplicate child process/spawn, and superseded green coverage found no existing issue.

## Impact

The redundant rows lengthen routine JVM and especially CLJS contract runs without expanding behavioral coverage. They also split the authoritative green-output contract across weaker and stronger tests, making future maintainers compare duplicate fixtures before knowing which assertion set is definitive.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `green-runner-contract` and retain `green-runner-exact-shape` as the single JVM one-test green process contract. Delete the clean focused-invocation branch from `unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green` and retain `real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet` as the single CLJS valid-selector/green-output control. If locality is valuable, reference the authoritative green test in a comment rather than spawning the fixture again.

## Risks / retained contracts

Do not merge genuinely distinct red, namespace-load, fixture-error, malformed-argument, unmatched-selector, timeout, warning-replay, or multi-test rows. Retain a real process boundary once per runtime, the exact JVM leading-blank contract, the CLJS valid `--test=` parser/runner path, canonical green summary assertions, platform newline normalization, and useful failure diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `green-runner-contract` is removed; `green-runner-exact-shape` remains the sole JVM one-passing-test subprocess row and still proves exit 0, no discovery banner, one leading blank, exactly `Ran ...` plus the zero tally, and cross-platform CRLF normalization.
2. The clean focused-invocation branch at CLJS lines 563-575 is removed; `real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet` remains and still invokes the exact valid green selector, rejects spawn errors, requires exit 0, rejects `Unknown arg`/`Testing`/other non-summary output, and requires `Ran ...` plus the zero tally.
3. Both malformed-argument branches still prove nonzero status, name their offending tokens, and prove the suite did not run.
4. No distinct red/error/timeout/replay/discovery/lifecycle process row is removed.
5. The relevant JVM and consolidated CLJS contract suites pass, with one fewer JVM runner process and one fewer CLJS runner process than before.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held on both rows; each successor named and its pins quoted. JVM: green-runner-contract removed. Successor green-runner-exact-shape spawns the same one-passing-test fixture through the same -main and asserts strictly more - (is (zero? exit)), (is (not (str/includes? out "Running tests in"))) which is literally discovery-banner-marker's value, (is (= 2 (count non-blank))) subsuming the old <=3, (is (str/blank? (nth lines 0 nil))), (is (str/starts-with? (first non-blank) "Ran ")), (is (= "0 failures, 0 errors." (second non-blank))) subsuming the old str/includes?, over lines CRLF-normalised by (str/replace out "\r" ""). Every clause of the deleted row follows. CLJS: the clean-focused-invocation branch of unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green removed. It spawned the exact same --test=re-frame.test-quiet-green-fixture-cljs-test invocation real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet already spawns and asserted a strict subset (nil err, zero status, no 'Unknown arg'); that row also pins canonical-lines-only, no Testing banner, Ran 2 tests, and the zero tally. Both malformed-argument branches and every distinct red/error/timeout/replay/lifecycle row kept. Each deletion leaves a comment naming the surviving row. JVM suite 53 tests / 275 assertions exit 0; the CLJS rows green.

title: Test-React tests: retire the superseded duplicate cache-lifecycle case
description:
## Finding

The single-frame dispose/reinstall cache regression is maintained twice under `implementation/adapters/test-react/test/` even though both copies now run on both hosts:

- `test_react_cljs_test.cljc:240-312` defines `default-sub-cache-keys`, `default-entry-ref-count`, and `dispose-adapter-clears-frame-sub-cache-no-stale-cross-lifecycle-reads`.
- `test_react_dispose_sub_cache_cljs_test.cljc:35-72` defines the same two queries and `dispose-adapter-clears-sub-cache-and-recomputes-fresh`.

Both cases register the same seed event/sub, seed `1`, materialise `[::n]` at ref-count 1, dispose, assert the slot/ref-count vanished, reinstall, seed `99`, and prove a fresh subscription reads 99 at ref-count 1. The companion docstring says this directly: "The substantive assertion lives in both" (`:5`) and identifies its only unique coverage as the second multi-frame case (`:16-18`).

## Supersession evidence

Commit `bd492e37c9` added both copies because the then-main namespace was `re-frame.adapter.test-react-test`: Cognitect discovered it on the JVM, while Shadow's `cljs-test$` selector did not, so the separate `-cljs-test` namespace supplied CLJS coverage. Commit `1a14917bda` renamed the main namespace/file to `test-react-cljs-test` specifically so that whole suite also runs under Shadow. Commit `1708179722` then removed the old JVM-only rationale but retained the duplicate. Today both files end in `-cljs-test`, both are `.cljc`, `clojure -M:test` discovers both, and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:650-653` selects both. The current standalone run is green at 35 tests / 160 assertions.

## Impact

The same seven assertions and setup/teardown execute and must be maintained twice on the JVM and twice in Node. The copies already use different lifecycle fixtures (hand-reset state in the main suite versus `make-reset-runtime-fixture` in the cache companion), so a future edit can create apparent coverage while only one copy matches the real fixture contract. The main copy also keeps three otherwise-unused requires (`re-frame.core`, `re-frame.subs`, `re-frame.frame`) and two one-consumer helpers in the lifecycle suite.

## Disposition

Keep the focused cache companion as the owner of both cache tests: retain its single-frame fresh-recompute case and its unique every-live-frame case, and delete the duplicated cache section/helpers from the main lifecycle suite. Remove imports made dead by that deletion. While touching these two test ns forms, remove the unreferenced `:as ctest` aliases (the referred test vars remain) and replace the seed handlers' unread `{:keys [db]}` bindings; clj-kondo currently reports the three unread `db` bindings at main `:264` and companion `:47,78` (the main one disappears with the duplicate). Do not weaken or delete the companion's multi-frame assertion.

## Risks and boundaries

This is test consolidation only. Preserve `dispose-adapter!`'s all-frame cache clearing, ref-count removal, reinstall freshness, JVM+CLJS coverage, and the standard fixture. Do not simplify the lifecycle simulator or fold the two genuinely different single-frame/multi-frame cache properties into one opaque assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Exactly one single-frame dispose/reinstall/fresh-recompute regression remains, alongside the existing multi-frame regression.
2. `test_react_cljs_test.cljc` no longer contains the duplicate cache helpers/test or its now-dead `rf`/`subs`/`frame` requires; both test namespace forms carry no unused `ctest` alias or unread seed-handler binding.
3. `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/adapters/test-react` passes with the expected duplicate removed (currently 34 tests / 153 assertions), and `npm run test:cljs` or a focused Shadow run proves both surviving Test-React namespaces execute under CLJS.
4. Any hard-coded Test-React suite counts in `TESTING.md` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` are updated from actual runner output.
5. The multi-frame case still fails under a negative control that clears only `:rf/default`, proving consolidation did not erase the all-frame tooth.

title: Remove the inert internal RouteAddress schema constant
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/address.cljc` defines a public `RouteAddress` Malli-form value, but routing never reads it. Validation is independently hand-coded in `valid-address?`; the optional Schemas artefact does not import it; and the API-manifest generator classifies `re-frame.routing.address` as internal rather than an authoring namespace. The value is therefore a second, inert spelling of the route-address contract.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide symbol search finds code symbol `RouteAddress` only at `address.cljc:99`; every other hit is prose or the separate normative schema example in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`.
- `clj-kondo` whole-routing analysis reports zero var usages for `re-frame.routing.address/RouteAddress` in both source and tests.
- `valid-address?` checks `address-keys`, `:to`, `:params`, `:query`, and `:fragment` directly and never derives behavior from the Malli form.
- No namespace under `implementation/schemas/src`, core, tools, examples, or skills requires or resolves this var.
- `re-frame.routing` deliberately does not re-export address internals (`routing.cljc:89-96`), and the API-manifest generator puts `re-frame.routing.address` on its internal-namespace roster (`gen.clj:363-388`).
- Git history shows the value arrived with EP-0037 R0b in `da9c355466`; no later commit introduced a consumer.

## Impact

The dead value adds an apparent schema authority that has no enforcement role and can drift from both `valid-address?` and the normative `:rf/route-address` schema text. Because it is a public var in an internal namespace, it also creates an accidental surface that readers may mistake for a supported schema API.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the unused `RouteAddress` var and revise the nearby comments/docstrings to point to the normative `:rf/route-address` schema plus the live `valid-address?` structural gate. Do not change the accepted address shape or add a Malli dependency to the routing hot path merely to preserve the dead constant.

## Risks

Although the namespace is explicitly internal and has no in-repo consumer, search release notes and migration/API docs once more before deletion for any intentional promise of the var itself. Preserve the route-address behavior and the normative schema; this is removal of an inert implementation symbol, not removal of the RouteAddress concept.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `re-frame.routing.address/RouteAddress` is removed, while `valid-address?` accepts/rejects exactly the currently documented closed shape.
2. Address comments and docs no longer imply that routing carries or executes a Malli-form value it does not consume.
3. Focused routing address/prefetch/route-url tests pass on both relevant hosts, including closed-key, required `:to`, and typed optional-field cases.
4. API-manifest and repo-wide symbol checks show no promised public row or remaining code reference to the removed var.
5. The normative `:rf/route-address` schema in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` remains unchanged unless an independently justified contract change is made.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip: a repo-wide search found the CODE symbol RouteAddress only at address.cljc:99 and at spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3732 (the normative schema example); every other hit is prose. No qualified (address/RouteAddress) or :refer consumer exists anywhere in implementation, tools, examples or skills. Deleted the def and replaced it with a comment pointing at the two real authorities — the normative :rf/route-address schema and the live valid-address? structural gate. The accepted address shape is unchanged and no Malli dependency was added. The hot-zone spec/Spec-Schemas.md normative example was NOT touched, per the bead's own caution. Gate: implementation/routing clojure -M:test exit 0, 553 tests / 3451 assertions / 0 failures, covering the address-extraction, prefetch and route-url closed-key, required-:to and typed-optional cases. No api-manifest row and no docs/api page named the removed var, so neither needed an edit.

title: conformance fixture loaders: an early ] escapes the one-form guard and hides trailing EDN
description:
FOLLOW-ON to rf2-x91a, which landed shape (a) - the corpus scanner - in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9038 and left shape (b) unbuilt.

rf2-x91a PREFERS (b): make the loaders themselves refuse trailing text, because a loader check cannot drift from what the runner actually parses. That was out of the landing dispatch's fence (implementation/**), so only (a) was built. (a) satisfies rf2-x91a's acceptance - a misplaced brace now fails a gate that runs on every PR - and it holds one advantage (b) can never have: a fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in it is invisible to any load-time check forever. The two are complementary, not alternatives.

title: MIGRATION.md M-51 calls the unary reg-fx failure a language-level arity error; the skill's three leaves class it SILENT on CLJS (the failure-visibility axis that picks the sweep method)
notes:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING rf2-a75ai (PR #9010), which added an M-51 section to skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md. Not fixed there: MIGRATION.md is a one-toucher hot-zone file and the worker's write scope was skills/re-frame-migration/** only.

THE TENSION.
- CORPUS, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1984 (inside M-51, heading :1980, Type line :1982 'Type A - pre-1.0 spec lock; mechanical rewrite.'): 'The runtime invokes every registered fx handler with two args; a unary handler raises a language-level arity error at the call site (ArityException on JVM, TypeError / "Cannot read ... of undefined" or similar on CLJS depending on shape).' That leads with the LOUD reading.
- SKILL, three leaves, mutually consistent and all SILENT for CLJS:
  - breaking-changes.md:208 (failure-visibility axis row): 'on CLJS (no arity check) the runtime context-map binds to args and the real fx args are silently dropped - the handler runs against the wrong value, no error (on JVM it throws an ArityException - loud - but v1 migration targets are CLJS)'.
  - inventory-and-plan.md:66 lists 'unary reg-fx handlers -> M-51' among the rules that 'compile clean and break only at runtime'; :81 repeats the silent-drop mechanism.
  - sequencing.md:82 row 14a: 'Type A but SILENT-fail - so swept by an exhaustive up-front grep'.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic). Loud-vs-silent is the axis that selects the SWEEP METHOD, and the skill says so explicitly: silent-fail rules get an exhaustive up-front grep and 'never march-the-wall', because a loud rule can be found by following compile/runtime errors while a silent one cannot. A reader who takes the corpus sentence at face value would conclude M-51 is discoverable by running the app and reading errors, and could legitimately skip the exhaustive grep - on a rule that fires in nearly every real v1 app with a custom reg-fx.

WHICH SIDE LOOKS RIGHT. The skill's, on CLJS. A single-arity CLJS (fn [request] ...) compiles to a one-parameter JS function; JS silently ignores extra arguments, so the v2 call with two args binds the CONTEXT MAP to request and drops the real fx args, with no ArityException and no TypeError at the call site. Any TypeError arrives LATER and elsewhere - when the handler destructures the context map and downstream code uses the nils - which is a different failure at a different place from 'at the call site'. The corpus's JVM half (ArityException) is correct; note the skill's own remark that v1 migration targets are CLJS. The corpus does hedge with 'or similar ... depending on shape', so this is an emphasis/accuracy problem rather than a flat contradiction - but the sentence's leading clause is the part a reader acts on.

SUGGESTED FIX (corpus side, one sentence, whoever holds the MIGRATION.md token next): split the claim by platform rather than presenting one failure with a parenthetical - JVM raises ArityException (loud); CLJS raises nothing at the call site, binds the context map to the unary parameter and silently drops the real fx args, surfacing later as wrong-value behaviour. Then M-51's existing rg -U sweep and 'apply to every unary reg-fx handler' instruction read as the consequence they already are.

NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME by this worker - the reasoning above is from CLJS/JS calling semantics plus the skill's three concurring statements, not from an executed repro. Anyone actioning this should confirm with a two-arg call into a single-arity CLJS fn before rewording the corpus.
FIXED in PR #9026 (worker cluster corpus-b). The bead's author flagged this as NOT verified at runtime; it has now been EXECUTED, and the skill's three leaves are confirmed right while the corpus was wrong. Probe: ClojureScript 1.12.145 on Node v24 via cljs.main -re node. A single-fixed-arity (fn [request] ...) reached through a registry lookup — the real fx path — called with two args threw NOTHING at the call site: it returned normally, the context map bound to the unary parameter (verified equal to the context map), and the real fx args were dropped. A statically-known direct call produced only a COMPILER WARNING ('Wrong number of args (2) passed to ...') and still no runtime throw; that warning does not reach the fx path, because there the call goes through a registry lookup, so on the path that matters nothing warns and nothing throws. CONTROL that makes the silence a finding rather than a swallowed exception: a MULTI-arity CLJS fn called at an unsupported arity DID throw 'Invalid arity: 3', so the probe can see throws. Downstream, (:real wrongly-bound) is nil. The corpus sentence is now split by platform — JVM ArityException (loud), CLJS silent — and M-51 is marked a silent-fail rule so its existing exhaustive rg -U sweep reads as the consequence it already is. skills/re-frame-migration/** deliberately untouched: its three leaves were already correct, so there is nothing to file against the skill.
close_reason: M-51's failure-visibility sentence split by platform in PR #9026 and marked a silent-fail rule. Executed CLJS probe (cljs 1.12.145 on Node): a unary handler called with two args through a registry lookup throws nothing, binds the context map to the unary param and drops the fx args; multi-arity control DID throw 'Invalid arity: 3'. The skill's three leaves were correct, so nothing filed against the skill.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): post-error trigger names 'red CI' while §Session evidence excludes CI runs, and never names the :ok? false / :reason envelopes and :rf.error/:rf.epoch traces the pair tools actually raise
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

Post-error trigger (b) is defined in four places with "red CI" as a firing condition:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:11-12` (frontmatter description): "**post-error within a re-frame2-pair session** — after a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or a runtime error during live pair work"
- `SKILL.md:37`: "a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or an `:rf.error/*` event fired during live re-frame2-pair work"
- `spec/design.md:106` and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:55` repeat "red CI".

But `SKILL.md:72` (§Session evidence): "**Exclude unrelated activity.** Background workers, CI runs, shell commands, code-review threads, and app-authoring edits are out of scope unless the user explicitly names one as pair-session friction."

## TRUTH AT TIP

A CI run is not something a pair tool raises, and the family disqualifier `skills/README.md:166` puts "post-mortems on shell sessions, IDE workflows, or test-suite runs" out of scope. What the pair tools DO raise, and what a post-error offer should recognise:

- `{:ok? false :reason <kw>}` envelopes — the discover-app ladder `:nrepl-unreachable` / `:build-not-running` / `:no-runtime-connected` / `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:302-310`), `:ambiguous-frame` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:173`), `:restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`), `:reset-rejected` (`tools/replace_app_db.cljs:114`), `:missing-baseline` / `:baseline-without-probe` (`tools/tail_build.cljs:148,172`), `:debug-disabled` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:8`).
- Error trace ops — `:rf.error/*` (`errors.md:43-47`, e.g. `:rf.error/handler-exception`) and the seven `restore-epoch!` failure ops (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`, six `:rf.epoch/restore-*` plus `:rf.error/no-such-handler` kind `:frame`).

The existing evals already model the boundary correctly (ids 4, 17, 18 positive; id 19 "wants it FIXED" negative) and none uses CI.

## IMPACT

The trigger admits an input (a red CI run) that the skill's own evidence rules then discard, so the offer fires with nothing to retro; and it gives the agent no vocabulary for the failures that SHOULD fire it — a refused write or a ladder miss looks like "ordinary pair operation" under the current wording, so the post-error offer under-fires exactly where pair friction is densest.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR: drop "red CI" from the four sites and define (b) in one clause — "a pair tool returned `:ok? false` with a `:reason`, or an `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace fired, during live re-frame2-pair work" — without restating the reason catalogue (that is the pair skill's errors.md). Keep "stack trace" (a handler exception is a runtime error). No evals change required; re-score ids 4, 17, 18, 19 by reading.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py` (description edited; evals untouched) and `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` (SKILL.md re-read). Prose by hand.

## ACCEPTANCE

No occurrence of "red CI" under `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/`; trigger (b) names the `:ok? false`/`:reason` envelope and the `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace families; §Session evidence :72 unchanged; both gates exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): correct deferred effect-map candidate for classification effects and fail-closed refusal
description:
CLAIM. The catalogue (`references/README.md:7-14`) is 6 leaves; `spec/design.md` §4 "Deferred catalogue candidates" (`:86-91`) holds 2. Compared against the 15 pattern leaves under `skills/re-frame2/patterns/`, the fundamentals leaves, `spec/Principles.md`, and Mike's standing rules (frames are isolated contexts; no raw atoms through views; no frame-ids as view args; no over-engineering), the common consumer misuses below have no leaf and are not queued. L6 (`design.md:57`) says a leaf lands only after 3+ real reviews — so the landable shape is the DEFERRED LIST, ranked, with detection signals, so the growth procedure has a queue rather than a blank.

TRUTH AT TIP — 13 candidates, ranked (source that discourages it -> canonical idiom):
1. Frame leakage / frame-ids as view args — a sub or handler reading another frame (`rf/app-db-value other-frame` in a sub; `(rf/dispatch ... {:frame :other})` from inside a handler of a different frame; views taking `frame-id` args and threading `capture-frame`). `fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`; Mike's rule "frames are isolated contexts". Already deferred as "foreign-frame write"; widen to reads + view args. Signals: `app-db-value` / `{:frame ...}` inside `reg-sub` / `reg-event` bodies; view params named `frame` / `frame-id`.
2. Views that fetch / boot in a mount hook — `:component-did-mount`, `use-effect`, `r/with-let` init dispatching `:*/load` / `:*/fetch` / `[:rf.resource/ensure ...]`. `patterns/resources.md:9,29` ("views are passive reads — they never trigger a fetch"), `patterns/boot.md:138` ("Boot logic in a view's `:on-mount`"). Fix: route entry / `:initial-events` / machine `:entry`.
3. Secrets in machine `:data` or `app-db` — bearer/refresh tokens in `:data`, passwords retained in a form's `:submitted` / `:draft`. `patterns/websocket.md:30,216`, `patterns/forms.md:34-36`. Signals: `:token` / `:bearer` / `:password` keys assoc'd into `:data` / db without `:sensitive`.
4. App code reading runtime-db through `:db` — `(get-in db [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots ...])` in a sub/handler instead of `[:rf/machine id]` / `[:rf.route/*]`. `fundamentals/frames.md:33`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md:146` (MUST NOT). Greppable: `:rf.runtime/` in app source.

## Scope (fence)

- `docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md`: a Ring-hosted section (the sidecar path).

- `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE) + `implementation/api-manifest.edn` + `implementation/api-manifest-metadata.edn`: every new public symbol — `:renderer`, `:render-state`, `re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer`, `re-frame.ssr.render-state`, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (or their landed names).

- The release/distribution roster: locate by grepping `re-frame2-ssr-ring` under `.github/workflows/` and `scripts/`; add the ssr-node package wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated.

## Acceptance

1. ONE recipe covering: build (client + `:node-library` server bundle), entry-table declaration (`stateAllowlist` + runtime allowlist), renderer selection (`:renderer`), state projection (`:render-state` vs `:payload` — why they differ), startup (the `serve` command and its ready line), hydration (`identifierPrefix`), and build-id skew.
2. Every code sample is pasteable against the merged code (run each once).
3. Manifests agree with the shipped surface — `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` is the arbiter.
4. The deployment posture from the ruling's S7 is in the recipe: loopback default, render state may carry server-only values, a remote sidecar is the operator's transport to secure; the adapter does not refuse.

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`mkdocs build --strict` (covers `docs/core/**`, `docs/ssr/**`, `docs/api/**`; NOT `docs/design/**` and NOT heading anchors — check those by hand and say so), `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (the ssr-node README and the example README are its surface, not the docs gate's), `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` for the changed page under `docs/design/hicasso/`, and the api-manifest gate from `implementation/package.json`.

## Traps

`docs/design/hicasso/` reports doc links INSIDE fences (its fences are pasteable deliverables). Guide code blocks under `docs/core/` may be digest-pinned — check `samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj`-style pins before editing any existing fence. Neither link gate reads inside a fence, so verify fenced links by hand. No `git stash`; commit then rebase. Worker worktree guard first; report `WORKTREE_ROOT`.

title: [uix] adapter/wrap-view is also consulted at registration, so a pre-init registration misses the substrate wrap
description:
## Scope

The :adapter/wrap-view (rf2-00li) consultation in views/apply-adapter-wrap-view, on the same registration pipeline rf2-oz7wr fixed one layer above.

## Finding

Found while fixing rf2-oz7wr and deliberately left out of that PR (#8909) rather than widening it.

:adapter/wrap-view is published through substrate-adapter/route-hook!, so like :adapter/componentize-view it answers only while ITS adapter is the rf/init!-installed one. views/apply-adapter-wrap-view consults it at REGISTRATION. Under the canonical boot order in docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md the registration namespaces load first and run calls rf/init! afterwards, so under UIx a top-level reg-view* gets nil back, wrap-applied? is false, and build-frame-aware-view falls through to the inline hiccup walk (source-coord/inject-source-coord-attr).

That walk exists for Reagent hiccup. On UIx the render-fn output is a React element, which is precisely why the UIx adapter publishes wrap-view at all — its own cloneElement path. The docstring on apply-adapter-wrap-view says the inline walk mis-classifies such a root and skips annotation.

## Severity, and why it is P3 rather than P2

Dev-only degradation, not a mount failure: the affected surface is the data-rf2-source-coord attribute (click-to-source in Xray and re-frame2-pair), which is elided from production builds anyway. Nothing throws and nothing renders wrongly. Contrast rf2-oz7wr, where the same routing/ordering mismatch made the advertised mount impossible.

## Suggested repair

rf2-oz7wr's fix moved the componentize step to lookup and memoized it on (wrapper identity x adapter spec) in views/view-head. wrap-view cannot simply move there — it is composed BELOW the frame-aware wrapper, so re-deriving it means rebuilding the wrapper, which changes the wrapper's object identity and therefore the cached head's. That is workable (re-derive the whole pipeline from the original render-fn, keyed the same way) but it is a bigger change than rf2-oz7wr's, and it needs its own check on what depends on wrapper identity across a re-derivation.

## Verification

Confirm before building: plant a top-level reg-view* under UIx, mount it, and read the rendered root for data-rf2-source-coord. Assert the attribute is ABSENT pre-fix and PRESENT post-fix, in a browser row (the annotation is a real-DOM fact).
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8919)

Dev-only classification: HOLDS at source, but the extent is wider than the description states. The spine's wrap-view body sits entirely inside (if interop/debug-enabled? ... user-fn), so :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false collapses it to the bare user-fn either way -- nothing throws, nothing renders wrongly, no production behaviour differs. P3 is right. But declining the wrap costs FOUR things, not one:
  1. data-rf2-source-coord -- the annotation the description names.
  2. data-rf-view -- Spec 006 view tagging contract, the view-hierarchy fallback when Fiber inspection is unavailable.
  3. the React-hook unmount sentinel (rf2-te71r), so :rf.view/unmounted never fires for that view. interop/make-reaction returns nil on a React-hook substrate, so the phase-A reaction-dispose hook cannot cover for it.
  4. a one-shot console.warn asserting the root element is not a DOM root -- about a view whose root is an ordinary span. The only one of the four that is actively misleading rather than merely missing.

Mechanism: REUSED #8909's lookup-time mechanism rather than building a second one, by generalising it. The description is right that wrap-view cannot simply move to view-head as-is: it composes BELOW the frame-aware wrapper where the shell composes ABOVE it, so re-deriving the wrap means rebuilding the wrapper, and rebuilding the wrapper means re-deriving the shell. That is an argument for ONE derivation, not for a parallel one. compose-view runs apply-adapter-wrap-view, view-coord-attr, build-frame-aware-view and apply-adapter-componentize-view against the adapter installed at call time; reg-view* runs it once to seed, view-head re-runs it when the seed was taken against a different substrate.

Two consequences the description's what-depends-on-wrapper-identity question asked for:
  - The cache key moved. #8909 matched the slot's handler-fn against either face of the entry (wrapper or head) because its re-derivation KEPT the wrapper object. This one rebuilds it, which would fail that check on every lookup and mint a fresh component type each render. The entry now records :registered, the exact object registration stored in the slot, and matches identity against that. One key instead of two faces.
  - Reagent keeps its object. A re-derivation whose wrap answer was nil before and is nil now has identical inputs to build-frame-aware-view, so it reuses the previous wrapper outright. Reagent publishes neither hook, so it takes that branch in every ordering and (rf/view id) hands back the very object registration built. Reagent behaviour unchanged; the Reagent adapter was not touched.
The registrar slot is still not rewritten on the lazy upgrade -- registrar/register! emits :rf.registry/handler-replaced on every call, and a phantom hot-reload on the first lookup after boot would be worse than the bug.

Evidence: new browser file implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs, three rows, asserting on the OUTPUT. reg-time-composition-is-unwrapped-while-the-lookup-is-not is the ABSENT half on the same registration (registration runs at ns-load with no adapter, premise asserted; the value registration stored is still readable and invoking it directly yields a root with NO data-rf2-source-coord, while the head (rf/view id) hands back post-init yields an annotated one). boot-order-registration-annotates-the-mounted-root is the PRESENT half as a real-DOM fact -- mounted through the documented route and read back off the committed node with getAttribute, plus a console check that the false non-DOM-root warning is gone. post-init-control-annotates-the-mounted-root is the non-vacuity control.

Gates, captured exit codes, on the rebased base: node-test compile 0 (1870 files, 0 warnings); node out/node-test.js 0 (11129 tests / 54979 assertions, 0 failures); shadow-cljs compile browser-test 0 (1012 files, 0 warnings); serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs 0 (760 tests / 4168 assertions, 0 failures); clojure -M:test -n re-frame.late-bind-drift-test 0 (8 tests / 686 assertions). No markdown changed, so neither check_doc_slugs.py nor check_readme_links.py has a surface here.

Controls, both red: (a) planting the pre-fix behaviour -- always reuse the reg-time wrapper, which is #8909's shape -- gave exit 1, 5 failures, ALL in the two boot-order rows, with both attributes nil off the committed node and the false warning back verbatim naming a span root; the post-init control and every #8909 row stayed green. (b) restoring #8909's own defect under the new structure gave exit 1, 11 failures and 1 error, with boot-order-registration-yields-a-mountable-head-after-init contributing 9 -- the same count #8909's own plant produced, so this change has not defanged it. Both plants recompiled 314 files; both restores verified by git blob hash against the committed object.

Two stale prose spots found and deliberately LEFT (both outside the fence, neither load-bearing for any assertion): implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/view_alias_registry_cljs_test.cljs says core consults :adapter/wrap-view AT REGISTRATION TIME, now registration-and-lookup; and the late-bind directory lists re-frame.hicasso.substrate as a :adapter/wrap-view producer, which is true only transitively (hicasso reaches it through spine/make-react-adapter, not by its own route-hook! call).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8919. compose-view now runs the WHOLE registration pipeline against the adapter installed at call time; reg-view* seeds it, views/view-head re-runs it when the seed was taken against a different substrate, and memoizes. One derivation serves both routed hooks rather than a second parallel mechanism.

title: implementation/machines: line-broken rf/machine-by-system-id survived the prefix sweep
description:
Residue deliberately left out of scope by rf2-wrzfb (PR #8905), which corrected the
105 in-scope markdown sites. Census instrument and full breakdown are on that PR.

Three separate remainders, all measured at the same tip:

1. FIFTY-NINE hits inside SOURCE-FILE docstrings, comments and test-name strings
   (implementation/**, tools/**, and skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/**.cljs).
   Every one was inspected during rf2-wrzfb: they are all prose, never a live
   call -- the calls themselves already use the machines/... alias and compile.
   Touching source files is a gate-bearing change (check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py
   guards the skills preload), so it was left rather than bundled into a
   documentation PR. Note these files use the BARE leaf alias :as machines,
   which Conventions reserves for APPLICATION namespaces -- so a proper pass here
   is an alias question as well as a prefix one.

2. migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md section O-9 was MISSED by PR #8902.
   That PR corrected lines 1356 and 2335 to rf.machines/, but O-9 still teaches
   (rf/machine-by-system-id sid) at three sites (approx lines 2944, 2948, 2950).
   Worse, the same section teaches (rf/dispatch-to-system sid event) -- and there
   is NO dispatch-to-system var in spec/api-manifest.edn under any namespace.
   Only dispatch-to-system-fx exists (row 217, :facade? false). So that call
   resolves under no prefix at all. The action-side surface is the reserved
   [:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [system-id event]] fx tuple.
   Out of rf2-wrzfb's fence because PR #8902 had just landed in that file.

3. spec/Conventions.md carries two sites -- line 517 ((rf/machines) in the
   reserved-metadata-keys table) and line 612 (rf/machine-by-system-id prose in
   the reserved runtime-db slot table). Out of rf2-wrzfb's fence for the same
   reason: Conventions was the authority it followed, not a file it edited.

SEPARATELY, one shape contradiction found in passing and NOT fixed, because
resolving it needs a ruling rather than a spelling change:
tools/xray/spec/API.md line 454 documents (machines) as 0-ary returning a SEQ of
machine-ids, while line 873 of the same file describes the get-machine-list MCP
tool source as a MAP keyed by machine-id. The implementation settles the fn --
re-frame.machines/machines returns a vector (machines.cljc line 174), and the
pair runtime's machines-list wraps it in vec -- so line 873 is either describing
an xray-side projection or is simply wrong. rf2-wrzfb corrected the prefix on
both lines and left the shape claim untouched.
acceptance_criteria: The query-API comment names rf.machines/machine-by-system-id; a whitespace-spanning census that handles Clojure comment leaders finds no unintended rf/-prefixed machines-helper references, while preserving the deliberate fixture/emitted-symbol exclusions.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8912: reopened after completeness/correctness review. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc still describes the third query helper as (rf/machine-by- on one comment line and system-id sid) on the next. That is the same non-facade rf/machine-by-system-id spelling this Bead owned, split by a Clojure comment leader. It survives at the merged PR head and on current main even though the PR says all 56 intended source-prose sites were corrected and says its whitespace-spanning census found no extra sites. The nearby machines and machine-meta references were corrected, making the leftover especially misleading. Minimal fix: spell the split reference rf.machines/machine-by-system-id and re-run the class census with comment leaders/newlines represented so the three documented deliberate exclusions remain the only old-prefix hits; no new checker or API work is needed.
VERDICT rf2-lzrza (PR #8939) — CONFIRMED and FIXED. Both deliverables landed.

SITE, re-derived at tip (line numbers drift; these were read, not carried over).
implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc lines 168-169 before the fix:

  ;; id)` returns the registered machine's spec map; `(rf/machine-by-
  ;; system-id sid)` resolves the spawned-machine id currently bound to

Literal on disk: `rf/machine-by-` + newline + `;; ` + `system-id`. No
line-oriented search can see it at all — not with a better pattern, because a
line is the wrong unit.

WHY IT WAS WRONG, not merely non-canonical. spec/api-manifest.edn row 220 carries
machine-by-system-id on re-frame.machines with :facade? false, and re-frame.core
re-exports no such var. Its two siblings in the same paragraph had already been
corrected, so a reader met three references to one namespace with one of them
naming a namespace the var is not on.

FIX. Reflowed the query-API comment block so all three references read
`rf.machines/...` and none is split at a line boundary. `(rf.machines/machine-meta
id)` was already spelled correctly but was broken at the same kind of boundary —
that is the blind spot rather than the error, and leaving it split would leave the
next census the same hole. Comment-only; no API, behaviour or code change.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT (the real deliverable). Two passes, because neither result is a
superset of the other. LINE: each physical line on its own (what ripgrep sees).
FLAT: per file, each line's comment leader stripped (`;` `//` `#` `*` `>`, applied
repeatedly so `> ;; ` nests), lines joined with a single space, pattern tolerant of
whitespace at the `/` and at EVERY hyphen.

That last clause is the whole point, and it is where the pre-dispatch attempt went
wrong: stripping the leader and joining still leaves a SPACE between `by-` and
`system-id`, so a flattened search for the fixed literal still reports a clean
zero. The pattern is therefore built from the var name with \s*-\s* at each hyphen
rather than as a fixed string. Line-end hyphen, break at the `/`, and break at a
non-final hyphen are all covered. Class = the 23 vars read from
spec/api-manifest.edn at the tip being censused, not a hardcoded list.

TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS, both caught by the control rather than by inspection:
(1) the first draft's character class ended `...'-` and then had `:/` appended,

title: schemas: malli.error's message table survives Closure after the humanizer gating — ruling wanted on an out-of-graph mechanism
description:
Follow-up from rf2-tiymn (PR pending). Measured 2026-08-30 on the matched schemas-bundle A/B, all gzipped, control 86851 B:

- unconditional humanizer publication (trunk before rf2-tiymn): margin 41595 B
- publication gated on interop/debug-enabled? (what rf2-tiymn lands): margin 40885 B (-0.7 KB). The :schemas/humanize-explain! keyword and malli.error/humanize's code leave the probe; malli/error.cljc drops 12.0 -> 10.5 KB optimized.
- adapter's [malli.error] :require deleted outright (counterfactual, not landed): margin 38333 B (-3.3 KB). Every malli.error literal gone.

The 2.5 KB between the last two is malli.error's `default-errors` message table (built through PersistentHashMap.fromArrays) plus its random-uuid negation prefix: top-level defs whose initialisers Closure cannot prove pure, so it keeps them with no reader. Gating cannot reach it; only taking malli.error out of the build's module graph does, and the library cannot do that for a consumer without a build-side knob (a dev-only :preloads ns that publishes the humanizer, a :reader-features conditional require, or an :ns-aliases stub). rf2-tiymn's brief ruled out a new knob and its non-goals rule out a dynamic loader, so the residue is recorded in Spec 010 §Bundle cost and priced inside the gate's margin.

Question for the mayor: is 2.5 KB gzipped per schemas consumer worth a consumer-side dev-only preload (the humanizer moves to a re-frame.schemas.malli.humanize ns wired via :devtools :preloads, with the JVM keeping the automatic publication)? If not, close this as recorded-and-accepted; Spec 010 already says what stays and why.
notes: Figure consistency (2026-08-31): the three margins above in bytes are 41595 B = 40.6 KB (unconditional), 40885 B = 39.9 KB (gated, what PR #8788 lands), 38333 B = 37.4 KB (require deleted, counterfactual). Spec 010 §Bundle cost and PR #8788 quote the same three in KB. Repeat builds of one tree vary by tens of bytes gzipped (raw identical), so the last two digits are noise.
close_reason: REJECTED AS GOLD-PLATING by the mayor 2026-08-31 00:56:58 AUSEST, on the read-only triage at 5d35356469 and a read of PR #8788: the branch already records the residue and its cause (default-errors via PersistentHashMap.fromArrays) at spec/010-Schemas.md:735, prices it inside the +39.9 KB margin, and re-derives the bundle band. The only thing left is a consumer-side dev-only :preloads knob for about 2.5 KB gz, a second wiring path through the template shadow-cljs.edn, the setup skill and the how-to for every consumer, against the stance. Recorded and accepted; reopen only if Mike wants the knob.

title: docs: the deferred-handler ':rf/default leak' claim is wrong the same way rf2-78wg was — ~10 files in tools/xray alone, and not confined to Xray
description:
FOUND BY `paletteprose-a` WHILE SWEEPING rf2-78wg, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED THERE. rf2-78wg's own
text says to stop and report past about a dozen sites rather than widening; this is that report, and
the worker was right to stop.

## THE CLAIM, AND WHY IT IS WRONG

Prose across the tree says that a bare `rf/dispatch` called from a DEFERRED HANDLER -- an
`:on-click`, an `:on-change`, a timeout callback -- "leaks to `:rf/default`".

IT DOES NOT. There is no `:rf/default` floor under EP-0002. The ambient read resolves to NIL and
RAISES `:rf.error/no-frame-context`: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1996` states it, and
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs` bottoms `current-frame` out at nil with a
docstring saying the runtime never synthesises `:rf/default`.

This is the SAME wrongness rf2-78wg corrected for the plain-fn-head case, reached through a
different door. The two were almost certainly copied from one another.

## SCOPE: LARGER THAN rf2-78wg, AND NOT CONFINED TO XRAY

Roughly TEN files in `tools/xray/src` alone, named by the finder as a starting point and NOT as a
census:

    panels/derivation_graph.cljs        panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs
    settings/view.cljs                  static/flows/panel.cljs
    static/interceptors/panel.cljs      static/schemas/panel.cljs
    static/shared/search_box.cljs       panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs

AND THE FINDER SAYS IT IS NOT CONFINED TO XRAY. Run a real census before scoping the work; the list
above is where to start looking, never the answer.

## THE INSTRUMENT LESSON THAT COMES WITH IT, BECAUSE IT WILL DECIDE YOUR COUNT

rf2-78wg's own sweep found a site that a LINE-ORIENTED pass read as absent: at
`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:115` the claim BREAKS ACROSS A LINE, so only the
FLATTENED pass found it. Expect the same here -- this is hard-wrapped prose in comments, which is
precisely the shape that defeats a single-line probe.

So run the census THREE ways and take the union: line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, and with
comment markers stripped BEFORE collapsing. A `;;` on the continuation line survives a plain flatten
and defeats the second pass on its own. Take a positive control on every zero.

## WHAT THE CORRECTED TEXT SHOULD SAY

Keep any warning that is TRUE -- a deferred handler really does run outside the React render window,
really has no in-flight component, and really will fail. Correct only the DESTINATION: it raises
`:rf.error/no-frame-context` rather than routing anywhere. Where the prose recommends a remedy, the
remedy is to capture the dispatcher during render and close over it, which is what the migrated
boundaries already do.

DO NOT generalise into the plain-fn-head case -- that one is the opposite direction (heading is the
footgun, inlining is the ruled repair, HD-016) and is already recorded on rf2-k97c.3.

## SCOPE BOUNDS

PROSE ONLY. No behaviour change, no test change, no migration. If the census turns up a site where
the CODE is actually wrong rather than the comment, STOP and file that separately -- it is a
different bead with a different shape, and mixing them makes both unreviewable.

## GATE

Whichever lane covers the files touched. If the diff is confined to comments and docstrings in
`.cljs` files, the node lane compiling clean is the whole of what is needed and a browser lane has
nothing to say -- say so rather than running one for form. If any `tools/*/spec` or `docs/` markdown
is touched, `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers it and runs unguarded in `test.yml`'s
`verify-readme-links` job; it validates link targets and heading anchors ONLY and does not look
inside fenced code blocks at all.

## SEQUENCING

None of the named files is currently held by a live worker, but re-check at dispatch time -- panel
migrations are landing steadily and several of these files sit in migration closures.
notes:
## WORKER REPORT (deferprose-a, PR #9659) — 2026-09-11

PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both hold:
  - spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md — the `:adapter/current-frame` impl "MUST return **nil**
    (not `:rf/default`) when no scope names a frame, so a public frame-scoped op raises
    `:rf.error/no-frame-context` rather than synthesising a default"; both impls "bottom out
    at **nil** (no `:rf/default` tier)".
  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs — `current-frame` "Returns the scope
    frame, or **nil** when no scope is established — it never synthesises `:rf/default`",
    body is `(or *current-frame* <react-context>)` with a trailing nil.
  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc — `require-current-frame!` emits then THROWS
    `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on a nil read.

A SECOND ERROR, found in the same passages and corrected with them: the Xray settings/palette
prose named the React context's DEFAULT VALUE as `:rf/default`. It is the NO-PROVIDER SENTINEL.
`re-frame.adapter.context`'s own docstring: "The React-context default value — the **no-provider
sentinel**, NOT `:rf/default`", and `coerce-context-value` maps it to nil. The two errors compose
into one false story — a "3-tier chain" whose bottom tier is a default frame. There is no third
tier.

## CENSUS — three passes, keyed on the CLAIM not the token

The bare token is useless as a discriminator: `:rf/default` reads 5837 occurrences across 919
tracked files, because it is the ordinary default frame id. The census therefore required
DEFERRED vocabulary plus a leak-verb in a +/-300-char window around each occurrence.

  pass 1  line-oriented                          6 files    8 candidate occurrences
  pass 2  whitespace-collapsed                  52 files  105 candidate occurrences
  pass 3  comment markers stripped, collapsed   52 files  107 candidate occurrences
  UNION                                         52 files

46 OF THE 52 CANDIDATE FILES ARE INVISIBLE TO A LINE-ORIENTED PROBE. The three-pass instruction
was decisive, not ceremony. Pass 3 added 2 occurrences over pass 2 but no new FILES.

Confirmed line-break instance: tools/xray/spec/027-Fresco-Evidence.md breaks the claim as
"would" / "leak to `:rf/default`" across lines 40-41.

Every zero was controlled with a positive of the same shape. Post-edit verification over the 13

settings/view.cljs taken from origin/main and 2 against EP-0002's motivation, so the instrument
is live and the zero is absence rather than breakage.

    routes dispatches to `:rf/default`". Its already-corrected twin is one sentence in
    skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md, now mirrored.
  - migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md — HIGHEST USER IMPACT. M-51 told a v1 migrator the
    mechanical ignore-`m` rewrite leaves ajax-callback dispatches defaulting to `:rf/default`.
    They raise. The section's own **Why** paragraph already said so, so the stale sentence
    contradicted its own section four paragraphs down. The dependent clause was corrected with
    it: handle-capture is needed for EVERY async-dispatching fx, not only multi-frame ones.

## FINDINGS THAT DIFFER FROM THE DISPATCH BRIEF

1. shell.cljs CONTAINS NO DEFERRED-HANDLER SITES. The brief predicted it was "the one most
   likely to contain sites your census will find". It carries 5 `:rf/default` mentions, and
   every one is the PLAIN-FN door (rf2-78wg / PR #9657's territory), not the deferred-handler
   door — lines 115 and 1087 are plain-fn claims, line 130 is already correct. Nothing there
   for this bead, and nothing to route once #9657 merges.

2. THE FENCE LIST UNDER-STATED PR #9657 AND #9655. #9657 also touches palette.cljs,
   static/shell.cljs and views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs; #9655 also touches
   tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md, 008-Embedding-Contract.md and API.md. None collided with this
   change, but the fence list was not the full file set. (#9655 and #9656 have since merged.)

3. NO CODE DEFECT FOUND. One near-miss worth recording: runtime_cljs_test.cljs asserts
   `(= :rf/default (rf/current-frame-id))` under the label "outside any binding the dynamic var
   falls back to :rf/default". `current-frame-id` RAISES — it has no `:rf/default` floor. The
   test passes because `make-reset-runtime-fixture` binds an `:ambient-frame` (default
   `:rf/default`) as `*current-frame*` around each test body. The CODE is correct; only the
   label misdescribes the mechanism.

## COVERAGE GAP WORTH KNOWING

ADAPTER_READMES roster, which is reagent + reagent-slim only. That is why the stale claim
survived there while its siblings were corrected. Not fixed here (widening a gate's roster is
not this bead's shape) — recorded so someone can decide.

## FOLLOW-UP POPULATION — TEST FILES, DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED

The bead bounds this to prose with NO TEST CHANGE, so these were left. Several sites sit inside

title: xray: machine_canvas stays on Reagent — record the disposition, do not migrate it
description:
A REFUSAL, PROMOTED TO ITS OWN RECORD. The rf2-k97c.3 increment-5 worker was briefed to migrate FOUR panels
to Fresco and migrated THREE. It reported `machine_canvas.cljs` as a STOP rather than attempting it, and the
reasoning is the deliverable — this bead exists so the next dispatch does not re-derive it or, worse, try.

WHY IT IS NOT LIKE THE OTHER PANELS, four independent reasons, any one of which would be enough:

  1. ITS PUBLIC VAR IS `Chart`, NOT `Panel`. It is a SHARED WIDGET mounted BY NAME from four other source
     files, and FIVE test files pin its var identity. The migration spellings ruled under rf2-k97c.3 both
     assume a panel whose outside name is either private or a `Panel`-shaped boundary; neither fits a widget
     with five identity pins on it.

  2. ITS BODY MOUNTS TWO FOREIGN COMPONENTS AS HICCUP HEADS — `mv-chart/MachineChart`, a plain `defn` living
     in `tools/machines-viz`, and `after-rings/AfterRingsOverlay`, a `reg-view`.

  3. `re-frame.fresco` SHIPS AN OUTWARD DOOR ONLY. There is no INWARD door for a Reagent component used as a
     boundary body's hiccup head. So (2) is not an inconvenience to work around inside this panel; it is a
     missing capability, and inventing one here would be a substrate change smuggled in as a panel migration.

  4. IT PERFORMS **ZERO** READS. The migration's whole value is the three severances that follow from owning
     the read path. A panel with no reads buys none of them, so even a successful migration would be churn.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ASKING FOR. It is NOT a request to build the inward door. That would be a substrate
decision with its own design question and its own owner, and nothing here establishes that it is wanted. If
someone later wants `machine_canvas` on Fresco, the inward door is the prerequisite and IT is the bead to
file — with an argument for why the capability should exist at all, not merely because one panel wants it.

SO THE LIVE QUESTION IS THE SMALL ONE: does `machine_canvas` stay on Reagent permanently, and if so, is that
recorded anywhere a reader will find it? Reason (4) suggests the answer is simply yes and costs nothing. What
should NOT happen is this panel sitting on a migration roster indefinitely as apparently-unfinished work.

RE-VERIFY EVERY CLAIM ABOVE AT SOURCE before acting — all four are the worker's measurements relayed by the
mayor, not the mayor's own readings, and the count of mounting call sites and identity pins is exactly the
kind of figure that drifts.

RELATED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN: the metadata-carried-key class defect is rf2-truw, and
`machine_canvas.cljs` measured 0 sites in both spellings, so it is clean on that axis and needs nothing.
close_reason:
RULED AND CLOSED BY THE MAYOR, 2026-09-10, WITHOUT CONSUMING A WORKER AND WITHOUT HOLDING IT FOR THE
OPERATOR. `machine_canvas.cljs` STAYS ON REAGENT. It is not on any migration roster, it is not unfinished
work, and nobody should attempt it.

THE RULING RESTS ON REASON 4 ALONE, AND REASON 4 IS ANSWERED BY THE PROJECT'S STATED STANCE RATHER THAN BY
TASTE — which is why this was never an operator call. The migration's whole value is the three severances
that follow from owning the read path. This panel performs NO READS, so a successful migration buys none of
them and costs a worker plus a diff across a widget with five identity pins on it. "We are not
over-engineering or gold plating" settles that; there is no version of the stance under which churn with no
benefit is the right call.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR before ruling, because the bead itself said every claim was a worker's
reading relayed second-hand:
  * `rf/read` 0, `@(` 0, and the only two `subscribe` hits are DOCSTRING PROSE at lines 224-225 describing
    what a plain fn USED to do. Control: `defn` 12 in the same file, and the reading panel `trace.cljs`
    carries 4 real ones through the identical probe. So the zero is measured, not assumed.
  * The public var IS `Chart`, registered at line 218 via `rf/reg-view`, and `machine-canvas` is named across
    8 files under `tools/xray/src/`. The shared-widget claim holds.

REASONS 2 AND 3 — the foreign hiccup heads and Fresco's outward-only door — WERE NOT RE-VERIFIED, and did not
need to be. They would matter if the ruling were "we cannot migrate it"; the ruling is "we should not", which
reason 4 establishes on its own. Anyone who later wants this panel on Fresco must re-establish 2 and 3 at
source, because the inward door is a SUBSTRATE decision with its own owner and its own argument, and wanting
it for one zero-read panel is not that argument.

ONE INSTRUMENT NOTE EARNED WHILE RULING, and it is the third instance in a single hour: PROSE IN THIS TREE
DESCRIBES THE VERY MECHANISMS A CENSUS LOOKS FOR, so a raw probe reads comment and docstring text as
evidence. Twice today it was `;` comments; here it is a DOCSTRING, which `sed 's/;.*$//'` cannot strip
because a Clojure docstring is a string literal rather than a comment. Any census over this tree strips
comments AND docstrings, and takes its control through the same pipeline. Recorded on rf2-truw, which owns
the census recipe.

NOTHING TO DISPATCH. NOTHING HELD FOR THE OPERATOR. If this ruling is wrong, the cheapest refutation is a
measurement showing the panel reads.

  emitted_test_run_test.clj (JVM, template)      leaf == a real deps-new emission   <- follows the template
  check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py (repo-invariants)  structure/vocabulary OF the leaf, by LITERAL TEXT

The first two are derivation-EQUALITY checks, so a rename inside the template propagates and they stay green with no edit — correctly, and that is exactly why running them both proved nothing about the third. Only the third pins literal text, and literal text is the only thing that goes stale. THE THREE DID NOT DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT THE LEAVES SHOULD CONTAIN; the third simply stopped recognising the block.

WHAT IT PINNED: `_reagent_core_blocks` recognised the copy-complete Reagent core.cljs by two substrings, one of which was the REQUIRE-ALIAS — `"re-frame.adapter.reagent" in block and "reagent-adapter/render!" in block`. After the rename to rf.adapter.reagent it matched nothing.

THE HALF WORTH RECORDING IS THE CLAUSE THAT STAYED SILENT. CANONICAL-SOURCE runs two clauses over that one detector: first-counter.md must carry EXACTLY ONE such block (loud on 0), and entry-namespace.md must carry NONE (`if en_blocks:`). A detector matching nothing satisfies the SECOND clause vacuously. So the alias move did not merely break one message — it DISARMED the duplicate check, and only the first clause was loud enough to say so. Had a genuine duplicate existed at the same time, this gate would have reported one failure and silently passed the other.

REPAIRED IN THE PIN, NOT THE LEAVES, because the leaves are right and the two equality locks agree they are: the match is now `"re-frame.adapter.reagent" in block and "/render!" in block`. The NAMESPACE is the stable fact; the alias is the caller's choice and this checker has no business knowing it. GENERAL LESSON FOR THE CAMPAIGN, since more slices will rename aliases: a require-alias rename can silently disarm any gate that recognises code by literal alias text, and the gate need not be in the surface you are editing. scripts/ carries 39 such checkers. Running the derivation locks is NOT evidence about them, for the structural reason above. The cheap sweep before pushing an alias rename is `grep -rn '<old-alias>' scripts/`.
