title: ci(observability): a path-gated gate left four consecutive trunk points ungraded and nothing reports it — 'never looked' is indistinguishable from 'passed'
description:
A path-gated gate can stop grading trunk without anything saying so, and a green that never looked is typographically identical to a green that passed. Nothing in this repo reports the difference.

## THE PREMISE, worded as what is SHOWN

**A path-gated gate left four consecutive trunk points ungraded, and nothing reports that.**

Read that wording carefully, because the tempting stronger claim is NOT shown and must not be substituted for it. The gate did not "sit red on trunk" — it did not run on trunk at all, which is a different thing and the reason nobody noticed. A gate that sat red would have been on every dashboard. A gate that was never scheduled is invisible by construction, and the trunk's check column looks exactly as it does on a healthy day.

## THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-09-21

The instance is the `story-static` static-export smoke inside the `Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)` job. Full evidence is on rf2-n7lql, which owns the REGRESSION; this bead owns the REPORTING GAP, and the two are independent — whatever broke the smoke, the fact that its absence went unreported is its own defect and outlives the fix.

- `a4e90ebaee` is the last trunk point at which the step ACTUALLY EXECUTED and passed.
- Every trunk push-run after it either skipped the whole job (`765c370308`, `9fc5274412`, `0d6f4e3f14` — doc-only pushes, filtered out by the job's path gate) or ran the job WITHOUT this step (`949e0245da`).
- On that last one the job reported **SUCCESS**, and the token `story-static` appears **0 times** in its 51,079-byte log, against **19** times in the red PR log. Nonsense control on the green log: **0**, so the instrument bites. The green job ran **11** step groups; the red ran **14**.

So four consecutive trunk points carried no verdict from this gate, and the four-in-a-row is the floor rather than the ceiling: the window has only widened since, and no instrument anywhere counts it.

## WHY IT IS EXPENSIVE RATHER THAN UNTIDY

It fails in the REASSURING direction, and it defeats the two checks a careful reader actually runs.

1. **The check column is complete.** The job is present and green. Nothing is missing, pending or red, so a rollup census — the merge criterion's own clause 1 — reads at band and settles.
2. **"Is trunk green?" answers yes, truthfully, about a gate that graded nothing.** The precise statement a reader wants is *green at `<sha>`, and NOT GRADED at these four*, and no surface in this repo can express the second half.

The cost lands on the next PR whose diff happens to arm the gate. It goes red, its own diff is innocent, and the natural reading is that the PR broke something — which is exactly what happened here: PR #10139's entire diff is **two lines, both inside comments**, and it failed three times. A comment cannot produce a runtime `pageerror` in a minified bundle. The PR is not the cause; it is merely the first change in a long while to ARM the gate, and it inherits the blame for a regression that landed up to four trunk points earlier.

## WHAT THIS IS NOT ASKING FOR

**Not** a proposal to unfilter the path gates. Path filtering is deliberate and it is what keeps the matrix affordable; `test.yml` deliberately keeps its own `pull_request` trigger unfiltered for a related reason already recorded in CLAUDE.md, and that asymmetry is a design choice, not an oversight.

**Not** a new gate. Adding a gate to watch the gates is the reflex answer and it is the wrong one — a fresh mechanism to keep in sync, for a problem whose whole nature is that mechanisms go quiet without saying so.

The question this bead asks is narrower and is genuinely open: **is there a cheap surface that answers "which gates have not graded trunk since commit X, and for how long?"** — a report, not an enforcement. If the honest answer after looking is that nothing cheap exists and the cost does not justify anything expensive, then CLOSE THIS BEAD WITH THAT REASONING RECORDED. A ruling that the cost is not worth paying is a complete outcome here and is worth more than a mechanism nobody maintains.

## FENCE

Do not dispatch this while rf2-n7lql is live. That worker owns the same job and the same logs, and two workers reading one CI surface will duplicate each other's measurements. It is also not urgent: the gap has existed for some time and costs nothing further while it is merely known.

title: False: commit-based trunk arming report can give a false all-clear after reverted changes
description:
Merged-PR audit #10141, merge a66d0f756960a4946d9f4d07668615c12905d354. scripts/report_ungraded_gates.py:87-91 claims that each commit diff is a subset of its push diff, so walking commits can only over-report staleness and cannot give a false all-clear. That claim is false when changes cancel within one push.

Reproduction with the exact merged report, classifier and test.yml in an isolated git fixture:
- Start at a baseline containing implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs.
- Commit A edits that file.
- Commit B restores its original contents and changes only bench/fresco/audit-fixture.txt.
- Treat A+B as one push with before=baseline and after=B, matching test.yml's CHANGED_SURFACES_BASE_REF=github.event.before and the classifier's aggregate git diff.
The actual push diff contains only the bench path. It is not paths-ignored, but the classifier returns story_static_gate=false. The report run with --branch main --since <baseline> --surface story_static_gate instead stops at B and prints B as LAST ARMED, COMMITS AGO 0, with no uncertainty warning. The restored gate file appears in B's parent diff even though it is absent from the push diff. No run exists for intermediate A in this one-push scenario.

The defect is in walk_trunk -> main:397-408 crediting a per-commit classification as actual push arming, compounded by the one-way-safe claim and definitive LAST ARMED heading. It can conceal the same missing-grade interval this report is intended to expose. The existing three historical self-test pins all pass alongside this counterexample; they do not establish push-boundary equivalence.

Evidence: gate-audit-ungraded-push-audit-sep20-monitor-2.log/.exit, captured exit 0; positive control with the direct gate path returns true. Gate root and isolated fixture path verified. A separate exact-snapshot run over actual merged history exits 0 and reports PR #10139's classifier change as the latest story_static_gate trigger, so the ordinary single-commit case remains useful. This is a reproducible algorithm defect, not a claim that the fixture occurred on live trunk.

Required correction: do not present commit-level predictions as confirmed push arming. Either evaluate accepted before/after push ranges when they are supplied/known, or label unverified rows as commit-level candidates/unknown and explain that uncertainty goes in both directions. Remove the false subset/one-way-safe claim and ensure the normal table communicates the limitation even when every surface is found. Preserve the cheap offline/read-only report; no new gate, workflow or mandatory online service is requested.
acceptance_criteria: Add a regression case with an edit and restoration in one multi-commit push plus an unrelated surviving bench change. Aggregate classification must remain unarmed; the report must not claim confirmed recent arming from either intermediate parent diff. The table and prose must distinguish inferred commit triggers from observed/known push arming for all rows, and acknowledge both false-positive and false-negative uncertainty if push boundaries are unavailable. Keep a direct single-commit gate-path positive control and the existing useful offline report behavior.
notes: Merged-PR audit #10143 (f921194ac2daead596817d984036f1d37dc828a9; merged 2026-09-21T06:33:26Z). Completeness: Full one-file landed diff, PR rationale and original finding/acceptance read. Every row is explicitly an inferred commit candidate; warnings now appear on all-green runs, cancellation probes are bounded/memoized, and the required edit-restore and direct-change controls are present. Correctness: Exact landed report/classifier/workflow equal this worktree. Absolute-path self-test with Git Bash selected: captured exit 0, all three historical pins and nine fixture checks passed, none skipped. Injecting pre-fix no-flag behavior into that exact imported module captured exit 1 on the cancellation check; restored execution returned 0. Logs gate-ungraded-audit-sep21-monitor-2 and -3 preserve runner exits and the negative control establishes the tested module. Attempt 1 exited 2 before testing because the environment selected WSL bash; it is not a test verdict. Reviewed history exhaustion and report-only exit semantics; no actionable residual established. Implementation quality: Reuses the existing offline classifier and shares aggregate work per commit/depth. Explicit uncertainty avoids an API dependency or new CI policy. The extensive explanatory prose does not warrant corrective work under the requested posture. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

FIXED. PR #10143 merged 2026-09-21 at trunk `f921194ac2` — one file, `scripts/report_ungraded_gates.py`, +439/−47. Merged on the five clauses at band 88 (re-measured that pass from three settled PRs): 0 pending, 0 failed, 69 skipped + 19 success, `All required checks passed` present BY NAME at COMPLETED/SUCCESS, 4 runs completed at the full 40-character head `99f5b56cdf87e44e2c798415d568752a9f3a5ab7`, merge base `e3da2d1e98` descending from the matrix commit with a zero workflow diff on both sides.

## THE DEFECT REPRODUCED, AND THE IDENTITY IS THE WHOLE THING

In an isolated fixture carrying the live classifier and `test.yml`: aggregate `baseline..B` contained the bench path alone, so `story_static_gate=false`, while the report printed `LAST ARMED bb917bd50d21 / COMMITS AGO 0` at **captured exit 0**. The positive control — a direct single-commit change to the gate path — classified true, was reported, and **rendered BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the false credit.** A reader had no way to tell an observed arming from an inferred one.

## THE MAYOR'S OWN BRIEF WAS WRONG ON THE MECHANISM, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE BEST PART OF THIS ITEM

The brief's correction (3) said "the uncertainty runs BOTH ways". **That is true of the REPORT and false of the MECHANISM the brief named**, and the distinction matters because it is what the new docstring has to state.

The original claim was not merely unproven — **it had the containment BACKWARDS.** A file enters an aggregate diff only if some commit touched it, so the PUSH's file set is a SUBSET of the union of its COMMITS' file sets, not a superset. And the classifier is monotone: measured 211 `=true` assignments with zero disarming assignments after init, and `classify(A+B) == classify(A) | classify(B)` on **45 of 45** pairs, with controls both ways. Monotone over a superset means the walk **can never MISS a push's arming — only over-credit it.**

So the commit/push mismatch runs **one way only**, toward the false all-clear. The false-ALARM direction is real but arrives from two OTHER mechanisms the old text folded into one sentence: a generous `paths-ignore`, and window truncation. The docstring now says this and carries its proof.

**The lesson for whoever writes the next brief of this kind:** a premise can be right about the observable and wrong about the cause, and copying the observable forward as though it were the cause is how a correction inherits the original's confidence. The mayor wrote "uncertainty runs both ways" from the report's behaviour and attached it to the wrong mechanism.

## CORRECTION (1): HONEST LABELLING — AND THE OTHER BRANCH IS UNAVAILABLE, NOT MERELY UNATTRACTIVE

The brief left the choice open between evaluating real push boundaries and labelling rows honestly. The worker established that the first branch **cannot be built offline**, which is stronger than preferring the second:

- `origin/main`'s reflog holds **fetch** boundaries, not push boundaries — 2 of 39 steps span more than one commit, both fast-forward fetches, i.e. the same aggregation error wearing an authoritative label;
- **a fresh clone of a 4-commit trunk has 0 reflog entries**, which is exactly what `actions/checkout` produces;
- it is per-clone state under the common dir.

A reflog-based report would credit nothing and call every surface unarmed — a different wrong answer, not a better one.

**Delivered:** `LAST ARMED` → `CANDIDATE`, plus a `BASIS` column reading `commit`; a fragility probe that re-classifies `C~k..C` for k = 2..8 and flags `commit!` (memoised, ~40 ms per call); and the both-ways caveat now printing on **every** run including all-green. It previously sat inside `if stale:`, so the all-green path — exactly where the false all-clear lands — printed nothing at all.

## THE REGRESSION CASE, SHOWN TO BITE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

`--self-test` keeps all three historical pins and adds **case 4** (9 checks). Because case 4 calls functions that did not previously exist, "fails before the fix" was demonstrated by planting rather than by running the old code: setting `cancellation_depth` to `None` — **literally the pre-fix behaviour** — reds only `flagged at k=2`, while flagging everything reds only `control: D is NOT flagged`. Restored, 9/9. Each restore verified by **blob** hash against the committed object, plus `git diff --quiet` exit 0.

## ONE UNREQUESTED FIX, FLAGGED BY THE WORKER AND ACCEPTED BY THE MAYOR

`--self-test` returned **0 unconditionally, even on DRIFT** — a self-check that could never fail anything. It now exits 1.

Accepted rather than waved through: the fence said "do not delete or weaken `--self-test`; extend it", and making a vacuous check capable of failing STRENGTHENS it. It is the vacuous-green class this project exists to catch, it is confined to the same file, the report path is untouched and still exits 0 (verified under the same plant: self-test 1, report 0), and nothing in the tree invokes the script.

## A TRAP THE WORKER FOUND THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ITEM

**`bash scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` with no flags would have taken the shadow-cljs lane on a `scripts/**` change.** Root `scripts/**` arms no CI surface and is not a doc surface, so it falls to the spine's own *"conservative fallback (unknown surface)"* and sets `jvm=true node=true`. **CI has no such fallback** — the classifier reads 0 of 29 surfaces for these paths.

So the local spine and CI disagree about a path in the direction that silently takes a machine-wide exclusive. The worker verified `--plan` exits before executing, ran only that, and did not take the lane. Anybody briefing a `scripts/**` item must either forbid the bare spine or grant the lane.

## GATES

Classifier handed PATHS: **0 of 29** armed; control `assertion_strip.cljs` arms **6**. Two repo-wide ratchets genuinely read the file and were green on the final tree: `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` (exit 0) and `check_view_lifetime_residue.py` (21/21 self-tests, exit 0). `check-commit-attribution.sh` clean over 5 commits, beads boundary, ai-tracking ratchet and `py_compile` all exit 0.

Also measured, and worth keeping because it bounds the new flag's noise: over 250 trunk commits the probe found **414 credits and 0 refuted at k=2**. The flag is rare, so it is worth reading when it fires. **No live-trunk occurrence of the synthetic scenario is alleged** — this was a reproducible algorithm defect, not an incident.

title: skills: re-frame2-setup and reagent-migration now teach OPPOSITE facts about a Fresco publication gap
description:
Two shipped skills now teach OPPOSITE things about whether Fresco has a publication gap, and both sentences are on trunk right now.

**`skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:54`** — cardinal rule 3, a 718-character line an agent reads on every greenfield task — says: "**Fresco** (re-frame2's re-frame-native view layer) is not a scaffold option: **it is pre-publication with no released coordinate**, so a greenfield project starts on an adapter and moves later if it wants to (the `reagent-migration` skill)."

**`skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:167`**, landed 2026-09-22 in PR #10155 (`rf2-ikbgk.6`), says: "Don't sell the rewrite as required. The Reagent and UIx adapters are first-class homes for views indefinitely. And **don't invent a publication gap either: Fresco ships in the same release set** as the adapters."

So the setup skill states as fact the very thing the migration skill names as a thing not to invent — and it does so in a sentence that ROUTES THE READER TO THAT OTHER SKILL.

**THE MIGRATION SKILL IS THE ONE THAT IS RIGHT, and it was corrected on measurement.** `VERSION` reads `0.0.1.alpha` and `git tag -l 'v*'` counts **0**, so nothing is published — the Reagent adapter no more than Fresco. `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh` lists `fresco` in the same 14-entry ARTEFACTS array as `reagent`, so they tag in lockstep. Drawing an asymmetry between them is false today and will be false after the first tag, which is exactly why the landed wording was chosen to be tag-neutral.

**THE SETUP SKILL'S ADVICE IS STILL CORRECT; ONLY ITS JUSTIFICATION IS WRONG.** Fresco genuinely is not a scaffold option — the template's `hooks.clj` knows `:reagent` and `:uix` and no third substrate, which the `rf2-ikbgk.9` reviewer verified independently. So the repair is to KEEP the advice and REPLACE the reason: a greenfield project starts on an adapter because the scaffold emits adapter projects, not because Fresco is unpublished. Do not delete the routing sentence.

**WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN EITHER SLICE.** The `rf2-ikbgk.9` worker was told to leave `SKILL.md:54` alone precisely to avoid two workers writing two different wordings for one fact while the sibling PR was in flight; that was the right call and the sibling has since merged, so the tension is now live rather than hypothetical. It was that worker who spotted it and said the follow-up was ready to file. Neither slice can close it alone: the fix spans `skills/re-frame2-setup/**` and, if the same framing survives there, `docs/skills/index.md`, which the whole skills wave shares.

**CANDIDATE SITES, NOT A ROSTER — re-census before acting.** `pre-publication` currently matches six tracked files: `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md` (the instance above), `skills/README.md`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md`, `skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json`, plus `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:86` and `references/procedure.md:53`. **The last two are NOT this defect** — they use the phrase in a different sense, about a coordinate being the tool's delivery mechanism "rather than a pre-publication detour" — so a blind sweep would rewrite correct text. The other three are unexamined and may or may not carry the asymmetry; read each in context. And note `docs/skills/index.md:42` was already corrected by PR #10155, so it is NOT a site.

Measured at trunk `1d98e21e31`, 2026-09-22.

**One reading note, because it nearly produced a wrong bead.** Line 54 is 718 characters, and the Fresco clause sits past the 260th; a `cut -c1-260` on the grep output showed only the Reagent/UIx opening and made the reviewer's cite look wrong. The cite was right and the display was truncated. Read the whole line before disputing a cite against a long one.

## The decision in one sentence

Whether the existing README layout-map ↔ disk ratchet should also read skill READMEs — all nine (A), only the ones that declare a locked layout, i.e. reagent-migration (B), or none (C) — given that, measured at trunk, **registering a skill README does not pass today** and every non-C option therefore carries a small parser repair the bead did not price.

## The problem, carefully

**What the gate is.** `scripts/check_readme_inventories.py` (968 lines, stdlib Python, last touched 4 commits ago) runs three registries. The one at issue is `LAYOUT_CHECKS` at `scripts/check_readme_inventories.py:439-458`, exactly three rows:

```python
LAYOUT_CHECKS: tuple[LayoutCheck, ...] = (
    LayoutCheck(readme="testbeds/README.md",       section="Layout", base_dir="testbeds"),
    LayoutCheck(readme="implementation/README.md", section="Layout", base_dir="implementation",
                ignore=frozenset({"scripts"})),   # build/test tooling, not an artefact entry
    LayoutCheck(readme="examples/README.md",       section="Layout", base_dir="examples",
                ignore=frozenset({"_shared"})),   # private cross-example helper lib
)
```

What one row asserts (`_run_layout_check`, `:567-604`): open the README, take the section whose heading text equals `section` (`_section_body`, `:108`), take the **first fenced block** in it, parse the shallowest tier of tokens ending in `/` (`_layout_top_level_dirs`, `:146-219`), list the immediate subdirectories on disk minus dot-dirs and gitignored build dirs (`_disk_dirs`, `:249-267`, dot filter at `:265`), subtract `ignore` from **both** sides (`:590-591`), and demand set equality. Two messages, `:594-601`: `layout map under <base>/ omits on-disk dir(s): …` and `layout map under <base>/ lists non-existent dir(s): …`. So for `examples/README.md` § Layout it asserts: the fenced tree's tier-1 directory names == the directories in `examples/` other than `_shared/`. Files and deeper tiers are deliberately ignored (`:150-153`).

**Where it runs.** CI: `.github/workflows/test.yml:940` `verify-readme-links` (no `if:` on the job, `:940-945`), steps `:1127` (self-test) and `:1130` (full run). Local: the fast-PR spine, `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:972` and `:1318`. Last green main run (155ff6871c, run 35696254173): both steps `success`.

**Does it have a self-test that pins its registry?** No. `--self-test` (`:783-957`) pins the parsing primitives — three layout blocks at `:839-868`: an indent tree, a deep indent tree, and a **flat** glyph tree (`├── spec/` / `└── src/` directly under a root label). Nothing asserts what `LAYOUT_CHECKS` contains; the file's own comment says the full-tree run is the integration test (`:774-780`). The three registered READMEs carry **0** box-glyph lines each (Python count over `│├└`), so the glyph path is exercised only by that one flat self-test block.

**How it was found.** rf2-ueyfn (PR #10181) fixed by hand a locked layout that omitted a directory: `skills/reagent-migration/README.md` § Layout, `spec/design.md` § 4 "File structure (locked)" and `spec/authoring-prompt.md` all lacked `tests/fixture/` — six tracked files run by the required `reagent-migration-fixture-cold-start` job. The worker noted that this gate is the right shape but never opens skill READMEs, and reported that registering `skills/*/README.md` "would PASS today". The mayor verified the registry at source and filed this bead rather than let the next editor of the file decide silently.

**What the gate reads today, on this checkout — exit 1.** `python scripts/check_readme_inventories.py --verbose` → `implementation/README.md:45  layout map under implementation/ omits on-disk dir(s): hicasso`, exit **1**. `implementation/hicasso/` is untracked (`git ls-files -- implementation/hicasso` → 0) and ignored (`git status --porcelain --ignored` → `!! implementation/hicasso/`, containing one leftover `scripts/`), a residue of the Hicasso→Fresco rename (`1ad1ea3f66`). CI is green on the same trunk. This is the local-false-red class the script already special-cases for `node_modules`/`out`/`target`/`classes` (`:233-247`, rf2-wv7d7z). It matters for pricing: **every registered directory is also a directory where a stray local folder reds the spine** for whoever has it.

**The skills surface, counted.** `git ls-files -- 'skills/*/README.md'` → 17 (git's `*` spans `/`, so that includes `evals/`, `references/`, `tests/fixture/` READMEs); the top-level `skills/<name>/README.md` set is **9** (Python glob; control: `git ls-files -- skills | awk -F/ '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c` lists nine skill directories plus the family `README.md`). Of the nine, **5 carry a `## Layout` section** (ripgrep `^## Layout` over `README.md` under `skills/`, and the gate's own `_section_body`): `reagent-migration:56`, `re-frame-migration:51`, `re-frame2:18`, `re-frame2-implementor:41`, `re-frame2-setup:140`. The other **4** have none: `re-frame2-xray` uses a bullet list under `## Repo contents` (`:19`), `re-frame2-improver` likewise (`:9`), `re-frame2-pair-retro` a bullet list under `## Directory contents` (`:22`), and `re-frame2-pair` has no contents section at all — its first fence is a slash command at `:189`. The family convention `skills/README.md:215-235` lists minimum contents and does **not** require a Layout section; the test-fixture rule at `:445-455` says only 5 skills warrant `tests/` at all. (Control on the census: `^## (Install|Repo contents|Directory contents)` hits the expected lines in all nine.)

**The premise "would pass today" is false — measured, not relayed.** I ran the gate's real `_run_layout_check` over all nine with `section="Layout"`, `base_dir="skills/<name>"`:

| skill | no `ignore` | `ignore={".claude-plugin"}` |
|---|---|---|
| re-frame-migration | RED `lists non-existent dir(s): .claude-plugin` | PASS |
| re-frame2-implementor | RED `… .claude-plugin` | PASS |
| re-frame2-setup | RED `… .claude-plugin` | PASS |
| **reagent-migration** | RED `lists non-existent dir(s): .claude-plugin, fixture` | RED `… fixture` |
| re-frame2 | RED `… .claude-plugin, cross-cutting, fundamentals, state-machines, tooling` | RED (four `references/` subdirs) |

**0 of 9 pass as-is; 3 of 9 with a `.claude-plugin` ignore; reagent-migration — the one skill the bead is about — passes under neither.** Two parser facts explain all of it:

## Recommendation

**B, with the two-line parser repair and without any `fixture` ignore.** Argued from the stance:

The parser repair is not gold-plating — the file's own docstring claims glyph trees are "handled uniformly" (`:156-176`), and they are not once a tree nests; fixing that makes the tool honest about a claim it already makes.

- *Don't litigate the minutiae*: that is the argument against A, not against B. Imposing a fenced tree on four skills whose bullet lists are fine is litigation; one row for the one skill whose omission cost a real PR is not.

What would change my mind: if Mike regards a skill README's layout as the skill author's own business — the bead's own case for C — then C is the honest reading of the stance and costs nothing; and if the plan is to retire hand-drawn trees in favour of bullet lists, C now beats B. title: docs: 11-ephemeral-state.md says re-registering reg-state with a different :default refuses; the implementation replaces it and the last default wins (one sentence)
description:
Filed 2026-09-22 by the delegated decider for rf2-d8n4k (dossier review). Both independent reviewers of that decision found this slip in passing and judged it a separate one-sentence correction, not gated by rf2-d8n4k's PR and not part of it. Nothing waits on this bead.

## Project stance (Mike's words, verbatim)

> The posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer. We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a minimal, ergonomic API and excellent tools, and low friction.
>
> For each review, remember that we don't want to over-engineer. We just want to create a library which has excellent ergonomics for creating SPAs. We don't need to litigate every last, fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (for the dispatched worker)

**The false sentence.** `docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md:62-64` (measured at trunk `d51a7f5a1c`, 2026-09-22; re-verify the line numbers before editing — `grep -n 'refus' docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md` reads exactly one line today, :64):

> The concern must be a namespace-qualified keyword — it is a sub id, an event id and an app-db key at once — and registering it again with a different `:default` refuses.

**Ground truth, two independent instruments.** The `reg-state` docstring at `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/state.cljc:210-211`: "Re-registering replaces all three, which is what a namespace reload is: the last `:default` written wins." Its refusal list at :213-215 names three refusals — an unqualified concern, options that are not a map or carry an unknown key, and a bad instance key at a read or write — and a different `:default` is not among them. The test `re-registering-replaces-the-registration-and-the-last-default-wins` at `implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/state_cljs_test.cljs:255-264` registers `::reloaded` with `{:default 0}` twice, then with `{:default 1}`, and asserts an un-set instance reads `1`. So the guide's "refuses" is the opposite of what ships.

**The fix: one sentence, one file.** Replace the "refuses" clause with a true one — the wording is yours; the size is fixed. A shape that matches the docstring: "… and registering it again replaces the registration — a namespace reload re-runs the same call, and the last `:default` written wins." title: http(managed): a :rf.http/managed request with :request-id and no :reply-to emits no issued or handled row — intended or silent drop?
description:
Reported, not investigated, by the rf2-6ooch worker (PR #10276): in an early test run, a `:rf.http/managed` request with a `:request-id` and NO `:reply-to` produced neither a `:rf.http/issued` row nor a `:rf.fx/handled` row; adding `:reply-to` restored both.

Unverified. It may be intended (a request with nowhere to reply is refused or short-circuited), a validation error swallowed somewhere, or a test-harness artefact. Establish which at source in implementation/http, with a minimal reproduction. If it is intended, confirm the spec (spec/014-HTTPRequests.md) says so and close with that citation; if a request is silently dropped with no trace and no error, that is the defect to fix.
notes:
PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD — intended, spec'd, and loud; not a silent drop. No code change, no PR. Verified at trunk a24d7b2321.

Mechanism (source): re-frame.http.handlers/managed-handler calls validate-reply-target! BEFORE the middleware chain, normalise-args, emit-issued-trace! and run-attempt!. With none of :reply-to / :on-success / :on-failure present it throws :rf.error/http-no-reply-target. The fx dispatcher (re-frame.fx/handle-one-fx) catches the throw and emits the ALWAYS-ON :rf.error/fx-handler-exception row (:failing-id :rf.http/managed, :exception carrying the http-no-reply-target ex-data, message naming the fix); by its own documented contract an error path does NOT additionally emit :rf.fx/handled. So "no :rf.http/issued row" is correct (the request is never issued) and "no :rf.fx/handled row" is correct (the fx failed); the reporter was not looking for the error row.

Spec citation: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Reply addressing — "Omitting every reply target (no :reply-to, no :on-success, no :on-failure) fails loud at fx-call time with :rf.error/http-no-reply-target" (also the rf2-et4c1s retirement callout under §Unified one-handler form, and the §Reply-to note near the end); spec/009-Instrumentation.md error catalogue row :rf.error/http-no-reply-target (fx-call-time, before run-attempt!, :no-recovery). :request-id plays no part — the guard keys on reply-address key presence only.

Minimal reproduction (JVM, implementation/http :test classpath, real dispatch-sync pipeline, trace listener; one event returning {:fx [[:rf.http/managed args]]}):
- {:request {...} :request-id :t/load} (no reply key): 0 :rf.http/issued, 0 :rf.fx/handled, 1 :rf.error/fx-handler-exception with fx-id :rf.http/managed and cause id :rf.error/http-no-reply-target. dispatch-sync did not throw.
- control, same + :reply-to [:t/done]: 1 :rf.http/issued, 1 :rf.fx/handled, 0 errors.
- control, same + :reply-to nil (explicit fire-and-forget): 1 :rf.http/issued, 1 :rf.fx/handled, 0 errors.

Control both ways: with the validate-reply-target! call removed (planted #_ on that one line in handlers.cljc), the no-reply-to case flipped to 1 issued + 1 handled + 0 errors, i.e. the retired silent behaviour — so the error row is produced by that guard and the repro can see its absence. Restored with git checkout; restore verified by blob hash: default-form git hash-object equals HEAD's committed blob 795e71985a9a51f3391c7b8214741580cb8083d9, porcelain empty.

Existing pin: implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj no-reply-target-fails-loud already pins the throw at the handler; the pipeline-level fx-handler-exception conversion is core's general contract. No further test wanted.

title: core-instrumentation: privacy/redact-path throws 'Key must be integer' on a vector payload parent, escaping dispatch-sync from prepare-handler-ctx and losing the event
description:
## Defect

`re-frame.privacy/redact-path` guards `assoc-in` only against a NON-associative parent, and a vector IS associative. When a redaction path's keyword segment lands on a vector in the event payload, `(assoc-in payload [:cards :number] :rf/redacted)` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Key must be integer`. The router calls `redact-event` from `prepare-handler-ctx`, which is always-on and outside the interceptor chain's capture. So the exception is not recorded as an interceptor error: it escapes the drain and is thrown out of `dispatch-sync`, and the event is lost. The source comment at `privacy.cljc:140-148` says this guard exists precisely so that "a redaction ... silently drops the event" cannot happen. It closes the String case and leaves the vector case open, in a worse form than the one it describes.

The paths come from the path-overlap arm: for a handler focused with `[:rf.interceptor/path P]`, every classified sensitive app-db path under P becomes a payload-relative redaction path. Those paths are derived from the DB's declarations, not from the payload's shape, so a payload holding a vector where the db slice holds a map — or simply a vector-valued key — trips it.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:133-153` — `redact-path`, with its `(associative? (get-in payload (butlast path)))` guard at line 149.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:100-113, 292-328` — `overlap-redaction-paths` / `collect-redaction-paths` derive the payload-relative paths.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2519-2521` — `prepare-handler-ctx` computes `:emit-event (rf.privacy/redact-event (:event envelope) all-paths)` on every dispatch, not debug-gated.
- The public entry `rf/dispatch-sync` (and the async drain) reaches it through `drain-block!` → `process-event!` → `run-handler-pipeline!` → `prepare-handler-ctx`. That is the observed stack below.

## Failure scenario

1. An event classifies `:sensitive [[:user :cards :number]]` (card numbers per card).
2. `(rf/reg-event :save-user {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:user]]]} (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ payload]] {:db (merge db payload)}))`.
3. `(rf/dispatch-sync [:save-user {:cards [{:number "4111"}]}])` → throws `IllegalArgumentException "Key must be integer"` at `re-frame.privacy/redact-path (privacy.cljc:150)`. The handler never runs, nothing commits, and the caller's `dispatch-sync` throws. The same event with a map under `:cards` works and redacts.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (nothing written to the tree):

- CONTROL `(rf/dispatch-sync [:save-user {:cards {:number "4111-map"}}])` → commits `{:cards {:number "4111-map"}}` with no error trace.
- PROBE `(rf/dispatch-sync [:save-user {:cards [{:number "4111-vec"}]}])` → the JVM process dies with `Execution error (IllegalArgumentException) at re-frame.privacy/redact-path (privacy.cljc:150). Key must be integer`, thrown out of `dispatch-sync`.
- Stack (from the error report): `redact-path privacy.cljc:150` ← `redact-paths :157` ← `redact-event :179` ← `router/prepare-handler-ctx router.cljc:2522` ← `run-handler-pipeline! :2985` ← `process-event! :3291` ← `drain-block! :4020` (inside `trace.tooling/call-with-deferred-fanout`) ← `dispatch-sync! :4692`.

What the async `dispatch` drain does with the escaped throw was not measured. It is inspected only: the same `prepare-handler-ctx` call site sits on that path. A tracker full-text search for `redact-path` / `Key must be integer` → 0 beads.

## Smallest fix

In `redact-path`, descend only into a parent that can take the segment: a map, or a vector with an in-range integer segment. Treat anything else as the same no-op the missing-leaf and scalar-parent cases already are. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc`, plus a unit case in the privacy / redaction tests. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. `privacy.cljc` has no reader conditional around `redact-path`. `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS lane. On CLJS, `assoc` on a vector with a keyword key throws `Error: Vector's key for assoc must be a number` — inspected, not run.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (2026-09-23): FIXED as prescribed, in PR #10281 (commit d1ea3bc301)

Reproduced at trunk 4b627ee9e2: the vector payload `{:cards [{:number "4111-vec"}]}` threw `IllegalArgumentException: Key must be integer` out of `dispatch-sync`. The map control `{:cards {:number "4111-map"}}` committed. After the fix, both commit.

Fix: `re-frame.privacy/redact-path` calls `assoc-in` only when the parent can TAKE the leaf segment: a map, or a vector under an in-range integer. Anything else, including a vector under a keyword and an out-of-range integer (which previously appended), is the same no-op as a missing or scalar parent, as the bead specifies. Note that this means a classified value inside a payload VECTOR is not redacted by the path-overlap arm (no-op, as ruled). Index-free matching into payload vectors would be a separate design call and was not attempted.

Regression: `re-frame.redact-path-vector-parent-cljs-test` (new, dual-runtime, always-on). It has a unit leg over map / vector-keyword / vector-in-range / vector-out-of-range / scalar parents, and a live path-focused dispatch leg. With the old `associative?` guard: 2 errors (`Key must be integer`) and 1 failure (out-of-range append). Restore verified by blob hash.
Merged-PR audit #10281 (ca03830caa98940c70532bb5d98a18edff364304; merged 2026-09-23T12:58:39Z). Completeness: The intended whole-root after-delta projection, vector-parent safe no-op, registration-owned error-event redaction and owning docstring correction are implemented. Overall after-delta privacy is still incomplete for focused slices, exactly as the PR declares; existing open/ready rf2-fc84b explicitly tracks that same defect and correction, so it is reused with its discovered-from link and a fresh source forward pointer. The separate snapshot-classification work rf2-3x7nj.4.3 is outside this PR. Correctness: Independent merged-source JVM regressions pass 29 tests/101 assertions (after-deltas, vector parents, error-record registration and epoch off-box projection), exit 0; always-on vector/error tests pass 3 tests/10 assertions under an asserted -Dre-frame.debug=false gate, exit 0. A separate real-producer focused-delta probe yields exactly 2 failures in 2 tests/10 assertions: the classified token remains in [:auth]-focused raw and off-box after-deltas; unrelated [:counter] focus and restored-root redaction controls pass. Evidence is ai/gate-classification-10281-audit-sep23-monitor-1, gate-classification-prod-10281-audit-sep23-monitor-1 and gate-focused-delta-10281-audit-sep23-monitor-1 log/exit pairs. CLJS was inspected and CI checked, not rerun locally: 75 success, 13 skipped, no failed/pending checks. Implementation quality: The implementation reuses established frame-scoped classification and late-bind hooks, preserves the ruled raw query-identity exceptions, and limits redact-path writes to compatible map/vector parents. No API growth or unrelated refactor is introduced. Keep the remaining focused-delta correction on rf2-fc84b rather than duplicate work or corrective-only notes. Guarded WORKTREE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/audit-sep23-monitor; no tracked source edits or mayor-checkout changes. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-fc84b.

DONE — merged as PR #10281 (head d1ea3bc301), with rf2-3x7nj.4.4 and .4.5; the sibling .4.3 was sequenced behind the elision PR (#10279). CI 88/88 at band. Local: core JVM 2320 tests exit 0, epoch 557 exit 0, ssr 688 exit 0, prod-gate lane 196 namespaces exit 0; CLJS legs graded by CI. Each control red with its fix removed, each restore blob-verified.

rf2-3x7nj.4.4 — FIXED as prescribed. privacy/redact-path now writes only into a map, or into a vector under an in-range integer; anything else is a no-op, so the vector payload that threw 'Key must be integer' out of dispatch-sync now commits. As the bead rules, a classified value inside a payload vector is not redacted by this path. CONTROL: new vector-parent test, fix removed -> 2 errors (Key must be integer) + 1 failure.

title: Correctness review: schemas — schemas
description:
Surface bead for slice `schemas` of the 2026-09-23 correctness review wave (epic rf2-3x7nj).

Surface: schemas (implementation/). Scope: 46 tracked files, 16855 lines; the exact file list is the slice scope file in the mayor's session scratchpad (review-wave/schemas.scope.txt), supporting detail only. Supporting context: spec/Spec-Schemas.md.

Frozen review tree: C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23 at trunk 034d0c8fc8.

One reviewer reads this slice and files ONE child bead per actionable correctness finding under this bead (labels review-wave:rf2-3x7nj, surface:schemas), appends its report to these notes, and closes this bead with the finding count and ids. The child beads are the fix work; this bead is the review.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.
notes:
## REVIEW REPORT: slice schemas (rf2-3x7nj.19), 2026-09-23 23:19:28 AUSEST

### Tree

Frozen tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23` at `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914`. `git rev-parse HEAD` was confirmed at the start and at the end.

### Scope read

Primary source, read in full (4,244 lines):

| File | Lines |
|---|---:|
| `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc` | 141 |
| `schemas/cache.cljc` | 45 |
| `schemas/digest.cljc` | 165 |
| `schemas/malli.cljc` | 75 |
| `schemas/storage.cljc` | 796 |
| `schemas/validate.cljc` | 1383 |
| `schemas/validator.cljc` | 405 |
| `schemas/walker.cljc` | 1234 |

Supporting material:

- Read in full: `spec/010-Schemas.md` (831 lines, the operative contract; the code cites it as "Spec 010"), `implementation/schemas/deps.edn` and `test/re_frame/schemas/test_fixture.clj`.
- Targeted: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (the `:rf/elision-marker` `:reason` enum) and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (the wire-marker `:reason`).
- Tests: `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (walker units, the `:set`/`:vector`/`:map-of` path pins), plus the deftest rosters of the fail-open, failure-paths, record-type-tag, validate-before-install and reg-side-effects files.
- Consumers: core `router.cljc:1180-1320` (the candidate-validation call site), `frame.cljc` (frame helpers), http `privacy_body.cljc` / `handlers.cljc` (`:decode` walker use), resources `classification.cljc` (params-schema walker use), epoch `tool_pair.cljc` (restore validation).

### Method

1. Traced every public entry: registration, the per-frame reads, the digest, the four `validate-*!` fns, the boundary seams, `redact-validation-tags`, and the late-bind publications. Each was checked against 010's validation-timing, per-step-recovery, `:sensitive?`, `:large?`, digest and production-elision clauses.
2. Walked the declaration walker (`walk-flags`), the value-path aligner (`align-in-path`) and the sanitizer in lockstep for every Malli op they classify, looking for a coordinate mismatch that fails open.
3. Checked both caches for staleness after re-registration.
4. Searched the tracker for each candidate. `bd search` matches titles only, so I searched a stdout `bd export` with Python across title, description, notes and close_reason, with a known-present needle as the control.
5. Confirmed findings with bounded process-local JVM probes. Each probe ran `java -cp <schemas :test classpath> clojure.main probeN.clj` from the frozen `implementation/schemas`, used the real `reg-app-schema`, `validate-*!` and `with-trace-recorder!`, and had controls both ways.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.19.1 | 1 | An app-db failure at a non-sensitive leaf inside a `:set` element ships the whole element, with its `:sensitive?` sibling, verbatim in `:path` and `:reason` (executed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.19.2 | 3 | The `:large?` size-safety arm is skipped for the app-db `:value` when any `:sensitive?` sibling exists (a 109 KB blob ships verbatim), and it overwrites `:rf.sub/query-v` with the value's marker; also 010:368 `:reason :frame` is spec-stale (executed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.19.3 | 3 | A `:map-of` KEY failure reports the entry's valid VALUE as the failing `:value` / "got <type>" (trace and always-on `:errors` record) (executed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.19.4 | 3 | The never-evicted sensitive-walker memo grows without bound in production when managed-HTTP feeds it per-request `:decode` schemas (executed: +93 MB per 200k requests, flat control) |

### Considered and rejected

- **Stale cache after re-registration.** Both memos (the printer and the sensitive walker) are keyed by schema VALUE, and `frame-schema-entries` reads the live atom. No stale entry is possible.
- **The malformed-schema dev trace's `:reason` embeds the throwing validator's message.** That message may carry the value, but 010:100 explicitly keeps it on the dev trace. The always-on record uses a constant sentence.
- **`:reason` carries `(pr-str schema)`.** 010:401 declares `:reason` structural, and the schema form is author data.
- **Keyword registry references are flag-invisible and do not fail closed.** This is a documented boundary (010:439, recorded under rf2-fzbj.25).
- **Walker and aligner coordinates.** Traced for `:map`, fixed and variable-width `:tuple`/`:cat`/`:catn`, `:map-of` (including sensitive and opaque keys), `:vector`/`:sequential`/`:set`, `:maybe`, `:and`/`:or`, `:multi`/`:orn`/`:altn`, `:ref`, local `:registry` and unknown ops. All are consistent or fail closed. A closed-map extra key fails closed whenever the map subtree is sensitive. The one open door is the `:set` segment (19.1).
- **`:rf.schema/violation` redacts on the NEW schema only.** A developer who removes `:sensitive?` in the edit is trusted.
- **A re-registration before the frame exists emits a spurious `:rf.schema/violation` with a nil value.** Dev noise only.
- **Production elision.** Every `validate-*!` body, warning, violation trace and `:errors` record sits under `debug-enabled?`. What survives (storage, path asserts, `validate-with-registered-fn`, `redact-validation-tags`, the walker) is the always-on contract by design.
- **Printer-memo equality collisions** (`[:a]` equals `'(:a)`, `1` equals `1N`). Contrived, and not valid or realistic Malli.
- **A CLJS anonymous predicate digests as `#fn`.** This is the documented fallback in `fn-token`.
- **`m/validate` re-parses vector schemas on each dev validation.** A dev-only cost, not pathological.
- **`reg-app-schemas` drops non-`:frame` opts keys.** Minor.
- **Prose drift in 010.** 010:664's `frame-reg-locks` no longer exists, and 010:117's "default is (current-frame-id)" is loose. Neither misleads anyone materially.
- **printer-seam test order isolation.** Already recorded as an observation under rf2-fzbj.25.

### Out of slice, for the mayor

`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:62-106` validates epoch restore by calling `:schemas/malli-validate` directly. That bypasses `set-schema-fns!`, which contradicts 010:23 ("every one routes through the registered validator fn"). A substituted validator, or `{:validate nil}`, does not reach restore. This belongs to the epoch slice and is not filed here.

### Could not verify

- **The CLJS host.** Shadow-cljs was forbidden. All four findings sit in plain `.cljc` with no reader conditional, so they are expected to reproduce there, but none was run on CLJS.
- **Finding 4's per-entry size.** Measured on the JVM only.

### Hygiene

No tracked file was edited and no git writes were made. The one `.cpcache` that the first classpath resolution created under the frozen `implementation/schemas` was removed afterwards (it was gitignored). The other `.cpcache` directories predate this review and were left alone.

## ADDENDUM: coordinator follow-up on the out-of-slice epoch item

The epoch reviewer's considered-and-rejected list (rf2-3x7nj.17 notes) does not cover this item. Its only schema entry is "restore validates only the app-db partition, not runtime-db", which is a different point. No tracker bead covered it either: the export search for `malli-validate-fn`, `restore-schema-mismatch` and `replace-schema-mismatch` returned 0 hits each.

I verified it with a bounded JVM probe (probe5.clj, schemas `:test` classpath plus `../epoch/src`):

- **Validation switched off** (`{:validate nil}`): the hot path committed `{:n "not-an-int"}` against `[:n] :int`, yet `restore-epoch!` to that very epoch returned false with `:rf.epoch/restore-schema-mismatch`, and `replace-frame-state!` returned false.
- **Substituted clojure.spec validator** (schema `::pos`): the hot path REJECTED `{:n -5}`, yet `replace-frame-state!` returned true and installed `{:n -5}`.
- **Control, default Malli bundle**: the probe refused `{:n "not-an-int"}` and admitted `{:n 7}`, as it should.

title: fresco: a nil controlled :value counts as uncontrolled - forms/buffered-field throws fresco-revision-not-controlled on a nil committed value, and a plain field remounts (focus lost) when its model moves between nil and text
description:
## Defect

The controlled-field path decides "is this a controlled `<input>`/`<textarea>`?" by whether the EMITTED `value` is non-nil (`controlled-text-tag?`), and that one predicate chooses two things that must not move with the model: the React element TYPE (the composition-shadow component vs the bare `"input"` string) and the `::h/revision` acceptance guard. So a field whose model value is `nil` — the ordinary reading of an unset draft or an entity that has no title yet — is a different element type from the same field one keystroke later, and refuses a revision outright. Two user-visible failures follow from the one rule: `forms/buffered-field` THROWS `:rf.error/fresco-revision-not-controlled` at render whenever its committed `:value` is nil and no draft is live (it always passes `::h/revision`), which is exactly the 05-forms guide's own example for a todo with no `:title`; and a plain controlled field whose model moves nil -> "a" (first keystroke) or "abc" -> nil (a commit that clears/dissocs the draft) has its element type flip between `"input"` and `shadow-input`, so React unmounts the DOM node and mounts a new one — focus, caret and any IME composition are lost, against 04-controlled-inputs guarantee 3 ("The node is not remounted").

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/controlled.cljs:195-206` — `controlled-text-tag?` = convergeable tag AND `(some? (unchecked-get js-props "value"))`.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/controlled.cljs:353-364` — `install!` refuses a revision unless `controlled-text-tag?`.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/controlled.cljs:375-379` — the same predicate picks the element type (`shadow-input` / `shadow-textarea` vs the tag string).
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:1392-1396` — `native-element` stashes the revision and creates the element from whatever `install!` answered; `convert-entry` (codec.cljs:393-414) emits a nil `:value` as `value: null`.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/forms.cljs:218-232` — `buffered-field` emits `:value (if (live? record revision) (:draft record) value)` (line 224) and ALWAYS `::rf.fresco/revision revision` (line 225).
- Public entry points: any `h/defview` body returning `[:input {:value (h/sub …) :on-input …}]` (the taught spelling, `docs/core/fresco/04-controlled-inputs.md:9-13`, also 01/02/03), and `re-frame.fresco.forms/buffered-field` as taught in `docs/core/fresco/05-forms.md:45-60`.

## Failure scenario

1. Crash. The 05-forms example verbatim: `:todo/title` is `(get-in db [:todo id :title])` (nil for a new todo — the example even carries `:placeholder "What needs doing?"`), `:todo/title-revision` defaults to `0`. Render `[title-field {:id 7}]` for a todo with no `:title`: `buffered-field` emits `{:value nil ::h/revision 0 …}` -> `native-element` sets the revision slot -> `install!` finds `value` null -> `:rf.error/fresco-revision-not-controlled` is thrown from the render ("…a non-nil :value to re-baseline TO"). The field never renders; the nearest error boundary (or the root) takes it.
2. Focus loss, first keystroke. `[:input {:value (h/sub [:todo.ui/draft id]) :on-input [:todo.ui/edit id ::h/value]}]` with the draft unset (nil). Render 1: element type `"input"`, `value: null` (uncontrolled). User focuses and types "a": the intent dispatches synchronously, the draft becomes "a", the boundary re-renders, `install!` now answers `shadow-input` — a different element type, so React deletes the focused `<input>` and mounts a fresh one showing "a", unfocused. The user's second keystroke goes nowhere.
3. Focus loss, clear. `[:form {:on-submit [:todo/submit]} [:input {:value (h/sub [:todo.ui/draft]) …}]]` (03-events-as-data.md:54-58) where `:todo/submit` dissocs the draft: after Enter the value returns to nil, the type flips back to `"input"`, the node is replaced and focus leaves the field — every "type, Enter, type the next one" loop breaks. `[::h/clear ::draft id]` on a `reg-state` concern with no `:default` does the same (reg-state's default is nil, state.cljc:245-249).

Plain React (and Reagent) keep the node across nil -> "a" (a dev warning about uncontrolled -> controlled, nothing worse); the remount is this runtime's own, introduced by choosing the element type off the value's nil-ness. React does print its one-shot "`value` prop on `input` should not be null" dev warning on render 1, so case 2/3 is not wholly silent in dev, but nothing connects that warning to the later focus loss, and case 1 is a hard throw on the guide's example.

## Evidence

Inspected (all CLJS; no JVM lane compiles these forms, and shadow-cljs is out of bounds for this review). Read `controlled.cljs` in full, `codec.cljs` `native-element`/`convert-entry`, `forms.cljs` in full, `state.cljc` (reg-state default nil). The type-stability concern is already a stated design law for the `:type` axis — `controlled_dom_cljs_test.cljs:311-330` (`the-element-type-does-not-move-when-the-input-type-does`: "A React element type that changed would REMOUNT the field — taking focus, selection and any composition with it") and `:515-533` — but no row covers the `value` nil <-> string axis: the only nil rows are `controlled_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363` (a nil value installs no wrapper) and `revision_dom_cljs_test.cljs:386-387` (a revision beside `:value nil` is refused, pinned as "the same statement" as no value). Control for the zero: grep for `:value nil` over `implementation/fresco/test` finds exactly those two rows, so the search can find the shape and no remount or buffered-field row exists. `forms_cljs_test` / `forms_dom_cljs_test` carry no nil-committed-value row (grep `:value nil|value nil` -> 0 in both, same instrument that found the two rows above). Tracker: `bd` search for `buffered-field`, `revision-not-controlled`, `controlled-text-tag` found no bead on this (6 / 1 / 0 unrelated hits).

## Smallest fix

Separate "which element type" and "may a revision sit here" from "is there a model value to converge to": choose the shadow component and accept the revision on tag + the `value` KEY being present (`(not (undefined? (unchecked-get js-props "value")))`), and keep `convergeable?`'s non-nil requirement for the converge wrapper. A nil value then stays React's uncontrolled rendering on a stable node, and `buffered-field` renders. (Alternative: have `buffered-field` coerce a nil `:value` to `""` — fixes the crash only, not the remount.) Update the `revision_dom_cljs_test.cljs:386-387` row, whose "same statement" premise this changes, and add rows for nil -> "a" keeping the node (browser lane) and for `buffered-field` with a nil committed value. Fence: `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/controlled.cljs`, `implementation/fresco/test/**`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

CLJS only: `npm run test:cljs` (node lane: `controlled_dom_cljs_test`, `revision_dom_cljs_test`, `forms_cljs_test` compile there) and the browser lane `npm run test:browser` for the DOM rows that prove the node is kept (`-dom-cljs-test` namespaces). A JVM green says nothing about these forms.

## Decision needed

No — unless Mike wants to keep "nil `:value` + revision is refused" for raw inputs, in which case `buffered-field` must stop emitting a revision (or coerce nil to "") when no model value exists.
notes:
## FIXED in PR #10283 (worker/fresco-nilvalue-3x7nj), 2026-09-23

**Premise verified at trunk 9b3e89f429.** implementation/fresco/ was unchanged since the frozen review tree 034d0c8fc8. The defect reproduced through the producer: with the fix removed, the real `forms/buffered-field` body rendered under `renderToString` with a nil committed `:value` refuses itself with `:rf.error/fresco-revision-not-controlled`.

**Fix, and how it differs from this item's "Smallest fix".** `controlled/install!` now writes `""` over a nil `:value` on any field whose value is its content (`empty-when-nil!`). That covers a `<textarea>`, and an `<input>` whose type is not a token/label/filename type: checkbox, radio, hidden, submit, reset, button, image and file keep nil, which React reads as no attribute. An unwritten `:value` stays uncontrolled. The emitted value is then non-nil, so the element type is stable across nil and text, the revision is accepted, and a model cleared to nil clears the box. `controlled-text-tag?` and `convergeable?` are unchanged.

The item suggested choosing the element type and accepting the revision on the `value` KEY, with nil staying React's uncontrolled rendering. That was planted and measured on the fresco browser lane (narrowed `:browser-test`, 507 tests). Node and focus were kept, but the box went stale:

title: core-reactive: egress resource-identity projection misfires on live sub nodes whose query vector is [kw kw map]
description:
## Defect

`project-graph` runs the live-RESOURCE identity projection (`project-resource-node-identity`) over EVERY node in the graph, whatever its family. The trigger is `scoped-resource-key?`, which matches ANY 3-vector with a keyword in the middle and a map at the end. A live SUBSCRIPTION node's `:id` and `:output` carry its concrete query vector, so a query vector shaped `[:sub-id :kw {…}]` is mistaken for a resource scoped key. Egress then replaces the sub-id and the map argument with opaque hashes in the node's `:id` and `:output`. Meanwhile the node KEY and every edge naming it keep the raw query vector.

The result is an egressed graph whose sub node no longer says which subscription it is, and whose `:id` no longer matches its own key. It hides nothing, since the key and the edges still carry the raw query vector. The docstring states the opposite: "Requiring the params map is what keeps this from misfiring on an unrelated 3-vector."

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:114-131` — `scoped-resource-key?` is a pure shape test, and its docstring at `:120-126` claims it does not misfire.
- `egress.cljc:248-279` — `project-resource-node-identity` projects `:id` whenever it matches (`:260-261`) and walks `:output` (`:263-264`).
- `egress.cljc:406-428` — `redact-node` applies that projection to every node with no family check. Node keys (`:290-296`) and edge endpoints (`:298-308`) are only remapped for `[:resource …]`, so the inconsistency is built in.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/tooling.cljc:475-476` — a live sub node's `:id` is the query vector and its `:output` is `[:fact query-v]`.
- Public entry point: `re-frame.derivation.egress/project-graph` (Xray's `redact-graph-for-egress`) over a `live-derivation-graph`.

## Failure scenario

A cached subscription `[:items/page :active {:limit 10}]` sits in the observed frame, and a tool egresses the live graph. The node stays under the raw key `[:sub [:items/page :active {:limit 10}]]`, but its fields are rewritten:

- `:id` becomes `[[:rf.resource/opaque "8dfb5748"] :active [:rf.resource/opaque "f9aa1a75"]]`;
- `:output` becomes `[:fact [[:rf.resource/opaque "8dfb5748"] :active [:rf.resource/opaque "f9aa1a75"]]]`.

A consumer grouping or labelling nodes by `:id` sees an unknown opaque "resource-like" identity. Equality between a node's `:id` and its key breaks for exactly these subs.

## Evidence

Executed: `scratchpad/review-wave/core-reactive/probe_egress_sub.clj`, one-shot `clojure -M` over the frozen `implementation/core/src`, run from the scratch dir. Nodes were shaped like `sub-cache-algebra-view`'s.

- `[:items/page :active {:limit 10}]`: `:id` and `:output` were rewritten as above, the key was kept raw, and `:id` no longer equals the query vector.
- Control, `[:items/page "active" {:limit 10}]` (middle not a keyword): unchanged.
- Control, `[:items/page :active]` (2-vector): unchanged.

The tracker export has no bead mentioning `scoped-resource-key?`.

## Smallest fix

Apply `project-resource-node-identity` only to resource nodes, gated on the node's KEY being a live resource key (`resource-node-key?`) or on `(= :resources (:rf/family node))`, so it is consistent with the key and edge remaps. Correct the `scoped-resource-key?` docstring. The fence is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`.cljc`, so both lanes:

- JVM: the `implementation/derivation-conformance` egress arms and `implementation/core`;
- CLJS: `npm run test:cljs`.

A regression row should egress a live sub node whose query vector is `[kw kw map]` and assert that its `:id` and `:output` are untouched.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix: PR #10280 (worker/reactive-graph-3x7nj), 2026-09-23 AUSEST

**Reproduced at trunk `2c8b8847a3`** (the fenced source was unchanged from the frozen `034d0c8fc8`). A one-shot `clojure -M` probe ran `project-graph` over a live sub node `[:items/page :active {:limit 10}]` stamped `:rf/family :subs`. Its `:id` became `[[:rf.resource/opaque "8dfb5748"] :active [:rf.resource/opaque "f9aa1a75"]]` and its `:output` became `[:fact <same>]`, while the key stayed raw. That matches the bead byte for byte. The controls `[:items/page "active" {:limit 10}]` and `[:items/page :active]` were unchanged. After the fix all three are unchanged.

**The fix** is in `egress.cljc` only. `project-graph`'s `redact-node` now takes the node key, and it applies `project-resource-node-identity` only when the new private `resource-node?` holds. That predicate is `(or (= :resources (:rf/family node)) (resource-node-key? node-key))`: the composer's family stamp, or a live resource node key.
- The family half keeps every resource node projected exactly as before, static nodes and tooling-projected keys included.
- The key half makes the field projection consistent with the key and edge remaps, so a hand-built resource node without a family stamp still has its `:id` projected whenever its key is remapped (it fails closed).
- No other family can match. The only inputs shaped `[:scope …]`/`[:param …]` are resources' (flows use `[:db …]`/`[:runtime …]`, routes and machines use `[:event …]`), so no other family was relying on the projection.

The `scoped-resource-key?` docstring now says it is a pure shape test that a sub query vector can match. The `project-graph` docstring notes the resource-only scope. The digest (rf2-3x7nj.3.4) is untouched.

**The regression row** is `g-egress-leaves-a-scoped-key-shaped-sub-node-alone` in the derivation-conformance `.cljc` suite, run on both lanes. The live graph comes from the composer, so `:rf/family` is stamped by the producer, not by hand. It holds a `[:items/page :active {:limit 10}]` sub next to the existing sensitive `egress-live-contributors` resource and route. It asserts the sub's key, `:id`, `:output` and `:id` = key-tail are unchanged. As a control that the fix narrows the projection rather than disabling it, the resource node is still projected: no secret anywhere, and the raw resource key gone.

**Control.** On the JVM with the gate replaced by `true`, the suite exited 1 with 3 FAILs, all in that row (`:id`, `:output`, `:id` = key), at the same 559 assertions. Restored from HEAD, `git hash-object` equals the committed blob hash `92eaabddf8759445c96df3b2500f58d791ad4499`.

**Gates.** Conformance JVM exit 0 (25 / 559). `implementation/core` JVM exit 0 (2314 / 12029). `tools/xray` JVM exit 0 (1364 / 6666); Xray consumes `project-graph`, and its redaction fixtures stamp `:rf/family` on every node. Egress-walker residue gate exit 0. The CLJS lane is left to CI on the PR.
## CORRECTION to the note above: the shipped gate is KEY-based (PR #10280, 2026-09-23 23:10 AUSEST)

The predicate described above, `(or (= :resources (:rf/family node)) (resource-node-key? node-key))`, is NOT what ships. On its first push it failed CI's `CLJS bundle isolation (counter, rf2-51x5)` positive control. The emitted `derivation-graph` module read 0 for its sentinel `rf/family` (expected >= 1). Reading `(:rf/family node)` in `egress.cljc` made egress reference that keyword for the first time (0 references on trunk), so the sibling `derivation-graph` and `derivation-egress` positive-control modules shared it and the literal left the `derivation-graph` module.

**Shipped:** `(resource-node? node-key)` = `(and (vector? node-key) (= :resource (first node-key)))`. The composer keys every resource node, static or live, `[:resource <id-or-scoped-key>]`, and the key and edge remaps read that same tag, so the projection stays consistent with them. `egress.cljc` references no `:rf/family`.

**Control, re-run on the shipped gate.** With the gate replaced by `true`, the conformance JVM suite exited 1 with 3 FAILs, all in `g-egress-leaves-a-scoped-key-shaped-sub-node-alone`. Restored, `git hash-object` equals the committed blob hash `6526d6d2681ffc158eeba5e6659eda43d4a3e61f`.

**CI on head `b839271e88`:** all 88 checks settled green, including bundle isolation and CLJS `:node-test` (12427 tests / 62603 assertions, 0 failures; the conformance namespace is on that build via `cljs-test$`).
Merged-PR audit #10280 (8ff2143962c9328267948eb8717327dbc3e0c1ab; merged 2026-09-23T13:11:32Z). Completeness: Complete: tolerant live-edge ordering covers out-of-CEDN float and function query arguments; resource identity projection is restricted to resource node keys. Both source claims and regression coverage inspected at merge 8ff2143962c9328267948eb8717327dbc3e0c1ab. Correctness: Correct: independently ran exact merged derivation conformance sources on JVM: 25 tests, 559 assertions, zero failures/errors, runner exit 0. Checked overlay resource identities and worker gate root. GitHub checks: 74 success, 14 skipped. No material actionable defect found. Implementation quality: Quality: narrow changes preserve canonical CEDN ordering, tolerate live query args, and align redaction with the existing resource-key convention without expanding the API or bundle dependencies. Trusted-programmer SPA posture respected. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
DONE — merged as PR #10280 (head b839271e88), with its sibling in the same PR. CI 88/88 at band; the CLJS node lane (12427 / 62603, 0 failures) carries the derivation-conformance rows. Local JVM: derivation-conformance 25 / 559, core 2314 / 12029, xray 1364 / 6666.

rf2-3x7nj.3.5 — FIXED with a different gate from the bead's two options. The egress resource-identity projection (derivation/egress.cljc) now runs only on nodes whose key starts with :resource, which the graph builder uses for every resource node, static or live. The bead's :rf/family option was tried first and turned CI's CLJS bundle-isolation check red (the derivation-graph module's "rf/family" string would have become shared with egress), so the key-prefix gate was used instead; the scoped-resource-key? docstring no longer claims the shape test cannot misfire. title: adapters: reagent-slim render-to-static-markup entity-escapes <style>/<script> bodies (corrupts inline CSS/JS) and drops pre/textarea leading-LF compensation
description:
## Defect `reagent2.dom.server/render-to-static-markup` entity-escapes the text inside ``. The mail client's CSS parser sees an invalid font-family value and an invalid selector, so the font and the rule are dropped. 2. `[:script "if (a < b && c) go()"]` emits `if (a < b && c) go()`, which is a JS syntax error. 3. `[:pre "\n indented"]` emits `
\n  indented
`. The parser eats the leading LF, so the rendered text is one line short of what the author wrote. React emits a compensating extra LF. ## Evidence - **Slim side: inspected.** The file is CLJS-only and shadow-cljs is out of bounds. description:
## Defect

Two pieces of normative spec describe `:rf.event/after-deltas` wrongly or not at all. The rf2-fc84b ruling (option B) keeps the slot, so both should now say what it is for.

- `spec/Conventions.md` row 122 (`:rf.interceptor.delta/*`) says the records are projected onto `:rf.event/run-end` "for the Xray AFTER INTERCEPTORS lens". That lens does not exist.
  * Its only reader, the Xray Handler panel's AFTER INTERCEPTORS section (`e4c1fbfd39`, rf2-9dk9y), was deleted with that panel in `aeb34400c0` (rf2-5gl5r, 2026-05-27).
  * The Epoch panel's speculative step was replaced in `7454b7056a` (rf2-se9a9t). `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` records it as a step "that the implementation never carried".
  * Today the slot reaches people through GENERIC inspection instead: the Xray Trace panel's raw payload inspector (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs` `render-payload`), and epoch `:trace-events` exported by the pair MCP `trace-window` tool.
- `spec/Conventions.md` row 69 lists `:rf.event/after-deltas` among the `:rf.event/*` tag keys and names 009 as the authoritative enumeration. Yet `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` never mentions the tag: `git grep -c after-deltas spec/009-Instrumentation.md` finds no match (exit 1), against a control of 12 for `rf.event/db-pending`.

The cost is not hypothetical. The decision dossier for rf2-fc84b read row 122's purpose clause, concluded the slot had no consumer, and recommended deleting it. The ruling rejected that recommendation on evidence at source.

## Fix

Both files are HOT ZONE, so sequence this behind any other holder. It lands AFTER rf2-fc84b, so that the text describes focus-anchored redaction as shipped.

title: flows: (rf/clear :flow id) from a user-registered fx deregisters the flow but leaves its output leaf and dependents stale until an unrelated drain - no settle is requested
description:
## Defect

`(rf/clear :flow id)` called from a user-registered fx runs during the `:fx` walk. `in-drain?` is true there, so `clear-flow*` takes the in-drain branch. It deregisters the flow, queues the output-path vacation for "the current pending-`:db` flow pass", and skips the direct settle on the grounds that "that pass performs the settle". But the `:fx` walk runs after this event's flow pass. No pending pass remains, and nothing requests one: only the reserved `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` bodies call `request-flow-settle!`. So the call returns with the flow's registry row gone while its own output leaf, and every dependent derived from it, stays in app-db until some later unrelated drain happens to run. That is the incoherent, self-healing state Spec 013 §Sequencing and §The same boundary for a direct `clear-flow` were written to eliminate, reached through a call site the in-drain reasoning does not cover. A same-frame `reg-flow` that moves its `:output-path`, called from a user fx, leaves the old leaf behind the same way (`registry.cljc:666-671`).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:892-897`: in-drain means queue the vacation. `:960-967`: the settle is excluded in-drain because "there the vacation is queued for the pending-`:db` pass and that pass performs the settle".
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1742-1765`: the flow pass is the outermost `:after`, before the install and the `:fx` walk.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:725-754`: `*flow-settle-requested*` is bound for one `:fx` walk. `:943-962`: only the two reserved bodies call `request-flow-settle!`.
- Contract: `spec/013-Flows.md:490` point 3 ("A `clear-flow` issued from inside a handler or a `:rf.fx/*` effect queues its vacation for the current pending-`:db` flow pass, and that pass performs the settle"). The premise is false for a user fx. Also `:453` (row gone while its value is still present) and `:484` (self-heals in a busy app, so presents as intermittent).
- Public entry points: `rf/reg-fx` whose handler calls `(rf/clear :flow id)`, dispatched from any event on the flow's frame.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-flow :p3/a {:inputs [[:x]] :output-path [:a]} identity)
(rf/reg-flow :p3/b {:inputs [[:a]] :output-path [:b]} identity)
(rf/reg-event :seed (fn [_ _] {:db {:x 2}}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:seed])                            ; {:x 2 :a 2 :b 2}
(rf/reg-fx :p3/clear-a (fn [_ _] (rf/clear :flow :p3/a)))
(rf/reg-event :go (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:p3/clear-a nil]]}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:go])
```

After `:go` settles, app-db is `{:x 2, :a 2, :b 2}` and `:p3/a` is no longer registered. The cleared flow's own leaf `:a` has not been vacated and `:b` is still derived from it. Only an unrelated no-op dispatch afterwards turns it into `{:x 2, :b nil}`. The identical clear via `[:rf.fx/clear-flow :p3/a]` settles to `{:x 2, :b nil}` within the dispatch.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. I ran a bounded JVM probe from a scratch deps project with `:local/root` pointing at the frozen tree (plain-atom substrate, standard `make-reset-runtime-fixture`), exit 0. Output: `P3 seeded: {:x 2, :a 2, :b 2}`. `P3 after user-fx clear: {:x 2, :a 2, :b 2} | :p3/a registered? false`. `P3 after an unrelated no-op drain: {:x 2, :b nil}`. CONTROL, re-registered and re-seeded, then `:rf.fx/clear-flow`: `{:x 2, :b nil}` within the dispatch.

Probe source (supporting only): `scratchpad/review-wave/flows/probe/src/flowprobe.clj`, case P3.

Tracker: rf2-g1zb (direct clear settles) explicitly preserved "in-drain behavior, where `clear-flow` already queues the vacation for the current pending-db flow pass", and rf2-kh73v (reserved-fx settle) scoped itself to the two reserved effects. Neither considered a clear issued during the `:fx` walk by anything other than the reserved body.

## Smallest fix

Request the settle from the lifecycle op itself, not only from the reserved bodies. `request-flow-settle!` is a no-op unless an `:fx` walk bound `*flow-settle-requested*`, so calling it on every in-drain clear (and in-drain path-moving `reg-flow`) is harmless from a handler body, where the current pass still settles, and correct from any fx, where the walk's terminal branch enqueues the one `[:rf/settle-flows]`. For example: publish it as a late-bind seam that `registry.cljc`'s two in-drain branches call, or call it from core's `clear-flow` wrapper path. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`, `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc`, and the late-bind directory (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc`) if a new hook is added. None of those is on the hot-zone list. Then correct the premise at `spec/013-Flows.md:490` point 3.

## Gates

Shared `.cljc` in both artefacts, with no reader-conditional branch at these sites. The JVM flows lane (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`) and the JVM core lane (`scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` includes `implementation/core`) grade it. If a late-bind hook is added, the late-bind drift test `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj` also grades it. The CLJS arm of a cross-host `*_cljs_test.cljc` pin is graded by `npm run test:cljs` only.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== NOTE FROM THE rf2-3x7nj.9.7 RULING (mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:08:41 AUSEST) ==

rf2-3x7nj.9.7 was ruled option (B): at the end of each `:fx` walk, a frame-state container that is no longer `identical?` to its start value, on a frame holding at least one flow (new flows-published hook `:flows/frame-has-flows?`), requests the same one head-inserted `[:rf/settle-flows]` the reserved flow effects request. That generic trigger does NOT fix this bead: a user-fx `(rf/clear :flow id)` mutates only side tables (the `flows-by-frame` row and the abandoned-path queue), so the container stays identical and the trigger never fires — measured: with no classified flow on the frame the state stays `{:x 2 :a 2 :b 2}` after one dispatch; it is "fixed" only when some flow on the frame carries `:sensitive`, because the clear then rewrites the elision registry in runtime-db (accidental coverage keyed to unrelated metadata). This bead's own smallest fix is therefore still required, and the ruling puts it in the SAME PR as 9.7:
- make `request-flow-settle!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc :772, currently `defn-`) public `^:no-doc` — flows requires core and `re-frame.fx` requires nothing from flows, so a direct `:require` is cycle-free and no late-bind hook is needed;

- rewrite the in-drain comment at :960-967 and spec/013-Flows.md :490 point 3 (the "that pass performs the settle" premise is false for a user fx).
Simulated alone (registry op calls `request-flow-settle!`, (B) off): `{:x 2 :b nil}` in one dispatch. Pin it on a frame with NO classified flow — that is the variant (B) alone leaves red. All line numbers re-verified at trunk a61f903c5c (flows/src and spec/013 byte-identical to 034d0c8fc8). Sequencing with rf2-3x7nj.18.2 (flows.cljc + spec/013 :482/:488/:502): no code overlap, adjacent spec edits — sequence or combine. Full reasoning and measurements are on rf2-3x7nj.9.7's RULING note.
== WORKER: FIXED — PR #10297 (branch worker/flows-3x7nj, with rf2-3x7nj.9.7 and .18.2), 2026-09-24 ==
