  - In clear-flow*, the single in-drain? reading now picks between two branches: (rf.fx/request-flow-settle!) in-drain, or the direct settle out of drain. It sits at the existing settle site, inside the exact-owner postcheck and the when-let on the flow row, rather than beside the vacation line the ruling cited, so a lost owner or an unknown id requests nothing.
  - The in-drain path-moving reg-flow branch requests the settle after record-abandoned-output-path!.
  - The in-drain comment is rewritten, and the clear-flow docstring gains an in-drain paragraph.

The §Sequencing NORMATIVE block now covers clear-flow and :output-path-moving reg-flow "called from any effect, reserved or application-registered". docs/api/re-frame.flows.md says the same.

title: epoch: a post-settle sub recompute's :where :sub-return schema failure is orphan-dropped while its sibling :rf.sub/run is back-filled — Xray shows the replaced nil as a clean sub, outcome :ok
description:
## Defect

A subscription recompute that runs after its event settled (post-settle) has two traces of interest. Its `:rf.sub/run` trace is back-filled into the frame's last-settled epoch record. But if the same recompute fails its `:schema`, the `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :sub-return` trace it emits is dropped by epoch capture's orphan-drop arm.

The record therefore keeps the sub-run while losing its failure. In Xray's Epoch panel the sub appears as a clean SUBSCRIPTIONS row showing the `nil` it was replaced with. No violation is attached, and the panel outcome reads `:ok`.

In a browser this is the common path, not an edge. Subscriptions deref lazily at React render time, which Reagent batches after the cascade settles, as `capture.cljc`'s own `sub-run-ops` comment says. So an event-driven sub-return failure in a real app essentially never reaches the epoch record. Only a recompute inside a drain reaches it: a handler that subscribes, or SSR.

The failure is not retained in the per-frame trace ring either, which keeps only emits carrying both `:frame` and a dispatch-id. This is inspected at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:261`, `(when (and dispatch-id frame-id) ...)`, and not measured. The orphan-drop arm's comment at `capture.cljc:294-295` says such an emit "still rides the raw trace ring", which is stale for this class. So after the fact, only a listener that was attached live ever saw it.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc:243-313`: `capture-event!`'s routing `cond`.
  - Post-settle `render-ops`, `sub-run-ops` and `unmount-ops` each have a back-fill arm (`:253`, `:262`, `:281`).
  - Everything else with `:frame`, no dispatch-id and no in-flight cascade takes the orphan-drop arm (`:308-310`, returns nil).
  - That arm's own comment scopes the drop class to frame-lifecycle and registry-time emits. The unmount comment (`:110-131`) calls "no signal anywhere in the epoch record" for a post-settle consequence the thing to avoid.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc:190-214` (`record-sub-run!`) and `:218-240` (`record-unmount!`): the back-fill hooks, which target `last-settled-epoch-id`.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:832-927`: `back-fill-event!` and its thin wrappers. `back-fill-unmount!` is already a trace-events-only back-fill with no structured row.
- Emit site: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1192-1225` (`validate-sub!`). Its docstring says "The optional frame is stamped on the trace so runtime calls join the in-flight epoch". The caller `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:272` passes the reaction's `frame-id`, and validation runs before the sibling `:rf.sub/run` emit.

Spec passages:

- `spec/010-Schemas.md:190` (§Per-step recovery). The `:frame` tag names "the reaction's frame for the sub-return surface". The passage calls that tag "load-bearing for per-frame epoch capture" and names the silent drop from the epoch's `:trace-events`, "leaving the per-frame timeline tools ... blind", as the failure it exists to prevent. It covers only the in-flight case.
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:276` (§Tooling surface — Xray attachment): "`:sub-return` to the matching SUBSCRIPTIONS row ... so no violation vanishes".
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:72`: a trace emitted outside the run carries no dispatch-id. So core's missing dispatch-id is per contract, not the bug.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:740`: the SAME epoch "re-publishes ... when a post-settle render / sub-run / unmount back-fills into that already-settled epoch". This is the designed home for post-settle consequences of an event.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:877-881` (B3+B4, frameless events are live-stream only) does NOT cover this. B3's class is emits with "no dispatch-id and no destination frame", and this trace carries its frame.

No passage rules that a post-settle sub-return failure belongs to no epoch. The implementation's decision to back-fill the sibling sub-run already assigns the recompute to the last-settled epoch. So this is a defect, not a design choice.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-sub ::cart-total {:schema :int} (fn [db _] (get-in db [:cart :total])))` is rendered by a view. An event writes `"12.50"` (a string) to `[:cart :total]`. At the next render the sub recomputes, fails its schema, and hands the view `nil` (`:replaced-with-default`).

Xray's Epoch panel for that event shows SUBSCRIPTIONS `::cart-total` changed to `nil`, with no violation, and outcome `:ok`. The programmer sees a total that vanished and a panel saying nothing went wrong. The one trace that explains it, the schema failure, is gone from the record and from the ring.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe (`probe3.clj`; earlier `probe2.clj` P6). It ran from the review scratch dir against the frozen tree via a `:local/root` on `tools/xray`, on the real core runtime (plain-atom substrate). The tree read 0 porcelain lines before and after.

P7a, post-settle (the sub is derefed after `dispatch-sync` returns):

```

deref (value handed to the consumer): nil
raw stream: sub-return violations 1 | :rf.sub/run for the sub 1
  violation tags :frame :rf/default :rf.trace/dispatch-id nil
  sibling :rf.sub/run tags :frame :rf/default :rf.trace/dispatch-id nil
epoch 1 :user/seed outcome :ok | :trace-events retained? true | sub-run traces for :user/total : 1 | :sub-runs rows for :user/total : 1 | sub-return violations in :trace-events: 0
  xray SUBSCRIPTIONS rows [sub changed? #violations]: [[:user/total true 0]] | steps carrying violations: [] | panel outcome: :ok
```

The two traces carry identical routing tags. The run is back-filled and the violation is dropped. `:trace-events` WAS retained, so the zero is not elision.

P7b, the control in-flight (the same bad sub, first derefed inside a handler):

```
violation tags :frame :rf/default :rf.trace/dispatch-id 3
epoch 3 :user/reads-in-handler outcome :ok | ... | sub-return violations in :trace-events: 1
  xray SUBSCRIPTIONS rows [sub changed? #violations]: [[:user/total2 true 1]] | steps carrying violations: [[:subscriptions 1]] | panel outcome: :error
```

Once the trace is in `:trace-events`, the rest of the chain works: Xray attaches it to the SUBSCRIPTIONS row and the outcome turns `:error`. That isolates the defect to capture routing.

P6, run earlier: 3 post-settle recomputes over 3 events gave 3 raw violations, all with nil dispatch-id, 0 in any record, and panel outcome `:ok` throughout.

Not executed: the browser path. The claim that render-time recomputes are post-settle comes from `capture.cljc:92-105` and `listeners.cljc:190-200`, and no CLJS was run. Two siblings are not measured: `:where :sub-override` (the render-phase override seam) and the reactive-path sub-compute exception. By inspection they route the same way.

Dedupe:

- Checked all 3 children of rf2-3x7nj.17 and its considered-and-rejected list. The only post-settle item there is LOCAL-state render back-fill.
- Checked all 7 children of rf2-3x7nj.4, plus rf2-3x7nj.3 and rf2-3x7nj.19 and their children.

- `bd search` is title-only here: it read 0 for `sub-return` where the full-text scan read 10.

## Smallest fix

The fix belongs in the EPOCH capture. Core's trace attribution needs no change: the `:frame` tag is right (measured `:rf/default`), and the missing dispatch-id is per 009:72. Xray needs no change (P7b).

In `capture-event!`, add an arm before the orphan-drop arm. It matches a `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` whose `:where` is `:sub-return` or `:sub-override`, arriving with no in-flight cascade, and routes it through a trace-events-only back-fill into `last-settled-epoch-id`. Model it on `record-unmount!` / `back-fill-unmount!` (row nil, listener re-notify, sensitive rollup already handled by `back-fill-event!`).

The violation then lands in the same epoch as its sibling `:rf.sub/run`, because both hooks target the last-settled record. Include the owner-claim condition at `:218-228` so the arm claims the frame like its siblings.

Spec, one clause at `spec/010-Schemas.md:190` (not hot-zone): a post-settle recompute's failure is back-filled with its sub-run into the causing epoch. If the enumeration at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:740` ("render / sub-run / unmount") is to stay exhaustive, it needs the same clause. **`spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is a HOT-ZONE file**: sequence it, or leave 009 alone and let 010 carry the rule.

Residual, stated rather than fixed: a record whose `:trace-events` was elided by the keep-window still cannot carry the violation, exactly as for unmounts.

Add a regression test pinning both directions: a post-settle sub-return failure lands once in the last-settled record, and an in-flight one is still buffered once, not twice.

No. The target epoch is already decided by the sibling sub-run's existing back-fill policy, and the violation should follow its run. The only alternative is to rule these failures live-stream-only. title: schemas: the :large? size-safety arm is skipped for the app-db :value when any :sensitive? sibling exists (blob ships verbatim), and it overwrites :rf.sub/query-v with the value's marker
description:
## Defect

The `:large?` size-safety arm of validation-failure traces is skipped for the app-db `:value` slot whenever the schema declares ANY `:sensitive?` slot, even when the failing leaf is not sensitive. `whole-large?` is gated on `(not whole-sensitive?)`, but `:value` is redacted only under the narrower `leaf-sensitive?`. When a `:large?` slot fails in a schema that also has a sensitive sibling, `:value` is neither redacted nor size-elided, and the whole blob rides the trace verbatim.

A second defect sits in the same arm. `elide-large-slots` writes the value's size marker into EVERY value-bearing slot, including `:rf.sub/query-v`. That slot is the subscription's query vector, not the checked value. A large sub-return (or `:sub-override`) failure therefore loses its query vector, which is replaced by a marker describing a different value (`:type :map`, `:bytes` of the return value). Xray matches sub-return violations to their SUBSCRIPTIONS row by `:rf.sub/query-v`.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1060-1061`: `whole-large? (and (not whole-sensitive?) (schema-has-large? schema))`.
- `validate.cljc:1120-1124`: `redact-tags-per-slot` scrubs `:value` only under `leaf-sensitive?`, then large elision runs only under `whole-large?`.
- `validate.cljc:102-103,137-153`: `value-bearing-slots` includes `:rf.sub/query-v`, and `elide-large-slots` overwrites each present slot with the marker of `v`.
- `validate.cljc:782-797` (`run-validation`, reached from `validate-sub!`) and `validate.cljc:1379-1383` (`redact-validation-tags`, reached from the `:sub-override` path) both reach the query-v overwrite.
- Public entries: `re-frame.schemas/validate-app-schema!` and `validate-sub!`, and the `:schemas/redact-validation-tags` hook.

## Failure scenario

Scenario 1, the `:value` slot:

```clojure
(rf/reg-app-schema [:doc]
  [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]
        [:pdf {:large? true} :string]])
;; a handler commits {:doc {:token "ok" :pdf <20000-element vector>}}
```

The trace carries `:path [:doc :pdf]`, `:value <the whole 20000-element vector>`, `:explain :rf/redacted` and no `:large?` tag. Its tags pr-str to 109,262 bytes.

Control: the identical failure without the `:sensitive?` sibling emits the `:rf.size/large-elided` marker, and its tags pr-str to 702 bytes.

Scenario 2, the query vector: `(validate-sub! :probe/sub [:probe/sub 42] {:pdf blob} {:schema [:map [:pdf {:large? true} :string]]})` emits `:rf.sub/query-v #:rf.size{:large-elided {:path [] :bytes 108898 :type :map ...}}`. The query vector `[:probe/sub 42]` is gone.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe (probe2.clj, run from the frozen tree's `implementation/schemas`) through the real `validate-app-schema!`, `validate-sub!` and `with-trace-recorder!`. It produced cases D, E (the control) and F as quoted above.

Contract: spec/010-Schemas.md:368. It says that when the schema declares any `:large?` slot "(and no `:sensitive?` slot governs the redaction)" the emit-site substitutes the marker "for the whole value-bearing slots". Nothing sensitive governs `:value` here, because the leaf decision is non-sensitive, and :431 reserves "sensitive wins" for a slot that carries BOTH flags.

The same paragraph also says the marker carries `:reason :frame`. The code emits `:reason :effect` (validate.cljc:124-135), which is what the `:rf/elision-marker` enum permits (spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3646 lists `:effect :machine :resource :route :flow`; `:frame` is not a member). That is spec-stale.

No tracker bead covers this: the export was searched for `whole-large?`, `elide-large-slots` and `size-safety`, with 0 hits each. The control needle `failing-in-path` returned 1 hit.

## Smallest fix

- In `validate-app-schema!`, elide the narrowed `:value` slot when the leaf is not sensitive and the schema has `:large?`. Build that marker from `leaf-value`, not the whole registered value, so no sensitive sibling contributes to `:bytes`.
- In `elide-large-slots`, leave `:rf.sub/query-v` alone, because it is not the checked value.
- Correct spec/010-Schemas.md:368 from `:reason :frame` to `:reason :effect`.

Fence: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc`, `spec/010-Schemas.md` (not a hot-zone file), and tests in `schemas_walker_large_test.clj` / `schemas_sensitive_test.clj`.

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/schemas`.
- CLJS: the code is plain `.cljc` shared by both hosts, so also `npm run test:cljs`.
- Docs: `python -m mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec edit.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## FIXED — PR #10303 (worker/schemas-3x7nj), 2026-09-24

Reproduced at trunk 328b6bd194. With a `:sensitive?` sibling present, a 20000-char `:large?` leaf rode `:value` verbatim with no `:large?` tag. `validate-sub!` replaced `:rf.sub/query-v [:probe/sub 42]` with a `:rf.size/large-elided` marker describing the return value.

Fix, following the bead's three parts:
- `validate-app-schema!` scopes the size arm per slot, like redaction: `leaf-large?` = schema-has-large? and not `leaf-sensitive?`, and it elides the narrowed `:value` with a marker built from `leaf-value`; `whole-large?` (not `whole-sensitive?`) elides the whole-payload slots with the `registered-value` marker.
- `elide-large-slots` takes a slot list whose default, `size-elided-slots`, is `value-bearing-slots` minus `:rf.sub/query-v`. This covers the `run-validation` path and the `redact-validation-tags` seam (`:sub-override`).
- spec/010-Schemas.md §`:large?` in validation-failure traces now says `:reason :effect`, not `:frame`, and describes the per-slot decision and the query-v exclusion.

Regressions (schemas_sensitive_test.clj):
- `app-db-validation-large-leaf-beside-sensitive-sibling-elides`: `:explain` is redacted and `:value` is a marker with `:type :string` (built from the leaf). The sentinel "BLOB-SENTINEL-19-2-…" is absent from `(pr-str trace)`, and so is the sibling token.
- `sub-return-large-elision-keeps-query-v`: covers the hot path and the seam.

Control: both were red at trunk, with the blob present. Planting the fix out again (`leaf-large?` gated on `whole-sensitive?`, and `size-elided-slots` back to `value-bearing-slots`) turned them red (6 assertions). The restore was verified by blob hash. Schemas JVM green after: 416 tests / 19473 assertions.

Accepted reported 21-artifact JVM run, schemas 416/19473, HTTP 524/4125, measured heap probe and targeted negative controls; CI 62 successful checks. Implementation quality: Keeps existing late-bind key and registered-schema memo, avoids an LRU or another public API, and distinguishes lookup identity from payload. No material additional finding. title: core-instrumentation: retire the dormant :as-of-epoch project-egress opt - its only effect is a four-element handle the normative marker schema rejects
description:
Discovered from rf2-3x7nj.32.5. That ruling (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-24) withdraws spec 009's promise of epoch-resolvable size-marker handles: a handle is always `[:rf.elision/at <path>]`, a live-path locator. The ruling deliberately left core's `:as-of-epoch` egress opt OUT of its change. This item is the leftover it creates.

## Defect

The public `rf/project-egress` door still accepts `:as-of-epoch` in its closed opts map. Its ONLY effect is to make `->marker` emit a four-element handle, `[:rf.elision/at <path> :as-of-epoch <id>]`. The normative marker schema REJECTS that handle: spec/Spec-Schemas.md :3647 types `:handle` as a two-tuple, and so does the conformance mirror at tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/wire_vocab/schemas.clj:246. Measured at trunk 6b787c338b (JVM probe, public door, verbatim `ElisionMarkerBody`): the four-element marker validates false and the two-element control validates true. Once rf2-c5ggd item 2 deletes the variant prose, nothing documents what the opt does, and a caller who passes it gets schema-invalid output. No caller passes it today: `git grep -n as-of-epoch -- 'implementation/*/src/**' 'tools/*/src/**' 'skills/*/preload/**'` finds definitional sites only (control: `rf.elision/at` is found in 6 files under tools/*/src).

## Where (trunk 6b787c338b)

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc: `handle-of` (:658-662), `->marker`'s destructuring (:669, :680), `marker-opts` (:698), the walk ctx (~:1112), and the closed walker-opt key list (~:1179). Its docstring shape is at ~:1240.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc: pass-through comments at :177, :230 and :713.
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1433 (`walker-overlay-keys`).
- Test: implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj:344-346 pins the four-element constructor output. implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_closed_egress_opts_test.clj:39 carries the "twelve-key" count.
- Prose naming the opt: spec/API.md :721 and :733 (HOT ZONE), spec/Spec-Schemas.md :3685 plus the count at :3672 ("holds **twelve** keys: the walker's own closed eight, ..."; both numbers drop by one) (HOT ZONE), spec/015-Data-Classification.md :231, the spec/009-Instrumentation.md :2324 row (HOT ZONE), docs/api/re-frame.core.md :982 and docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md :176 ("twelve-key"), and docs/EP/EP-0015-frame-owned-egress-policy.md :761. It is not in the spec/api-manifest*.edn sidecars: `git grep as-of-epoch -- 'spec/api-manifest*.edn'` exits 1.

## Smallest fix

Retire the opt: delete it from the closed opts map and the walker, fix the "twelve-key" counts to eleven (and the walker's "closed eight" to seven), delete the constructor pin, and correct the prose. A caller passing it then gets `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts` naming the key, which is the closed-map contract working as designed. Do NOT instead widen the schema to admit the four-element handle: rf2-3x7nj.32.5 ruled epoch-resolvable handles out, and a handle that no reader resolves is noise.

## Gates

title: story-ui-workspace: Controls infer [:int {:min :max}] (the spec's flagship prop) and other property-carrying scalars as a text box that writes strings
description:
## Defect

The Controls panel's schema-to-widget inference recognises scalar schemas only as bare keywords. `infer-widget` matches `(= :int schema-fragment)`, `:double`, `:boolean`, `:keyword` and `:string`. A vector scalar schema carrying Malli properties goes to the vector branch, where the `case` has no `:int`/`:double`/`:boolean`/`:keyword`/`:string`/`:maybe` arm, so it falls through to `{:widget :text}`. Examples of such schemas are `[:int {:min 8 :max 64}]`, `[:double {:min 0}]` and `[:boolean {:doc ...}]`.

A plain text control writes the raw DOM string through `on-string-change`. It has no `:coerce`, unlike the `:keyword` arm fixed by rf2-i6v4.

So the bounded-int prop in the spec's own headline example renders a text box instead of the promised slider or number input. Editing it writes the STRING `"24"` into the arg. The view receives a string. The Controls panel then flags that row as violating the very schema that generated the control.

`[:int {:min ...}]` is the ordinary way to write a bounded number in Malli, so every story of such a view hits this.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/controls.cljs:148-197`, `infer-widget`: the bare-keyword scalar arms are at `:180-184`, the vector `case` at `:186-194`, and its `{:widget :text}` fallback at `:193-194`.
- `schema-op` is `rf.story.malli-schema/schema-op`, the first element (`malli_schema.cljc:21-25`), so `[:int {...}]` dispatches as `:int`.
- `controls.cljs:451-458` is `render-text`: with no `:coerce` it wires `on-string-change` (`:395-399`), which writes the raw string.
- `render-number` (`:466-474`) is the typed path this arg should have taken.
- Contract:
  - `tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md:262-304`: "Write `[:int {:min 0 :max 100}]` once on the view's props schema ... and every story of that view gets the slider". The headline table maps "`:int` / `:double` with `:min :max`" to a slider, and the flagship view declares `[:size [:int {:min 8 :max 64}]]`.
  - `:1619-1625` (§Schema-derivation pipeline) says "`:int` / `:double` (optional `:min` / `:max`) → `{:widget :number}`".
- Public entry: the Controls panel on any variant whose view declares a properties-carrying scalar prop.

## Failure scenario

The view declares `:rf/props [:map ... [:size [:int {:min 8 :max 64}]] ...]`, as in `001-Authoring.md` verbatim, and the variant compiles its schema (for example, it restates its props).

1. Open Controls. `:size` is a text input showing `20`.
2. Type `24`. The cell-override becomes `{:size "24"}`.
3. The canvas re-runs with `:size "24"`, a string, in the view's args.
4. The Controls row for `:size` shows a schema violation.

The same happens for `[:double {...}]` (numbers become strings), `[:boolean {...}]` (a text box instead of a checkbox) and `[:maybe :int]`.

## Evidence

INSPECTED for the widget choice. `controls.cljs` is CLJS-only, so it is not JVM-loadable. The branch structure is unambiguous at the cited lines.

EXECUTED for the two facts the inspection rests on, and for the consequence. This was a bounded JVM probe from `tools/story` at `034d0c8fc8`:
- `(rf.story.malli-schema/schema-op [:int {:min 8 :max 64}])` = `:int`, which is not a `case` arm. Control: `(schema-op :int)` = nil, the bare-keyword path.
- With the flagship view and a variant restating its props, `rf.story.plan/effective-args` with `{:cell-overrides {:size "24"}}` = `{... :size "24" ...}`. The string reaches the view.
- `rf.story.ui.schema-validation/args-violations` over those args against the view's `:rf/props` (Malli validate/explain) = `[:size]`.
- Control, `{:size 24}` (what `render-number` writes): `args-violations` = `[]`.

Not covered by rf2-i6v4, which fixed enum selects and the bare `:keyword` coercion; its record has no mention of property-carrying scalars. Tracker search for `infer-widget` returns only rf2-i6v4. No test pins a vector scalar anywhere. The regex `\[:(int|double|boolean) \{` returns 0 matches across `tools/story/test/re_frame`. The same pattern returns 7 matches in `tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md`, so the instrument can find the shape. The existing `infer-widget` tests (`story_ui_cljs_test.cljs:194-198`, `controls_scalar_widgets_cljs_test.cljc`) use only bare keywords.

Interaction with rf2-3x7nj.28.3, the view-args-schema finding filed beside this one: under the flagship story shape the schema currently resolves to nil, so this path is masked by value-shape inference (`16` becomes a number widget). Fixing that finding exposes this one on every flagship variant.

## Smallest fix

In `infer-widget`, dispatch vector scalars on `schema-op` the same way the bare keywords are dispatched:
- `:int`/`:double`/`:number` → `{:widget :number}` (plus `:min`/`:max` from `schema-properties` if a slider is wanted);
- `:boolean` → `:boolean`;
- `:keyword` → `{:widget :text :coerce :keyword}`;
- `:string` → `:text`;
- `[:maybe X]` → recur on X.

Optionally have `render-number` honour an integer schema (`parseInt`), since `:int` currently accepts `2.5`.

Fence: `ui/controls.cljs`, plus a CLJS test. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`controls.cljs` is CLJS-only, so only the CLJS lane (`npm run test:cljs`) compiles and grades the fix. No JVM artefact loads it.

## Decision needed

No. Slider versus number input for bounded ints is the spec's own call: the headline says slider, the pipeline says `:number`. Either is correct as long as the value is a number.

Implementation quality: Focused changes reuse existing helpers. Remaining corrections should preserve one component/arg resolution policy and the existing reproducibility classifier rather than add new APIs. Actionable findings: rf2-yfwfa, rf2-nlvgc. title: story-ui-evidence: multi-substrate cell error boundary never renders its captured error, so a view that throws under one substrate re-throws past it and unmounts the whole Story shell (and no substrate failure record is written)
description:
## Defect

The multi-substrate grid's per-cell "error boundary" does not isolate anything:

- Its `:get-derived-state-from-error` records `#js {:error ...}`, but the `:reagent-render` never reads that state. It always re-renders the same child.
- Its `try`/`catch` only guards building the hiccup vector. The view itself renders later, as a child component during React's render, outside the `try`.

So when a view throws under one substrate, the boundary captures, re-renders the same throwing child, and React skips the boundary on the retry, because it has already captured. The error then propagates to the next boundary up. Story has none: this is the only `componentDidCatch`/`getDerivedStateFromError` in `tools/story/src`. The React root unmounts, and the whole Story shell goes blank instead of showing a red cell beside the healthy substrates.

The failure is also never appended to the variant's `:assertions` as the spec requires, so a substrate-portability gap leaves no evidence at all.

Secondary: `r/create-class` is minted inside `safe-render-cell` on every render. The grid derefs `shell-state-atom`, so every shell-state change makes a new component type and remounts every cell, discarding the subject's local state.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:410-465` (`safe-render-cell`):
  - `:component-did-catch` returns nil;
  - `:get-derived-state-from-error` returns `#js {:error (str error)}`;
  - `:reagent-render` is `(try [:div ... (render-fn ...)] (catch ...))` and ignores state.
- `:257-281`: the `:reagent` render-fn returns `[resolved eff-args]`, so the view renders as a child component outside the `try`.
- `:511-550`: `multi-substrate-grid` derefs `shell-state-atom` at `:524` and calls `safe-render-cell` per cell.
- Entry point: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:700-708` renders this grid whenever a variant declares two or more `:substrates`.
- Contract: `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md` §Multi-substrate side-by-side rendering (lines 268-277) says:
  - "Each per-substrate render runs in a try/catch boundary";
  - "A substrate-specific failure renders inline alongside the other substrates' healthy renders";
  - "The failure record is appended to the variant's :assertions list, tagged with the substrate that failed".
- The ns docstring (`:5-9`) and the grid docstring (`:516-517`) make the same claim.

## Failure scenario

1. A variant declares `:substrates #{:reagent :fresco}` with both registered. Its view throws during render under one of them, which is the portability gap this feature exists to show.
2. Expected: the healthy cell renders, the failing cell shows "<substrate> — render error", and an assertion record names the substrate.
3. Actual: the boundary's retry re-throws, React propagates the error past it, and with no outer boundary the root unmounts. The Story UI blanks: sidebar, canvas and panels are all gone. No assertion record is written.

## Evidence

INSPECTED only. This is a `.cljs` file, and the brief allows no shadow-cljs build or browser.

- A search for `component-did-catch|getDerivedStateFromError|get-derived-state-from-error` over `tools/story/src` returns only this file.
- A search for `substrate[- ](failure|render-error|error)` over `tools/story/src` returns only the docstring at `:412`. That is both the control (the pattern can match) and the proof that the `:assertions` append is not implemented.

The retry-skips-a-boundary-that-already-captured behaviour is React's documented error-boundary semantics: a boundary whose fallback render throws again hands the error to its parent boundary. With no outer boundary the root unmounts. React is 19.3.0 per `implementation/package.json`. This is reasoned from React semantics and was not run.

Dedup: there is no bead on the multi-substrate error boundary. rf2-3x7nj.6.3 (the adapters ratom leak under error boundaries) is unrelated.

## Smallest fix

1. Define the boundary class ONCE at namespace top level.
2. Have its render read the captured error from `(.-state this)` and render the existing red error cell (the `:error-cell` / `:error-head` / `:error-body` styles already exist) instead of the child.
3. Optionally append the failure record per the spec from `:component-did-catch`.
4. Remove the misleading `try`, or keep it only for render-fn lookup errors.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

A `.cljs` file is compiled only by the CLJS lane. Run `npm run test:cljs`, plus a browser/DOM test that mounts the grid with a throwing view and asserts one error cell plus one healthy cell. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No. One choice is optional: whether the `:assertions` append is still wanted, or spec 003 should drop that bullet as spec-stale.
notes:
## Fix — PR #10326 (worker story-ev-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Re-verified at trunk 63e118215c, after PR #10317's rework: `safe-render-cell` still minted `r/create-class` per render, its render ignored the captured state, and the `try` wrapped only the hiccup build.

Fix in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs`:
- `cell-boundary` is ONE class at namespace level, and it takes a single props map.
- Once it has captured an error, it renders the existing red error cell (`<substrate> — render error` plus the message) instead of the child.
- `getDerivedStateFromProps` clears the captured error when the cell's props change.
- The render fn is called from a child (`cell-subject`), so a throw from the render fn itself is caught too.
- The misleading `try` is gone.

`canvas_substrate_routing_cljs_test`'s `grid-cells` (from #10317) read the cell positionally; it now reads the props map.

Decision on the optional choice (mayor's call: take the smaller change). The append is NOT implemented, and nothing depends on it:
- the only code or spec hit for `substrate[- ](failure|render-error|error)` in `tools/story/src` was the docstring;
- a tracker search for substrate-tagged / "substrate that failed" wording found only the closed survey rf2-m6tu, this item and its closed surface bead.

So the spec 003 bullet ("The failure record is appended to the variant's :assertions list…") was DROPPED as stale, together with the matching clause in DESIGN-RATIONALE §inline-substrate-failures' Implication. The locked decision itself (inline, not auto-skipped) is untouched.

Regression: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs` mounts the real grid via `reagent.dom.client` inside a test-owned outer boundary. There are three rows:
1. the throwing `:uix` cell is red beside the healthy `:reagent` cell, and nothing escapes;
2. a shell-state change does not remount the subject;
3. a captured error clears when the cell renders another variant.

Control: CI's browser lane ran these tests WITHOUT the fix (first push of #10326) and read 10 failures, all in the two new namespaces:
- "Error: boom under uix" reached the outer boundary;
- the healthy cell was gone;
- the mount count was 2 after a shell-state change.
Merged-PR audit #10326 (ed48977d96e1d92e1642f4a1fc88c3455e1c20e5; merged 2026-09-24T00:45:32Z). Completeness: All four evidence-surface claims addressed: generated expectation variants redeclare child-only script/plays; a stable per-cell boundary renders captured failure and resets for changed inputs; EDN false positives recover after JSON refusal; only the top mounted trap handles Escape. The source explicitly permitted dropping the optional substrate assertion clause; both corresponding spec claims are removed. Correctness: Accepted author final Story 2077 tests/7801 assertions and successful CI, including real browser boundary/isolation/remount/recovery and stacked-Escape regressions. Negative controls recorded 10 browser failures, 3 node payload failures, and 4 snippet replay failures. Read all production changes and affected spec hunks. No concrete remaining defect; no reruns. Implementation quality: Small boundary-local fixes reuse existing rendering, parsing and snippet helpers. JSON-first fallback preserves compact JSON semantics; the dialog stack is minimal and unmount cleanup removes the exact handler. No unnecessary framework or API expansion. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: xray-shell-views: unscoped React Flow palette override injected into the host document re-themes and de-attributes the host's own flows
description:
## Defect

Xray's React Flow palette override is unscoped, and `install!` injects it into the HOST page's `<head>`, so it re-themes and de-attributes any React Flow instance the host application renders itself. `react-flow-xray-theme-css` sets the `--xy-*-default` custom properties, with `var(--rf-xray-…)` values, on the bare selector `.react-flow`, and it adds `.react-flow__attribution { display: none !important; }`. `install!` appends this to the host `js/document` on the shell's first paint, after the host's own stylesheets. At equal specificity it therefore wins over the host's `@xyflow/react/dist/style.css`, and every light-mode host flow takes Xray's node, edge, Controls and edge-label colours. The `--rf-xray-*` values come from `:root` and a theme class that `apply-theme!` also writes to `<html>`, so when the operator picks Xray's dark theme, the HOST app's flow nodes turn dark (`#242424` fill) on the host's own light canvas. The host's attribution badge is hidden with `!important` whatever the host configured. Hiding it is the host's decision, and React Flow's docs reserve `hideAttribution` for Pro subscribers. The code comment says the block "only fixes the chrome xyflow paints itself", but nothing restricts it to Xray's charts.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs:1583-1613`: `react-flow-xray-theme-css`, with the unscoped `.react-flow {…}` at `:1594` and the `!important` attribution rule at `:1613`.
- `…/global_styles.cljs:1615-1623`: `inject-react-flow-style!` appends the base sheet plus the override as one `<style>` element.
- `…/global_styles.cljs:1661-1675`: `install!` targets the host `js/document`. It is called from `ShellView` (`shell.cljs:3581`).
- `…/global_styles.cljs:243-272`: `themes-css` publishes the palette at `:root` and on `.rf-xray-theme-dark` / `.rf-xray-theme-light`. The docstring says `apply-theme!` writes the class on the shell AND `<html>`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc:457-465`: every token is `"var(--rf-xray-<key>)"`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:3366`: the shell root carries `data-rf-xray-mode`, a ready-made scope.

## Failure scenario

A re-frame2 app renders a workflow editor with React Flow, in light colour mode, and loads Xray via `:devtools/preloads` in development. Open Xray: the app's own editor edges, node borders and Controls switch to Xray's greys, and its attribution badge disappears. Switch Xray to the dark theme: the app's nodes go dark on its light canvas. Close Xray: the style element stays in the head, so none of it reverts until reload. A flow in xyflow's `.dark` colour mode escapes, because `.react-flow.dark` outranks the single-class override.

## Evidence

- **Inspected**: the selector text, the host-document injection target and the append-to-head order, all at the lines above.
- **Inspected**: the `var()` indirection in `tokens.cljc` and the `:root` and `<html>` theme-class publishing.
- **Not executed**: a two-flow browser page, which the brief rules out.
- **Scope**: dev-only. Xray is a preload, so production hosts are unaffected. That is the reason for P4.

## Smallest fix

Scope the override to Xray's own surfaces, for example `[data-rf-xray-mode] .react-flow {…}` and `[data-rf-xray-mode] .react-flow__attribution {…}`. That is one selector prefix per rule. The verbatim xyflow base sheet can stay as it is: hosts using React Flow already load the equivalent rules.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs` and its `global_styles_cljs_test`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`, the node lane (`.cljs` only). A string assertion that the override selectors carry the scope prefix is a sufficient pin. Take visual confirmation from the Machines panel in a browser, or say it relies on CI.

## Decision needed

No.

title: machines: spawning onto an OCCUPIED :fixed-actor-id must destroy the occupant cleanly first (RULED)
description:
## RULED 2026-09-08 — this is now an implementation bead, not a question

A `:rf.machine/spawn` arriving at a `:fixed-actor-id` that a LIVE actor occupies overwrites that
actor's snapshot with a plain `assoc-in` at
`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:542`. Nothing reads the slot
first. Because Spec 005 makes liveness IDENTICAL to snapshot presence, that one write is both a birth
and an unannounced death: none of `teardown-live-actor!`'s steps run, so all three of Spec 005's
NAMED destroy guarantees (005:3600-3612) are silently void — in-flight `:rf.http/managed` requests
are not aborted, armed `:after` timers stay armed, `:rf.resource/*` owners are not released — and the
author's `:exit` cascade never fires. MEASURED in an isolated JVM probe: authored `:exit` calls 0 (vs
1 for an explicit destroy); one 60-second `:after` entry retained with no cancellation (vs 0).

## THE RULING

Run the occupant through the ORDINARY destroy path — the same one `[:rf.machine/destroy <addr>]`
takes, join preparation at `destroy.cljc:551` included — under the EXISTING `:reason :explicit`, then
install the new actor from the POST-TEARDOWN runtime-db. Replacement stays ONE verb at ONE address.

REJECTED, decided not deferred: no `:rf.error/machine-spawn-occupied-address`; no warning trace of
any kind (that was this bead's original option 2); no `:replace?` opt-in key; no new `:reason` enum
member; no second name registry (rf2-kuky.15 stands); no descendant reaping.

The full reasoning, the leak enumeration with file:line evidence and its controls, the four points
where the second reviewer corrected the first, the bounds on the unproven leak claims, and the
step-by-step implementation notes are in the RULING note on this bead. READ IT BEFORE STARTING —
three of the four corrections are traps that fail silently.

## The three traps, in one line each (detail in the note)

- Use `:reason :explicit`, NOT a new `:replaced` — `destroy.cljc:403` and `traces.cljc:65` gate
  join-child cancellation on `:explicit`, so a new reason skips them.
- Ordinary destroy does NOT reap children (`transition.cljc:2783`;
  `machine_reply_lowering_test.clj:250-262`), so this fix does not cure the orphaned-child /
  spawn-counter recursion. That is filed separately. Do not build an ownership cascade here.
- `install-fn` at `spawn.cljc:540` DISCARDS its `_rt` argument and returns a pre-captured
  `rt-after-alloc`; a teardown inserted before it would be undone. Rebuild the install from the
  post-teardown runtime.

## Scope

- ONLY the ordinary spawn-fx path installing at a supplied `:fixed-actor-id` that is currently LIVE.
- Re-entry at an EMPTY address (previous incarnation already destroyed) is correct and stays correct.
- The within-batch `:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id` rejection is untouched.
- The spec is SILENT on the live-occupant case, so writing the contract into
  `spec/005-StateMachines.md` is part of the deliverable — hot-zone, one holding with `spec/API.md`
  and both `spec/api-manifest*.edn` sidecars.
acceptance_criteria:
• A spawn at an OCCUPIED :fixed-actor-id runs the occupant through the ordinary destroy path (join preparation included) under :reason :explicit, then installs the replacement from the POST-TEARDOWN runtime-db.
• spec/005-StateMachines.md states the occupied-address rule beside :fixed-actor-id and qualifies the 005:2618 'teardown is explicit' paragraph with this narrow case, saying explicitly that independent CHILD lifetimes are NOT reaped.
• implementation/machines/test/re_frame/fixed_actor_id_addressing_test.clj's spawning-onto-an-occupied-fixed-address-replaces-the-occupant is rewritten from characterisation to CONTRACT: occupant's :exit runs exactly once; its armed :after is cancelled; fresh snapshot at the address; :rf.machine/destroyed observed BEFORE :rf.machine/spawned; a later dispatch to the address reaches the replacement.
• Focused coverage added: a rejected incoming spawn leaves the occupant intact; replacing a join child retains its cancellation facts; teardown's writes survive installation; frame loss during :exit stops the install.
• A CHILD-LIFETIME CONTROL test proves this change did not introduce a descendant cascade.
• No new :rf.error/*, no warning, no :replace? key, no new :reason enum member, no second name registry (rf2-kuky.15 intact).
notes:
--- MAYOR 2026-09-08 22:0x AUSEST — THE PRINCIPLE THIS BEAD CITES DOES NOT REACH THIS CASE. I CHECKED IT AT SOURCE ---
This bead's "Why it wants a ruling" section rests on spec/Principles.md §No silent swallow: "a replacement
disposes of a live actor without saying so". I read that principle rather than taking the citation, and it
is scoped more narrowly than the bead uses it.
ITS TEXT, at spec/Principles.md:83-87: "a recognised input that cannot be honoured produces a signal —
never silence ... When the runtime RECOGNISES a user-supplied value as input but CANNOT ACT ON IT — an
unknown opts key, a reserved-fx override it ignores, a callback whose return it drops, a conflicting pair
of explicit options — it MUST emit a structured warning or error".
WHY IT DOES NOT BIND HERE: in this case the runtime CAN act on the :fixed-actor-id, and does. The input is
honoured exactly as supplied — the actor is installed at the address the author named. Nothing is ignored
and no supplied value vanishes. What is lost is the PREVIOUS OCCUPANT, which is not the user-supplied
value the principle is about. Every example the principle gives is WITHIN ONE INVOCATION — an unknown key,
an ignored override, a dropped return, two conflicting options in one call. Replacing a prior actor is a
cross-invocation state effect, a different thing.
THE COUNTER-READING, stated honestly rather than suppressed: one could call the first spawn's address
claim and the second's "a conflicting pair of explicit options". I think that is a stretch — they are
separate operations at different times, not a pair supplied together — but it is the argument someone
would make, and it is the only route by which the principle reaches this.
WHAT THAT DOES TO THE RULING: it removes the bead's strongest argument for options 2 and 3. Option 1
(leave as-is, document it as last-write-wins at an author-chosen address) is now SUPPORTED by the stance —
"we trust the programmer", "low friction", and the bead's own counterweight already says so — and
UNOPPOSED by the normative principle it was thought to violate. What survives for a signal is the XState
divergence alone: system._set throws on a duplicate systemId. That is a real difference, but parity with
XState has never been this project's governing rule, and the bead itself says the divergence is "real
rather than parity-preserving" without arguing that parity is owed.
MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is still Mike's call because it is a taste question about what kind of project
this is: OPTION 1. Document last-write-wins at an author-chosen address and close. An author who writes
:fixed-actor-id twice at one address has said what they want twice; a diagnostic there is the nagging kind
the stance rejects. If that reads wrong to you, option 2 (a warning trace, not an error) is the cheap
middle and does not break the existing test.
I HAVE NOT CHANGED THE BEAD'S OPTIONS OR CLOSED IT. This note is the measurement that prices them.
--- RULING 2026-09-08 23:08 AUSEST — DECIDED: DESTROY THE OCCUPANT CLEANLY, THEN INSTALL ---

DECISION. A `:rf.machine/spawn` arriving at a `:fixed-actor-id` that a LIVE actor occupies must run
that occupant through the ORDINARY destroy path — the same one `[:rf.machine/destroy <addr>]` takes,
join preparation included — and then install the new actor from the POST-TEARDOWN runtime-db, under
the EXISTING `:reason :explicit`. No new `:rf.error/*`, no warning, no `:replace?` key, no new
`:reason` enum member, no second registry. Replacement stays ONE verb at ONE address. Spec 005 gains
the paragraph that says so: the spec is currently SILENT on this case, so writing the contract is
part of the deliverable, not a footnote to it.

This SUPERSEDES the mayor note above, which recommended option 1 (status quo). It does not refute it.
That note's reading of `spec/Principles.md` §No silent swallow is CORRECT and is adopted: the
principle governs a recognised input the runtime CANNOT HONOUR, and here the supplied address IS
honoured exactly as given, so the principle does not reach this case. Both reviewers agree with the
note on that point. What carries the decision instead is an independent, MEASURED fact the note did
not have in front of it: the replaced actor's authored `:exit` never runs and its armed `:after`
timers are never cancelled. The principle argument is gone; the leak is not.

The ruling is NOT any of the three options as filed. The bead's option 2 was "emit a warning trace";
that is REJECTED. A warning whose recommended response is "write the destroy yourself", for a cleanup
the framework is perfectly capable of performing, is exactly the nag shape the house stance rejects —
and a leak that only announces itself in dev is a leak that ships.

WHO WON THE CONFLICTS. Two independent analyses agreed on the diagnosis and on the fix's shape. They
conflicted on four points of substance and CODEX WON ALL FOUR, each on a source citation or a probe,
and I re-verified all four in this checkout:

(1) THE REASON KEYWORD. The dossier proposed a NEW `:reason :replaced`. That is wrong, and it would
have failed silently: `destroy.cljc:403` gates live-join-child cancellation on
`(and current (= :explicit requested-reason))`, and `traces.cljc:65` computes `cancelled? (= reason
:explicit)` so it emits cancelled reply facts only for that reason. A `:replaced` reason SKIPS both
branches — replacing a join child would leave its attempt uncancelled and its reply facts unemitted.
Verified both lines. Use `:explicit`. This also deletes the dossier's proposed 005 trace-enum edit
from the change, making the fix smaller.

(2) CHILDREN ARE NOT REAPED, SO THE FIX DOES NOT CURE THE RECURSION. The dossier claimed "Children
tear down, so §5.2's recursive collision never arises." False, and it was the fix's headline benefit.
Ordinary destroy tears down the PARENT ONLY: `run-active-exit-cascade` (`transition.cljc:2783`)
collects the authored `:exit` action-refs and synthesises NO child-destroy fx, and
`machine_reply_lowering_test.clj:250-262` pins a declaratively-spawned child SURVIVING an imperative
parent destroy in as many words ("the imperative `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent>]` tears down only the
parent ... the independently-spawned child survives"). That agrees with the resolved
"teardown is explicit in v1" decision at 005:2618. Codex measured it: the old child is present after
replacement AND after an explicit destroy-then-spawn. Verified the test and the fn. CONSEQUENCE: the
fix hands the author back the `:exit` hook from which they can destroy their own children; it does
NOT reap descendants and must not be sold as doing so.

(3) THE INSTALL SITE CARRIES A TRAP. `install-spawn!`'s installer is
`(fn [_rt] (cond-> rt-after-alloc ...))` at `spawn.cljc:540-556` — it IGNORES the swap's input and
returns a runtime-db value captured BEFORE the swap. Inserting a teardown immediately before it
therefore RESTORES the very state the teardown deleted. Verified at source. The install must be
rebuilt from the current post-teardown runtime. This is why the dossier's "perhaps ~30 lines" is an
under-estimate.

(4) THE EXISTING FENCE IS A FRAME FENCE, NOT AN ACTOR FENCE. The dossier asserted the existing
`continue?` / `owner-token` fence already covers the callback re-entry that a teardown introduces.
`spawn.cljc:839`'s own comment names it "A's exact-frame-incarnation continuation predicate": it
guards against the FRAME being destroyed and a same-id successor published by application code, not
against same-ADDRESS actor churn. Verified. A replacement that runs authored `:exit` — application
code, synchronous, able to dispatch — needs that case reasoned about explicitly rather than assumed
covered.

Codex also BOUNDED several of the dossier's leak claims, correctly, and the bounds are adopted:
same-key timer supersession does cancel (`timer.cljc:667`) and a fired timer releases its own
resources (`timer.cljc:875`), so "indefinite subscription-delay retention" is a SOURCE-BASED RISK
rather than an established finding — as are stale HTTP reply misdelivery into the successor and
cross-type classification contamination. All three are worth covering in tests; none of them is what
the decision rests on.

THE DOSSIER WON on the framing that decides the bead: this is not "fix a bug against a written
contract", it is CHOOSE THE CONTRACT AND WRITE IT — and the leak is the fact that survives every
posture argument. Trust-the-programmer is a reason not to nag an author about a thing they chose. It
is not a reason for the framework to skip its own teardown contract. An author who spawns at an
occupied address has, on the trusting reading, ASKED for the actor at that address to become the new
one; honouring that request means the old one is finished with, which is what destroy means. Today
the runtime honours half the request and drops the rest on the floor.
--- RULING (cont.) — THE LOAD-BEARING ANALYSIS, PRESERVED ---

THE ONE WRITE. `spawn.cljc:542`, inside `install-spawn!`'s `install-fn`: a plain
`(assoc-in (rf.machines.paths/snapshot-path spawned-id) initial-snap)`. Nothing reads the slot first.
Verified in this checkout. Because Spec 005 §Liveness is derived from runtime-db (005:2622-2626)
makes a spawned actor's liveness IDENTICAL to the presence of its snapshot "and nothing else", that
single write is simultaneously the BIRTH of the new actor and the DEATH of the old one — one write,
two lifecycle events, one of them unannounced. The id is resolved with no occupancy question asked at
`spawn.cljc:46-58` (`pre-allocated-actor-id` = `(or (:fixed-actor-id args) (:rf/spawned-id args))`).

THERE IS NO READ TO REMOVE — THE GATE WAS NEVER WRITTEN. Census of `spawn.cljc` (1608 lines):
`snapshot-path` 1 hit (the write itself), `snapshot-present?` ZERO. Controls: `contains?` 3 hits in
the same file (the instrument discriminates on this file), `snapshot-present?` 3 hits in
`destroy.cljc` (the predicate exists in this codebase and simply is not reached from spawn).
`spawn-fx` (734-831) has exactly two gates — the `:spawn-all` invoke-reject sentinel and the
unregistered-TYPE reject — and neither reads the target address.

THE EXISTING COLLISION GUARD CANNOT SEE THIS. `reject-address-collision!` /
`spawn-all-address-collisions` (`spawn.cljc:159-215`, 1224+), firing
`:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`, is a WITHIN-BATCH check and structurally so: it compares
the children of ONE `:spawn-all` invoke against each other before any of them installs. It cannot
reach a plain `:spawn` at an occupied address; a hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn ...]` fx; two
`:spawn` declarations in two REGIONS of one parallel machine (two separate fxs, not a batch); or two
`:spawn` declarations on two different parents. The 009 catalogue row for that error names the harm
it prevents in the batch case — "would silently overwrite one prepared entry / one live actor" —
which is precisely the harm going unprevented one metre away on the single-spawn path.

THE THREE NAMED GUARANTEES, ALL SILENTLY VOID. Spec 005:3600-3612 §What auto-cancels on destroy
enumerates exactly three framework-managed resource kinds released when an actor dies: (1) in-flight
`:rf.http/managed` requests the actor issued, aborted; (2) armed `:after` timers it scheduled,
cancelled by `cancel-actor-timers!`; (3) `:rf.resource/*` owners it holds under
`[:machine <actor-id>]`, released — 005:3606's own words for the harm being "leak[ing] a
refetching/polling owner past the actor's death". EVERY one is released ONLY from
`teardown-live-actor!` (`destroy.cljc:168-297`). A silent replace calls none of it. Against that
nine-step pipeline, the steps that DO NOT RUN: (1) the `:exit` cascade (`destroy.cljc:225`) — the
author's own teardown never runs, and 005:3610 designates `:exit` as the SUBSTITUTE for resources the
framework cannot manage (sockets, `clearInterval`, workers, SDK subscriptions), so skipping it voids
the escape hatch as well as the guarantee; (2) abort in-flight managed HTTP (231) — replies keep
flying and address an actor-id that now resolves to the WINNER; (3) drop the loser's per-instance
`:sensitive` / `:large` classification (244-248), which stays in the frame's elision registry
re-rooted to that absolute snapshot path; (4) `cancel-actor-timers!` (253); (6) the
`:rf.machine/destroyed` trace (270) — so any tool pairing lifecycle events sees spawned(:x) twice
with no destroyed(:x) between, a BROKEN PAIRING CONTRACT rather than a missing nicety; (8) clear the
registrar entry (286), usually a no-op for spawned actors; (9) release `[:machine <actor-id>]`
resource owners (296). Step 5 (teardown projection) runs PARTLY BY ACCIDENT — the snapshot is
replaced rather than removed, so runtime-db does not grow, but the LOSER's parent's tracked
`[:spawned ...]` slot is left naming a live address it no longer owns. Step 7
(`spawn-order/forget!`) is idempotent by value and stays clean.

MEASURED, not merely read. Codex ran two isolated JVM probes (Clojure 1.12.4, this checkout's cached
classpath, both processes exit 0, one runtime-reset fixture, overwrite vs explicit-destroy-then-spawn
compared directly): old parent's authored `:exit` calls — 0 vs 1. Old 60-second `:after` entry after
replacement by a type with no timer — 1 RETAINED with no cancellation, vs 0 retained with one
cancellation. Those two rows are the evidentiary floor of this ruling. The timer probe substituted
only host scheduling/cancellation to count handles; it exercised the real machine timer table and the
real spawn/destroy paths.

THE TIMER LEAK'S MECHANISM, AND ITS BOUND. `:after` timers live in a PROCESS-SIDE table
(`timer.cljc:88-102`) keyed `frame-id -> {:parent <actor-id> :spawn <invoke-id> :delay <delay-key>}
-> entry`. It is NOT frame state. It is cleared only by `after-cancel-fx` (state exit),
`cancel-actor-timers!` (destroy), `cancel-all-timers!` (frame destroy),
`cancel-frame-timers-on-restore!` (epoch restore), `cancel-timers-absent-from!` (SSR hydration
reconcile), and `schedule-after-timer!`'s leading `:on-supersede` (`timer.cljc:667`) which touches
ONLY the one key it is arming. A silent replace triggers none of them; the loser's entries stay in
the table under the SAME `:parent` key the winner will use, host clock still armed. When a leaked
timer fires, the TRANSITION is suppressed — the carried per-decl-path epoch is compared against
`[:data :rf/after-epoch <path>]` in the current snapshot (`transition.cljc:942`, defaulting to 0) and
drops as `:rf.machine.timer/stale-after` — so CORRECTNESS IS BACKSTOPPED AND HOST WORK IS NOT. The
codebase states this itself for the exactly-analogous hydration case at `timer.cljc:1064-1068`: "the
epoch / active-path gates suppress the eventual stale TRANSITION, but they release no host work."
BOUND (Codex, adopted): the leak is the timers at keys the winner does NOT re-arm, not every timer,
and a fired timer releases its own resources.

THE CHILDREN, AND THE SPAWN-COUNTER RECURSION — real, and NOT cured by this fix. The loser's own
spawned children are ordinary actors at their own addresses, torn down by the loser's `:exit`
cascade, which never runs. So: they stay live with their own timers, HTTP and resources; the tracked
slot that pointed at one is OVERWRITTEN the moment the winner reaches the same state and spawns its
own child, making the orphan permanently unaddressable by any exit cascade; and it is reaped only at
frame destroy, whose membership is read from the durable snapshots plus the durable spawn-order
vector (`spawn_order.cljc:50-57`) — for an SPA's main frame, the page session. THEN IT RECURSES:
`build-initial-snapshot` seeds `:rf/spawn-counter {}` FRESH (`parallel.cljc:395-397` — verified in
this checkout) while 005:2794 puts the declarative allocator's counter INSIDE the parent's snapshot,
so the winner's counter resets to zero while the loser's children are still alive at `#1`, `#2`. The
winner's first child allocates the address its orphaned predecessor still holds, and takes the same
unguarded `assoc-in` at line 542 — one collision at the top manufacturing a second one level down
with no author involvement. CRITICAL QUALIFICATION: Codex's probe read this row the SAME in BOTH
columns — it happens after an explicit destroy-then-respawn too — so it is a property of
"teardown is explicit in v1" (005:2618), NOT a regression this bug introduces nor one this fix
removes. Filed separately (see NEXT STEPS). Do NOT invent an ownership cascade inside this bead.

WHAT DOES NOT BREAK, stated for honesty. The durable spawn-order vector does not double-enter
(`spawn_order.cljc:92-106`, idempotent by value). runtime-db does not grow at the colliding address;
the snapshot is replaced, not duplicated. The DESTROY side is ALREADY incarnation-fenced:
`slot-owned-incarnation?` (`destroy.cljc:607-630`) compares the snapshot's `:rf/parent-id` /
`:rf/invoke-id` stamps against the slot's coordinates, so the loser's parent's exit PRUNES its stale
slot and leaves the live winner alone rather than compounding the damage. Joins are fenced too: the
`:work-generation` / opaque `:rf/attempt` token exists precisely because "actor ids alone cannot
discriminate a re-entry respawn" (005:3698, `spawn.cljc:1137-1148`). Read that pair twice — THE
CODEBASE ALREADY TREATS SAME-ADDRESS REPLACEMENT AS A HAZARD EVERYWHERE IT READS AN ADDRESS. The one
place that does not is the write that CREATES the hazard.

THREE CASES THE RUNTIME CANNOT TELL APART TODAY, because it never looks at the slot at all:
(a) LEGITIMATE RE-ENTRY — a declarative `:spawn {:fixed-actor-id :x}` on a state; leaving runs the
desugared exit cascade which destroys the child, and re-entering spawns a fresh incarnation at an
EMPTY address. Correct today, stays correct, explicitly OUT OF SCOPE (005:2966-2975; pinned at

**THE WORKER DID NOT NARROW `actor-live?`, AND THAT IS THE DECISION WORTH KEEPING**, because narrowing was the obvious fix and would have been wrong. The two callers ask different questions: `actor-live?`'s registrar disjunct is deliberate and documented — destroy must "recognise and clear a stale or externally installed entry", which answers *is there anything here to clean up* — while replacement asks *is a live ACTOR occupying this address*, which `spec/005` §Liveness makes identical to snapshot presence and nothing else. Narrowing the shared probe would have stripped a real affordance from all four of its call sites to fix one, and cut across rf2-s2bsmw's "ONE liveness probe every destroy shape consults" ruling. Instead: a replacement-scoped `occupant-actor-live?`, which also drops the spawn-order clause, since that covers a drain-time stale-`old-db` window its only caller cannot be in.

THE SECOND CHANGE, ALSO REPLACEMENT-SCOPED: `*definition-preserved-at*` keeps teardown step (8)'s `rf.registrar/unregister!` off the one address a replacement is preserving a machine DEFINITION at. Prevention rather than capture-and-re-register, because `register!` would fire the hot-reload hooks and emit a `handler-cleared`+`handler-registered` pair for a definition that never changed — and would open a fresh callback-bearing boundary between the teardown and the install, which is precisely what #9508's design is careful about.

**THE HONEST STOP IN THE SABOTAGE PROOF IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING HERE.** The first plant — widening the predicate back — came back **GREEN** at 11 tests / 68 assertions. The worker stopped rather than concluding. The cause is that the two changes are partly redundant: with `*definition-preserved-at*` in place, widening the predicate alone leaves the OBSERVABLE first-spawn outcome benign, because the phantom teardown finds no active configuration, so no `:exit` runs and the definition survives. It is still wrong — a full ordinary destroy runs and emits `:rf.machine/destroyed` for an actor that never lived. The worker strengthened the first test with that trace assertion, which is the better contract anyway, and the plant then went red on it alone. Three plants in total, each match-counted at 1 before the run, each restored and verified by `git hash-object` against the committed blob (`b085d802d3` for `destroy.cljc`, `6a0ba793ef` for the test). **Under all three plants the nine pre-existing tests stayed green — including #9508's rejected-spawn and child-lifetime CONTROLS, which the restored close reason says must hold under both behaviours.**

title: xstate-parity: the parent's :data :rf/spawned stamp is written at allocate-time and survives every fx-time rejection (unregistered type, address collision, fixed-id replacement) so it names an actor the parent does not own
description:
## Gap

The parent's `:data :rf/spawned {<invoke-id> <spawned-id>}` stamp is the spec's id-recording story for declarative spawns: spec/005 §Reserved snapshot-internal keys (line 88) says it is "Written by the **pure transition reducer** at allocate-time", and §Recording the spawned id user-side (3121-3131) teaches reading it — `(get-in data [:rf/spawned [:working]])` → `[:rf.machine/destroy …]` — as "the re-frame2 spelling of XState v5's `const ref = spawn(child)` captured into `context`". But the reducer stamps BEFORE the spawn fx decides, and the fx's three rejection / replacement outcomes leave the stamp standing, so it names an actor the parent does not own:

1. **Unregistered type** — the fx rejects fail-closed (`:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type`), which spec/005:3214 calls a TOTAL reject ("no snapshot installs, no spawned-id is allocated, no `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned …]` slot"); the parent's `:data` nevertheless reads `:rf/spawned {[:busy] :c/ghost-1}` for a child that was never born.
2. **Generated-address collision** — the fx rejects (`:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`), and the rejecting parent's stamp names the OTHER parent's live child at that address.
3. **Fixed-id replacement** — a second parent's spawn destroys the first parent's incarnation and installs its own; the displaced parent's stamp still names the address, now owned by the replacement.

In XState there is no analogue to compare: a failed spawn errors the actor (row 4p), and `snapshot.children` only ever lists children the actor actually holds — the record and the fact cannot disagree. The runtime registry slot is correct in all three cases (absent / other parent's / pruned on exit), and the exit cascade reads the registry, so the runtime itself never acts on the stale stamp. The hazard is the AUTHORED path the spec teaches: an action that reads `:rf/spawned` and emits `[:rf.machine/destroy …]` destroys nothing (case 1, `:rf.error/no-such-handler`), or ANOTHER parent's child (cases 2 and 3).

## XState evidence

- `xs/C-13.out`: unknown src → parent `status error`, `children []`. `xs/C-5.out`, `xs/C-11.out`: duplicate `registryKey` → the second actor errors, the first keeps its child; `snapshot.children` lists only held children. Nothing to pair beyond "the record cannot go stale".

## re-frame2 evidence

- Executed, trunk fe8de195bd:
  - `jvm/C/c11.out` #2 (unregistered type): `parent :busy {:err nil, :rf/spawned {[:busy] :c/ghost-1}} | live (:c/pu) | registry nil` beside `[:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type {:machine-id :c/ghost …}]`.
  - `jvm/C/c8.out` (generated-address collision): `A :rf/spawned {[:busy] :c/w#1} | B :rf/spawned {[:busy] :c/w#1}` with `registry slots: #:c{:pa {[:busy] :c/w#1}}` — B's stamp names A's child; control: B leaving `:busy` did NOT destroy it (cascade reads the registry).
  - `jvm/C/c10.out` #2 (fixed-id replacement): `P1 :busy {[:busy] :c/shared} | P2 :busy {[:busy] :c/shared}` after P2's spawn destroyed P1's incarnation (`:rf.machine/destroyed :c/shared :reason :explicit`, child now `:rf/parent-id :c/p2`).
- Mechanism (read): `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:593-622` (`bind-spawned-id`, the reducer's stamp at allocate-time) and `:2493-2547` (`:rf/spawned-id` allocation); `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:164-205` (`reject-unregistered-type!` — emits and returns without touching the parent's `:data`) and `:624-635` (the fx RE-WRITES the mirror beside the registry slot on a successful install, with a comment that the teardown projection "clears the two TOGETHER" — the rejection paths clear neither).
- spec/005:88 (reducer writes at allocate-time; "mirrors the runtime registry slot"), :3214 ("The reject is total"), :3121-3131 (the authored read idiom), :3044-3062 (replacement rules; "What it guarantees is that neither case LEAKS").

## Why it matters

Small and contained: every one of the three outcomes already emits an always-on error record or lifecycle trace, so the parent is not silently wrong about WHAT happened. What is wrong is the one field the spec tells authors to read for their child's id, in exactly the three situations where reading it matters most (the child is missing or belongs to someone else). Cases 2 and 3 need two spawn sites resolving to one address — misconfiguration the spec says the runtime cannot distinguish from intent — so the everyday instance is case 1 during development, where the fix is a registration and the stale stamp is merely confusing. P4.

## Options

1. **Clear the mirror on rejection, in the fx (runtime, tiny).** `reject-unregistered-type!` and the duplicate-address reject `dissoc` the parent's `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` (for `:spawn-all`, the whole children map) in the same store write that records the rejection marker — the counterpart of the `:624-635` re-write on success, so the mirror and the registry slot move together on BOTH outcomes, as the existing comment already promises. For replacement (case 3) the displaced parent's mirror is pruned when its registry slot is (its own exit), or on the replacing spawn — the latter is the spec-literal reading of "mirrors the runtime registry slot".
2. **Move the stamp from the reducer to the fx entirely** — one writer, no stale window at all; but it changes the pure Level-1 result (the reducer's `:rf/spawned` bind is visible in `machine-transition`'s snapshot) and the conformance fixtures that pin it.
3. **Spec-only**: say in §Recording the spawned id user-side that the stamp is the reducer's INTENT and the registry slot is the FACT, and that an author must tolerate `:rf.error/no-such-handler` from a destroy aimed at it. Cheapest; leaves the record false in the collision cases.

## Recommendation

Option 1 — it is the missing half of an existing pairing (the success path already re-syncs the mirror), and it keeps the Level-1 surface untouched.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc` (`reject-unregistered-type!` :164-205, the duplicate-address reject, the install write :616-640)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE — line 88 row, §Errors 3214, §Recording the spawned id user-side 3121-3131) — one sentence each saying the mirror is cleared on rejection
- tests beside `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/spawn_unregistered_type_test.clj` (or wherever `machine-spawn-unregistered-type` is pinned — grep `implementation/machines/test`) and the collision tests pinning `machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` (the spawn fx is `.cljc` and the CLJS spawn tests exercise it); `spec/conformance` corpus if any fixture pins `:rf/spawned` after a rejected spawn (none expected — grep the corpus for `rf/spawned`).

## Decision needed

No.

Reproduced at trunk 2c626b1845 before the fix, with the registry slot as control each time:

What changed (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc):

- The Level-1 surface is untouched: the reducer still binds the mirror at allocate time; only the fx side clears it on rejection.

So the mirror mirrors the registry slot exactly there; it is the first alternative the bead's Option 1 offers ("pruned when its registry slot is, its own exit") and is the existing behaviour. Pruning both at the replacing spawn would change replacement semantics rather than rejection, and the ruling was rejection-only, so it was not done.

title: xstate-parity: a history target's transition domain is computed from its RESOLVED LEAF, so a child-declared history transition keeps the recorded child standing where XState exits and re-enters it
description:
Split out of rf2-2n6uv.4.1 (the LCCA ancestor-target fix). Worker lcca-41 reproduced this and correctly stopped on it, because it needs a change to history-resolution code that .4.1's brief excluded. First noticed by worker xseng-2n6uv on rf2-2n6uv.4.2 (closed, PR #10363).

## Defect, executed

Chart: `:p` has children `:b` (with children `:b1`, `:b2`) and a shallow history `:hist`. The machine is at `[:p :b :b2]`, and the recorded history is `{[:p] :b}`. A transition declared on `:b2` targets `[:p :hist]`.
- re-frame2, before AND after the .4.1 LCCA fix: `[:exit/b2 :act :enter/b1]`. `:b` stays standing.
- xstate 5.32.6 and 6.0.0-alpha.59 both give: exit b2, exit b, act, enter b, enter b1. `:b` is exited and re-entered.

## Cause

For the transition domain (the LCCA), XState treats a history target as the history pseudo-state. That node is a CHILD of `:p`, so the domain is `:p`, and everything active under `:p` exits. re-frame2 resolves the history target to its RESOLVED LEAF (`[:p :b :b1]`) before computing the domain. The LCCA of `:b2` and `:b1` is `:b`, so `:b` stays. A resolved leaf can never be a proper ancestor of the source, so the .4.1 LCCA fix cannot reach this case.

## Options

1. ALIGN (recommended). For the LCCA and exit set, a history target counts as the history node's own position (a child of its parent state), as SCXML and XState do. The resolved configuration is still what gets ENTERED. This makes a history transition's exit set the same as a literal transition to the history's parent's child, which is the reading SCXML specifies.
2. KEEP and document. re-frame2's spec already says a restore "behaves like a literal :target" (to the resolved configuration). Record the divergence in spec/005's parity text, so nobody re-opens it.

## Recommendation

Option 1, under the stance and the parity campaign's direction. It is the same geometry principle rf2-2n6uv.4.1 ruled for ancestor targets (align with the ordinary LCCA rule), and it removes a divergence rather than documenting one. It is pre-alpha, so no compatibility shim.
- Sequencing interplay: rf2-2n6uv.4.2 (closed) made history exits use the macrostep-start recording. Keep that ordering; this bead changes only which node the domain is computed against.
- Operator may reverse: this narrows the spec/005 sentence "a restore behaves like a literal :target". If Mike prefers Option 2, it becomes a prose-only change.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc`: where a history target is resolved before `compute-transition-geometry`. Keep the change local to which path feeds the domain computation.
- The machines tests beside the history and geometry tests, e.g. `machine_history_smoke_test.clj`, `machine_active_path_geometry_test.clj` and the scxml conformance tests.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT): the history and geometry passages, including qualifying "a restore behaves like a literal :target" to say the domain is taken at the history node.

## Sequencing

Dispatch AFTER rf2-2n6uv.4.1's PR (#10372, worker lcca-41) has MERGED, because it owns transition.cljc's geometry and spec/005 until then. Re-derive line numbers at that trunk.
