title: INCOMPLETE audit handoff: focused after-delta privacy (resolution reported)
description:
Recovery of prior merged-PR audit work, explicitly requested by Mike on 2026-09-25.

Source: rf2-fc84b; status at recovery: closed. No original Bead has been reopened or claimed. This is a new, independently trackable record.

Audited PRs: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10281

Historical handoff — resolution already reported. This record does not assert that the original defect still exists.

Evidence and scope
Original claim and required correction, preserved verbatim:
## Defect

rf2-3x7nj.4.2 added a `project-trace-event` arm for `:rf.event/after-deltas` on `:rf.event/run-end`. It walks every `:db` value in each after-delta record through `rf.elision/elide-wire-value {:frame f}` from the APP-DB ROOT, as the bead prescribed. That closes the whole-app-db leak: the path interceptor's `:after` values are the restored / widened ROOT db. It does NOT reach the `:db` values that are FOCUSED SLICES rather than the root.

- The standard `[:rf.interceptor/path P]` `:after` diff: `:coeffects :changed :db :before` is the focused slice the handler saw (at absolute offset P), and `:effects :changed :db :before` is the slice the handler returned (at P). Only the `:after` values are root-anchored (and only when no OUTER path interceptor is active; nested focus makes even those slices of the outer focus).
- Any user `:after` interceptor positioned INSIDE a path focus (later in the chain than the path interceptor) runs its `:after` while `:db` is still focused, so BOTH its `:before` and `:after` `:db` values are slices.

A root-anchored walk cannot match a declared `[:auth :token]` against a slice `{:token …}`, so when a handler focuses AT OR ABOVE a classified path, the classified value still ships raw at its slice-relative position. It ships to the trace stream, the ring, the epoch record and the off-box epoch projection.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc`: `project-after-deltas-tags` (added by rf2-3x7nj.4.2) walks from the root.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc`: `invoke-after` / `compute-ctx-delta` capture the delta. The record carries only `:rf.interceptor.delta/id` and `:rf.interceptor.delta/ctx-delta`, with no focus offset.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc`: `standard-path-interceptor` stacks `[original-db focused]` on `:rf.interceptor.path/stack`, and not the path vector, so the absolute focus of a ctx is not recoverable at capture time either.
- `spec/Conventions.md` (`:rf.interceptor.delta/*` row) documents the record namespace as a CLOSED reserved set of two member keys.

## Failure scenario (measured on the rf2-3x7nj.4.2 branch, with that fix applied)

JVM probe, core `:test` classpath:
1. `(rf/reg-event :seed (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :auth {:token "SECRET-TOKEN-4242"} :counter 0) :sensitive [[:auth :token]]}))`, dispatched.
2. `(rf/reg-event :set-token {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:auth]]]} (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ t]] {:db (assoc db :token t)}))`, then `(rf/dispatch-sync [:set-token "SECRET-TOKEN-NEW"])`.
3. The `:rf.event/run-end` trace still carries:
   - the OLD secret at `[:tags :rf.event/after-deltas 0 :rf.interceptor.delta/ctx-delta :coeffects :changed :db :before :token]`;
   - the NEW secret at `[… :effects :changed :db :before :token]`.
   The `:after` twins are now `:rf/redacted`. The off-box-tool `rf/project-egress` of the `:set-token` epoch record still carries the NEW secret at `[:trace-events 5 :tags :rf.event/after-deltas 0 :rf.interceptor.delta/ctx-delta :effects :changed :db :before :token]`.
CONTROL, same run: the `[:counter]`-focused `:bump` handler's run-end trace and its off-box projection carry the secret at 0 paths after the 4.2 fix (2 paths each before it). (The `:rf.event/v 1` hit on `:set-token` is its POSITIONAL arg, the documented structural limitation of `redact-event`, and not this defect.)

## Fix shape (common to both options)

Record each captured delta's absolute `:db` focus offset at capture time:
- the path interceptor stacks its path vector (or the absolute focus) alongside `[original-db focused]`;
- `invoke-after` reads the focus of the before-ctx and the after-ctx from that stack;
- the projection walks `:before` / `:removed` values with `{:frame f :path <before-focus>}` and `:after` / `:added` with `{:frame f :path <after-focus>}`. `elide-wire-value` already takes an absolute `:path` offset.

## Decision needed

Yes. Where the focus offset rides on the delta record:
- **Option A**: add a third member key to the CLOSED `:rf.interceptor.delta/*` set (for example `:rf.interceptor.delta/db-focus {:before [...] :after [...]}`). It's public, documented and visible to tools. It needs a `spec/Conventions.md` edit (HOT ZONE, sequenced) and the matching Spec 009 text.
- **Option B**: an INTERNAL key on the record that `project-after-deltas-tags` consumes and strips before egress, the way `project-sub-tags` consumes `:rf.sub/classification`. No spec change, but it lives in the trace pipeline as an unwritten contract between `interceptor.cljc` and `classification.cljc`.

Out of scope for either: `:rf.event/after-deltas` has no consumer anywhere in `tools/` today (the Xray "AFTER INTERCEPTORS" step was never implemented, per `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`). Summarising or dropping the slot instead is a third route, and a larger design call than either option.

## Gates

JVM core `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`; epoch `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/epoch` for the off-box leg; `npm run test:cljs` for the CLJS lane. Extend `re-frame.after-deltas-classification-cljs-test` with a `[:rf.interceptor/path [:auth]]` leg asserting both `:before` slices redact.

description:

chart/layout.cljc now projects root and region :entry/:exit/:tags and coeffect requirements onto their containers. chart/projection.cljc passes entry, exit, tags, entryRequires and exitRequires into xyflow data. But chart/nodes.cljs root-container-node (:783 onward) reads the label, parallel flag and context, with no lifecycle/tag rendering. Compound and region container renderers likewise omit those fields; the existing leaf renderer reads entryRequires near :346 and paints lifecycle rows. Consequently a root or region body's actions and tags, which the engine executes/includes, remain invisible to the chart user despite successful projection. This is not a claim that the projection tests are false or that the worker should have designed a new header under its scope.

Required correction: surface the already-projected container lifecycle and tags using the existing action/tag presentation, with the smallest suitable container-header treatment and matching layout space. Cover actual rendered output, including a lifecycle-free control and coeffect requirement text, so merely attaching unused data cannot satisfy the display requirement. Keep the UI vocabulary consistent; no new inspector or public API.

title: XState 6.0.0-alpha.59 parity comparison 2026-09-24 — expressiveness, semantics, microsteps, interpretation, tooling; file actionable gaps
description:
Mike's request (2026-09-24, verbatim): "Do a careful comparison between re-frame2 and XState v6 on FSM expressiveness, semantics, microsteps, interpretation, etc. We want to have xstate v6 parity and conformity, where possible. We consider it the gold standard we aspire to (given the different execution models). Create beads for any actionable insights."

## Stance (verbatim, CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## What this campaign is

A five-dimension comparison of re-frame2's machine substrate (`implementation/machines`, spec/005) against XState **6.0.0-alpha.59** (npm `alpha` dist-tag measured 2026-09-24; `latest` 5.33.2, `beta` 5.0.0-beta.54; 59 alphas, no stable v6). It supersedes the 2026-09-07 review rf2-2qfi (which compared against alpha.52 from the CHANGELOG alone) in METHOD: this time the XState side is executed, not recalled — the package is installed in the session scratchpad and driven with node (`transition` / `getMicrosteps` / `createActor`), and re-frame2's side is driven on the JVM through `reg-machine` + `dispatch-sync` and the pure `machine-transition`. Paired machines, same event sequences, compared traces.

Dimensions (one background agent each, findings under `ai/findings/xstate-v6-parity/`, beads as children of this epic):

- A — statechart structure and expressiveness (the grammar: state kinds, targets, transition kinds, guards, actions/effects, delays, spawn/invoke, meta/tags/output/input/schemas, wildcards, choice, always, route states).
- B — execution semantics (the SCXML algorithm: microstep/macrostep, selection and conflict, exit/entry sets, action ordering, raise queue, eventless stability, done/final, history, self-transitions, error handling).
- C — interpretation and actors (lifecycle/status, persist/restore, children, errors, system/addressing, subscriptions and inspection, mailbox ordering, pure transition API, durable execution).
- D — the v6 changelog delta alpha.1..alpha.59 and the standing docs (EP-0029 groups A/B/C, spec/005 §Lessons, CP-5 table, docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md, the xstate-translation skill): what is stale, what is confirmed.
- E — tooling, serialization, testing and inspection (graph/test model, SCXML, JSON serialization, machine versions, inspector protocol, simulated clock, registration-time validation, fsm entry).

## Rulings that stand — not re-litigated by this campaign

rf2-569h (cross-region region-sourced targets DECLINED; trigger: programmer friction), rf2-hu69 (atomic root suppression over a `:final?` region RETAINED), rf2-1r69 (`[:schemas :events]` PARKED, wiring semantics pre-decided), rf2-ry7x (`:after` on restore RULED: full client-resolved delay, no entry replay), rf2-w8gxxz (non-cancelling join cut), nested parallel regions DEFERRED with a written trigger (spec/005 §Four non-substrate divergences item 2), and EP-0029 Group C (C1–C17). A finding may say a ruling's PREMISE has changed and cite the measurement; it may not refile the question.

## Classification every row must carry

MATCH / LEAD (re-frame2 ahead) / GAP (actionable: XState has it, re-frame2 does not, no ruling excludes it) / DIVERGE-RULED (a closed bead or spec ruling records it) / DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE (the execution-model difference makes it inapplicable: one router queue vs per-actor mailboxes, data snapshots vs actor objects, fx vs promises) / N-A (JS/TS-only).

Only GAP rows and stale-record findings become beads. Each bead carries its executed evidence from BOTH systems and a `## Decision needed` section; a bead that needs a ruling from Mike gets a dossier under `ai/decisions/` per the standing instruction.
notes:
== CAMPAIGN SUMMARY (mayor, 2026-09-24) — XState 6.0.0-alpha.59 parity comparison ==

METHOD. Five background agents, one per dimension, each with the XState side EXECUTED (xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59 installed in the session scratchpad and driven with node through transition / getMicrosteps / createActor) and the re-frame2 side EXECUTED on the JVM (reg-machine + dispatch-sync + the pure machine-transition, from a scratch directory via clojure -Sdeps against implementation/machines), paired machines and paired event sequences, every row classed MATCH / LEAD / GAP / DIVERGE-RULED / DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE / N-A. XState ground truth was primary-source only: the installed package, the 63 v6 docs pages and the core CHANGELOG from the xstate `next` branch (the main-branch changelog carries no v6 entries), and fetched next-branch tests. Trunk fe8de195bd at dispatch, 2c349f0a60 at the last reading; the machines source and the four XState-citing documents did not move during the campaign. Findings docs (local-only ai/ tree): ai/findings/xstate-v6-parity/{A-grammar,B-semantics,C-actors,D-changelog-and-records,E-tooling}.md; probe scripts and outputs under the session scratchpad xstate-parity/{xs,jvm}/.

MATRIX TOTALS (386 graded rows across the five dimensions; each doc's counts computed by Python over its own table):
- A grammar (rf2-2n6uv.5, 78 rows): MATCH 33, LEAD 7, GAP 7, DIVERGE-RULED 19, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE 5, N-A 7.
- B semantics (rf2-2n6uv.4, 86 rows): MATCH 60, LEAD 5, GAP 6, DIVERGE-RULED 9, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE 5, N-A 1.
- C actors (rf2-2n6uv.2, 62 rows): MATCH 27, LEAD 5, GAP 6, DIVERGE-RULED 19, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE 5, N-A 1.
- D changelog alpha.0..alpha.59 (rf2-2n6uv.3, 127 rows): MATCH 28, LEAD 6, GAP 4 (all handed to A/C), DIVERGE-RULED 36, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE 7, N-A 42, unverified 4.
- E tooling (rf2-2n6uv.1, 34 rows): MATCH 11, LEAD 6, GAP 2, DIVERGE-RULED 10, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE 1, N-A 4.

HEADLINE. The statechart core is at parity: transition selection (exact-before-wildcard with guard fallback), parallel conflict resolution (rf2-hu69 re-confirmed at alpha.59), exit/entry ordering, raise FIFO, eventless settling, final/on-done, history shallow/deep, self-transition geometry — all MATCH with paired traces. re-frame2 LEADS on registration-time validation (37 of 38 defect classes refused at reg-machine, where alpha.59 refuses 8 at construction and 19 never), effects-as-data, non-resetting sibling regions, keyword state names, :exit running on explicit destroy, inline :definition children persisting, and the trace vocabulary (the v6 inspector protocol carries no guard facts at all). XState's core semantics have not moved since alpha.27; everything in alpha.53–.59 is types, durable-execution plumbing and the fsm bundle split, bar four small runtime items (named guards as plain predicates, state input preserved on non-reentering transitions, async action rejection to onError, children stopped on unhandled parent error).

WHAT WAS FILED — 25 beads under this epic (P1 1, P2 7, P3 14, P4 3), seven of them needing a ruling from Mike (each has a dossier under ai/decisions/, see the close reason):
- SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE (the one P1): rf2-2n6uv.4.1 — a child-declared transition targeting a proper ANCESTOR keeps the ancestor standing here; XState 5.32.6 and alpha.59 both exit and re-enter it (LCCA), and spec/005:342 plus the SCXML conformance test record today's behaviour as v5 parity. Decision: align or keep-and-correct-the-claim.
- CAPABILITY / SHAPE GAPS needing a ruling: .5.1 root is not a state node (root :entry/:exit/:tags/:spawn silently inert); .2.1 :spawn :on-done map shape (the EP-0029 A8 teaching) silently inert; .2.2 explicit destroy orphans declarative :spawn children where XState stops them; .2.5 no production-legal persist/restore install primitive; .1.5 the model-based test walker (a 22-line BFS over machine-transition reproduces xstate/graph exactly — hold the trigger or ship); .1.6 arm (c) a :ns/* member in :internal-events is a literal, refuse or implement.
- VALIDATION HOLES (no ruling): .1.1 phantom :initial boots an undeclared state; .1.2 :entry/:exit/:action vectors pass registration and kill the first drain; .1.3 transition-spec keys not vocabulary-checked (:cond false FIRES, :actions plural drops the action, :reenter without ? inert) — bumped to P2 on E's and A's agreement; .1.6 arms a/b/d/e.
- SMALL SEMANTICS / TRACE (no ruling): .4.2 history target resolved from the pre-transition recording, .4.3 unguarded targetless :always aborts at 16 where XState rests after one, .2.3 the Level-1 result cannot say handled?, .2.6 :cause :spawned on a singleton reset, .2.7 stale :rf/spawned mirror after fx-time rejections, .6 :microsteps undercount inside raised handling, .7 :actor-id nil on destroy-exit action-ran (same root as .2.2), .5.2 :after refuses the ISO-8601 string :timeout accepts.
- STALE RECORDS (no ruling): .3.1 spec/005 (4 claims), .3.2 CP-5 table (8, one wrong about re-frame2 itself), .3.3 coming-from-xstate.md (6), .3.4 the xstate-translation skill leaf (7), .1.4 two XState-side claims in the E surface, .2.4 no lifecycle rows in the two translation docs, .5.3 Pattern-LongRunningWork teaches :after 0 which registration rejects.

NOT FILED, ON PURPOSE (recorded in the findings docs so nobody re-litigates): route states (N-A — sugar over root :on + :reenter? true, and its payload-selected target is the function-valued transition C1 rejects); state input (B1: the v6 surface has settled, the "concrete need" half of the deferral is unchanged); durable execution (v6 converged on re-frame2's epoch/reply-envelope shape; the only missing piece is .2.5's install primitive); duplicate :fixed-actor-id (spec forbids a registry); the five rf2-2qfi not-filed items all stand, three now with executed evidence; EP-0029 graded but not filed against (C4's premise reversed — alpha.59's setup() registers guards/actions again — every decision stands).

POSTURE. "Periodic re-validation at a named alpha, not continuous tracking" HOLDS (dimension D's sentence, no decision needed): 59 alphas, no beta, no stable, docs and package disagreeing in four measured places. What changed is the METHOD — executed probes, not changelog reading — and the named alpha, now 6.0.0-alpha.59 (rf2-2n6uv.3.1 carries the stamp refresh). Next trigger: the first beta/stable dist-tag, or an alpha whose entry names transition selection / parallel / history / final semantics.

RULINGS RE-CONFIRMED UNCHANGED at alpha.59: rf2-569h, rf2-hu69, rf2-1r69, rf2-ry7x, rf2-w8gxxz, nested-parallel deferral, EP-0029 Group C.

DOSSIERS (ai/decisions/, local-only): rf2-2n6uv.4.1.ancestor-target-lcca.md (recommends ALIGN: widen reenter-active-path? for a child-declared proper-ancestor target; :reenter? true already restores parity); rf2-2n6uv.5.1.root-as-state-node.md (option 2: honour root :entry/:exit/:tags/:spawn, refuse the rest); rf2-2n6uv.2.1.spawn-on-done-map-inert.md (widen :on-done to the :on-shaped transition, :on-error symmetry; refuse-and-fix-A8 as the floor); rf2-2n6uv.2.2.destroy-orphans-spawn-children.md (reap TRACKED children on parent destroy — a premise-changed re-ruling of rf2-dokz confined to declarative children); rf2-2n6uv.2.5.persist-restore-install-primitive.md (name :rf/install-frame-state in core as a factoring of :rf/hydrate; the mechanism already ships); rf2-2n6uv.1.5.model-based-test-walker.md (hold the trigger; publish the ~25-line walker as a doc recipe with one guide-truth pin); rf2-2n6uv.1.6.internal-events-wildcard-member.md (REFUSE a *-named member at registration — ruled REFUSED and dispatched the same evening).
EPIC LEFT OPEN (mayor, 2026-09-24 20:52:19 AUSEST): the comparison and filing are complete (see the CAMPAIGN SUMMARY above); bd refuses the close because two direct children, rf2-2n6uv.6 and rf2-2n6uv.7, are still open. Close this epic when those two close; no further campaign work remains on it.
MAYOR 2026-09-24: RULINGS RECORDED on rf2-2n6uv.1.5 and rf2-2n6uv.2.5 (label decision-ruled), with dossier and Codex Recommendation weighed. Where this epic's notes summarise those dossiers' original recommendations, the RULING notes on the child beads GOVERN.
- .1.5: HOLD the walker/harness. Authorised only a small spec/008-Testing.md correction: qualify the "sufficient … without runtime changes" claim, fix the rf/test/machine-paths sketch, and add a demand-based trigger. The docs recipe (the dossier's option 1b) is rejected: it skips the initial :entry step, and public-result hides :handled?.
- .2.5: ADD :rf/install-frame-state to core. It is framework-authority, with a restore-rules reconcile (not hydration), per-subtree runtime replacement, timers rebuilt through artefact hooks, and no new error id. The full implementation brief is on the bead.
MAYOR 2026-09-24: RULINGS RECORDED on rf2-2n6uv.4.1 and rf2-2n6uv.5.1 (label decision-ruled). The ruling notes on the child beads GOVERN over this epic's dossier summaries.
- .4.1 (P1): ALIGN with SCXML/XState LCCA. A transition declared below the ancestor it targets exits and re-enters that ancestor, routed to the existing :reenter? path; an ancestor-declared self-target stays non-reentering. Lands AFTER the .4.2/.6 PRs. The regression asserts ancestor-owned effects (a restarted spawn, a re-armed timer), not only the exit/entry log. Search for the prose sites by phrase.
- .5.1: OPTION 2, STAGED. The root gets :entry at birth, :exit at teardown and :tags; every root key the runtime never reads gets one registration refusal, including root :spawn for now. Root :spawn is split to rf2-rkkse, which lifts that refusal when it lands. Do not add the root to nodes-along-path.

description:
## What

```
If this region moved, update this row — do NOT delete it
```

Restore the SCOPE/ENSURE boundary pair in `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md`'s use-sub standard-chain text, in the form the guard pins: `` `frame-provider` (SCOPE) / `frame-root` (ENSURE) ``. It is the contract the guard exists to keep true, and it fits the rewritten prose.

`docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md`, one passage. The test row only in the moved case.

description:

title: Machine :state normalisation: hierarchical keyword target commits a keyword (spec says vector); flat region vector target stays a vector
description:
Two follow-ons from rf2-gk36e (PR #10510, merged), which made a FLAT machine commit a keyword :state for a one-element vector target. Both are in commit-snapshot, implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc.

1. HIERARCHICAL keyword target. In a hierarchical machine, the target [:out] commits :state [:out], but the keyword target :out commits :state :out. spec/005 says a hierarchical machine's :state is a vector path, so the KEYWORD target is the one that departs from the spec. The same state then has two representations, and a sub or guard comparing :state misses one of them. The rf2-gk36e worker reproduced this, and the bead's docs-review addendum records it.
2. FLAT PARALLEL REGION. A flat region's [:b] target still commits {:r1 [:b]}, because rf2-gk36e's flat-machine? excludes :rf/region specs. The root-level target path (apply-root-region-target) already passes a single-state target as a keyword.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): normalise per spec/005's snapshot-shape rules, so that one state has exactly one representation.
- (1) A keyword target in a hierarchical machine commits the vector path the spec prescribes.
- (2) A flat region's one-element vector target commits a keyword, if spec/005 §Parallel states says a flat region's value is a keyword. Settle that from the spec first. If the spec is SILENT on a region's value shape, do (1) only and report (2) with the evidence.
Regression both ways for each: the normalised shape commits, and the already-correct shapes are unchanged (flat :b stays :b; hierarchical [:in :home] stays). Show each red with its fix removed. Check the machines examples and docs/machines samples that compare :state against a keyword in a hierarchical machine: a normalisation can break a (= :out (:state snap)) check, so census those and fix the ones the change breaks.
notes:
== WORKER REPORT (machines cluster, PR #10523, trunk 968ccab3bb) ==

Item read as a field: one description version, no notes, no children. The history was walked back to creation; status was the only field that changed.

(2) FLAT PARALLEL REGION: FIXED in PR #10523.
Spec settles it. spec/005 §Parallel regions §Snapshot shape reads ";; flat region — the value is a keyword", and §Snapshot shape says each region's value "follows the flat-or-compound arms above".
Reproduced at trunk: a region-local [:b] committed {:r1 [:b]} where :b committed {:r1 :b}.
Fix: transition.cljc flat-machine? drops its (nil? (:rf/region machine)) clause, so a region's synthetic spec passes the same every-state-a-leaf test. A flat region's [:b], {:target [:b]} and :b now all commit :b. Compound regions keep their vector path.
Regressions: flat_vector_target_state_cljs_test.cljc covers the pure transition and a registered machine's live snapshot. Controls that must not move: a root region-qualified [:flat :b] stays :b, the sibling region is untouched, a compound region's [:y :deep] and [:x] stay vectors, a flat machine's :b stays :b, and a hierarchical [:in :home] stays. region_cross_region_target_test.clj pinned the old [:two] for a flat region and now expects :two.
Red with the fix removed: 4 failures, exactly the vector-target assertions. Every control stayed green. Restore verified by blob hash.
Machines JVM before: 1526 tests / 6514 assertions / 0 failures. After, inside the implementation sweep: 1528 / 6529 / 0.

(1) HIERARCHICAL KEYWORD TARGET: STOPPED, spec/** needs changing.
Reproduced at trunk. For {:initial :out :states {:out {...} :in {:initial :home ...}}}:
- keyword target :out from [:in :home] commits :out;
- vector target [:out] commits [:out];
- the initial snapshot is :out too (parallel.cljc build-initial-snapshot goes through transition/denormalise-state, which returns a keyword for a length-1 path).

Blocker: spec/conformance/fixtures pins the keyword. With the normalisation applied, the machines conformance corpus (machines_conformance_test, Mode B) fails 4 fixtures, 5 calls:
- after-hierarchy.edn, :logout: expects {:state :idle}
- history-shallow-restores-direct-child.edn, :eject: expects {:state :tray}
- machine-root-on-fallback.edn, :logout: expects {:state :idle}
- scxml-history-test388-deep-vs-shallow.edn, two :leave calls: each expects {:state :away}
Each needs its expected :state changed to the one-element vector. Those files are normative spec artefacts, so the spec owner has to make that change first.

Measured shape of the change (tried, run, then withdrawn):
- transition/denormalise-state takes the MACHINE instead of the original :state. It returns (first path) when the path has one element and no state in (:states machine) has :states; otherwise it returns (vec path).
- commit-snapshot becomes (if internal? (:state snapshot) (denormalise-state machine target-leaf)).
- Both initial-snapshot call sites in parallel.cljc (build-initial-snapshot and region-initial-state) pass the machine or region body.
- The single-element keyword special case in parallel.cljc apply-root-region-target becomes redundant.
The initial-snapshot half is needed. Without it a hierarchical machine whose :initial names a root-level leaf reads :out before boot and [:out] after boot, so one state still has two representations over time.
The same rule also normalises the compound-REGION analogue. Spec says a compound region's value is a vector path, but today a keyword target to a region-root leaf commits a keyword, and a compound region's leaf :initial is a keyword. The rule makes both vectors.

Census under that change. Besides the 4 fixtures, 20 assertions in 12 machines test files pin the keyword shape:
- after_test.clj:419
- after_value_forms_test.clj:286
- done_signal_cljs_test.cljc:69, :110 and :336 (region)
- final_region_sourcing_test.clj:162 (region)
- machine_after_hydration_rearm_cljs_test.cljc:278
- machine_cascade_instrumentation_cljs_test.cljc:522
- machine_cofx_mint_policy_test.clj:262
- machine_history_smoke_test.clj:125

- machine_root_on_fallback_test.clj:56
- machine_transition_domain_test.clj:253
- scxml_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:522 and :539, plus :679, :723, :766, :802 and :834 (region)
I also read every :state site in examples/, docs/machines and testbeds/: 18 sites. Every keyword comparison or keyword sample among them is on a FLAT machine or region: tutorial, inspecting-machines, concepts, tags, glossary, coming-from-xstate, and the realworld :feed and :tab regions. The hierarchical ones (hierarchical-states.md, history.md, the websocket connection machine, the deep_machine :work region) either show vector paths, read through tags, or pr-str the value. None of them breaks under (1). There is one consumer OUTSIDE those trees. tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs (runDeepMachine, about line 1698) waits for the deep_machine work-state text to differ from ':idle'. title: Fix factual errors in docs/core/fresco/api-reference.md
description:

**Type:** task (docs) · **Priority:** P3 · **Surface:** `docs/core/fresco/api-reference.md`

5. The page earlier claimed to hold "the shapes an `on-*` prop may take … and the render rules". It holds neither; `docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md` now has an Event props section.

title: Tool-Pair Performance API consumption: getEntriesByType is empty by default and observer delivery is batched
description:
spec/Tool-Pair.md section "Performance API consumption" contradicts the observer-first contract in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (Consumer access) and docs/api/re-frame.performance.md. Found while re-deriving rf2-x8ghp's site list at origin/main 954e86a4fe. That bead's worker did not edit Tool-Pair.md, because it is a CLAUDE.md hot-zone file outside its write surface.

(1) The intro says any consumer that knows about `performance.getEntriesByType` can read the entries, and the first "Consumer pattern" pulls every rf: entry with `performance.getEntriesByType('measure')`. With the default `re-frame.performance/retain-entries? false`, each bracket clears its measure straight after emitting it, so that call returns []. Measured with a Node v24 perf_hooks probe: measure, then an immediate clearMeasures, leaves 0 retained. Either present getEntriesByType as the retain-entries?-only one-shot read, or lead with the observer.

(2) "Live: PerformanceObserver fires per emitted entry" misdescribes delivery. Under the W3C Performance Timeline queueing algorithm (https://www.w3.org/TR/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry), measure() appends the entry to each registered observer's buffer and queues one task, and a callback receives every entry queued since its last run. The observer is also the PRIMARY read, not the live alternative. The example's `buffered: true` cannot recover entries already cleared, so the observer must be attached before the work.

Model the fix on Spec 009's Consumer access section as corrected by rf2-x8ghp (PR #10678). Prose only.

Done, one commit, prose only: spec/Tool-Pair.md section "Performance API consumption", nothing else in the file.
(1) getEntriesByType('measure') is now the one-shot read, populated only under retain-entries? (with retention off, the default, it returns none because each entry was delivered to observers and then cleared). It is placed after the observer, with its own code block.
(2) The observer is now the PRIMARY read (observer-first, linking 009 section Consumer access). Each measure() queues its entry for every observer registered at that moment, and the clear does not reach that queue. Delivery is batched: the callback runs later as a task and receives every entry queued since its last run. The observer must be attached BEFORE the work, because buffered: true replays only what the retained buffer still holds and so cannot recover a cleared entry. title: Coverage gap: run-variant-blocking's unwrap-async-cause is never asserted (story-mcp)
description:
Found by rf2-3h7v2.13 (owner), not fixed there: a pruning PR adds no tests.

`re-frame.story-mcp.tools.lifecycle/run-variant-blocking` peels the worker future's `ExecutionException` (and a rejected Story future's `CompletionException`) with `unwrap-async-cause`, so the canonical `:rf.error/run-failed` record's `:reason` is the underlying Story throwable's message rather than the executor wrapper's. No test reads that reason on the throw route.

Measured at the rf2-3h7v2.13 branch, with the base `tools_test.clj` restored for the run (before any removal): replacing `(error-outcome vk (unwrap-async-cause e))` with `(error-outcome vk (Exception.))`, which discards the cause entirely, left `re-frame.story-mcp.tools-test` green (235 / 1367, 0 failures, exit 0).

A test that fails on that plant asserts that the run-failed record's `:reason` carries the thrown message, through `run-variant` with `rf.story/run-variant` redefined to throw.
notes:
== RESULT (worker, 2026-10-02 02:15:41 AUSEST): PR #10701 (draft), head 0edfeea888 ==
Witness folded into `lifecycle-error-outcome-surfaced-by-both-consumers`, which already redefines `rf.story/run-variant` to throw. For a synchronous throw through BOTH run-variant and preview-variant, the run-failed record's `:reason` is asserted EQUAL to the thrown message. A new row covers a rejected Story future (`CompletableFuture/failedFuture`), which arrives wrapped twice. The match is exact rather than `includes?` because `ExecutionException`'s own message is its cause's `toString` ("clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo: ..."), which an includes check would pass with the wrapper left on.
Controls (tools-test alone, exit 1 each, restores verified by blob hash): the bead's plant `(Exception.)` -> 3 red rows. No unwrap (`e`) -> 3 red. A single peel (`(.getCause e)`) -> exactly 1 red, the rejected-future row, which therefore witnesses the loop.
Counts: this bead's share is 0 tests / +4 assertions.

title: Trunk red: docs/core/testing/views.md §4 no longer shows the UIx recipe verbatim, so the uix-adapter docs pin fails (broken by #10754)
description:
TRUNK IS RED on a docs pin, and every PR whose CI arms the UIx adapter JVM lane inherits the red. First hit: PR #10772 (rf2-zbnoc.9), whose check "Diagnostic skip-ok JVM uix-adapter guards" failed. Job log, run 37045671508 / job 110968081589: re-frame.adapter.uix-component-recipe-docs-pin-test, views-page-shows-the-recipe-verbatim, 2 failures. "the page carries a fenced clojure block opening with that ns form": expected (some? shown), actual nil. "docs/core/testing/views.md §4 and implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_component_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs have drifted apart; make the page's block the file's exact contents."

CAUSE, measured: PR #10754 (Codex, rf2-uf1ic, merged as d91e445fb8, "docs(core): teach a runnable progression and separate optional depth") rewrote docs/core/testing/views.md §4 ("UIx hook components: mount it for real"). It replaced the verbatim recipe with a shorter, simplified example using different aliases (uix-adapter, uix-adapter/client-root, an :rf/set-db init) and linked to the recipe file (views.md:175). git grep for "ns re-frame.adapter.uix-component-recipe-dom-cljs-test" finds 1 hit in views.md at d91e445fb8~1 and 0 at trunk. #10754's own CI was docs-only, so it never armed this pin.

THE PIN IS RIGHT. Its purpose is that what a reader copies is what CI runs (implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj). Do not retire or weaken it. Make the page and the recipe file agree again, one of two ways, on evidence:
(a) RECIPE FOLLOWS THE PAGE (preferred if it holds). Codex's simplified code is the teaching voice the Core guide now wants. If it is valid and runnable (check that uix-adapter/client-root and the other names it uses exist), make uix_component_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs say exactly what the page shows (the pin's normalisation rules apply). Show it passes in :browser-test, since it is a -dom-cljs-test file.
(b) PAGE FOLLOWS THE RECIPE. If the page's code is not runnable as written, put the recipe file back into §4 as the fenced block, verbatim, and keep #10754's surrounding prose where it still reads true.
Either way, the pin test must go green, and must go red with a one-character drift planted in either file.

FOLLOW-ON, not in this bead: why a docs-only PR could break a JVM-pinned page without its CI noticing is a CI-classifier question, filed separately.
notes:
== NOTICED, LEFT (mayor, 2026-10-03 04:5x AUSEST) ==
PR #10773 (merged at 072b6dc505, resolution (b): the page follows the recipe) reported three things outside its fence. (1) Its own CI did NOT run the pin: a views.md-only path sets adapter_diagnostic=false. That is exactly rf2-q6qzw's classifier gap, already in flight. (2) No link gate checks links from docs/ into implementation/: a broken target on the §4 link left both mkdocs --strict and check_doc_slugs.py at exit 0. The gap predates this change. (3) The "A real DOM" bullet below §4 says to follow §4 "using the Reagent adapter's client-root"; §4's code now uses uix.dom directly. It is still true but reads slightly off. The prose keeps the #10754 wording where it still holds, and adds one sentence explaining the exists? js/document guard.

Why not (a). The simplified example could not become the recipe file:
- Namespace. Its ns is my-app.counter-view-test, but the file's path fixes its ns, and the pin selects the page's block by that ns opening line.

title: Live render-to-string examples in docs/ssr/
description:
## This section

`docs/ssr/` teaches server-side rendering with static code only. `re-frame.ssr` is in the engine now, and `render-to-string` is a pure function from hiccup to an HTML string, so a cell can show exactly what the server would emit:
- `[:pre (ssr/render-to-string [...])]`
- or the string beside the rendered result.

Pages:
- `concepts.md`: "the render tree is data" and `render-to-string`; escaping, void elements, `:tag#id.cls` parsing.
- `tutorial.md`: the steps that build the HTML (`make-frame`, an event, `render-to-string`) can run in a cell. The Ring handler and request steps stay static.
- `head.md`: if `re-frame.ssr.head` helpers produce a string a cell can show, demo them; otherwise leave the page.
- `response.md`, `streaming.md`: probably static, since they are about the server response. Check.
- Leave `coming-from-nextjs.md` and `testing.md` static unless a cell clearly helps.

The Ring and Node hosts (`re-frame.ssr.ring`, `.ring.node`) are not in the engine.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

title: re-frame-migration: M-25/M-52 test-double audit for macro interception and compiled arities (GH #10859)
description:
GitHub #10859. The M-25/M-52 test recipes in skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md (M-25 ~L147, M-52 ~L161) cover API renames and registrar isolation but direct no test-double audit for two traps a compiled consumer suite hit: (1) a with-redefs against the function-facing name (dispatch / subscribe) does not intercept a macro expansion that targets dispatch-impl / subscribe-impl; (2) a replacement fn whose fixed/multi/variadic shape differs from the original lacks the compiled caller's cljs$core$IFn$_invoke$arity$N or variadic entry, so compilation succeeds and runtime throws a missing-entry TypeError or silently captures nothing. The framework contract already explains both in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc (~L191): the ^:no-doc def aliases dispatch-impl / dispatch-sync-impl / subscribe-impl are the shared internal seam the macro expansion and the capture frame call through, deliberately def (not defn) so no static arity dispatch is emitted, and explicitly NOT a public facade.

Ask: a generic audit step in the recipes: classify each mocked call as macro expansion or function value; reference the version's documented interception boundary (prefer the public test seams the docs already name; never present the ^:no-doc aliases as public API); match the fixed, multi-arity and variadic contracts compiled callers need; keep a positive assertion that the intended interception happened; run the actual compiled test suite before acceptance. No weakened assertions, no undocumented public API claims.

Acceptance: the recipe names both traps with the discharging check for each, links the documented boundary, and states that a JVM/BB green is not evidence for compiled callable shapes.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. Re-read at trunk 227d877eae: the core.cljc comment block is present as the issue quotes it, and M-25/M-52 carry no test-double audit. Docs fix in the skill's voice; executed controls in the worker's scratch where they are cheap (JVM for the macro-interception half; the compiled-arity half needs a CLJS build, which is a lane question for the mayor, not a default). title: Pair skill: browser reload guidance conditional on capability and ownership, not a blanket user handoff (GH #10921)
description:
GitHub #10921. skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md says 'You cannot reload the browser; ask the user to.' (L85), and the freshness workflow (L117) repeats it, telling the agent to relay the reload hint as the single next step. Verified at trunk d0b29226e8. Observed: a worker owning a disposable browser and authorised to reload it did so through Playwright, and Pair reconnected to the new runtime.

Ask: check whether usable browser controls exist and whether the reload is within the session's ownership and its already-authorised task. When both hold: announce, reload, rediscover, and verify the new runtime and source before trusting reads. Otherwise give one actionable user reload instruction. Keep the warning that a reload drops temporary REPL changes and may affect live state. Never assume a browser, never reload a user's personal tab, and never turn an :unknown token into acceptance. Generic, any repository.

Mayor triage 2026-10-05 at trunk d0b29226e8: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10921 --json body,comments`), comments included: they carry later diagnosis and a verified private repair where one exists. title: Fresco census: count the call at the head of a #(...) anonymous fn, and prune inert quoted/comment/discarded bodies there (GH #10943)
description:
GitHub #10943. The Fresco API census (migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/fresco/census.clj, `scan` at about L534 at trunk 279fd6d193; the issue's L563 has moved) misses the call at the head of a direct anonymous-fn reader form, and counts a call inside an inert quoted body in that same form. Mayor verified the cause at trunk 279fd6d193: rewrite.clj `head-symbol` (about L135) admits only `(list-node? nd)`, so a `:fn` node (`#(r/flush)`) has no head, and `inert?` (about L163) uses that reader for the quote/comment heads. Mike's same-input control: `#(r/flush)` reports 2 of 3 flush sites, while `(fn [] (r/flush))` and `#(do (r/flush))` report 3, and `#(quote (r/flush))` reports 3 where 2 is right. Every variant reads `:recognised? true`.

Ask: teach the source walk the executable body of an anonymous reader fn (a `:fn` node's first element is its call head), keep correct call coordinates and alias/refer resolution, and prune inert quote/comment/discard bodies there. Verify the parser's node semantics rather than treating every fn value as a call. Keep the call-site versus symbol-as-value distinction and syntax-quote's documented treatment. Do not rewrite consumers. Acceptance: direct anonymous, expanded and nested forms each count the same API call once; inert anonymous bodies contribute none; mixed inputs keep the ordinary positives and their positions; aliases, referred calls and the fixer's output stay correct. Add focused reporter regressions (census_test.clj / inert_source_test.clj) that are red at base. No runtime API change, and no change to the skill's MIG tiers. JVM lane: the codemod's own clojure -M:test.

description:

title: HTTP body trace ships secrets off-box from [:ref]/local-registry decoders and vector-of-maps bodies, stamped :classify
description:
## Bug

The HTTP response-body classifier misreads the schema walker's answer in two ways. Each ships a `:sensitive?` secret off-box under a `:classify` stamp:

1. **Completeness.** It treats any vector `:decode` as fully classifiable. The walker sees no marks behind `[:ref :app/user]` or a local `{:registry …}`, so the body rides unredacted with `:classify`, although the schemas artefact itself reports both shapes as opaque.
2. **Coordinates.** It matches the walker's paths exactly. The walker writes collection-element marks without an index (`[:items :token]`), so a token inside a vector of maps (`{:items [{:token …}]}`) is never redacted, on-box or off-box.

Developers notice this only when a dev-session export (Xray, tool-pair / AI-pair egress, captures) carries the token. A list endpoint is the commonest JSON response.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc:111-138` — `introspectable-schema-decode?` is `(and (schema-decode? decode) (vector? decode))`.
- `privacy_body.cljc:231-258` — `off-box-body-disposition` returns `:classify` whenever that holds.
- `privacy_body.cljc:272-295` — `classify-decoded` calls `(rf.classification/redact-with-paths decoded (keys sensitive) (keys large))` (`:294`) in the default exact mode.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:596-625` — `opacity-child-schemas` returns `::opaque` for a local `:registry` and for `(= :ref op)` (`:619`). `schema-has-opaque-child?` (`:655`) therefore answers `true` for both. HTTP never consults it, because the schemas artefact publishes only the two extract hooks (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:137-138`).
- `walker.cljc` docstring at `:203-207` — `:vector` / `:set` / `:sequential` "descend into each child at the SAME `base-path`", so element marks are index-free by construction.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:335-353` — `redact-with-paths` matches exactly unless `{:index-free? true}` is passed. Resources already opts in for the same walker output (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/classification.cljc:304`).

Repro (*probed* at trunk on the JVM: real `:rf.http/managed` requests against an in-process server; the `:rf.http/replied` row is passed through epoch's `omit-off-box-http-bodies`; a Malli default registry holds `:app/user [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]`):

| `:decode` | Stamp | Off-box projected `:value` |
|---|---|---|
| `[:ref :app/user]` | `:classify` | `{:id 1, :token "SECRET"}` |
| `[:schema {:registry {:app/u2 [:map … [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]}} :app/u2]` | `:classify` | `{:id 1, :token "SECRET"}` |
| `[:map [:items [:vector [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]] [:meta …]]` | `:classify` | `{:items [{:id 1, :token "SECRET"}], :meta {:n 1}}` |
| Control: `[:map [:session [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]` | `:classify` | `{:session {:token :rf/redacted}}` |

`(re-frame.schemas/schema-has-opaque-child? [:ref :app/user])` and the local-registry form both return `true` (*probed*).

Fix candidate for (2) (*probed*): `redact-with-paths` with `{:index-free? true}` over the walker's marks gives:
- `{:items [{:id 1 :token :rf/redacted} {:id 2 :token :rf/redacted}] :meta {:token "public"}}` — every element is redacted and the unmarked sibling `[:meta :token]` stays visible;
- `{:pair ["x" {:token :rf/redacted}]}` for the position-pinned tuple path `[:pair 1 :token]`, which still matches.

Contract:
- Spec 014 §Response-body classification rule 1 (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1415`): a marked slot redacts before the body rides a trace.
- Rule 3 (`:1417`) and its sub-bullet (`:1418`): `:classify` is reserved for schemas the walker can read, and the off-box disposition fails closed "where classification is unknown". The sub-bullet equates "readable" with "vector form", which `[:ref …]` and a local registry are not.
- Spec 010:439 already names `[:ref …]` and a local `{:registry …}` as opaque forms that fail closed.

## Expected

An off-box `:classify` stamp is given only when the walker can see every mark, and a marked slot inside a collection is redacted in every element.

## Fix direction

- **Completeness:** have the schemas artefact publish a completeness answer through a late-bind hook. That can be `schema-has-opaque-child?` itself, or one hook returning `{:sensitive :large :complete?}` as the Opus schemas review proposes. `off-box-body-disposition` returns `:classify` only when the answer is complete; an opaque child or an unbound hook means `:omit`.
- **Coordinates:** `classify-decoded` passes `{:index-free? true}` to `redact-with-paths`, as resources does.
- **Spec:** amend 014 rule 3's sub-bullet: a vector form the walker reports opaque (`[:ref …]`, a local `:registry`, an embedded compiled child) fails closed too. Amend rule 1: a slot inside a collection redacts in every element.
- Whether a qualified-keyword child (`[:map [:user :app/user]]`) also counts as incomplete is a separate decision (rf2-mn2ht.49). Once ruled, it becomes one more clause in the same completeness answer.

## Acceptance

- JVM regressions, plus CLJS where the harness allows, through a real request:
  - `[:ref ::User]` and a local-registry decoder are stamped `:omit`, and no secret appears in the off-box projection;
  - the vector-of-maps decoder redacts every element's `:token` on the dev trace and off-box, while `:id` and an unmarked sibling stay visible.
  All three fail today.
- Controls stay green: a plain walkable map decoder keeps per-slot redaction with `:classify`, and the app receives the raw body in every case.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (10 §4 completeness; 08 §2 coordinates), probed during the Opus cross-review; re-probed end to end at trunk.
- Related:
  - closed rf2-3aafh and rf2-amgtr made the walker fail closed on `[:ref …]` and local registries for validation traces, but HTTP's disposition never consults the walker's opacity answer;
  - rf2-mn2ht.47 (`:accept` reshape) touches the same emit site, so do both in one worker or sequence them;
  - rf2-mn2ht.49 (qualified-keyword child) extends the same completeness answer;
  - resources' invalid-params projection (`resources/classification.cljc:594-649`) reads the same extract hooks the same way: exact match, no completeness check. That reading is not probed. Include it if the shared hook lands, or file it separately.
- Hot-zone files: none (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` and `spec/010-Schemas.md` are not hot). If the new hook needs a late-bind directory row, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` is not hot either.

title: Schemas printer and sensitivity-walk memos keep every schema value ever seen, across replaced schemas and destroyed frames
description:
## Bug

The schemas artefact has two never-evicted memos: the digest printer and the sensitive-path walker. They keep an entry for every distinct schema value they ever see, and neither replacing a schema registration nor destroying its frame releases one. The documented bound, "steady-state size equals the registry size", is false. Growth is unbounded whenever schema values are fresh per registration: closure-bearing schemas, HMR edits, per-request frames that build their schema. In practice that means dev and test processes, plus any JVM host that builds schemas per request.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/cache.cljc:39-47`: `clearable-memo` is an atom-backed map keyed by the argument vector, with no eviction. Its namespace docstring (`:14-20`) claims the memo is "bounded by the registered-schema cardinality".
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:203-230`: the `default-edn-print` memo, hit on every `app-schemas-digest` call. Epoch also computes a digest per recorded epoch (`epoch/assembly.cljc:102`).
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:384-417`: the `extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` memo, reached through `schema-has-sensitive?` (`:432-447`) on every validation-failure redaction (`validate.cljc:804, 1420`), boundary rejection (`core/spec.cljc:173`), and hot-reload violation (`storage.cljc:562`).
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:650` (replacement) and `:811-823` (`on-frame-destroyed!`) drop only the registry entry. Nothing touches either memo.

**Repro (*probed*, `clojure -M` from `implementation/schemas`, plain-atom substrate, at 989a1c6d53, which is identical to 475bdcaacf for `implementation/core/src`, `implementation/schemas` and `implementation/epoch`; the memo size is read from the memo fn's closed-over `cache` field by reflection):**

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :u/bad (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :user {:n -1})}))
(defn request-cycle! [i schema-fn]            ; one "request": make, register, digest, fail, destroy
  (let [id (keyword "req" (str i))]
    (rf/make-frame {:id id})
    (rf/with-frame id (rf/reg-app-schema [:user] (schema-fn)))
    (schemas/app-schemas-digest {:frame id})
    (rf/dispatch-sync [:u/bad] {:frame id})
    (rf/destroy-frame! id)))
;; 200 cycles, one shared schema value [:map [:n [:fn pos?]]]  => {:printer 1,   :walker 1}
;; 200 more, fresh [:map [:n [:fn (fn [x] (pos? x))]]] each    => {:printer 201, :walker 201}
;; frames still holding schemas afterwards                      => 0
;; 100 re-registrations of one path on one live frame (data-only
;; [:map [:n [:int {:min i}]]], digest each)                   => {:printer 301, :walker 300}
```

**Contract:** Spec 010 §Schema digest, the non-normative memo note (line 535): "its steady-state size equals the registry size". The same claim appears at `cache.cljc:14-20`, `validator.cljc:203-204` and `walker.cljc:404-411`. Spec 013 line 147 and 002 §Destroy set the frame-isolation expectation that per-request frame churn on a long-running JVM SSR host leaks nothing.

**Reach in production:** small. App-db validation is dev-only, and the SSR guide computes the digest once at boot (`docs/ssr/concepts.md:693-702`). The production-reachable memo calls (boundary rejection and recordable-cofx redaction) see registered event and cofx schemas, which form a fixed set. So production growth needs schemas built fresh per request plus a per-request digest or rejection. Dev (HMR, epoch per event) and long test runs are where it grows.

## Expected

Memo entries live no longer than the schemas that own them, or there is no memo.

## Fix direction

- Delete both memos and `cache.cljc`. Both memos sit only on failure branches or per digest call, and the HTTP and resources extractors already walk unmemoised (`schemas.cljc:132-137`), so the cost is a re-walk or re-print on a cold path. This is the reviewers' shared recommendation.
- That also deletes `clear-edn-print-cache!` and `clear-sensitive-paths-cache!`, and their callers in tests: `schemas/test_fixture.clj:75-76`, `digest_parity_test.clj:26,34`, `http_privacy_body_test.clj:77`, and two `security/test` suites.
- If a measurement shows a memo earns its place, key it weakly on the schema value instead (`WeakHashMap` on the JVM, `WeakMap` in CLJS). Do not add an LRU or any cache configuration.
- Correct 010 line 535 and the docstrings to match.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test: run N `make-frame` / `reg-app-schema` (fresh closure-bearing schema) / `app-schemas-digest` / failing dispatch / `destroy-frame!` cycles. No cache retains an entry for a dead schema: either no memo exists, or a `WeakReference` to each schema clears after GC. It fails at trunk.
- Digest bytes and redaction outputs are identical before and after; the existing digest parity fixtures and security redaction suites stay green.
- Gates: the schemas, http and security JVM lanes, plus CLJS via the PR's CI. If a public var is removed, the api-manifest drift check is needed too.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/10 §5, the false bound); probed during the cross-review.
- Related: rf2-s8sth (open) lists a stale `clear-sensitive-paths-cache!` docstring, citing a stress test and a fixture teardown that do not hold. Deleting the memo moots that line. rf2-fzbj.25 / rf2-gwye.14 (closed) made `compute-edn-print` ignore ambient printer limits, and that behaviour must survive.
- Not the same fix as the schema hot-reload freeze bead in this batch. No shared code, so the two can run in parallel. Both reviews also recommend a weakly keyed compiled-validator cache for Malli: probed at 5.33 µs per check uncached, 0.10 µs weak-cached, 0.06 µs precompiled (JVM, Malli 0.20.1). That is a performance change, not part of this bug.
- Hot zones: removing the two `clear-*` vars deletes two rows of `spec/api-manifest.edn` / `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` (`:tier :implementation`), and `spec/API.md` plus both sidecars are one hot-zone holding. Sequence it accordingly, or take the weak-key route, which keeps the vars and avoids the holding.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/schemas.md` decision 12 and action 5; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/10-schemas.md` §5.

title: Xray install guide omits the @xyflow/react and elkjs npm peers; make the guide the one home for Xray prerequisites
description:
## Problem

The canonical Xray installation guide, `docs/xray/01-installation.md`, omits the two npm peer packages that Xray's machines chart requires. Any app not scaffolded from the template that follows the guide gets a missing-module compile error. The fix this week landed only in the skill.

## Evidence (verified at trunk 9e84689562)

- **3b06e8286a (rf2-m5q0v.7)** added `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs` to `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/launch-modes.md` (~L55) only.
- **The guide has 0 mentions of either package:** a git grep for `xyflow|elkjs` under `docs/xray/` returns nothing.
- **The packages are required:**
  - `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:36` requires `"@xyflow/react"`, as do `chart/edges.cljs:42` and `chart/nodes/xyflow_node.cljs:19`;
  - `elkjs` is required at `chart.cljs:37` (`["elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js" :as elkjs]`);
  - `tools/xray/deps.edn` (~L69) pulls in machines-viz;
  - the pinned versions live in `implementation/package.json`.
- **Template apps are fine** because the template's `_shared/package.json` already carries the peers, which is presumably why no field report has hit this yet.
- **Related:** #10980 (4ba53943ca) showed restated Xray contract prose (the inline-width CSS variable) sitting wrong and unchecked from May to October, repeated in two skills, four specs and docstrings.

## Direction

- Add both peers, with where their versions are pinned, to the guide's "Add the dev dependency" section (~L7-30).
- Add a troubleshooting entry that shows the missing-module error text and points to that section.
- In `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/launch-modes.md`, keep a one-line pointer to the guide's anchor plus the failure signature, instead of restating the pin policy. This follows the family "one owner per fact" rule in the sibling bead.

## Acceptance

- The guide lists `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs`, and the troubleshooting entry exists.
- The skill links to the guide's anchor and does not restate the pins.
- `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.

## Notes

No hot-zone files. Small.

title: Nav-token allocator resets on frame destroy, so a same-id successor re-issues tokens and accepts stale continuations
description:
## Bug

The nav-token and pending-nav allocators are per-frame high-water marks, and `destroy-frame!` drops the frame's entry. A same-id successor frame therefore restarts at `nav-1`/`pn-1` and re-issues tokens its predecessor already handed out. A predecessor continuation that is addressed by frame keyword and carries one of those tokens passes the `:rf.route/with-nav-token` stale check in the successor and is delivered as current. Nothing reports it.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/nav_counters.cljc:120-127` (`next-id`): the next token is `(inc (or (get snapshot counter-key) 0))` from the frame's own snapshot.
- `nav_counters.cljc:153-160` (`release-frame!`) dissocs the frame's entry. It is called from `routing.cljc:521-544` (`release-routing-host-caches!`, the `:routing/on-frame-destroyed!` hook).
- `nav_token.cljc:313-416` (`with-nav-token-handler`): the stale gate compares only the carried token with the live slice token (`:393`, `suppress? nav-token current`). Token strings are not scoped to an incarnation.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_nav_counters_test.clj:67-79` pins the drop on purpose, so that a process creating per-request frames does not leak one entry per frame.

Repro (*probed* on the JVM at 9b20bf0093, whose routing sources are identical to 475bdcaacf; script `managed-routing-codec.clj`):

```clojure
(rf/make-frame {:id :f})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :r/a}] {:frame :f})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :r/b}] {:frame :f})        ; predecessor token "nav-2"
(rf.frame/destroy-frame! :f)
(rf/make-frame {:id :f})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :r/a}] {:frame :f})        ; successor token "nav-1"
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :r/b}] {:frame :f})        ; successor token "nav-2"
;; a predecessor continuation carrying "nav-2", dispatched by frame keyword:
(rf/dispatch-sync [:app/deliver "nav-2"] {:frame :f})
;; :app/deliver emits [:rf.route/with-nav-token {:nav-token "nav-2" :value :OLD-FRAME-RESULT :rf/reply-to [:app/loaded]}]
```

Observed:
- The successor's tokens restart at `nav-1`.
- The successor's app-db receives `{:status :ok :value :OLD-FRAME-RESULT :rf.reply/work-status :completed …}`. The predecessor's result is delivered rather than stale-suppressed.

Scope: managed HTTP is aborted on frame destroy (`http/managed.cljc:242-247`), so it does not cross. The hazard needs an unmanaged, keyword-addressed continuation, for example an app's own promise or socket callback that does `(rf/dispatch ev {:frame :f})`.

Contract:
- Spec 012:1095 (§Navigation tokens) says the counter is "monotone and unbounded … without ever needing to wrap or reset", and that implementations "MUST NOT wrap or recycle the counter — doing so would risk colliding a freshly-allocated token with one still carried by a slow in-flight continuation".
- Spec 012:1097 calls a collision "structurally impossible".
- Spec 012:1877 and :1901 prescribe releasing the per-frame counter entry on destroy. That is the reset the never-recycle rule forbids.

## Expected

A token is never re-issued under the same frame id. A same-id successor's first token is strictly greater than any token its predecessor issued.

## Fix direction

Replace the per-frame allocator map with one process-global monotone counter per allocator. Keep:
- the recordable `:rf.route/nav-allocation` / `:rf.route/pending-nav-allocation` cofx;
- the `max`-install on replay.

Drop `release-frame!` for counters. That stays bounded with no per-frame entries to leak, and it is incarnation-safe by construction.

Update Spec 012:1097, :1877 and :1901, which describe a per-frame cache released on destroy.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test that fails before the fix. Destroy and recreate a frame under the same id: the successor's first `:nav-token` is not equal to any predecessor token, and the `:app/deliver` continuation above is suppressed with `:rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed` instead of reaching `:app/loaded`.
- Tokens still never recycle across epoch restore and replay. Strict replay still fails loudly on a missing recorded allocation (`routing_nav_allocation_record_replay_test.clj` stays green).
- Replace `destroy-frame-releases-host-counter-entry` with a test that destroying many frames leaves allocator storage constant. Update tests that pin an exact per-frame token sequence across two frames to assert uniqueness and monotonicity instead.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (routing D8 Attack 2 / action 7). Sol supplied the acceptance properties: non-recycling, recordability, incarnation safety.
- Related: rf2-inhw8 (routing prune follow-ups; a different defect).
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/routing.md` §D8 and the "Allocator" conflict in its cross-review section.

title: doc_api_check and xray_spec_check resolve (rf/x against every namespace, so stale calls to moved vars pass
description:
## Bug

`doc_api_check` resolves every `(rf/x …)` and `(rf.story/x …)` reference in the API reference docs against the bare var names of **every** manifest row, in every namespace. `xray_spec_check` does the same for Xray's `(rf/x` facade references. So a call through `rf/` to a var that lives on another namespace passes. Concretely, after a var moves off `re-frame.core`, stale `(rf/x …)` examples keep passing on the strength of the var's new home row. Developers and AI pairs copy those calls, and they fail.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_api_check.clj`:
  - `check!` builds `manifest-vars (set (map :var rows))` over all rows (`:284`).
  - `reconcile` (`:110-141`) accepts any reference whose bare var is in that set.
  - References are extracted for the aliases `rf` and `rf.story` (`:143-151`), which the ns docstring (`:22-27`) defines as `re-frame.core` and `re-frame.story`.
  - The docstring's "RESOLUTION LATITUDE" paragraph (`:39-47`) defends the latitude: "the API reference legitimately names vars across several public namespaces (`re-frame.core`, `re-frame.story`, `re-frame.machines`, …) under the `rf` alias". The census below shows nothing uses it.
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/xray_spec_check.clj:155-166`: the comment calls `(rf/<var>` "the re-frame CORE surface", yet it resolves against `all-vars (set (map :var rows))` (`:159`).
- **Contrast.** `doc_guide_check.clj:32, :79` already resolves `rf` against `re-frame.core` rows only (`rows-in-ns rows "re-frame.core"`).
- Repro (*probed*, JVM, from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`):
  - `spec/api-manifest.edn` carries `machine-transition` only on `re-frame.machines` (tier `:advanced`).
  - This call returns `[]`, so the wrong call passes:

    ```clojure
    (doc-api-check/reconcile {:references    [{:var "machine-transition" :line 1 :raw "(rf/machine-transition" :file "docs/api/x.md"}]
                              :manifest-vars (set (map :var (projection/manifest-rows)))
                              :scoped-allow  {}})
    ```

- Census of the scanned trees (*probed*):
  - `spec/Privacy.md`, `docs/api/` and `docs/story/api/` carry 483 `(rf/` references and 13 `(rf.story/` references.
  - **0** of them resolve only through a row outside `re-frame.core` or `re-frame.story` respectively.
  - `tools/xray/spec/API.md` carries 16 `(rf/` references, 0 off core.
  - So exact resolution reds nothing on trunk.

## Expected

`(rf/x` resolves only against `re-frame.core` rows, and `(rf.story/x` only against `re-frame.story` rows, in both `doc_api_check` and `xray_spec_check`'s facade path.

## Fix direction

- In `references-in-files`, assoc the alias onto each reference; the function already loops over the aliases.
- In `check!`, build one var set per alias (`{"rf" core-vars, "rf.story" story-vars}` via `projection/rows-in-ns`), and have `reconcile` look a reference up in its alias's set.
- In `xray_spec_check`, resolve facade references against `re-frame.core` rows.
- Delete the RESOLUTION LATITUDE paragraph. Keep the scoped removal allowlists unchanged.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests:
  - a synthetic `(rf/machine-transition` reference produces a problem whose detail names `re-frame.core`, while `(rf/dispatch` passes;
  - a `(rf.story/<core-only-var>` reference reds;
  - the same pair holds for `xray_spec_check/reconcile`'s facade references.
- The live `doc_api_check` and `xray_spec_check` stay green.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Sol review (surface 35, insight 2), adopted by the Opus tooling and core-public-api cross-reviews (D10, action 2d; core-public-api Insight 2).
- **Related:** rf2-mn2ht.58 and rf2-mn2ht.60 are in the same artefact, with no file overlap.
- **Hot-zone files:** none.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/tooling.md` §D10; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-public-api.md` Insight 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/35-api-manifest-spec-resource.md` §2.
