title: Spec 005's Level-2 testing example throws :rf.error/no-frame-context: make-machine-handler requires :rf.frame/id
description:
## Bug

Spec 005's documented Level-2 test ("unregistered handler fn") does not run: the handler `make-machine-handler` returns throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on the example's db-arg, because the example passes no `:rf.frame/id`. Anyone copying the testing pyramid's middle rung gets an exception instead of a snapshot.

## Evidence

- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:4342-4357` (trunk 475bdcaacf), §Testing → Level 2:
  ```clojure
  (handler {:rf.db/runtime {:rf.runtime/machines {:snapshots {:drawer/editor {:state :idle :data {}}}}}}
           [:drawer/editor [:right-click-circle some-id 30]])
  ```
  The prose under it says this works "without going near the dispatch pipeline ... no registration, no test frame". `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1047` repeats that Level-2 testing is possible "without a test frame".
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:1033-1042`: the returned handler destructures `frame :rf.frame/id` from its first argument and calls `(rf.frame/require-frame-stamp! frame :rf.machine/event-received ...)` before anything else.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1278-1303`: `require-frame-stamp!` returns the id when non-nil, else emits and throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
- Repro, *probed* (JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/machines`, trunk source):
  ```clojure
  (def handler (rf.machines/make-machine-handler
                 {:initial :idle :states {:idle {:on {:go :busy}} :busy {}}}))
  (def db-arg {:rf.db/runtime {:rf.runtime/machines {:snapshots {:drawer/editor {:state :idle :data {}}}}}})
  (handler db-arg [:drawer/editor [:go]])
  ;; => throws :rf.error/no-frame-context ("a frame-scoped event-received ran with no frame context ...")
  (handler (assoc db-arg :rf.frame/id :rf/default) [:drawer/editor [:go]])
  ;; => returns; the snapshot at [:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :drawer/editor :state] is :busy
  ```
  Adding any `:rf.frame/id` makes the example work, and still with no registered machine and no frame created.

## Expected

The spec's Level-2 example runs as written and returns the `{:rf.db/runtime ... :fx ...}` map it promises.

## Fix direction

Minimal: correct the example (and the "no test frame" wording at 005:1047 and :4355) to pass a frame id in the db-arg, e.g. `{:rf.frame/id :test/frame :rf.db/runtime {...}}`, and say the id only stamps traces. Do not relax `require-frame-stamp!`; the nil-stamp check is deliberate.

The Opus review recommends a different end state: demote `make-machine-handler` to internal and delete Level 2 (no production caller; its only documented use is this broken example). Sol's review prefers keeping the factory as a supplied-coeffects test seam. That choice is Mike's; fixing the example does not foreclose it.

## Acceptance

- A machines test runs the corrected spec example verbatim (the db-arg shape from 005 §Testing → Level 2) and asserts the returned runtime-db snapshot; it fails against the current spec text (throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context`) and passes against the corrected text.
- `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` pass for the spec edit.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (machines #12), confirmed by Sol's own source reading; first executed during bead drafting.
- Related: none open. If Mike chooses to demote the factory, that also removes `*in-registration-home?*` and `:rf.error/machine-schema-requires-reg-machine`.
- Hot zone: `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (sequence with any other 005 bead).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/machines.md` §12 and Action 9; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/11-machines.md` §8.
notes:
2026-10-10 22:59:35 AUSEST

== FIX (worker egress-machines, PR #11091, commit "fix(machines): Spec 005's Level-2 handler example carries a frame id")

Premise verified at base c318ef11f2: the spec's db-arg threw :rf.error/no-frame-context.

Minimal fix taken: spec/005-StateMachines.md §Testing → Level 2 example's db-arg now carries :rf.frame/id :test/frame, its code comment says the id is required and only stamps traces; the prose under it and §make-machine-handler is a pure factory (the old "without a test frame") now say no registration and no frame are needed, the id only stamps traces. require-frame-stamp! and make-machine-handler untouched.

Verified at source: with the example's existing snapshot the handler uses the frame id for the trace stamp and a frame-meta platform lookup that defaults to :client for a missing frame; lower-at-spawn! runs only on a singleton first boot (no snapshot), which the example is not.

Test: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/level2_handler_spec_example_test.clj reads the (handler ...) form out of the spec and runs it against a machine that takes :right-click-circle; asserts no frame exists under the id and the returned [:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :drawer/editor :state].
Evidence: red at base exit 1 (no-frame-context); green exit 0 (1 test, 4 assertions); red again with only the spec reverted exit 1 (no-frame-context); restore checked by blob hash. machines clojure -M:test exit 0 (680 tests, 1537 assertions). check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 (a planted bad anchor on the edited line went red, exit 1); mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

Not done (Mike's call, unchanged): whether make-machine-handler is demoted. Unrelated nit seen beside the edit: the next paragraph says the handler reads (get-in db [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :drawer/editor]); it reads from the :rf.db/runtime coeffect, not db.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:45:18 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Demote `make-machine-handler`. The fn stays internal in `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.registration` for its two callers (`reg-machine*`'s body and the spawned-actor seam). The public re-export, the `:machines/make-machine-handler` late-bind hook, the `*in-registration-home?*` guard and `:rf.error/machine-schema-requires-reg-machine` are all deleted. Spec 005 drops §`make-machine-handler` is a pure factory and §Testing Level 2, and teaches two test levels: pure `machine-transition`, and registered in a frame. There is no replacement testing API. The work is filed as **rf2-mn2ht.69**, a new bead parented to rf2-mn2ht. It is not a widening of this bead, which closed when PR #11091 merged.

SCOPE OF THIS RULING. This bead was closed at 2026-10-10 23:27:06 AUSEST by the merge of PR #11091 (merge commit `45960a05c8`). That happened after the review dossier was written at 23:18:38. The close reason settles only the example fix, and says in terms "whether to demote the factory remains Mike's call". This ruling answers that residual question. It does not revisit the close. The bead stays closed, and nothing about its close reason changes.

WHY (under the stance: minimal, ergonomic API, low friction, trust the programmer, no gold plating):

- **The var has no job left.** It is public for one documented reason, Level 2. Level 2 threw `:rf.error/no-frame-context` for as long as it existed, until #11091 added `:rf.frame/id` on 2026-10-10, and its second copy in `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` throws still. The other stated job, at 005:1039 ("code-gen and loader pipelines minting handlers for computed ids"), belongs to `reg-machine*`, and that is what Story's loader calls. The API-review wave that kept the factory public (rf2-kuky.16, rf2-kuky.26, rf2-u91d, rf2-z442) rested on exactly these two reasons, and both have collapsed. rf2-z442 called the Level-2 test "the primitive's whole reason for staying public".
- **The seam is not ergonomic.** A caller hand-builds framework-internal coeffect keys: `:rf.frame/id`, `:rf.db/runtime` and `[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id>]`. It refuses every machine with a `[:schemas :data]` schema. The handler it returns is not pure: it reads the frame registry, emits traces, and on first boot writes elision claims into whichever live frame the id names.
- **Removing it is subtraction, and that is how trust the programmer applies here.** The guard, its error id, drift Rule 4, four skill warnings and an evals line exist only to fence off a door the project does not need to offer. Remove the door and every fence goes with it.
- **What a test author loses is small.** For an ordinary transition, Level 1 gives the same answer as Level 2 (probe below). Level 2's only unique reach is the frame-free first-boot cascade, and a frame test covers that in about four JVM lines.
- **The move is reversible.** We are pre-alpha, and the migration README already states the no-back-compat-shim posture (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2390`). If a real need for registration-free handler tests ever appears, a purpose-built helper can be designed then. Re-exporting the var is one line. So this is not a one-way door, and it does not need Mike personally.

REJECTED:

- **A: keep it as a public supplied-coeffects test seam.** This was the Sol review's choice, and Codex called it defensible. It is honest and cheap. It would mean stamping the Construction-Prompts copy, fixing the wording, and aligning 005:1039 with API.md:1004. But it keeps every upkeep cost (guard, error id, gate rule, skill warnings) for a rung whose results duplicate Level 1. It also goes on teaching internal envelopes to authors and AI pairs.
- **C: keep the var public, drop Level 2 from the pyramid.** This option is dominated. It keeps all of A's upkeep and removes the one use API.md names. The dossier author, who raised it, also rejected it.
- **Escalate to Mike.** Not warranted. The reviews agree on both the facts and the values, the change is reversible pre-alpha, and Mike delegated the decision.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:

- **The dossier author and Codex both recommend demotion.** The author agrees with the Opus review and with this bead's framing that fixing the example does not foreclose demotion. So the recommendation on the bead is two to one: the dossier author, Codex and the Opus review against the Sol review.
- **The only factual disagreement was freshness, and it is settled.** The dossier said #11091 was OPEN and that HEAD's example still threw. Codex said it had merged. `gh pr view 11091 --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit` returns `state MERGED`, `mergedAt 2026-10-10T12:26:39Z`, merge commit `45960a05c83ea2285504af9041927b75510e4197`, exit 0. At HEAD, 005's Level-2 example carries `:rf.frame/id :test/frame`, and the Construction-Prompts copy does not.
- **Codex's caveat is accepted, and it does not change the outcome.** A repo census proves repo usage only; it cannot prove that no downstream programmer uses the var. Pre-alpha with no shims, that is the posture.
- **Codex's point that a broken example is not, by itself, evidence the capability has no value is also accepted.** The ruling rests on the duplication with Level 1 and on upkeep, not on the breakage alone.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 200a67df2d unless stated):

title: Spec 002/008 + testing-doubles skill: state frame-derived resolution and the test fixture frame's live-registrar resolution (docs only)
description:
Possible spec gap, measured on the JVM by the rf2-ux850 worker (PR #11077), stated here as a CLAIM to re-check. Re-registering a product fx from a test body behaves three ways, depending on the frame:
- on the test fixture's default frame, the later registration wins;
- on a frame created AFTER the re-registration (make-frame), it throws :rf.error/image-duplicate-id;
- on a frame created BEFORE it, the product handler silently keeps running.
The skill text (skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-doubles.md) now describes this. Spec 002 (Frames) and Spec 008 (Testing) do not say it.

Task: find where Spec 002 / 008 define frame image capture and the duplicate-id rule. State the three outcomes in the present tense where the contract lives, with a pointer from the other spec. If the behaviour contradicts an existing normative sentence, do NOT change code; record the contradiction on this bead with [MIKE DECISION] in the title and stop.
Hot zone: spec/002-Frames.md is one-editor-at-a-time. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict.
notes:
== MEASURED, AND HELD FOR A DECISION (2026-10-10 22:42 AUSEST, worker contract-truth, PR #11088) ==

No spec text was written for this bead: the measured behaviour contradicts existing normative sentences in Spec 002, so per the bead's own instruction this is held for Mike. Spec 002 and 008 are untouched in PR #11088.

MEASUREMENT. JVM probe from implementation/core at tip 9d3f4a8ef6 (scratch, not committed). A product namespace registers (rf/reg-fx :probe/effect ...) and an event :probe/go returning {:fx [[:probe/effect "x"]]}; a second namespace re-registers :probe/effect (the test double, a cross-namespace duplicate). Each case ran inside (ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter plain-atom/adapter}). Controls first, so a zero means something:
- CONTROL, product only: fixture :rf/default ran the product fx; make-frame {} ran the product fx.
- 1. Fixture's ambient :rf/default, double registered in the test body: the DOUBLE ran (later registration wins). That frame carries NO resolved image generation (frame-generation :rf/default => nil): ensure-default-frame! seats it through the internal upsert-frame!, so lookups take the registrar-atom path, which is last-writer-wins.
- 2. make-frame {} AFTER the double: throws :rf.error/image-duplicate-id.
- 3. make-frame {} BEFORE the double: the PRODUCT fx keeps running (two dispatches, product both times). NOT silent: the read-time reprojection flush reports ONE always-on :rf.error/reprojection-failed record, {:frame :probe/before :registration [:fx :probe/effect] :namespaces ["<double ns>" "<product ns>"] :recovery :kept-prior-generation}, and the second dispatch does not repeat it. With a 300 ms sleep first, the deferred next-tick flush reports the same single record. This matches the Spec 009 :rf.error/reprojection-failed catalogue row exactly, so the bead's word "silently" is wrong: the frame keeps its prior generation for EVERY id, and says so once.
- D. CONTROL, make-frame {} BEFORE a SAME-namespace replacement: the new fx runs and no error is reported, so reprojection is live and case 3 is the duplicate, not a frozen frame.
- E. Explicit image selecting only the product namespace, made before the double: the product fx runs, no duplicate.

THE CONTRADICTIONS (line numbers at 9d3f4a8ef6):
(A) spec/002-Frames.md:412, "Resolution is process-global": "the runtime resolves the event handler, every coeffect supplier, every effect, AND every subscription from the one process-global registrar ... There is no per-frame handler routing: two frames running the same app resolve identical handlers and differ only in their state." And :401, observation 1: "every frame in the process resolves against the one registrar ... Frames isolate state, not behaviour." Measured: in one process at one moment, the fixture's :rf/default runs the double while a default-image frame made earlier runs the product fx. The two frames resolve DIFFERENT handlers for one id. Spec 008:318 already says the opposite of 002:412 ("Each frame runs its own resolved image generation, so two frames can hold different handlers for the same id without collision"), so 002 contradicts itself here independently of this bead.
(B) Spec 002 makes make-frame "the ONE constructor" (:1003, :2771), and every live frame owns its resolved image generation (:384, :403). Spec 001 rule 2 (§Re-registration of a different function): a cross-namespace duplicate "fail[s] loudly rather than being masked ... load order never picks a survivor", and 002:1079 says "there is no last-writer-wins on the default path". Measured: the fixture's ambient :rf/default is seated outside make-frame, has no generation, and resolves last-writer-wins, so a cross-namespace duplicate is masked there with no error.

DECISION WANTED (either is small):
1. Make 002 true: rewrite 002:401 and :412 so that a frame resolves through its own resolved image generation (assembled from the one process-global source store), not "the one registrar". Then state the three outcomes in 002 §Image resolution and composition, with the pointer from 008.
2. For the fixture frame, either (a) the spec carves it out: 008 Pattern 5 states that the fixture's ambient :rf/default is a test-support frame that resolves the live registrar, so the latest registration of an id wins there, or (b) the code changes: ensure-default-frame! seats it through make-frame {:id :rf/default}, so outcome 1 becomes image-duplicate-id like every other default-image frame. (b) changes test-fixture behaviour suites lean on, because the skill text today recommends body registration against the fixture frame.
Once ruled, the spec text is a short paragraph plus a pointer; the measured outcomes above are the content.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:43:48 AUSEST at HEAD 9b51da3393) ==
DECISION: Docs only, no runtime change. (1) Spec 002 is rewritten to describe frame-derived resolution: registrations go into one process-global source store, and each frame `make-frame` constructs resolves every handler through its own sealed resolved image generation, assembled from that store. (2) The test fixture's ambient `:rf/default` keeps resolving the live registrar (latest registration of an id wins there), and Spec 008 Pattern 5 states that as a property of the test-support construction path, with a pointer from 002. The skill's word "silently" is corrected in the same PR.

WHY: Part 1 is barely a decision. The code, EP-0023 (and its addendum), Conventions, Spec 008 and Spec 009 already agree on frame-derived resolution; only 002's "process-global resolution" sentences (and a few echoes) say otherwise. They date from commit `14a0e95b85` (2026-06-20), which retired multi-realm addressing: the intended meaning was "one registrar, not one per realm", and it overreached into "every frame reads the same table". Rewriting the code to match them (1B) would delete explicit images, hermetic test frames, `:rf.gen/shadows` and 008's whole hermetic-frame section. Part 2 is decided by the stance: trust the programmer, low friction. The fixture frame is test support (its docstring already says "TEST-ONLY ... NOT a runtime path"), and last-writer-wins there is exactly what a test author stubbing an effect wants. Writing that down costs one paragraph. Option 2(b) buys uniformity at a real ergonomic cost, and does not even make the mistake loud: it turns a working body-registered mock into an ignored one (the product effect fires, with one error record).

REJECTED:

title: Public rf/unsubscribe releases by address: after an eviction a late release disposes a successor's cache entry
description:
## Bug

The public `rf/unsubscribe` releases by address, `(frame-id, query-v)`, not by the reaction the caller acquired. After a hot reload, `clear-sub-cache!` or re-registration evicts the caller's slot, a late `unsubscribe` decrements, and can dispose, a successor entry that another holder built under the same query. On CLJS the successor's holder loses its notifications. Tools, REPL sessions and tests that subscribe imperatively hit this. So does any in-tree consumer that releases through the public door, and `machines/timer.cljc` already carries a private guard against it.

## Evidence

Trunk 475bdcaacf.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2640-2686`: `unsubscribe` resolves the frame and calls `rf.subs.cache/unsubscribe!` with only the cache key.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:215-270`: `unsubscribe!` decrements whatever entry currently sits at that key, and disposes it on 1 → 0.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2688-` and `subs/cache.cljc:273-`: the identity-guarded `unsubscribe-if-reaction` already exists. It is marked internal. Its docstring explains the hazard: "an unguarded decrement would either underflow a successor entry rebuilt under the same key or steal a ref another subscriber owns." Core's own long-lived holders use it: the hook spine's cleanup at `substrate/spine.cljs:3555`, `subscribe-once`, and layer-2+ input release.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:179-200`: the timer table releases through the public door and threads an `owner-gone?` predicate so that "A's decrement would dispose B's fresh reaction" cannot happen. This is the same hazard, worked around locally.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter, exit 0):

```clojure
(rf/init! rf.substrate.plain-atom/adapter)
(rf.frame/ensure-default-frame!)
(rf/reg-event :seed (fn [_ _] {:db {:n 7}}))
(rf/reg-sub :n (fn [db _] (:n db)))
(rf/with-frame :rf/default
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:seed])
  (let [a (rf/subscribe [:n])]                    ; holder A acquires R
    (rf/reg-sub :n (fn [db _] (* 10 (:n db))))    ; hot reload evicts R
    (let [b (rf/subscribe [:n])]                  ; holder B acquires successor S
      (rf/unsubscribe [:n])                       ; A's late release
      (ref-counts))))                             ; sub-cache query-v -> :ref-count
```

Observed:

```
re-register:      before A's release: {[:n] 1} | B identical? slot: true
re-register:      after  A's release: {}       | B's slot still present: false
clear-sub-cache!: before A's release: {[:n] 1} | B identical? slot: true
clear-sub-cache!: after  A's release: {}       | B's slot still present: false
control (unsubscribe-if-reaction on the same sequence): {[:n] 1}
```

B's entry is evicted and disposed by A's release. B still holds S, but S is no longer cached, so B's own later `unsubscribe` is a no-op. On a CLJS spine or ratom substrate, S's disposal also removes its source watches and watchers.

Contract contrast: Spec 006 §Render-phase provisional acquisition (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:946`) requires exactly this guard for internal holders: "a late release MUST no-op rather than underflow a successor entry rebuilt under the same key". The public door that Spec 006 §`unsubscribe` (`:989`) teaches to "tests, REPL sessions, and tools" has no such guard.

## Expected

A release returns the reference its caller acquired. If that reference has already been evicted, the release is a no-op and never touches a successor.

## Fix direction

Give the public door the identity guard core already uses, through a small additive change: either an arity that names the acquired reaction, which is `unsubscribe-if-reaction` made public, or `unsubscribe` accepting the reaction `subscribe` returned. Keep address-only release only if it is still wanted as an explicit operation. Then update `machines/timer.cljc` to release by reaction and drop its `owner-gone?` workaround. The exact call shape should follow the ruling on rf2-xkog1, which is already deciding the 2-arity of `unsubscribe`.

## Acceptance

- A new JVM test beside `unsubscribe-if-reaction-no-ops-against-a-successor-entry` in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_test.clj`:
  1. A subscribes; the slot is evicted by re-registration and, in a second case, by `clear-sub-cache!`.
  2. B subscribes.
  3. A releases through the public door.
  4. B's slot keeps ref-count 1, and the slot still holds B's reaction.
- The test fails on today's code.
- The existing `sub-cache-ref-counting` behaviour is unchanged: release past zero is idempotent, and a missing frame is a silent no-op.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (report 05, insight 2), adopted by the Opus core-reactive-substrate cross-review.
- Related: rf2-xkog1 ([MIKE DECISION] on `unsubscribe`'s call shape). Both change the same public fn and its API rows, so land them together or in sequence. rf2-1frc (closed) fixed the same hazard inside the hook spine's cleanup.
- Hot zones: `spec/API.md` with `spec/api-manifest.edn` (regenerated) and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` if the public signature changes; `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §`unsubscribe`.
- Probe script: `scratchpad/bugbeads/views-work/probe_unsub_identity.clj` (session scratch, not durable).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-reactive-substrate.md` decision 13 and action 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/05-core-subscriptions-substrates.md` §2.
notes:
== RULED UNDER rf2-xkog1 (2026-10-10 23:57:49 AUSEST, HEAD f678139da9) ==
Mike delegated the rf2-xkog1 decision; it was ruled Option H, and that ruling decides this bead's fix direction. The full ruling, evidence and implementation guidance are in rf2-xkog1's notes (two parts).

WHAT IT MEANS HERE:
- The public release becomes `(rf/unsubscribe r) → nil`, taking the reaction `subscribe` returned. It returns one counted share of `r` through the existing atomic identity guard (`rf.subs.cache/unsubscribe-if-reaction!`), locating the slot by scanning the visible frames' caches for the `identical?` reaction. So after an eviction — re-registration, `clear-sub-cache!`, hot reload, or `destroy-frame!` + `make-frame` with the same id — a late release finds no slot holding `r` and no-ops: the successor is never touched. That is this bead's Expected, delivered BY CONSTRUCTION at the public door rather than opt-in. Both address forms leave the public surface.
- Of this bead's "Fix direction" options, it is the second one ("`unsubscribe` accepting the reaction `subscribe` returned"). Publishing `unsubscribe-if-reaction` as an arity, and keeping address-only release as an explicit public operation, were both rejected: two ways to tear down.
- In-tree holders that already know their address move to the internal O(1) `rf.subs/unsubscribe-if-reaction frame q r`: `substrate/spine.cljs:3223`, `fresco/impl/collector.cljs:167`, and `machines/timer.cljc:198` and `:727`. Each already has the reaction at its release site. The timer's `owner-gone?` workaround goes if its scenario passes on the identity guard alone.
- TRAP carried from the ruling: `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_destroy_tail_incarnation_fence_test.clj:95` and `machine_lifecycle_tail_exact_handoff_cljs_test.cljc:190` count calls to a `with-redefs` spy on `rf.subs/unsubscribe`, using a fake `:reaction (atom 5000)`. Once the timer calls `unsubscribe-if-reaction`, the lost-owner arm (expected 0) passes vacuously. Rewrite them to assert the observable outcome with a real subscribe.
- This bead's Acceptance stands as written, with the release spelled `(rf/unsubscribe a)`, plus a third eviction case — destroy + recreate of the same frame id. A JVM probe at f678139da9 showed that the address door disposes B's slot in all three cases, and a handle-release sketch leaves `{[:n] 1}` with B still in the slot in all three. The existing behaviours restate cleanly: release past zero is a silent no-op, and a reaction whose frame is gone is a silent no-op.

SEQUENCING: no separate PR for this bead. The rf2-xkog1 PR delivers this bead's acceptance test and fix, and closes both beads together, citing that PR. A dependency has been added (this bead depends on rf2-xkog1) so this bead is never dispatched alone ahead of it.
== WORKER (2026-10-11 02:27:42 AUSEST): delivered in PR #11118 (draft) with rf2-xkog1 ==
Acceptance test `late-unsubscribe-after-an-eviction-leaves-the-successor-alone` in implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_test.clj beside `unsubscribe-if-reaction-no-ops-against-a-successor-entry`: A subscribes in frame :xkog1/f; the slot is evicted by (a) re-registration, (b) `clear-sub-cache!`, (c) `destroy-frame!` + `make-frame` with the same id; B subscribes; A releases with `(rf/unsubscribe a)`; B's slot keeps ref-count 1 and still holds B's reaction; B's own release then empties the cache. Written with the base address spelling it is red at base in all three cases (B's slot `{}`, B not in the slot); green with the fix; red again with the fix reverted. `sub-cache-ref-counting` keeps its substance in the handle form (slot shared on hit, one share per release, past-zero no-op, nil no-op). The machines timer releases by reaction and its `owner-gone?` no longer gates the release. Full verdict on rf2-xkog1's notes.

title: FALSE: emit-ui-tree refuses reserved non-attribute keys in tree attrs
description: Audit of PR #10392 at 611ef0d630c6587c6cd78aeb7e90d08ed17f0bb9. Retained Spec 004B rows require children/dangerouslySetInnerHTML refusals and ref/key handling outside ordinary attrs. ui_tree.cljc:691-707 sends every non-class/style/property key to serialise-attr (:625-671), which has no reserved-slot refusal and serializes string-valued :ref, :key, :children, :dangerouslySetInnerHTML and name-equivalent namespace/string/symbol spellings as HTML attributes. Dropping the top-level :key/:events is insufficient: these values are inside :attrs. Required correction: enforce the kept tree-space refusal at emit-ui-tree using existing name canonicalization and structured errors; preserve ordinary qualified props. Do not alter Fresco React-space ref/key routing or broaden the test kit. Static code evidence, not an executed reproduction. rf2-a5ara already includes implementation work but is IN_PROGRESS and therefore ineligible for exact reuse; leave its status untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Each forbidden emitted-name slot inside :attrs fails with a structured error before markup, including supported alias key types. Valid title/data-/aria- attributes and separate top-level tree :key/:events controls keep their existing behavior. No new public API.
notes:
Audit PR #10398, 094e778b9290468aef23281de561a2b76730747d: exact defect remains unimplemented. description:

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a

## Worker rules

- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: skills/re-frame2-implementor

Reviewer persona: senior implementor-facing reviewer; treats every spec number, artefact name, API name, fixture name and reply-contract field the skill teaches as a claim to check against spec/ and implementation/*/deps.edn at the frozen tree, and looks hardest at what the two implementor gates do not pin.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The EP index carries none of the worked-example artefact pointers its own design promises, and the only artefact roster is in a non-loaded meta-doc that is already stale  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: self-contract] [size: S]
- Where: skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:31-39 and :69-80 (the two EP index tables); skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/design.md:28 (L1) and :112 (§7); skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/inputs.md:30

- Evidence: Grep `implementation/(core|adapters|machines|routing|flows|http|schemas|ssr|ssr-ring|epoch|resources|fresco)` over the skill returns 2 lines — inputs.md:30 and conformance.md:44 — and 0 in phase-2-impl-order.md (control: conformance.md carries 2, so the instrument sees pointers where they exist). `git ls-files 'implementation/*/deps.edn'` at b60a20abca lists core, adapters/{reagent,reagent-slim,uix,test-react}, machines, routing, flows, http, schemas, ssr, ssr-ring, epoch, resources, fresco (+ test/build-support artefacts); Ownership.md rows 42/59/60/61/63/68 name the Maven artefact per EP. - Action: add a fourth column "Worked example (descriptive, not normative)" to both EP index tables — core for 001/002/006/009/015, `implementation/flows/` for 013, `implementation/schemas|machines|routing|ssr (+ssr-ring)|http|resources|epoch/` for the optional rows, `implementation/adapters/*` (+ `fresco/`) for Views — and correct inputs.md:30 to the same roster. (The order guard scans these lines: a bare `implementation/…` path carries no `009` token, so it cannot trip line_states_foundation_boundary; re-run the gate anyway.)

### 2. Two owner cites in the EP index point the wrong way — `emit-ui-tree` is named the ABI's "producer" (it is its consumer), and the flow-input partition rule is sent to 002 (it lives in 013)  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: cite-integrity] [size: S]

Two sentences; no gate change.

### 3. Two leaves are over the 16 KB ceiling while design.md says three sit inside it and skills/README.md records only phase-2-impl-order.md exempt  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md (whole file), references/conformance.md (whole file); skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/design.md:19 (Pillar 3) and :103 (§6); skills/README.md:258-309 (§Leaf size discipline)

**THE CONVENTION QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE TREE ANSWERS IT IN THE ENFORCING CODE ITSELF.**
`committed-byte-size`'s docstring reads: *"The leaf's size as git stores it: UTF-8 with LF line

convention**, it is written down, and the docstring names precisely the error the mayor made when it
first reported CRLF figures. The LF column of the measurement above is the one that counts; the CRLF
column and the "which convention?" question should both be disregarded.

title: api(schema): {:schema S :boundary? true} replaces the :rf.schema/at-boundary ref; delete Var + 4 mechanisms
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:23:06 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.40 ruling agent (delegated by Mike) from the ruled dossier; parent epic rf2-kuky; discovered-from rf2-kuky.40 (RULED A). Evidence: the dossier is attached verbatim to rf2-kuky.40's notes (DOSSIER ATTACHMENT), with its Codex section carrying the implementation contract. Line numbers were verified at tip 6d513ba07f; between that tip and 13884f326f nothing under `implementation/` moved, but `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md`, `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` were reflowed, so their numbers below are re-measured at 13884f326f. RE-MEASURE EVERYTHING at dispatch tip with `git grep -n -F` (never Bash `grep -iF`, which aborts silently on this machine)._

## Problem

Production enforcement of a `reg-event` `:schema` is spelled as an interceptor that is not an interceptor. A bare `:schema` is a dev-only diagnostic (`validate-event!` sits behind `(if interop/debug-enabled? ...)`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1148,1172`). To keep the check in a release build a handler adds `:interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary]`, and to make that chain entry behave the registrar and router carry four mechanisms plus a public Var:

1. Chain scan at registration: `at-boundary-entry?` / `attaches-validate-at-boundary-interceptor?` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:201-232`).
2. Missing-schema rejection: `reject-at-boundary-without-schema!` (`events.cljc:234-263`, called at `:1008`) raises `:rf.error/at-boundary-missing-schema` when the ref is present and the `:schema` KEY is absent.
3. Dev-side marker predicate: `boundary-guarded-handler?` (`events.cljc:265-284`), read by `router.cljc:2558-2562`; re-scans the AUTHORED chain on every refusal and deliberately ignores a per-frame chain carrying the same id.
4. Registration + re-seed: `register-schema-interceptors!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc:316-344`) registers `{:before ...}` under the `:interceptor` kind at ns load AND again from `init!` after every `clear-all!` (`core.cljc:2799-2803`).
- The Var `validate-at-boundary-interceptor`: `spec.cljc:129` and facade `core.cljc:2115-2126`; manifest `spec/api-manifest.edn:181`, `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1319-1325`; every doc naming it says do not call it and do not put it in a chain (`spec/API.md:565`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:564-569`, `spec/010-Schemas.md:225`). Zero app/tool consumers; `docs/EP/EP-0022-registered-interceptors.md:229` already rules it out.

Three facts make the chain entry a boolean wearing an interceptor's clothes: (1) the `:before` fn returns `ctx` untouched when `(dev-mode?)` (`spec.cljc:160-166`) and only runs its body in a release build; (2) dev validates the ORIGINAL event vector at router step 1 (`router.cljc:790,3076`) while prod validates `(get-coeffect ctx :event)` at its chain position, after per-frame interceptors (prepended at `router.cljc:2405-2407`) and any preceding handler interceptor, so an event-transforming interceptor makes the two builds check different values, and the prod path re-derives the event id from that value and may select a different schema or no metadata; (3) `{:interceptor-overrides {:rf.schema/at-boundary nil}}` removes the check in prod only (`router.cljc:2408-2412`), while dev step 1 still refuses and mechanism 3 still stamps `:rf/boundary-rejected?`. Consumers relying on any of (1)-(3): zero (only `docs/EP/EP-0022:28` pairs the id with overrides; no tool references the id; `tools/story` and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` use overrides generally, in dev, where the override on this id was already inert).

## Target (RULED: rf2-kuky.40 Option A; key name settled as `:boundary?`)

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :ws/handle-message
  {:doc       "Fold one inbound frame into app-db. UNTRUSTED INGRESS"
   :schema    [:cat [:= :ws/handle-message] schema/InboundMessage]
   :boundary? true}                      ; this :schema runs in every build
  (fn handler-ws-handle-message [{:keys [db]} [_ body]] ...))
```

Contract (Codex's, adopted in substance): when `:boundary?` is true, check the ORIGINAL dispatched event vector against the ALREADY-RESOLVED handler's `:schema` (pass the router's resolved metadata in; never re-derive the id from the ctx event) ONCE, at the router's existing step-1 site, BEFORE the interceptor chain, in EVERY build. Dev and prod validate the same value at the same point. No shim: the keyword ref, the Var and the mechanisms are deleted, not deprecated, and the ref and the flag never ship as peers.

Mechanics:
- `:boundary?` joins the `:event` bare-key set (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc:64-72`; an unknown bare key warns `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key`, `:139`) and `EventHandlerMeta` (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:362-370`, hot-zone) as `[:boundary? {:optional true} :boolean]`. The name follows the `?`-boolean precedent already in that vocabulary (`:recordable?`, `:provided?`, `:large?`); `:at-boundary?` was considered and not chosen. Do not put the flag inside the schema value: schema values are opaque to the framework and the flag must be readable without a validator loaded.
- Mechanism 2 becomes a map lookup: `(and (:boundary? meta) (not (contains? meta :schema)))` raises `:rf.error/at-boundary-missing-schema` (keep the error id; the `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2076` row text changes). KEY PRESENCE, not truthiness: `{:schema nil :boundary? true}` and `{:schema false :boundary? true}` register, as today, and the nil/false token is delegated to the backend as an opaque value.
- Mechanism 3 becomes `(true? (:boundary? handler-meta))`. Use the SAME boolean predicate for registration, enforcement and rejection attribution.
- The prod body of `spec.cljc:160-291` moves behind the flag at the step-1 site, still reached through the late-bind seams (`:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn`, `explain-with-registered-fn`, `redact-validation-tags`), stamping `:rf/skip-handler?` and `:rf/boundary-rejected?` exactly as today so everything downstream survives unchanged: outcome `:rejected` (`router.cljc:2754`), the always-on structural record (`:3118-3121`), the `:source :boundary` tag, redaction, SSR's 400 projection (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc`). They key off the marker, not the id.
- Keep the optional-backend contract: no schemas artefact loaded, or an explicitly disabled validator, means no validation. Preserve `run-chain`'s behaviour of still executing interceptors after a refusal so `:after` cleanup runs; retain the tail emission, downstream drain and frame-owner liveness checks; preserve the frame-destroyed continuation checks already in `validate.cljc` (callback code can destroy a frame during validation or explanation). Do NOT route the new always-on branch through the router helper's existing catch-and-pass fallback: a throwing validator must remain a rejection, and a throwing explainer must not reverse that verdict. Share the decision point without keeping every dev diagnostic in production: the dev validation and the ungated backend seams may stay distinct internally.
- Hot path: one `(:boundary? handler-meta)` read per prod dispatch replaces a chain entry on guarded handlers only; negligible; say so in the PR body.

## Deletion list

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc`: the Var at `:129`, `register-schema-interceptors!` `:316-344`, and the `:before` interceptor wrapper (the validation BODY at `:160-291` is relocated, not deleted).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc`: facade Var `:2115-2126`; the `init!` re-seed `:2799-2803`; the remaining docstring mentions (5 ref lines in this file) re-worded.

- Manifest: `spec/api-manifest.edn:181` row and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1319-1325` entry removed; regenerate; `--check` must be green. This is why the bead is ONE PR: the manifest check reds the moment the Var goes without its row.

## Target API (spelled in @registry-introspection.2's grammar)

```clojure
;; before                                   ;; after
(rf.routing/route-ids)                      (keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route}))
(rf.routing/route-meta id)                  (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :route :id id})
(rf.resources/resource-ids)                 (keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :resource}))
(rf.resources/resource-meta id)             (:rf/resource       (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource       :id id}))
(rf.resources/mutation-meta id)             (:rf/mutation       (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :mutation       :id id}))
(rf.resources/scope-resolver-meta id)       (:rf/resource-scope (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource-scope :id id}))
(rf.machines/machines)                      (into {} (filter (fn [[_ m]] (:rf/machine? m))) (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}))  ; keys for ids
(rf.machines/machine-meta id)               (:rf/machine (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :event :id id}))   ; nil unless :rf/machine?
```

The inner-key projection becomes a DOCUMENTED contract, not a helper: a `:resource` / `:mutation` / `:resource-scope` registration carries its spec under `:rf/resource` / `:rf/mutation` / `:rf/resource-scope`; a machine is an `:event` registration with `:rf/machine? true` carrying its spec under `:rf/machine` (both reviewers). Machines stay a filter over `:event` (codex floor); a virtual `:machine` KIND is @registry-introspection.4's ruling, not this bead.

description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Two projection-side surfaces have no consumer after ~200 opportunities:

- `rf/projected-history` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2494-2512`, late-bound through `core_epoch.cljc:258-272` → `re-frame.epoch/projected-history` `epoch.cljc:733-739` → `tool_pair.cljc:2074-2081`, which is literally `(mapv #(projected-record % opts) (state/history-for frame-id))`). Callers outside `docs/`, `spec/` and tests: **0** — the single `tools/` hit is a docstring (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:18`); Pair pages first and projects each selected record (`epoch_egress.cljs:245`). The facade docstring justifies it as protection against a hand-`mapv` "one missed call away from leaking" (`core.cljc:2497-2506`) — a docstring guarding nobody.
- `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:redact-fn f}})` — a fourth, function-shaped projection door: `re-frame.epoch.assembly/apply-redact-fn` (`assembly.cljc:94-122`), invoked only at `tool_pair.cljc:2072`, its state in `epoch/state.cljc:40-43, :60, :78-88, :119-124`, its own warning category `:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` (`capture.cljc:74-79`; `spec/API.md:674`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2132`). Installers outside tests: **0** (all `tools/` and `docs/` hits are prose; `skills/…/privacy-and-elision.md:258` already lists "an epoch-history `:redact-fn` storage hook" under "not part of the API"). It is `comp` wearing a `configure!` key: a forwarder that wants an extra scrub writes `(-> r (rf/projected-record opts) scrub)`.

## Evidence

Counts at tip (`git grep -c`, re-measure): `projected-history` — 17 files non-test, of which code: `core.cljc` 3, `core_epoch.cljc` 3, `late_bind/directory.cljc` 1, `epoch.cljc` 5, `epoch/state.cljc` 1, `tool_pair.cljc` 5, `epoch_egress.cljs` 1 (docstring); test files 9. `apply-redact-fn` — `assembly.cljc:12, :94`, `capture.cljc:75`, `tool_pair.cljc:2072`, `implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs:314-320`, `epoch_jvm_prod_gate_test.clj:358, :382`. `epoch-redact-fn-exception` — 15 files (6 test/probe). `:redact-fn` code sites: `epoch.cljc:84-109, :242, :721`, `assembly.cljc:12, :94-122, :222, :335-337`, `state.cljc` (above), `tool_pair.cljc:1405, :1924, :1966, :2024, :2072`, `core_epoch.cljc:246-249`, `late_bind/directory.cljc:861`, `test_support.cljc:445`, `privacy.cljc:231`. (The `redact-fn` locals in `cofx.cljc:611-627`, `spec.cljc:248-277` and `resources/classification.cljc:629-640` are the schema validation-tag redactor — a different hook, NOT in scope.)

## Target API

```clojure
;; whole ring — before                      ;; after (ordinary composition)
(rf/projected-history f opts)                (mapv #(rf/projected-record % opts) (rf/epoch-history f))

;; post-hoc scrub — before
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:redact-fn scrub}})   ; global, runs inside projected-record, own warning category
;; after — at the forwarder / sink
(-> r (rf/projected-record opts) scrub)
```

`:epoch-history` keeps `:depth` and `:trace-events-keep`; an `:redact-fn` key is UNKNOWN (per the `configure!` unknown-key posture the boot/adapter area is ruling on; until then it is silently dropped like any other unknown sub-key — say so in the PR). `projected-record` (the record-level door) is UNCHANGED by this bead; its epoch-side fate belongs to `@trace-epoch.n` and egress.5.

## Corroboration

`projected-history`: two-reviewer — codex `trace-and-epoch-inspection.md` §Compose selection with projection ("a `mapv` over the full history, so it can leave the supported public surface in favor of ordinary composition") and `fable-reread-2.md` ("retire the whole-history convenience from the supported surface"). `:redact-fn`: one-reviewer with codex's qualified support — "defensible given the measured absence of application installers, but ordinary composition is not automatically equivalent to a globally installed post-projection transform. Its current throwing behavior falls back to built-in output. If removed, explicitly update each affected egress boundary and document that policy; do not change raw replay storage." The affected boundary is exactly one (`tool_pair.cljc:2072`); raw storage is untouched by construction.

## Deletion list

- `core.cljc:2494-2512` (`projected-history` re-export + docstring); rewrite the `projected-record` docstring at :2480-2493 to show the `mapv` composition.
- `core_epoch.cljc:258-272` (`defwrapper projected-history`).
- `epoch.cljc:733-739` and the late-bind registration `:809`; docstring lines :67, :84-109 (`:redact-fn` contract), :242, :721.
- `tool_pair.cljc:2074-2081` (`projected-history`); `:2072` (`apply-redact-fn` call — `projected-record` returns `built-in-projected-record` directly); comment lines :1405, :1924, :1966, :2024.
- `assembly.cljc:94-122` (`apply-redact-fn`) and the step-3 line :12; keep `:rf.epoch/redacted-modified-paths-count` (computed from the projection, :335-337 — rewrite the comment, the count is not redact-fn-derived).
- `state.cljc:40-43` (`:redact-fn nil` default), :60, :78-88 (validation arm), :119-124 (`redact-fn` reader).
- `capture.cljc:74-79` (warning catalogue entry `:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception`).
- `late_bind/directory.cljc:879-882` (`:epoch/projected-history` row); :861 description text (drop `:redact-fn`).
- `implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs:305-320` (the `apply-redact-fn` production-elision sentinel row) and the matching rows in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs` (3 hits).
- Tests: `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_redact_fn_test.clj`, `epoch_redact_fn_projection_test.clj` (delete); `epoch_jvm_prod_gate_test.clj:358-382` (the redact-fn leg); `epoch_test.clj` (1 hit); `error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj` (the warning row); `test_support.cljc:445` reset-hook comment; the 9 `projected-history` test files (re-measure with `git grep -l projected-history -- '*test*'`).

## Consumers to migrate

Code: none (0 callers, 0 installers). Prose that names the surfaces: `epoch_egress.cljs:18, :91-96, :181, :229, :232`; `descriptors_data.cljs:513` (regenerate `tool-descriptors.edn`, `clojure -M:gen --check`); `dispatch.cljs:409`; `snapshot.cljs:115`; `trace_window.cljs:61`; `watch_epochs.cljs:61`; preload `runtime.cljs:1561, :1680`; `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md:387` (drop "or `(rf/projected-history frame-id)` for the whole ring").

notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): recorded 2026-07-28 07:48 AUSEST from ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, reconciled; the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD).

DECISION, in three parts:
(1) VERIFICATION-FIRST SEQUENCING STANDS, but the canary-by-tag route is REJECTED as the verification instrument (Codex position, adopted). Mike's authoritative act is the zero-mutation one: verify io.github.day8 via Clojars' self-service GitHub-org proof (see MIKE'S ACT below), optionally glancing at day8's standing from his logged-in account or asking Clojars support as belt-and-braces.
(2) RULED FALLBACK GROUP if day8 is blocked (and the evidence below says it is): io.github.day8 for ALL 18 Maven coordinates, moved in ONE sequenced rename campaign BEFORE anything publishes.
(3) NO-TAG RULE: NO v*, story-v*, xray-v*, or machines-viz-v* tag is pushed until this bead resolves (io.github.day8 badge confirmed + rename campaign merged + lockstep/preflight/release-DAG gates green on the new coordinates). This is STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut-time checklist, ahead of its existing step 1 (credentials); rf2-2ii52 step 3 (manual first publish of mcp-base/story-mcp) is equally blocked on it.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMITS (three independent sources; two re-verified from primary sources 2026-07-28):
- The 2026-05-13 403 on day8/de-dupe's tag-triggered publish — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects" — is real but was a DIFFERENT project path; on its own it is suggestive, not conclusive (the bead itself warns against inferring from it alone).
- Clojars' Verified Group Names wiki (fetched 2026-07-28): since 2021-04-18 "creating new libraries in non-verified groups will be disabled", while "the group does not need to be verified for new versions" of EXISTING libraries. Bare `day8` is neither reverse-domain nor a githost-org pattern, so it is STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE — there is no route to a verified bare day8, and seeking a policy exception would couple every release to an exception Clojars explicitly designed away.
- clojars.org/users/mikethompson (fetched 2026-07-28): `day8` is listed WITHOUT the verified badge; only net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson carry it. Codex traced the badge to find-group-verification in clojars-web's web/user.clj (not cosmetic) and the enforcement to check-group+project in db.clj: an unverified group is accepted ONLY when that exact group/artifact pair already exists; a new artifact is rejected as group-non-verified.
- All 18 intended day8/* coordinates 404 on Clojars (re-verified 2026-07-27, per-coordinate) — every one is a NEW project as far as Clojars is concerned, so every one enters the rejected branch. The day8 group page returning 200 with mikethompson permitted proves only maintenance rights over existing projects, not creation rights.
- LIMIT: what stays unobservable read-only is Mike's account-side view and any bespoke admin exception. That residual is why this bead stays with Mike — but it is small, and it does not justify a canary.

VERIFICATION ROUTES WEIGHED (canary trade-offs recorded):
- (a) Account/settings check or asking Clojars admins: zero-risk, zero-mutation. Fine as belt-and-braces; not required given (c).
- (b) Canary publish by pushing the ready machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha tag: REJECTED as a probe. A 403 merely re-demonstrates documented policy at the cost of a burned tag-push cycle; a surprise success is an IMMUTABLE public act that permanently pins machines-viz to day8/* — either splitting the family when the rest moves, or accidentally committing the whole family to an unverifiable legacy group. Never use an immutable registry operation to learn an observable fact; if state might have changed, re-read the profile/API or ask support instead. (The primary analysis's "nothing is wasted on success" framing undercounts this: success is exactly the outcome that forecloses the group decision.)
- (c) The act that actually advances things — verify io.github.day8 NOW: create the empty public repo github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group while logged in as mikethompson, confirm the badge appears. Cheap, self-service, and harmless even in the unlikely event day8 turns out grandfathered (verifying a group publishes nothing). It doubles as the authoritative test: Clojars' own flow granting io.github.day8 while day8 stays unverified closes the question.

FALLBACK GROUP CHOICE (io.github.day8), alternatives weighed:
- io.github.day8 — CHOSEN. GitHub-org-verifiable self-service; matches the existing in-repo precedent io.github.day8/re-frame2-template; expresses the durable owner users already see (the day8 GitHub org).
- com.github.day8 — the verification flow verifies both com. and io. simultaneously, but io. is the cleaner match to the existing precedent. Publish under ONE only — Clojars itself warns that the same library under two group IDs can put both on a classpath.
- au.com.day8 — DNS-TXT-verifiable via day8.com.au; defensible if Day8 deliberately wants DNS (not GitHub) as the permanent package identity, but it adds a separate DNS proof and stewardship path, has zero consumer precedent, and buys no ergonomics.
- net.clojars.mikethompson — already verified and usable today, but makes organisation-owned libraries look personally owned. Rejected.
- Policy exception for bare day8 — structurally impossible (not reverse-domain) and bad posture even if grantable. Rejected.

WHY DECIDE BEFORE FIRST PUBLISH (irreversibility): Clojars has no yank; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is immutable. Any rename AFTER a first publish leaves permanently orphaned day8/* coordinates and creates the two-groups-one-library classpath hazard. The current all-404 state — pre-alpha, zero consumers — is the cheapest this move will ever be.

- :clein/build :lib in all 18 publishable deps.edn (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), plus the internal cross-artefact dependency maps the :local/root rewrite resolves (31 in-repo coordinates inventoried by the lockstep gate).

- Credentials: the planned group-scoped reusable Clojars deploy token must be scoped to io.github.day8, not day8 (rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist step 1 wording changes accordingly).
- EXPLICIT NON-SCOPE (Clojars documents that the Maven group does not constrain Clojure namespaces): NO Clojure namespace renames, NO repo URL changes, NO npm @day8 scope change.

INTERACTIONS: this bead is now STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut checklist (cross-ref appended there) — its steps 3 (404 re-probe: probe the NEW coordinates), 4/6 (PR #7167 re-cut) and 1 (token group scope) all shift under this ruling. rf2-2ii52's remaining step 3 (manual first publish per release-machines-viz.yml's header protocol) proceeds only after this resolves, on io.github.day8 coordinates.

RUNBOOK CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-28): Codex second-opinion review of the operator runbook (ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md, written 2026-07-28 16:36 AUSEST) CONCURS with the morning RULING on every decision point — io.github.day8 destination, canary-by-tag rejected, no-tag rule, verification-first sequencing, and the group-alternatives weighing all match. No contradictions; this is a consolidation, not a re-ruling. It adds the following NEW verified mechanics the ruling did not yet carry. The dossier file is deleted after this note — this note is the canonical record of its Codex section.

(1) VERIFY-FORM MECHANICS (verified against clojars-web verification.clj, 2026-07-28): the clojars.org/verify/group flow's GitHub/GitLab repository section takes the FULL proof-repo URL (https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson) — the form does NOT ask for the group name. It accepts exactly https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<clojars-user>, checks the public repo exists, and creates/verifies BOTH com.github.day8 AND io.github.day8 in one act. Publish under io.github.day8 as the ONE public Maven identity (per the ruling; never both). KEEP THE PROOF REPO PUBLIC PERMANENTLY — it is the standing evidence of org control, not a one-shot token. (As of the 2026-07-28 check, github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson returned 404 — the verification act has not yet happened.)

(2) TOKEN ORDER (inserts a step between MIKE'S ACT and the rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist's credentials step): create or replace the CI deploy token scoped to io.github.day8 only AFTER verification — Clojars does not allow a group-scoped token before the group exists (Deploy-Tokens wiki, Scoping). Sequence: badge confirmed -> mint io.github.day8-scoped token -> cut checklist step 1 (credentials) proceeds with that token, never a bare-day8-scoped one.

(3) ENFORCEMENT CONFIRMATION: current clojars-web db.clj check-group+project structurally confirms the ruling's reading — it first accepts an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair, then rejects a NEW artifact when the group has no verification record. Existing day8 projects therefore do NOT grandfather any new day8/re-frame2-* artifact.

(4) CAMPAIGN COMPLETION CRITERION (tightens the ruling's "gates green" close condition): a hand-written file roster is NOT a safe completion criterion — an exact-token scan (2026-07-28 snapshot) found ~428 candidate references to the 18 published coordinates across hundreds of tracked files, and the repo is still moving, so the count itself must not be relied on. Re-cut any staged documentation change (PR #7167) against the new group from the same structural inventory.

(5) COORDINATE-SPECIFIC FENCE (sharpens the ruling's explicit non-scope): NO repository-wide day8 -> io.github.day8 text replacement. **The guard that actually works here is mechanical rather than verbal: derive the claim from the
`blocks` edges at the moment of writing it, and put the derivation's qualifier INTO the sentence** —
"of the N available today" — so the sentence cannot be read outside the scope it was measured in.
## MAYOR COUNT — re-measured 2026-09-22, and the figure everyone was quoting was STALE

**This bead now roots ALL NINE held beads — 9 of 9, not "8 of 11".** Re-measured this pass over the
full export at trunk `a36cbcb5a6`, walking `blocks` edges transitively to roots and discarding
closed blockers: 48 non-terminal issues, of which **9** carry an open blocker and **39** are
dispatchable on that axis. Root tally: `rf2-uelji` **9**, `rf2-pdbe` 7, `rf2-pv7p` 1 (items with two
roots are counted under each). Controls: a nonexistent id roots 0, and the held total equals the
tally's own denominator.

**BOTH halves of the old figure had drifted, in opposite directions, which is why nobody noticed.**
The backlog shrank 11 → 9 as beads closed, and this bead's share grew 8 → 9 as the last
independently-blocked items cleared. So the number went on looking plausible while the claim it
encoded — *most but not all* — became *all*. A figure that moves in two directions at once stays
believable longest.

**HOW THE STALE FIGURE SURVIVED, recorded because the mechanism is the point:** it was restated in
every mayor report for a session without being re-derived once, each restatement reading as
corroboration of the last. `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` §5 names exactly this — *a conclusion
you keep restating is a rule you are enforcing, and your own last report is not among the things the
reread loop rereads* — so nothing brought it round. The discharging question it prescribes is
whether you can state the check you made THIS pass; until this one, the honest answer was no.

**A SECOND INSTRUMENT DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME ACT, worth knowing before anyone re-runs this.** The
first attempt at this census read **0 held beads** — a reassuring answer, and entirely false. It
assumed dependencies were their own `_type == "dependency"` records in `.beads/issues.jsonl`; they
are not. There are exactly two record types in the export, `issue` (1974) and `memory` (1030), and
edges live on the ISSUE record in a `dependencies` array shaped
`{issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by, metadata}`, where `depends_on_id` BLOCKS
`issue_id`. A census keyed on the wrong record type finds nothing, reports a clean board, and the
control passes because a nonexistent id also reads 0. Read the shape before counting.

**Dependency-type vocabulary, with the question each answer belongs to** — because a bare list of
these is what went stale last time. Across the WHOLE export: `discovered-from` 741, `parent-child`
647, `blocks` 301, `related` 91, `relates-to` 61, `duplicates` 2. Restricted to NON-TERMINAL issues:
`blocks` 33, `discovered-from` 22, `parent-child` 13, `relates-to` 1 — and `related` and `duplicates`
read 0 there, so a non-terminal census cannot see those two types at all and is not wrong for
omitting them. Any figure quoted from this paragraph must carry its scope.

**Nothing here changes what this bead needs**, which is unchanged and still only the operator's:
create the empty public repo `day8/clojars-mikethompson` and paste its URL at
`clojars.org/verify/group`. What changes is the cost of not doing it — it is now the sole root of
every held item on the board.

description:
STEP 2 of a two-step ruling (delegated by Mike, ruled 2026-09-23 — see the `== RULING` note on this bead for the full reasoning and the preserved dossier + Codex review). BLOCKED BY rf2-x8oz5 (step 1: the framework emits `:rf.http/issued` and numbers anonymous issuances); dispatch this bead only after rf2-x8oz5 has MERGED. The pre-ruling description — the original A design and the seven "why it is heuristic" items — is preserved verbatim in the `== PRIOR DESCRIPTION` note; items 1-3 there are answered by rf2-x8oz5, items 4-6 survive as the notes at the end of this description, item 7 was closed by rf2-st7j0 (PR #10010).

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## What this feature is

The 019 F.1 / F-C2 "wire-boundary" hero record for `:rf.http/managed` (`tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:569-650`). Today (after rf2-y8doi.18, ruled B) the Epoch panel's managed-HTTP record truthfully says only `◦ ISSUED` — `http-adapter` sets `:phase`, `:wire`, `:res`, `:duration-ms`, `:http-status` to nil BY CONSTRUCTION (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:661-714`), because every HTTP row after issuance is emitted outside the issuing run's scope and lands under `[nil :ungrouped]` or in another bundle (see the prior description's "Why it cannot land in the issuing bundle" — still true, still verify at your trunk). This bead makes the record show the request's real outcome — `✓ OK 200 · elapsed 82ms`, `✗ ERROR 500 · 2 attempts`, `◌ CANCELLED :actor-destroyed`, `STALE (superseded)`, or `◦ ISSUED · no completion in this capture` — by joining the runtime's terminal row to the record across the WHOLE trace buffer on an EXACT key.

## The key (exact, after rf2-x8oz5)

Every terminal HTTP row already carries the attempt identity `[:rf.work/http logical-id issuance attempt]` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:84-98`): `:rf.http/replied` as `:rf.reply/work-id` (`transport.cljc:557`), `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` as `:rf.reply/work-id` plus `:rf.reply/carried` (superseded) / `:rf.reply/current` (superseder) (`transport.cljc:622-635`), `:rf.http/aborted` and the failure kinds as `:work/id` (`:775`, `:919`). After rf2-x8oz5 the issuing bundle carries an `:rf.http/issued` row (in `:other`, with the run's dispatch-id) whose `:rf.reply/work-id` is `[:rf.work/http logical-id issuance 1]`, and anonymous requests no longer all read issuance 1. The join key is the issued row's FRAME plus `(subvec work-id 0 3)`; work ids are frame-local (`spec/Managed-Effects.md:196`), so the frame is part of the key.

## Mechanism

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_subs.cljs:59-72` — `:rf.xray/managed-fx-for-focused-event` adds `[:rf.xray/trace-buffer]` as a composite input (the Resources composite already does exactly this).
- Build ONE index per recompute, not one scan per record: pre-filter the buffer to HTTP reply-envelope rows with `reply_envelope/reply-trace-op?`, then `{[frame (subvec work-id 0 3)] -> rows sorted by :id}`; for a stale row index the CARRIED id, never the current one.
- Pair each HTTP `:rf.fx/handled` record with the bundle's `:rf.http/issued` rows by ORDINAL over the monotonic trace `:id` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:713`): the issued row is emitted inside the fx handler and `fx.cljc:1273` emits `:rf.fx/handled` after the handler returns, so issued(k) precedes handled(k). A handled row with no issued row (a capture from before rf2-x8oz5, a skipped/overridden effect) stays `ISSUED` with no join and no error.
- Terminal row = the FIRST index row with `:id` greater than the issued row's whose `phase-of` is `:completed` or `:stale-suppressed` and whose key matches. Canonical rows (`:rf.http/replied`, `:rf.http/stale-suppressed`) take precedence over `:rf.http/aborted` (also `:completed` in the op table, `reply_envelope.cljc:426`, and it fires at the SUPERSEDED attempt's id inside the SUPERSEDER's bundle — rf2-n3sx9). Do NOT take "the latest by `:time`" — a named id is legitimately reused (`[x 1 1]` then `[x 1 1]` after eviction) and "latest" hands the earlier record the later outcome.
- Read the status through `reply_envelope/work-event-row` (`:562-698`), which already projects every HTTP completion op to `{:phase :completed :status :ok|:error|:cancelled|:stale ...}`. Elapsed = `(:time terminal) - (:time issued)` — one clock (`trace.cljc:713`); label it ELAPSED (it includes retry backoff); never subtract `:completed-at` (epoch ms) from trace time. Attempts = the terminal row's `:attempt` (retry rows carry no work-id and are not joined). `:http-status` reads `[:meta :status]` on ok and `[:error :status]` on 4xx/5xx (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:552-554`). RESPONSE shows the elided summary the row carries — the elision walker's output is the ceiling, and under `:sensitive?` it is the `:rf/redacted` sentinel.
- Reply link `→ reply ↗`: the `:source :http` bundle whose event's reply map carries the same `:rf.reply/work-id` (rf2-st7j0's matcher reads reply maps off event args — the model). Delivered replies only: a stale row has none; an actor-destroy abort with an OBSOLETE target is stale (no link), one with a LIVE ordinary target is delivered as `:cancelled` (link) — `transport.cljc:789-813`.
- No terminal row in the buffer -> `ISSUED · no completion in this capture`. Never "in flight": the buffer cannot separate pending from aged-out, and the in-flight registry is an atom, not runtime-db — do not read it.
- Taxonomy: the framework's closed reply statuses as `work-event-row` projects them (`:ok :error :cancelled :stale`) plus `:issued`; `common-record` (~:452-484) stops folding a cancel into `:error`; `status-pill` gains the glyphs/colours for cancelled and stale; `timing_waterfall.cljc` may draw `:issued -> :elapsed` bars (019:616-618) once elapsed exists.
- Flip `tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:610-650` from designed-not-built to built for the HTTP record, in the same PR (not hot-zone; rf2-y8doi.46 recorded the B-time state and is closed).

## Fence (files)

rf2-y8doi.18's seven: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc`, `.../panels/managed_fx_template.cljs`, `.../panels/managed_fx_subs.cljs` (code this time), `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/chart/timing_waterfall.cljc`, `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc`, `.../panels/managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs`, `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/chart/timing_waterfall_cljs_test.cljc`; plus `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc` (+ its `reply_envelope_cljs_test.cljc`) only if `work-event-row` needs widening; plus `tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md`. NO `implementation/` change — the producer is correct after rf2-x8oz5. Hot zone: none.

## Acceptance bar (RED first, then GREEN; fixtures DERIVED FROM THE PRODUCER per rf2-y8doi.28's model — capture real rows from the http artefact after rf2-x8oz5, never hand-build; quote every RED with its count)

(a) two overlapping ANONYMOUS requests of one event-id completing in REVERSE order -> each record reads its OWN status and elapsed (control: before the join both read `ISSUED`). (b) named request, 500 retried once -> `ERROR 500 · 2 attempts`, elapsed spanning both attempts. (c) actor-destroy with an obsolete target -> stale/cancelled, NO reply link; actor-destroy with a live target -> `CANCELLED` WITH a reply link. (d) supersession -> the superseded record reads its stale status off the CARRIED id, the superseder reads `OK`; neither takes the other's row. (e) the rf2-n3sx9 residue: an explicit `[:rf.http/managed-abort :x]` beside a same-id re-issue in ONE bundle -> the two records resolve by work-id (control: today they are byte-identical to the already-aborted-signal case). (f) issued row present, no terminal row -> `ISSUED · no completion in this capture`. (g) terminal row present, issued row aged out of the ring -> the record stays unattributed. (h) a pre-rf2-x8oz5 capture (handled row, no issued row) -> `ISSUED`, no join, no error. (i) two HTTP effects in one run pair to their own issued rows by ordinal. (j) a resource row / a nonsense op never joins an HTTP record (control both ways). Plus the existing helpers/template suites green with identical counts red and green.

## Gates (by path — say which lane compiled the changed forms)

- `.cljc` files (`managed_fx_helpers.cljc`, `reply_envelope.cljc`, `timing_waterfall.cljc`): state which reader branch each changed form sits in. Forms outside any `#?(...)` are graded by BOTH `tools/xray` `clojure -M:test` and `npm run test:cljs`; a form inside `#?(:cljs ...)` is graded by `npm run test:cljs` ALONE — a JVM green is not evidence about it (CLAUDE.md § Build & Test).
- `.cljs` files (`managed_fx_template.cljs`, `managed_fx_subs.cljs`, `*_cljs_test.cljs`): `npm run test:cljs` (namespaces ending `-cljs-test`); any `-dom-cljs-test` namespace touched -> `npm run test:browser`. The shadow-cljs lane is a MACHINE-WIDE EXCLUSIVE — ask the mayor for it, take it once, release it.
- `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` for the xray JVM roster; clj-kondo WITHOUT `--fail-level error` (instrument item (w)).
- 019 edit: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (`tools/*/spec` is in its roots; `mkdocs` stages no `tools/` tree, so do not nominate it).
- Surface classifier: hand `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` PATHS, never revisions.

## Pins that legitimately redden

`managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` assertions that `http-adapter` leaves `:phase`/`:wire`/`:res`/`:duration-ms`/`:http-status` nil by construction, on fixtures that now carry a terminal row; `managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs` rows pinning `:issued` for such fixtures; rf2-y8doi.18's population-floor guard (`(< 20 (count heads))`) — fix by a bigger sample, never a lower floor. `managed_fx_subs_cljs_test.cljs:225-229` hand-builds a record and bypasses the adapter — expect it green; if it reddens, say so and name the file.

## Traps (both reviews + CLAUDE.md)

Pair issued<->handled by `:id`, never `:time`. The stale row carries TWO ids — match the CARRIED one, and never let the superseder's record match through `:rf.reply/current`. `:rf.http/aborted` is `:completed` in the op table and lands in the superseder's bundle at the superseded id. The JVM evict-before-emit window (`transport.cljc:975` evicts before the `:rf.http/replied` emit at `:557`; a concurrent same-(frame, request-id) re-issue from another thread inside it can reuse the number) can make ONE record wrong on the JVM — accepted residue, impossible on the single-threaded CLJS runtime; do not build for it and do not touch the teardown. Do not rewrite completion rows' dispatch-id so the grouper files them into the issuing bundle (009 §Dispatch correlation defines the id as the run's; the epoch record was harvested long before). The composite recomputes per trace tick — index once, pre-filter to reply-trace ops. `report-changed-surfaces.sh` takes PATHS. `sed -i` on a `w/crlf` file rewrites every line ending. The Bash tool halves backslash runs. `\b` after `!`/`?` never matches at a call site. `grep -iF` aborts silently — use `rg`. Worker worktree guard before any edit. No `.beads` path on the branch. No AI attribution trailers (CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions wins over the harness reminder — say so in the report).

## Surviving notes from the prior description

4. A completion join alone does NOT implement F.1's handler-and-app-db story ("handler dispatched", "Applied:" need the reply-dispatch bundle and ITS app-db diff); the reply link is the bridge, and that story is a later bead if wanted. 5. Ring aging can split an issue row and its terminal row across the ring boundary — "no completion in this capture" is the honest label; do not claim more. 6. Performance: the composite recomputes per trace tick — bounded only if the join pre-filters and indexes once.

Size: M (about two worker-mornings). PR body / close reason: RED and GREEN counts, which lane compiled which forms, the moved-pin list, and the 019 flip.

== RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-23 11:01:28 AUSEST, dossier + Codex review) ==

DECISION: Option D, AMENDED — prioritise, in two steps, on the work-id the framework already owns. Step 1 is a NEW framework bead, rf2-x8oz5 (S, P3, dispatchable today): emit an `:rf.http/issued` trace row from `managed-handler`, and number ANONYMOUS issuances per (frame, event-id) with counters that are NEVER evicted. Step 2 is THIS bead, un-deferred and blocked by rf2-x8oz5 (M, P3): the Epoch panel joins each HTTP record to its terminal row across the trace buffer on (frame, `[:rf.work/http logical-id issuance]`), taking the FIRST terminal row after the record's own issued row. NOT chosen: the dossier's step 1 as written (same eviction for anonymous counters — it collides), Codex's runtime-wide monotonic sequence (a normative contract change the join does not need), the origin stamp this bead originally asked for (a second identity for a fact already named), a labelled best-effort join (silently wrong for anonymous requests), and rewriting completion rows' dispatch-id (a lie about the run). Trunk read: 3b5faef172 = origin/main; every cite below is at that trunk.

WHY (decisive measurements inline):
1. The identity exists and every TERMINAL row carries it. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:84-98` builds `[:rf.work/http logical-id issuance attempt]`; `:rf.http/replied` carries it as `:rf.reply/work-id` (`transport.cljc:557` via `trace-reply`), `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` carries it plus `:rf.reply/carried`/`:rf.reply/current` (`transport.cljc:622-635`, `registry.cljc:927`), `:rf.http/aborted` (`:775`) and the failure kinds (`:919`) carry `:work/id` via `self-identify` (`:876`). The issue side carries none: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1273-1278` tags `:rf.fx/handled` with `{:rf.fx/id :rf.fx/args :frame}` only.
2. No HTTP issuance row exists. 17 `rf.trace/emit!`/`emit-error!` sites under `implementation/http/src` (rg), none an issuance; `:rf.http/issued` reads 0 in source (1 tree-wide hit, a hypothetical in a comment at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/success_path_trigger_handler_test.clj:468`); `spec/Managed-Effects.md:234` REQUIRES "issuance/start (with `:work/id`, frame, owner/cause, target summary)"; resources and mutations emit one (`reply_envelope.cljc:387-398` lists `:rf.resource/work-started`, `:rf.mutation/started` under `:issued`, and records HTTP as having none).
3. The anonymous collision is real and by construction. `registry.cljc:527-529`: `(if (nil? request-id) 1 ...)`; `reply.cljc:97`: anonymous `logical-id` = `(first origin-event)`. Two anonymous requests of one event-id in one frame therefore share `[:rf.work/http :ev 1 1]` on every row. (The dossier's 83%-anonymous census was reproduced by neither reviewer nor by me and is NOT load-bearing — the collision stands at source whatever the frequency.)
4. Codex's counterexample against the dossier's allocator is CORRECT, verified by reading `registry.cljc:556-563`: `evict-issuance-on-completion!` is a compare-and-drop `(if (= issuance (get counters k)) (dissoc counters k) counters)` that protects only a supersession's NEWER successor. Anonymous siblings a=1, b=2 with b finishing first evict the counter and the next request reads 1 while a is live: `[1 2 1]`.
