title: Unit-test pruning: story-testbeds
description:
Apply the exact requested pruning prompt recursively to tools/story/testbeds. This is a distinct worker cluster under rf2-0wcq5. Production code remains unchanged except temporary hash-verified fault plants. Push a draft test-only PR, babysit all latest-head checks to green, then mark ready. A measured no-op or unexecuted-file report is valid; do not manufacture changes.

Simplify the unit tests under tools/story/testbeds. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside tools/story/testbeds. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
tools/story/testbeds to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in tools/story/testbeds; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If tools/story/testbeds plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside tools/story/testbeds that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Make an absent app-db path unchecked: a reg-app-schema path schema constrains a value only when its path exists, and a first registration checks a present value
description:
## Ruling

A path schema registered with `reg-app-schema` constrains the value at its path only when that path EXISTS in the app-db being checked. An absent path (a missing key anywhere along it, as `(get-in db path ::absent)` sees it) is not checked. A present value, `nil` included, is checked exactly as today. Whether a key must exist is said by an enclosing schema, usually the root `[]`, with required map entries, the way Malli's `:map` works: `(rf/reg-app-schema [] [:map [:cart CartSchema]])` restores presence for exactly the keys it names. A first registration also checks a live value that is present and emits `:rf.schema/violation`, as a re-registration with a changed schema already does; every registration skips an absent value. This is option B of the decision; option A (today) and option C are rejected below.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. `spec/010-Schemas.md:158` checks an absent slice "on every commit, so an unseeded non-nullable path still rejects every write (which is why a slice that boots empty takes `[:maybe …]`)". `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:836-843` (`unchanged-slice?`) implements it: an absent slice is never "unchanged", and the walk then validates plain `(get-in db registered-path)` (`validate.cljc:948`), which is `nil`. So two bare non-nullable slices seeded by separate events veto each other forever in a dev build (every seed is rejected and app-db never leaves `{}`), while a release build, which elides the check, boots fine. `:failing-id` blames whichever event committed, for a slice it never wrote.
2. Every multi-slice app in the repo has already switched the check off with `[:maybe …]` to get through that window: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs` (23 of 23 paths), `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/schema.cljs` (5 of 5), `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs:153-156` (4 of 4). So the typo protection option A offers (a non-nullable registration over a misspelt path rejects loudly) is already gone in practice, and `:maybe` no longer means "may be nil".
3. A first registration emits nothing because `maybe-emit-schema-violation!` is gated on `prior-registered?` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:536-538`). With changed-slice skipping, a non-conforming value already present at a newly registered path can go unreported indefinitely. Under A that gate cannot be lifted cleanly (every unseeded non-nullable path would report against `nil`); under this ruling it can.

Rejected:

- A, keep presence in every path schema: a dev-only check stops a correct app from booting and disagrees with production about whether it works, and it forces a `[:maybe …]` idiom that weakens every schema for the life of the app.
- C, this ruling plus a per-path `{:required? true}` registration flag: a second vocabulary for what a root `[]` schema already says, and the flag lives in registration metadata outside the schema digest (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/digest.cljc:132-143`), so a presence change would be invisible to the SSR and epoch drift checks.
- A stateful "never written" variant (check a slice once it has ever been present): needs per-path history and makes restore and replace ambiguous.
- An absent-path warning, or an Xray "registered, no value" affordance: not needed to ship this; no runtime nag.

Supersedes: the absent-slice clause and the "A first registration emits no violation" sentence at `spec/010-Schemas.md:158`, and "The first registration of a path emits nothing" at `spec/010-Schemas.md:829`. Both are choices recorded on rf2-mn2ht.14 (commit 511e96991f), which kept absent slices checked "so the boot-window behaviour is unchanged" pending this ruling and did not take the optional first-registration extension. The changed-slice skip itself, from that bead, stays.

## Work

Code, `implementation/schemas/`:

- `src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:836-843`: the skip becomes "absent in the candidate, OR present and `identical?` to db-before". Apply the absent skip in EVERY arity of `validate-app-schema!`: today the filter runs only when `db-before` is supplied (`validate.cljc:941-943`), so the 1- to 4-arities would still check absent paths. Update the docstrings at `:836-839` and `:881-890` ("an absent slice on every call. Without db-before every entry is checked"). The docstring at `:505-506` uses "seventeen red lines … ending `got nil`" (the boot-window incident) as its example; reword it.
- `src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:513-574` (`maybe-emit-schema-violation!`) and its call at `:648-657`: drop the `prior-registered?` gate for a PRESENT live value, so a first registration checks it and emits `:rf.schema/violation` (`:warning`, `:logged-and-skipped`, the existing redaction posture unchanged). Skip an absent live value on every registration (sentinel `get-in`, not the plain `get-in` at `:540-541`). Keep an unchanged re-registration silent (same token, `nil` to `nil` included). Decide what `:pre-reload-schema` carries on a first registration, where there is no prior declaration, and say so in the docstring.

Tool walks, so commit, restore, replace and seed checks give one answer:

title: Conformance: grade or drop the five expectation channels that no runner grades
description:
The conformance runners let five expectation channels pass ungraded. A fixture states the claim, the README credits the fixture with it, and no runner ever checks it. That is a gate passing on input it cannot see. This was found by a static read at trunk 89517e8f54; whether the reference would pass these expectations once they are graded is unknown until it is run.

## The five channels

| Fixture | Expectation | Why nothing grades it |
|---|---|---|
| `frame-lifecycle.edn` | `:on-destroy-emissions`, `:on-destroy-effects` (the destroy half of the fixture) | The runner delegates them by name to "the frame-lifecycle / destroy runners" (runner ~:247). Those runners don't exist, and neither key appears anywhere else in `implementation/`. |
| `sub-chain.edn` | `:sub-graph-topology` (the "static dependency topology" its README row advertises) | Same delegation. Spec-Schemas declares the key, but no code reads it. The `:derivation-graph` fixtures may already cover the topology. |
| `spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn` | `:trace-not-emitted`: the timer is never scheduled or fired, and the machine never reaches `:ready` | Delegated to the SSR runner. That runner only loads files whose names start with `ssr-`, so it never loads this one. |
| 9 machine fixtures, e.g. `after-single-delay.edn`, `always-single-microstep.edn` | `:expect-trace` (19 call records) and `:expect-microsteps` (4): the timer and microstep claims the README credits these fixtures with | These are call-record keys. Neither `:machine-transition` realiser reads them (core runner ~:940-969; machines runner ~:130-150), and nothing checks call-record keys. |
| `ssr-redirect.edn` | `:ssr/request-result {:html :absent :payload :absent}` ("redirect truncates the body") | The SSR matcher builds its ACTUAL value as `{:response … :html :absent :payload :absent}` (`ssr_conformance_test.clj:879-881`), so those slots always match. The runner's own comment assigns HTML truncation to `ssr-end-to-end-test` and the ring tests (~:869-872). |

## Change

For each channel, either the shared runner grades it or the fixture drops the claim. Nothing is delegated by name to a runner that doesn't load it.

If grading shows the reference failing an expectation, decide case by case and record the reason: fix the reference, or correct the fixture.

Expect to touch the shared runner, about 13 fixtures, and the README rows. No hot zone.

## Related

The decision dossier `conformance-fixture-grammar.md` proposes one closed, schema-checked fixture grammar with one matcher per expectation key. That would stop this class of gap recurring, and its bead may already be filed under the `dossier-ruling` label. This bead is the immediate correctness fix and stands whatever that ruling says. If the grammar bead is filed, sequence this one FIRST, or have the grammar bead carry these per-channel decisions.

The same dossier also found that the published fixture schema in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (SA-3) rejects about 112 of 241 fixtures. That came from a Python approximation, not a Malli run, and it belongs to the grammar work rather than to this bead.

Supporting detail, local to this machine only: `C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\ai\decisions\conformance-fixture-grammar.md`. It may already be deleted; this bead is self-contained.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each of the five channels is either graded by a runner that actually loads the fixture, or removed from the fixture together with its README credit.
2. For each graded channel, a planted fault in the reference (or in the fixture's expected value) turns the conformance run red.
3. No expectation key is delegated by name to a runner that does not load that file. A matcher-coverage check, or a recorded census, shows that every remaining expectation key has a grader.
4. Any expectation the reference fails once graded is resolved, with the reason recorded on this bead.
notes:
== WORKER RESULT (PR #11366, branch worker/conformance-ungraded, on trunk a7e0979946)

Per-channel decisions, for rf2-nbgqz to carry forward:

1. frame-lifecycle.edn :on-destroy-emissions / :on-destroy-effects: GRADED in the shared runner (conformance_runner.cljc). After every other expectation has read the live frame, the runner destroys the fixture's frame and grades only the traces that window adds. Emissions use the :trace-emissions law and effects the :effects-routed law. Once graded, :on-destroy-effects failed: the fixture registered no :log fx, and the runtime correctly traces an unknown fx id as :rf.error/no-such-fx without routing it. FIXTURE CORRECTED: it now registers a no-op :log stub.
2. spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn :trace-not-emitted: GRADED in the shared runner, with the submap? law the SSR runner already uses. Its third row named :to :ready, a tag the runtime :rf.machine/transition row never carries (that row carries :before/:after snapshots), so graded as written it passed vacuously. FIXTURE CORRECTED to :after {:state :ready}. A control row with :after {:state :loading} goes red.
3. sub-chain.edn :sub-graph-topology: DROPPED. derivation-graph-algebra.edn already grades the same cart/items -> cart/total :input edge.
4. :expect-trace (19 records) and :expect-microsteps (4) on 9 pure :machine-transition fixtures: DROPPED. Spec 005 Level 1 makes the plain {:status :snapshot :fx :handled?} map the whole pure contract; trace events are a Level 2 surface. Measured with a JVM probe at trunk dbb2b1a0bd, the pure call emits these traces:
   - always-single-microstep call 0: [:rf.machine/action-ran :rf.machine/guard-evaluated :rf.machine.microstep/transition]
   - after-single-delay call 0: [:rf.machine/action-ran :rf.machine.timer/scheduled]
   - after-single-delay call 1: [:rf.machine.timer/fired]
   None of them is the :rf.machine/transition row every :expect-trace lists, and the public result keys are (:fx :handled? :snapshot :status), with no microstep count. Grading the claim as written needs a runtime change.
5. ssr-redirect.edn :ssr/request-result {:html :absent :payload :absent}: DROPPED. The SSR runner no longer fabricates those slots; its actual value is now {:response (get-response)} only. Hosts build :html and :payload (Spec 011 Request-handler return shape), and ssr-ring's handler-redirect-short-circuits grades body truncation.
6. Found by the census, outside the bead's five: ssr-head-emits.edn :ssr/html-attr-present was on the sibling-owned roster, but no runner read it. DROPPED. ssr_emit_test covers the data-rf-render-hash root attribute.

sibling-owned-expect-keys now holds only flow keys (on flow-*.edn, which the flows runner loads and fails rather than skips) and SSR keys (on ssr-*.edn). README rows were corrected for sub-chain, ssr-redirect, ssr-set-status ("HTML body still renders" was ungraded), always-single-microstep, always-depth-exceeded, after-single-delay and after-stale-detection.

Evidence:
- At tip, planted wrong expected values in frame-lifecycle (both destroy channels) and spawn-all (a not-emitted row naming a trace that fires) left re-frame.conformance-test green: exit 0.
- On the branch the same plants go red (exit 1), and the report names each one.
- Putting :html :absent back into ssr-redirect turns re-frame.ssr-conformance-test red on the branch (exit 1).
- A grader census of every top-level expect key and every call-record key against a runner that loads its carriers finds 0 ungraded on the branch. At tip it finds 7: both destroy keys, :trace-not-emitted, :sub-graph-topology, :expect-trace, :expect-microsteps and :ssr/html-attr-present.
- JVM gates on the branch: core conformance-test 0, ssr-conformance-test 0, machines-conformance-test 0. All 44 CI check_*.py invocations plus the ai-tracking and hardcoded-paths ratchets exit 0, and mkdocs --strict exits 0.
- The CLJS lane (shared .cljc runner) relies on PR CI, job "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)".

Left for rf2-nbgqz (outside this fence, a Spec-Schemas hot zone): spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4706 still declares [:sub-graph-topology {:optional true} :map].

Merged PR #11366 as 6aa11968b0a7ab4c83b781bb13f2e697b9935b03 (rebase), 2026-10-16. title: Deliver trace listeners from one FIFO queue owned by the outermost deliverer: a nested emit enqueues and returns, and no callback is re-entered
description:
## Ruling

Deliver `:trace` listener events from **one FIFO queue drained by the outermost deliverer**. A trace emitted from inside a listener's body enqueues its event and returns at once. Every event still reaches every listener, in emission order per listener, before the outermost delivery returns. No listener callback is ever re-entered.

This retires "law 2": the rule that a nested `emit!` returns only after its event has reached every listener. Change the spec contract, not merely the implementation.

All the safety machinery stays:
- post-drain deferral;
- the process-wide `fanout-monitor`;
- `deferred-continue`;
- the continuation fence.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. His instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

The original dossier and the Codex review both chose this option, S1. Codex: "FIFO delivery owned by the outermost caller gives stateful tool callbacks a simpler guarantee: finish processing A before handling B. This avoids re-entry into a partially updated fold and removes recursive driving."

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:
1. **Today's behaviour re-enters a callback and contradicts the public API page.**
   - The pinned test asserts that "the emitter also receives its own nested inner" while its call for the outer event is still on the stack. It also asserts that the observer already holds the inner event when the nested emit returns (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_listener_nested_emission_order_cljs_test.cljc:36-62`, especially `:53` and `:58-59`).
   - The public API page says "Delivery is synchronous: the callback returns before the next record" (`docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1457`).
   - Spec 009 makes law 2 normative at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:809`.
2. **Law 2 is the only reason for the hardest machinery in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc`:**
   - the shared resumable cursors kept in `*fanout-ctx*` (`:901`);
   - `drive-fanout!` (`:1034-1085`), which advances `:lcursor` before each callback so a nested call can resume the outer event;
   - the integrate-and-drive branch for a listener's `dispatch-sync` (`:1197-1214`);
   - the drive-now nested branch (`:1375-1376`);
   - the 56-line note that reconciles the two laws (`:739-794`).
3. **No in-tree consumer depends on nested completion** (read, not run).
   - Xray's collector emits nothing from its body and coalesces onto `next-tick` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs:297-360`).
   - Story buffers failures until dispatch settles (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:138`; its capture brackets wrap top-level walks, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/error.cljc:140-160`).
   - The pair MCP reads the per-frame rings.

Rejected options:
- **Keep law 2 (S0).** It keeps a contract clause that no consumer relies on, contradicts the API page, and is the hardest clause for a port to reproduce.
- **Also remove the continuation fence in this change.** That is a separate change, and it depends on destruction moving to the event boundary (`jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`).

This supersedes the normative clause "Reentrant emits complete synchronously and in order" at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:809`, and the nested-completion half of `:632` and `:643`. No ruling bead or EP establishing law 2 was found.

## Work

Code, all in `trace/tooling.cljc` unless noted:
- Branch (b) at `:1375-1376`, an emit inside a listener body with no drain: append the event and return; do not drive.
- The integrate branch of `drain-deferred-batch!` (`:1187`, `:1197-1214`): append and return.
- `drive-fanout!` (`:1034-1085`): make it one loop owned by the outermost deliverer (`run-outermost-fanout!`, `:1087`). Its cursors become locals, and `*fanout-ctx*` carries only the queue.
- Take the listener snapshot at enqueue time for a nested emit, as the deferred path already does. The rule there is "Deferral moves only the TIMING of delivery, never its CONTENT" (`:866-873`), so one rule then covers both deferral and nesting.
- Rewrite the section note at `:739-794` to state the FIFO law. It gets shorter.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:848-856`: the `emit!` docstring.
- The dossier estimates 60 to 100 lines removed, mostly prose.

Spec, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`:
- `:632` and `:643`: "before that operation returns" becomes "before the outermost delivery returns", for an emit made inside a listener.
- `:807-809`: replace law 2 with FIFO: per-listener emission order, no re-entry, and complete before the outermost delivery returns.
- `:996-999`.

Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1457` becomes true as written. Check that it still reads right.

Tests:
- Restate `trace_listener_nested_emission_order_cljs_test.cljc:36-62` so that:
  - the emitter is not re-entered;
  - both listeners see `[outer inner]`;
  - both have `inner` before the outermost emit returns;
  - the observer does NOT yet hold `inner` at the nested return.
- These suites keep their intent: post-drain delivery, re-entrant `dispatch-sync`, deferred-batch FIFO, deadlock, and JVM serialisation (for example `implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_listener_concurrent_serialization_test.clj`).

Preserve, from the Codex list:
- whole-batch FIFO;
- enqueue-time listener snapshots;
- post-drain deferral, so that no listener code runs under a drain lock (009:637-641; `tooling.cljc:819-829` is the JVM AB-BA deadlock it prevents);
- the process-wide `fanout-monitor` (`:910-921`);
- `deferred-continue` (`:1121-1185`) and the per-event continuation snapshot (`trace.cljc:111-131`);
- neutral authority for listener-authored work;
- the inline ring push and epoch capture;
- the router tail's boundaries. Inside the drain it publishes taps, then sinks, then the post-drain trace delivery, with exact-owner checks between publications (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2907-2956`).

Document one hazard in the listener contract: a register-run-unregister capture bracket placed *inside another listener's callback* closes before its events are delivered. No in-tree bracket sits there, and a bracket inside a drain already behaves this way today.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zone**: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`.
- **Within this dossier**: this is the third and last of three chained beads. It depends on the handled-event vocabulary bead, for the same Spec 009 hot zone; that bead in turn follows the bead that makes error taps own only what they claim. Their code is disjoint.
- **Cross-dossier**:
  - `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`: its core work moves destruction to the event boundary, deletes the in-event fence, and delivers always-on listeners after the event, "coordinated with" this dossier. Both edit the delivery and fence region. Sequence the two, never in parallel. This bead keeps the fence intact, so either order is sound; the later one rebases.
  - `epoch-listener-silencing-and-incarnation-storage.md`: it covers the `:epoch` stream's own listener delivery, in the epoch `listeners.cljc`, not `trace/tooling.cljc`. It relies on this bead keeping post-drain deferral, which it does. If its work edits Spec 009's listener-delivery clauses (`:807-810`), sequence it with this bead.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`, the one i/crlf file, is not touched.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:**
  - `tooling.cljc:739-794`, `:808-829`, `:866-873`, `:901-921`, `:1034-1087`, `:1121`, `:1187-1214`, `:1300-1384`;
  - `trace_listener_nested_emission_order_cljs_test.cljc:36-62`;
  - `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1457`;
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:632`, `:643`, `:807-810`, `:996-999`;
  - `trace_collector.cljs:297-312`;
  - `play.cljc:136-140`.
- **Needs a run:**
  - whether the deferred-batch suite reorders under FIFO. A reorder would reopen this ruling;
  - whether any external tool reads another listener's state straight after a nested emit. None is known. A named one would warrant reconsidering.
- Neither review ran tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Set up two trace listeners: an emitter that emits event B from inside its callback for event A, and a plain logger. The emitter's callback is never re-entered: no callback for B starts while the emitter's callback for A is on the stack.
2. Both listeners see [A B], and both have received B before the outermost emit returns.
3. The nested emit returns before B has been delivered to any listener. The restated trace_listener_nested_emission_order test pins this.
4. When a listener calls dispatch-sync, app-db is settled when it returns, and (rf/trace-buffer frame) read straight after it holds the run's traces, because the ring push stays inline.
5. The existing post-drain, re-entrant dispatch-sync, deferred-batch FIFO, deadlock and JVM serialisation suites stay green with their intent unchanged.
6. The following state the FIFO law:
   - spec/009-Instrumentation.md (:632, :643, :807-809, :996-999);
   - the emit! docstring;
   - the tooling.cljc section note.
   No text still promises that a nested emit returns only after its event has reached every listener, and docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1457 is true as written.
7. The shared resumable cursors and the integrate-and-drive branch are gone. deferred-continue, the per-event continuation snapshot and fanout-monitor remain.
8. The PR quotes the runner's own exit codes for the CLJS node lane, the browser lane, and scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh.

The edge to rf2-ot1aa is hot-zone ordering only: rf2-ot1aa (clustered with rf2-qb4ua and rf2-2krdz) holds spec/009-Instrumentation.md alone while it is in flight. It releases when rf2-ot1aa closes on merge.

title: Carry adapter capabilities on the adapter map, publish them at install, and delete route-hook! routing
description:
## Ruling

An adapter's capabilities move onto the adapter map itself. Every capability an adapter publishes at namespace load through `route-hook!` today becomes an optional key on its map. `install-adapter!` publishes exactly the installed map's capabilities into the existing `:adapter/*` late-bind slots; a key the map lacks is published as absent, so no other adapter's capability can answer. `dispose-adapter!` tears down through the DEPARTING map and then clears those slots, never touching a replacement generation's. `route-hook!`, its routing chains and `plain-atom/route-disposal-hooks!` are deleted. Consumers keep calling `get-fn-cached :adapter/...` unchanged. Core's `dispose-adapter!` takes over frame sub-cache teardown. That completes the move rf2-ygdzp deliberately deferred: "Do NOT move the walk into core's `dispose-adapter!`. Routed disposal hooks close when the generation is claimed, so that move belongs to the larger 'adapter capabilities on the adapter map' refactor."

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **The map is only part of the contract, and copying it cannot override anything.** The ratom family's adapter is an 11-key map, plus 15 capabilities routed separately through `route-hook!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:4377-4500`). The React-hook spine (UIx, Fresco) routes 6 or 7 more (`spine.cljs:3868-3908`). `route-hook!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:898`, closure arities at `:942-958`) runs the namespace's own closure when `same-adapter?` matches `current-adapter`, and otherwise walks the chain. It never consults the supplied map, so `(rf/init! (assoc reagent/adapter :after-render f))` still serves Reagent's own closure.
2. **A missing capability fails silently.** `interop/add-on-dispose!` and `interop/dispose!` are `when-let` no-ops when no hook answers (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:120-130`). SSR has to route plain-atom's disposal hooks for itself (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/substrate.cljc:94`). test-react's derived value is `IDeref` only and publishes no disposal hook (`implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:47-57, 622-624`), so on CLJS evicting a layer-2 subscription under test-react releases none of its inputs.
3. **Spec 006 does not describe the real contract.** It declares the contract "closed for v1" at ten fns (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:99-132`), and justifies each extra hook with the refrain that it "rides the late-bind table ... so the ten-fn contract shape is unchanged" (`006:199, 203`). A port written from §Normative contract implements ten functions and misses `:adapter/dispose!`.

Rejected options:
- **Leave as is (route-hook! chains):** keeps the silent no-op class, the spec/code mismatch, and rf2-ygdzp's deferred teardown move.
- **Read `(:k (current-adapter))` at every call site:** rewrites about 15 consumer sites, adds an atom deref plus a map lookup per call, and needs the departing map threaded through teardown by hand. Publishing at install keeps every consumer call site unchanged, and each call stays one cached slot.

Supersedes: Spec 006's "closed for v1 ... ten fns" contract statement and its "rides the late-bind table so the ten-fn contract shape is unchanged" rationale, together with §Hook routing by stable token. No bead or EP is overturned. This bead completes the move closed bead rf2-ygdzp deferred.

## Work

**Code**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc`
  - `install-adapter!` (`:126`) publishes the installed map's capability keys with `rf.late-bind/set-fn!`, which already invalidates the `get-fn-cached` slot (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc:112-123`). It publishes absent keys as absent.
  - `dispose-adapter!` (`:283-330`) runs cleanup against the departing map's capabilities, moves `re-frame.subs.cache/clear-all-frame-sub-caches!` into core, and then clears the slots.
  - Delete `route-hook!` (`:898-958`).
  - Keep `same-adapter?` (`:835`). `init!` uses it to stay idempotent across hot reload (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:3087-3090`); only its per-call hot-path use goes.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs`: both route blocks (`:3868-3908` and `:4377-4500`) become map entries. The adapters keep a private copy of their own dispose dispatch so cleanup still works after public routing closes (`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:151`, `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:45`). That copy goes if cleanup now reaches the departing map's `:dispose!`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc`: `route-disposal-hooks!` (`:195-211`) goes, and the map carries `:add-on-dispose!` and `:dispose!`. SSR's map (`ssr/substrate.cljc:66-90`) carries the same two plain-atom functions directly, and the `:94` call goes.
- `test_react.cljc`: its `:current-frame` moves onto its map. If test-react is still in tree when this lands, it meets the disposal obligation the spec now states, so layer-2 evictions release their inputs.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:763-862`: re-describe the `:adapter/*` rows as published at install from the installed map, not routed. `:adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!` is published by `re-frame.views`, is not an adapter capability, and stays as it is.

**Lifecycle requirements.** These are not optional. Each one is a place where "just clear the slots last" is not enough.
- **Rollback and finalization are generation-safe.** A failed install is rolled back, because `install-adapter!` is failure-atomic and arms the emitter inside its transaction (`adapter.cljc:111-124`). Neither that rollback nor a stale generation's finalization may erase or overwrite another generation's capabilities. Guard them by generation, as `dispose-adapter!`'s `finally` already does for the lifecycle slot (`adapter.cljc:319-327`).
- **Cleanup access is separate from admitting new public work.** `claim-installed-for-dispose!` closes public delegation before cleanup runs (`adapter.cljc:209-225`), so `current-adapter` reads nil during teardown. Cleanup must still reach the departing map's `:dispose!` and `:add-on-dispose!` while fresh public work stays refused.
- **Hot reload is a deliberate choice.** A same-kind `init!` skips `install-adapter!` (`core.cljc:3087-3090`), even when a reloaded adapter namespace hands over fresh function identities. Decide how published capabilities refresh on that path, for example by republishing the supplied map's capabilities without reinstalling. Pin the choice with a test.

**Spec** (all hot zones; one PR)
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §The adapter API contract (`:99-132`): the contract becomes one map. It holds the required functions plus named optional capability keys, and each key documents what happens when it is absent. State explicitly when `:add-on-dispose!` and `:dispose!` are required; an optional no-op on a map is not a contract. Replace §Hook routing by stable token, and every "rides the late-bind table" paragraph (for example `:199`, `:203`), with the capability-key description.
- `spec/API.md`: the adapter rows, `current-adapter`, and the "11-key adapter spec map" wording. Hand-edit `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`, then regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` with `generate!` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`. The three files are one holding.
- `spec/Conventions.md`: the `:adapter/<surface>` row and the adapter-Var paragraph.
- One sentence each in `spec/002-Frames.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, wherever they describe routed adapter hooks.

**Tests**
- About 26 test files reference the hooks or `route-hook!`. Delete the routing-specific ones: the routing-token and routing-arity tests (`routing_arity_cljs_test`), the slim publication test, and the per-call `same-adapter?` bench rows. Edit the rest.
- Add the five cases in the acceptance criteria, plus the rollback, generation and hot-reload tests.

**What deliberately stays.** Moving these, not deleting them, is this bead's job. Whether any of them goes is the separate map-shrink decision, which Mike has not yet ruled on.
- The three map slots core never calls (`:render-to-string`, `:subscribe-container`, `:register-context-provider`) and their delegators (`adapter.cljc:723-795`).
- `:adapter/derived-container?`, `:adapter/ratom`, `:adapter/ratom?` and `:adapter/reactive?`. They move onto the maps like every other routed hook.
- The hiccup-emitter arm (`:adapter/arm-hiccup-emitter-if-unarmed!`, read from the map being installed) and the `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` chain.
- The `:rf.adapter/ssr` kind. SSR keeps its own map.

title: Align the machine destroy-tail contract with pending frame destruction
description: PR #11423 (6b26ad25ca) changes Spec 002 Destroy to defer a frame destroy requested on its active drain stack until the current event completes, with the id reserved through terminal publication. Spec 005-StateMachines.md:2950, Exact-incarnation terminal fence (the destroy tail), still says an ordinary machine destroy effect's callbacks can synchronously destroy frame A and publish a same-id successor B, and normatively requires ownership rechecks after every callback and before every remaining destroy action. A port implementing the newly settled boundary semantics cannot encounter that in-event successor window; this paragraph preserves the superseded fence contract and directs implementors to retain complexity that the core follow-up rf2-a19oz removes. The PR explicitly reports this outside its file fence, but the separately staged runtime implementation does not itself correct this specification paragraph. Small correction: rewrite the ordinary in-drain destroy/finalize-tail paragraph around pending frame teardown at the event boundary, linking Spec 002 Destroy. Distinguish any still-applicable direct-call or stale-async owner protection without weakening it or adding an API. Verify the revised Spec 005 contract and Spec 002 agree on when the current event finishes, when teardown occurs, and when a same-id successor can be constructed; retain the existing exact-token durable-write protection where it remains needed.

That commit was pushed before this bead was filed, so its message does not carry this id; the PR title and body name it. History is not rewritten.

Spec 005 "Exact-incarnation terminal fence (the destroy tail)" now reads in three parts.
1. Drain path, by citation of Spec 002 Destroy. A callback that destroys A inside the drain does not cut the tail short: the destroy is pending until the event boundary, and A's per-id reservation is held until its teardown has finished, so no same-id successor B can be published while the tail runs. The two tail traces reach listeners only after the drain.
2. Direct-call path: the effect called under A's event owner with no drain on the stack. A frame destroy is immediate there, so the callbacks and the two traces' listeners can still destroy A and publish B mid-tail. The fence is kept as the contract on that path without weakening it: a terminal fence on the classification drop, timer cancellation, durable teardown projection, registrar unregister and resource-owner release; rechecks against A's owner token after every callback boundary; durable writes riding that token; registrar/unregister! rechecked after the destroyed trace.
3. Code as it is: the reference implementation does not yet defer a mid-drain destroy, so it applies the same fence inside the drain. The core bead rf2-a19oz removes that in-event fence. The eventless frame-destroy cascade keeps full authority, and the :final? auto-destroy tail follows the same discipline.

Agreement with Spec 002: the current event finishes first; teardown runs at its boundary; a same-id make-frame fails with :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress until teardown step 10 has finished. title: Make reg-http-interceptor a top-level definition and name each frame's ordered chain with :http-interceptors
description:
## Ruling

HTTP interceptors split into a definition and an activation. `(rf/reg-http-interceptor :shop/auth {:before … :after …})` is a top-level, frame-agnostic definition under a new registrar kind `:http-interceptor`, with no `:frame`. Each frame names its chain, in order, through a new frame-config key, `:http-interceptors [:shop/auth :shop/telemetry]` — the shape the frame `:interceptors` ref chain already has. The ids resolve through the frame's registrations when a request is issued; `:before` runs in vector order and `:after` in reverse. A frame that names no chain gets none, and registration or load order no longer configures any chain.

This is also the HTTP half of B1, the principle both recommendations ruled: every `reg-*` declares a frame-agnostic program member, registration never reads a frame, and what is genuinely per frame instance — here, which interceptors and in what order — becomes frame config.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

This bead is sub-decision C-h2 (with its share of B1) of the dossier "Should every `reg-*` be a top-level program registration in one registration table" (local `one-registry-top-level-reg.md`, now deleted). The same ruling: A1 one registration table, C-s1 app-db schemas as a registrar kind (the bead before this), D2 facade placement, and E0 — images stay opt-in, and a later image can now shadow an interceptor definition (a test double, a Story variant's fake auth).

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. Today an interceptor is a per-frame install: the chain lives in a `defonce` atom keyed `frame-id → [slot …]`, "Order is registration-order; clearing an id and re-registering re-appends to the end" (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:77-86`), and `reg-http-interceptor` resolves a frame from `:frame` or the scope chain, raising `:rf.error/no-frame-context` without one (`middleware.cljc:172-185`, written at `:194`). Spec 014 §Chain order and frame scope specifies registration-order chains, append-after-clear and per-frame isolation (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:879-886`).
2. Chain order is semantic — `:before` in order, `:after` in reverse (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:881-882`) — and the registration store is a map with no cross-namespace order, so the order has to be stated somewhere other than load order; rf2-bmrh9 ruled that load order never decides.
3. The pattern already exists for event interceptors: each behaviour is registered once with `reg-interceptor`, and frame config names the ordered refs, `:interceptors [:dev/event-recorder …]` (`spec/002-Frames.md:2468-2488`). Issue-time capture already gives the semantics this keeps: `capture-chain` snapshots one vector per request that drives `:before`, `:after` and every retry (`middleware.cljc:313`), and `run-after-chain!` walks it in reverse (`:494`).

**Rejected:**

- **C-h0, keep the per-frame side table with registration order:** registration stays a per-frame install, so `reg-` keeps two meanings and a test frame lacks the chain only by accident of its id.
- **C-h1, pure image members (every frame runs every registered interceptor):** chain order would come from load order, which the store cannot express and rf2-bmrh9 forbids deciding anything.
- **C-h3, inline interceptor maps on frame config:** loses source coordinates, `clear`, image shadowing, hot reload by re-registration, and frame config as serializable data (`spec/002-Frames.md:2519`).

**Supersedes:** Spec 014 §Chain order and frame scope's registration-order, clear-then-re-register-appends and per-frame-registration rules (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:879-886`); the "context-required frame-local" registration rule cited in the code at `middleware.cljc:173-182` (EP-0002); the HTTP half of Conventions §`reg-*` frame-binding convention (`spec/Conventions.md:1594`).

## Work

- **Registrar:** add `:http-interceptor` to `kinds` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:146-147`). It joins `clear` without opts and the hot-reload sweep like any other kind; `clear-frame-scoped-kinds` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1143-1147`) shrinks to `#{:flow}`, and `clear-kinds`' special-casing of `:http-interceptor` (`:1149-1159`) goes.
- **`http/middleware.cljc`** (651 lines): delete the per-frame `interceptors` atom and its frame resolution; `reg-http-interceptor` writes a definition; `capture-chain` reads the frame's `:http-interceptors` vector and resolves each id through the frame's registrations at issue time. Capture the resolved function-bearing chain once per request — including the empty chain — and keep it across retries and response handling; the reply-tail fence is unchanged. A chain naming an unregistered id fails at issue, the way an unknown interceptor ref does.
- **`:frame`** in the interceptor map is an error whose message names the `:http-interceptors` frame-config key.
- **Frame config:** `make-frame` / `frame-root` accept `:http-interceptors`, a vector of keyword ids, validated with the other frame-config keys; `frame-meta` shows it. Because the chain lives on frame config, `destroy-frame!` drops it and `frame-root` re-supplies it on every mount.
- **No warning** for a definition no frame names: trust the programmer, and say so in the docstring.
- **Examples:** `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:438-446` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs:435-443` register `:realworld/bearer-auth` at top level and name it on their frame; their frame-scope wrappers go.
- **Tests:** chain-order, per-frame and clear-then-append tests are rewritten to the config vector (the dossier counted 25 test files at trunk).
- **Spec:** Spec 014 §Middleware and §Chain order and frame scope (order from the frame's vector; per-frame divergence by naming different ids, e.g. a user frame naming `:user/auth` and an admin frame `:admin/auth`); Spec 002's `make-frame` key list; Conventions §`reg-*` frame-binding convention narrowed to what remains (flows); `spec/API.md` rows and manifest sidecars.
- **Docs and skills sweep** in the style of rf2-sugyt for every `reg-http-interceptor` teaching site (the dossier counted 13 docs files and 8 skill files).
- **Deliberately stays:** issue-time capture, skip-when-absent, and the rule that an interceptor must carry `:before` or `:after`.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** `spec/002-Frames.md`; `spec/API.md` with `spec/api-manifest.edn` (generated) and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`; `spec/Conventions.md`. Possibly `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` if it teaches the interceptor's `:frame`.

title: Router: send framework-built envelopes through enqueue-envelope!, so known-dispatch-opts holds only public opts
description:
## Current

`known-dispatch-opts` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc` ~136-190) mixes the public dispatch opts with four internal control flags: `:rf.trace/call-site`, `:rf.flow/settle?`, `:step-index` and `:rf.frame/expected-incarnation`. They ride the public opt map because framework callers re-enter through `dispatch!`. A private `enqueue-envelope!` already exists (`router.cljc` ~4052).

## Change

Route framework-built envelopes through `enqueue-envelope!`, carrying those controls as envelope fields, so they leave `known-dispatch-opts` and the public opt grammar. Framework-built envelopes include the flow settle, machine steps and incarnation-checked dispatch.

For `:rf.trace/call-site`, which the dispatch macro stamps at the user's call site, take whichever is smaller: move it into the envelope the macro builds, or keep it with an internal marking in the grammar. Add no new entry point and no queue abstraction.

## Acceptance

- `known-dispatch-opts` lists only documented public opts.
- A user dispatch carrying `:rf.flow/settle?`, `:step-index` or `:rf.frame/expected-incarnation` gets the ordinary unknown-opt warning.
- The JVM core suite and `test:cljs` stay green.

Touches `router.cljc`, `fx.cljc` and `router/diagnostics.cljc`; sequence it with the fx-override reject-tier bead.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER (router-fx-cleanup), PR #11502 — PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD; no code change

Verified at source at 9a69891d05. known-dispatch-opts (router/diagnostics.cljc 136-190) and enqueue-envelope! (router.cljc 4052) are where the bead says, but enqueue-envelope! is not a route framework callers can take:

1. It is (swap! router insert-envelope envelope) and nothing more: a lane inserter that sits below dispatch!'s frame resolution, the exact-incarnation fence, the :rf.event/dispatched trace and drain scheduling (ensure-drain-scheduled!). Its only caller is dispatch!'s destroy-cascade branch.
2. Two of the three producers are synchronous and never enqueue. :step-index is stamped by frame.cljc run-setup-events! on each :initial-events step, which runs through the :router/dispatch-sync! hook. It is a frame-construction setup step, not a machine step as the bead says. :rf.frame/expected-incarnation also rides capture-frame's :dispatch-sync op.
3. All three producers live in namespaces that cannot require the router: fx.cljc settle-flows-after-walk! (through the :router/dispatch! late-bind hook), frame.cljc (:router/dispatch-sync!) and capture_frame.cljc capture-dispatch!, through core's :core/dispatch-impl / :core/dispatch-sync-impl seams. The known-dispatch-opts docstring names re-frame.core/capture-dispatch!, but the fn is re-frame.capture-frame/capture-dispatch!. Handing them envelope fields therefore needs a new late-bind hook or a new dispatch arity, which is the new entry point the bead rules out. capture_frame.cljc and core.cljc are also outside this dispatch's fence.

:rf.trace/call-site already carries the bead's permitted alternative: the docstring marks it as macro-stamped and dev-only.

Recommended close: premise does not hold. Doing it would mean a private internal-dispatch entry for framework callers, which is new mechanism for a P4 grammar tidy.
close_reason: Not done: the premise does not hold (verified by the router-fx-cleanup worker at trunk 9a69891d05, no code change). enqueue-envelope! only puts an envelope into a queue. It sits below dispatch!'s frame resolution, incarnation check, trace and drain scheduling, and only the destroy-cascade branch calls it, so it is not the shared entry point the bead assumed. :step-index is a frame-setup step that runs through dispatch-sync!, not a machine step, and :rf.frame/expected-incarnation rides capture-frame's :dispatch-sync; neither ever enqueues. The three producers (fx.cljc, frame.cljc, capture_frame.cljc) reach the router only through late-bind hooks or core seams, so giving them envelope fields would need a new hook or arity, which is the new entry point the bead itself forbids.

title: Render-trace cap never fires without epoch or after settle: count :rf.view/rendered on core-owned run state
description:
## Defect

`emit-view-rendered-trace!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs` ~294-319) takes its per-run count and `:cause-event-id` from optional epoch's `:epoch/run-cause`. It defaults the count to 0 when epoch is absent. The cap is `view-rendered-cap`, 100 (~201). This misses two cases:

- **Without epoch,** the cap never fires, so a render storm emits unbounded `:rf.view/rendered` traces into the ring.
- **With epoch,** `run-cause` returns 0 outside the in-flight buffer (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc` ~366-368). That includes post-settle React renders, the common browser case, so those are never capped either.

It is also a core→epoch inversion.

## Change

Keep the per-run render count on core-owned run state, with an explicit post-settle window: renders after the drain settles count against the last run until the next run starts. Epoch may still supply the `:cause-event-id` attribution, but budgeting no longer depends on it. Spec 009 drops the cap's "absent when re-frame.epoch is not on the classpath".

## Acceptance

- With epoch absent and tracing enabled, 101 renders in one run emit 100 `:rf.view/rendered` plus one `:rf.view/rendered-cap-reached`, and the next run's budget resets.
- The same holds for post-settle renders with epoch present.

title: Schemas weak-cache reachability test flakes after its weak references have cleared
description:

(.size cache)), actual (not (zero? 400)). The run had 127 tests / 396 assertions and exactly 1 failure, so the preceding all-WeakReference-cleared assertion passed. Rerunning the failed jobs on the same PR passed. This blocked an unrelated Markdown-only PR and is an actionable CI flake, not evidence that its documentation introduced a schema leak. The observed mismatch is consistent with reference-queue/cache cleanup lag after the independent weak references have cleared.

Keep the deadline and both assertions, and preserve the existing strong-key sabotage's ability to fail; do not weaken the zero-cache assertion or change the production cache merely to make this test green. The separate port-cache reachability test can retain its appropriate predicate.

title: HTTP install-transport! misses frame values and retains their transport after destroy
description:
Observed while auditing merged PR #11528 at 1bb12f48d46f6d9e5889ecedb07cd7f6ace5a8a5. The new per-frame stub transport works with a keyword id, but silently fails with the live frame value returned by make-frame.

Reproduction: make a live frame f with id :audit11528/frame; (install-transport! :audit11528/frame t) makes registry/frame-transport at that id return t, and uninstalling by id clears it. After (install-transport! f t), the lookup at the frame id instead returns nil. The transport was stored under the entire frame value. With no with-transport scope, requests issued by that frame therefore miss the installed stub and select the host adapter. Destroying f also leaves that transport entry behind, since teardown removes the keyword-id key rather than the value key.

Evidence at the merge: stub_transport.cljc:150-156 forwards frame-id unchanged. registry.cljc:245-255 uses the argument directly as the frame-transports key; transport.cljc:1569 reads it using the issuing ctx's :frame id; registry.cljc:488 drops it by that id at teardown. The current normative Spec 002, Frame identity at line 25 and Frame addressing/Frame values, says a public operation accepts the id or live value directly and normalizes the value one way to its id. The historical EP's original id-only grammar is not the current amended contract. Existing stub-transport tests install only with keyword ids.

Focused JVM probe against an isolated archive of this exact merge, loading the real core, managed HTTP and stub namespaces: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11528-frame-value-1.clj; 1 test, 5 assertions, 2 failures, 0 errors, process exit 3. The frame-value premise and id install/uninstall controls pass. The value install and post-destroy cleanup assertions fail. Log: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11528-frame-value-1.log. No network request was made and no shadow-cljs lane was entered.

Small correction: normalize the public install/uninstall target with the existing frame-value->id primitive before keying the per-frame registry. Pin id/value equivalence for installation and nil uninstallation, and verify destroying the frame drops the entry. Keep transport lookup and cleanup keyed on the canonical id; no new scope, registry or lifecycle mechanism is needed. Read the complete rf2-1iz80 record before filing.
notes:

title: Fresco: prototype explicit event and render callback carriers in place of h/event's prop-name-selected contract
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

`h/event` only marks a fn; the prop's spelling selects its contract (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/intent.cljs`, `event-prop?` and the lowering beside it):

- at an `on*` prop, the wrapper dispatches a returned vector and returns nil;
- at any other prop, it restores the supplying frame and returns the result.

So an interactive render prop needs both `h/event` and `h/as-element` (the virtual-list recipe in `docs/core/fresco/09-interop.md`). An `on*`-named render prop, such as Fluent UI's `onRenderItem`, also needs `:callbacks {prop :render}` on its `defhost`. Without that declaration the list blanks silently (09-interop § Overriding the spelling). Moving a marked fn to another prop changes both its return and its effect.

This is the one position-dependent rule in Fresco that fails silently, in a layer that otherwise refuses loudly. rf2-bapdr teaches it as a cost of the taught default; this bead tries to remove it.

## Change

Prototype two explicit carriers:

- an **event** callback that dispatches its returned vector;
- a **render** callback that carries its frame and converts its returned Hiccup to a React element.

A carrier means the same thing at any prop, so `h/as-element` at render props and `:callbacks` overrides on `defhost` become unnecessary. Plain fns stay ordinary foreign behaviour, and data intents keep their native event spelling. Settle the names.

**Adopt only if the concept count falls.** Compare complete application snippets for the virtual-list and `onRenderItem` recipes. Renaming `h/event` or adding an alias while keeping every existing rule does not count. If the prototype does not reduce the count, close this bead with the comparison recorded.

## Spec and docs that move with it (on adoption)

- Fresco's contract in `implementation/fresco/spec/`, the `defhost` and intent docstrings in `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco.cljc`, and `docs/core/fresco/09-interop.md`.
- Fresco rows in `spec/API.md` with both manifest sidecars. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

- The virtual-list and `onRenderItem` recipes need neither `h/as-element` nor `:callbacks`.
- A carrier moved between props keeps its effect.
- Frame capture stays correct for event vectors inside rendered Hiccup.
- Fresco suites green.

## Sequencing

Related to rf2-bapdr (teaching) and to the Fresco authoring-contract bead, which should describe whichever rule this settles. Adopting it is a breaking change. Effort S to prototype.

title: Router hygiene and routing-skill truth: router.cljc kondo warnings, unresolvable § in diagnostics :reason strings, scroll-storage bullet
description:
## Problem

Three small truth and hygiene findings, reported by the workers on #11565 (router commentary) and #11564 (routing scroll). They are claims, so re-check each at tip.

1. **Skill reference misstates scroll storage.** The *Multi-frame routing* bullet in `skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md` says saved scroll positions live in runtime-db. They live in a host-side cache.
2. **Four clj-kondo warnings in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`:** an unused `re-frame.substrate.adapter` require, a redundant `let`, and unused bindings `event` and `frame-record`.
3. **Emitted `:reason` strings in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc` cite `§` sections that don't resolve**, e.g. "Spec 002 §Run-to-completion §Rules rule 1".

## Change

1. Correct the skill bullet to say where scroll positions actually live, citing Spec 012.
2. Remove the dead require and the unused bindings, and collapse the redundant `let`, without changing behaviour.
3. Point each `:reason` string's `§` at a heading that exists. If a test asserts the exact string, update that assertion in the same commit. Change only the pointer text.

## Acceptance

- clj-kondo on `router.cljc` reports none of the four warnings. Run it without `--fail-level` (CLAUDE.md hazard (w)).
- Every `§` in `diagnostics.cljc`'s emitted strings resolves to a heading in `spec/`.
- `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`, `npm run test:cljs`, `check_doc_slugs.py` and the skill gates are green.

Effort XS.

title: Schemas: redact failures with the same event's classification effects
description:
At PR #11561 merge 07250ba2b04fe1a1f5c43083bddbed15c846c46b, project-through-registry in implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc reads the frame's live elision registry. During candidate app-db validation, the event's commit-plane classification effects have not been installed. One event returning both {:db ...} with a schema-invalid secret and {:sensitive [the-path]} therefore exposes the secret in its schema-validation-failure trace even though the whole write is rejected. This contradicts the declare-once registry redaction contract added to Spec 010 and Spec 009.

Confirmed with the focused JVM probe ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11561-same-event-classification-1.clj (log and captured .exit beside it), using the installed JVM dependencies and code whose schemas/validate.cljc, core/router.cljc and core/elision.cljc blob hashes match the exact merge.
- Pre-classified control: 1 app-db failure, raw-secret-present? false, value-redacted? true, write-rejected? true.
- Same-event classification: 1 app-db failure, raw-secret-present? true, value-redacted? false, write-rejected? true.
- Java exit 0 means both behavioral witnesses matched. No shadow-cljs run or application-source edit was made.

The source rf2-ughf3 closure acknowledges this residual and the separately read rf2-a46kl is already in progress. This new OPEN Bead is the independently trackable merged-PR audit finding; it does not replace or mutate that work.

Small correction: project validation diagnostics through the candidate registry derived from this event's classification effects, using the existing classification path. Keep candidate validation atomic: a rejected event must not install its db or classification effects merely to redact the report.

Acceptance: a same-event sensitive classification plus invalid write emits a failure with no raw secret in any value-bearing diagnostic slot; the already-classified control stays redacted, and both rejected writes leave installed state untouched.

title: Flows: one event, one commit; settle walk-time writes inside the event and publish flow bookkeeping only on install (prototype)
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 to prototype "one event, one commit" for frames running flows. The exit: if the prototype only moves complexity elsewhere, keep today's design and record why on this bead.

This is the question that the static-flows ruling (rf2-yl9dt) left open under "Out of scope, and not decided here": the state-write settle, whether machine and resource writes join the pending commit, and publishing memo rows at install. It is not a reversal of rf2-yl9dt.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

**1. A hidden event per walk-time write.**
- Event stages run in this order: chain, flows (the outermost `:after`), validation, install, then the `:fx` walk.
  - The flows interceptor is prepended at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:984` and runs `run-flows-on-db` at `:772`.
  - `commit-frame-effects!` validates at `:681` and installs at `:690`.
  - `run-fx-effects!` follows at `:1083`.
- So the walk runs after the install. When an effect writes frame state during the walk on a frame with flows, `do-fx` calls `settle-flows-after-walk!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:887`). That queues `[:rf/settle-flows]` with `:rf.flow/settle?` (`:399-403`), head-inserted on the internal lane (`router.cljc:1900`).
- Each settle is its own event with its own epoch, and nothing under `tools/` recognises it. Xray history and time travel show an event nobody dispatched.
- The writers:
  - `:rf.machine/spawn` and `spawn-all-init` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:159`, `:539`, `:1342`, `:1392`);
  - `:rf.machine/destroy` and its exit cascade (`destroy.cljc:223`, `:389`, `:472`, `:631`; `exit_cascade.cljc:119`);
  - machine classification claims (`machines/classification.cljc:182`, `:207`);
  - a user fx calling `swap-runtime-db!`.
- No resource effect writes frame state today, although `fx.cljc:374` and Spec 013:430 name resource writes.

**2. Speculative bookkeeping, rolled back.**
- The flows pass advances the frame's evaluation memo (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:332`) and claims output marks in the live runtime-db (`flows.cljc:325` → `flows/registry.cljc:331`, `:342` → `swap-runtime-db!`) before anyone knows whether the candidate installs.
- Every non-commit path then undoes them:
  - the pass's own throw arm (`restore-output-claims!`, `registry.cljc:70`);
  - the router's `restore!` on each error arm of `commit-and-flow!` (`router.cljc:1037-1073`, `:1077-1079`), reached through the late-bind hooks `:flows/snapshot-last-inputs` and `:flows/restore-last-inputs!` (`flows.cljc:353-354`);
  - epoch's `reset-flows-dirty-check!` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:893-901`, called at `:1163` and `epoch.cljc:622`).

## Change (prototype)

**1. Publish on install.**
- The pass returns a candidate result: the db plus the proposed memo rows and output claims.
- Claims are written into the candidate runtime-db, not the live one, so they install, or vanish, with the frame transition.
- The memo is published only after a successful install.
- Delete `restore-flow-snapshots!`, the two snapshot/restore hooks and the pass's claim hand-back.
- If the memo then lives in frame state, epoch restore rewinds it for free and `reset-flows-dirty-check!` goes. Delete it behind a test that restores, then returns to the cached input.

**2. Settle inside the event.** Replace the queued `[:rf/settle-flows]` event with a flow pass inside the same event, after the walk, before any queued continuation runs. Two shapes to compare; take the smaller:
- **(a)** At the end of the walk, run the flows pass over the post-walk frame state and install its outputs in the same event: one epoch, a second install.
- **(b)** Move the install after the walk, with effects reading a pending overlay. Effects such as `spawn.cljc:1016` read the live container mid-walk and would need redirecting. This is likely the larger change.

**Keep:**
- Spec 013's freshness rule (`spec/013-Flows.md:417`): every flow reflects the walk's writes before any queued continuation runs.
- Failure atomicity.
- Candidate validation.

**Retire `:rf/settle-flows` and `:rf.flow/settle?`.** Keep the id reserved, as retired ids stay reserved.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- Spec 013:
  - §Sequencing (`:417-432`);
  - the drain steps (`:185`, `:192`, `:202-203`);
  - §Failure semantics (`:296-305`; rule 2 becomes "rows advance only with the install");
  - the Resolved section (`:549-555`).
- **Hot zones:**
  - `spec/Conventions.md:46` (the reserved row);
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:2008-2011` (the enqueue pseudocode);
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2029`;
  - `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:483`.
- `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:126`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:90`, and `skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:86`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:264-281`, and `events.cljc:811` and `:1341-1359`.

## Acceptance

**If adopted:**
- A spawn on a flowed frame produces one event and one epoch, and its flows reflect the spawn before the next queued event. Rewrite `flows_mid_walk_write_settle_cljs_test.cljc` (`:89`, `:102` asserts `[:p/two-writes :rf/settle-flows]`, `:104`, `:123`, `:154`) and `flows_user_fx_write_settle_cljs_test.cljc:23` to that.
- Flow-throw and commit-rejection behaviour is unchanged (`flows_rollback_dirty_check_test.clj`: `:40`, `:60`, `:78`, `:94`, `:139`, `:145`). A same-input event after a rejected candidate recomputes.
- Epoch restore and replace leave flows correct (`flows_tool_write_test.clj`: `:56`, `:60`, `:65`, `:75`).
- Count the epoch-count assertions on flowed frames that spawn or destroy actors; they lose an epoch.
- The PR body states the net line count and the hooks removed.
- JVM, `npm run test:cljs`, and the flows, machines and epoch suites green.

**If not adopted:** a note on this bead with the measured reason, and the bead closed.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 15:58:21 AUSEST: dispatched to worktree flows-one-commit (branch worker/flows-one-commit), cut from origin/main at cb9cb3c074. A prototype with the ruling's exit clause. The worker holds spec/009, spec/002, spec/013 and the migration README for this wave.
== WORKER SUMMARY (flows-one-commit), 2026-10-20 16:47:15 AUSEST: ADOPTED, shape (a); draft PR #11576 ==

MEASURED AT TRUNK cb9cb3c074 (JVM, plain-atom substrate, epoch recording on; a container watch counted frame-state writes, the always-on event-emit stream counted events):
- A `:p/spawn` event on a frame running one flow over the spawned child's snapshot, with a `:dispatch` queued before the spawn: 4 events (`:p/spawn`, `:rf/settle-flows`, `:p/record-child`, `:c/one`), 4 epochs, 5 frame-state writes. The `:p/spawn` epoch's `:db-after` holds the flow output stale (`:cstate nil`), so restoring that epoch restores a stale flow.
- A user fx writing runtime-db twice in one walk: 2 events (`:go`, `:rf/settle-flows`), 2 epochs, 4 writes.
- Order at trunk: chain, flow pass (memo advanced and output claims written live), validation, install, `:fx` walk (live writes), then a head-inserted `[:rf/settle-flows]` event with its own pass, install and epoch.

PROTOTYPE, the same two runs: 3 events / 3 epochs / 5 writes, and 1 event / 1 epoch / 4 writes; the spawning event's epoch holds `:cstate :born`. Writes per event do not change: the settle's install moves inside the event, so an event whose walk writes frame state installs twice. "One event, one epoch" holds; "one install per event" does not, which is shape (a) as the ruling describes it.

DECISION: ADOPT. Numbers over the 8 source files (core router, fx, events, late-bind directory, router diagnostics; epoch tool_pair; flows facade and registry): +277 / -454 lines, net -177 (docstrings and comments included); non-comment lines -111; branch forms 554 -> 551.
- Removed: the framework-private settle event (its id constant, nil handler, handler-meta and the router's unresolved-handler entry for it); the `:rf.flow/settle?` envelope flag, child-dispatch opt and known-dispatch-opt entry; the head-insert lane rule for it; the walk-time settle in `do-fx`; the late-bind hooks `:flows/frame-has-flows?`, `:flows/snapshot-last-inputs` and `:flows/restore-last-inputs!`; the router's memo rollback on its five non-commit arms (`restore-flow-snapshots!`); `restore-output-claims!`, `reset-frame-last-inputs-to!`, and the pass's own catch arm.
- Added: `settle-flows-after-walk!` and `publish-flow-memo!` in the router (the post-walk pass reuses `commit-frame-effects!`, so validation, install and traces are the event's own); the pass result `{:db :publish! :claims}`; the claims fold in `commit-frame-effects!`; one late-bind hook, `:flows/distrust-memo!`.
- Concepts a reader holds. Before: a hidden event with its own lane rule, resolution seam, envelope flag, hook and epoch; a memo and claims snapshot taken before every pass and restored on every non-commit path. After: an event runs the flow pass again when its walk wrote state; a pass proposes and the install publishes.

WHERE THIS DIFFERS FROM THE BEAD'S CHANGE TEXT:
1. Claims. The exact claim set rides the candidate runtime-db, but a pass still ADDS (union only) the claims of an output it computes to the live registry before it emits. The `:rf.flow/computed` trace and the t2 `:rf.event/db-pending-post-flow` trace are projected at emit time against the live registry; carrying a candidate registry into t2's projection needs `re-frame.classification`, which is another worker's file. Adding never un-redacts, so a failed pass needs no undo; at worst a throwing replacement that moves its output leaves an extra claim on the new path no output holds (pinned in flows_rollback_dirty_check_test).
2. Memo in frame state: not done, so `reset-flows-dirty-check!` stays, on the narrower `:flows/distrust-memo!`.
